ITID-31111.def: An encrypting ransomware infection in which the initial malware or dropper reached the victim environment through a phishing attachment or a malicious link (e.g., a weaponized document, macro, or hyperlink to a payload host).
ITID-31111.purpose: Captures ransomware encryption incidents that trace back to a phishing email or malicious link as the initial delivery mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Ransomware payload or loader delivered as an email attachment (document, archive, executable)
Ransomware fetched via a link in a phishing email leading to a malicious download
Macro-enabled document that drops a ransomware loader upon user execution
scopeExcludes: Ransomware delivered via an exploited public-facing vulnerability (ITID-31112)
Ransomware delivered via compromised RDP/remote access (ITID-31113)
The extortion/leak-site publication angle of a ransomware incident (handled under the Public Disclosure/Extortion Threats domain, e.g. ITID-23431)
ITID-31111.severity: High. Encryption of endpoint or shared data has immediate business impact regardless of initial vector.
ITID-31111.priority: P1 upon confirmed encryption activity; P2 if caught at the delivery/detonation stage before encryption begins.
ITID-31111.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident response upon detection of ransomware binary execution or mass file-modification behavior; isolate affected hosts before eradication.
indicators: Mass file renaming/extension changes across user or shared drives
Ransom note files dropped in multiple directories
EDR alert on known ransomware loader or packer signature
Email gateway log showing malicious attachment delivered to the affected user
vectors: Phishing email with malicious macro-enabled attachment
Phishing email containing a link to a malicious payload download
Malicious archive attachment bypassing attachment filtering
rootCauses: Insufficient email attachment filtering/sandboxing
Macro execution enabled by default on endpoints
Lack of user awareness training on phishing lures
controls: Email gateway attachment sandboxing
Macro execution blocking via group policy
EDR behavioral detection for mass file modification
Immutable/offline backups
ITID-31111.detection: Strong technical signal from EDR mass-encryption behavioral detection and email gateway logs correlating the delivery artifact to the detonation host.
ITID-31111.response: Isolate affected hosts immediately, identify and block the delivery indicator (sender, URL, attachment hash) across the email gateway, and initiate recovery from backup rather than considering payment.
metrics: Time from delivery to detonation
Time from detonation to containment
Number of hosts encrypted before containment
detections: EDR mass file modification/encryption behavior alert
ITID-31111.notes: Scope is limited to the malware-infection/encryption-technique angle; extortion demands and leak-site publication tied to the same incident are tracked under the Public Disclosure/Extortion Threats domain (e.g. ITID-23431, ITID-23115) to avoid duplicate classification of a single incident.

playbook.name: Response: Ransomware Delivered via Phishing Attachment/Link
playbook.description: For a confirmed encrypting-ransomware incident where the initial infection vector was a malicious email attachment or link.

steps.title: Confirm encryption activity and scope across the environment
steps.desc: Identify all hosts and shares showing active or completed file encryption, not just the first reported system.
steps.guidance: Check file servers and backup targets, not only endpoints — ransomware often reaches mapped/network shares.
steps.outcome: Full scope of encrypted/affected systems established.

steps.title: Trace the phishing delivery vector
steps.desc: Identify the originating email, sender, attachment/link, and every recipient who received the same message.
steps.outcome: Delivery vector confirmed; list of all recipients obtained for containment.

steps.title: Identify the ransomware family and known behaviors
steps.desc: Determine the specific ransomware strain via IOC/sample analysis to inform containment and eradication decisions.
steps.outcome: Ransomware family identified with known TTPs referenced.

steps.title: Isolate the entire affected network segment immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect affected systems from the network at a segment level, not host-by-host, given ransomware's rapid lateral-spread nature.
steps.outcome: Further encryption and lateral movement halted.

steps.title: Block the phishing sender/domain and purge remaining copies of the email
steps.desc: Add sender/domain/URL to email security blocklists and remove the phishing message from all mailboxes org-wide.
steps.outcome: No further users can trigger the same delivery vector.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence before any remediation
steps.desc: Image affected systems and preserve logs/mail artifacts before wiping or rebuilding anything.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for investigation and potential law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Remove the ransomware and any persistence mechanisms
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts of the ransomware payload and any dropped persistence artifacts.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of the ransomware.

steps.title: Verify backup integrity before restoring
steps.desc: Confirm backups predate the compromise and are themselves free of the ransomware before restoring from them.
steps.guidance: Do not restore from a backup that has not been verified clean — this can re-introduce the infection.
steps.outcome: Clean, verified backup identified for restore.
steps.abort: If no clean backup exists, escalate rebuild timeline and options to leadership.

steps.title: Do not pay the ransom; coordinate with Legal and law enforcement if demanded
steps.desc: If a ransom demand is presented, engage Legal and consider law-enforcement referral before any decision is made. Standard guidance is against payment.
steps.guidance: Payment does not guarantee data recovery and may fund further criminal activity; the decision rests with Legal/Executive leadership, not the SOC.
steps.outcome: Leadership/Legal engaged; no unilateral payment made.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce phishing defenses
steps.desc: Record the full timeline and remediate the specific gap (e.g., attachment filtering, user reporting friction) that allowed the phishing email through.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete remediations tracked to completion.

ITID-31112.def: An encrypting ransomware infection in which the adversary gained initial access by exploiting an unpatched or misconfigured internet-facing service or application.
ITID-31112.purpose: Captures ransomware encryption incidents where a public-facing vulnerability was exploited to gain the access used to deploy the payload.
scopeIncludes: Ransomware deployed after exploitation of a public-facing VPN, firewall, or web application vulnerability
Ransomware deployed following exploitation of an unpatched internet-facing server
scopeExcludes: Ransomware delivered via phishing (ITID-31111)
Ransomware delivered via compromised RDP/remote access credentials rather than a software vulnerability (ITID-31113)
ITID-31112.severity: High to Critical, particularly where the exploited service fronts production infrastructure.
ITID-31112.priority: P1 upon confirmed encryption; P1 also for confirmed exploitation of a public-facing vulnerability even pre-encryption given the likely follow-on impact.
ITID-31112.escalation: Escalate to IR and vulnerability management immediately; patch or isolate the exploited service network-wide, not just the initially affected host.
indicators: Exploit-pattern traffic against a public-facing service preceding lateral movement
Web shell or loader artifact on the exploited server
Mass encryption activity originating from the exploited host's network segment
vectors: Exploitation of an unpatched public-facing application or appliance vulnerability
Exploitation of a known CVE with available public proof-of-concept
rootCauses: Delayed patching of internet-facing systems
Lack of network segmentation isolating the exposed service from the broader environment
controls: Timely patch management for internet-facing systems
Network segmentation of exposed services
WAF/IPS virtual patching
Immutable/offline backups
ITID-31112.detection: Good signal where perimeter IDS/IPS and WAF logs capture exploit-pattern traffic; weaker if the vulnerability is zero-day.
ITID-31112.response: Contain the exploited system, patch or remove it from exposure, hunt for lateral movement from that entry point, and restore encrypted assets from backup.
metrics: Time from CVE disclosure/patch availability to exploitation
Number of exposed systems affected
Mean time to patch internet-facing critical vulnerabilities
ITID-31112.notes: Scope excludes the extortion/leak-site publication angle of the same incident, tracked separately under the Public Disclosure/Extortion Threats domain.

playbook.name: Response: Ransomware Delivered via Exploited Public-Facing Vulnerability
playbook.description: For a confirmed encrypting-ransomware incident where the initial access vector was exploitation of a vulnerable internet-facing service or application.

steps.title: Confirm encryption scope across the environment
steps.desc: Identify all hosts and shares showing active or completed file encryption.
steps.outcome: Full scope of encrypted/affected systems established.

steps.title: Identify the exploited vulnerability and public-facing asset
steps.desc: Determine which internet-facing system, application, and CVE (or exploit technique) was used for initial access.
steps.guidance: Check web/application logs and WAF logs around the estimated intrusion window.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable asset and exploit vector confirmed.

steps.title: Determine dwell time and lateral movement path from the entry point
steps.desc: Trace attacker activity from initial exploitation through to the systems where encryption occurred.
steps.outcome: Attack timeline and lateral-movement path established.

steps.title: Isolate the entire affected network segment immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect affected systems from the network at a segment level given ransomware's rapid lateral-spread nature.
steps.outcome: Further encryption and lateral movement halted.

steps.title: Take the vulnerable public-facing service offline or virtually patch it
steps.desc: Remove the exploited service from internet exposure or apply a WAF rule/emergency patch to close the entry point.
steps.outcome: Exploited entry point no longer accessible to attackers.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence before any remediation
steps.desc: Image affected systems and preserve web/application logs before wiping or rebuilding anything.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for investigation and potential law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Patch the vulnerability and remove ransomware/persistence mechanisms
steps.desc: Apply the permanent vendor patch and clean confirmed-compromised hosts of the ransomware payload and any webshells or footholds left behind.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability closed; environment confirmed clean of the ransomware and attacker footholds.

steps.title: Verify backup integrity before restoring
steps.desc: Confirm backups predate the compromise and are themselves free of the ransomware before restoring from them.
steps.outcome: Clean, verified backup identified for restore.
steps.abort: If no clean backup exists, escalate rebuild timeline and options to leadership.

steps.title: Do not pay the ransom; coordinate with Legal and law enforcement if demanded
steps.desc: If a ransom demand is presented, engage Legal and consider law-enforcement referral. Standard guidance is against payment.
steps.outcome: Leadership/Legal engaged; no unilateral payment made.

steps.title: Document the incident and remediate the patching gap
steps.desc: Record the full timeline and address the vulnerability-management gap (e.g., patch cadence, external attack-surface visibility) that allowed exploitation.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete remediations tracked to completion.

ITID-31113.def: An encrypting ransomware infection in which the adversary gained access via compromised Remote Desktop Protocol or another remote-access service (e.g., stolen or brute-forced credentials, exposed RDP).
ITID-31113.purpose: Captures ransomware encryption incidents delivered through compromised RDP or other remote-access credentials/services.
scopeIncludes: Ransomware deployed after brute-force or credential-stuffing compromise of an exposed RDP endpoint
Ransomware deployed using stolen VPN or remote-access credentials purchased from an access broker
scopeExcludes: Ransomware delivered via phishing (ITID-31111)
Ransomware delivered via exploitation of a software vulnerability rather than credential compromise (ITID-31112)
ITID-31113.severity: High. Remote-access compromise often grants broad interactive access before encryption begins.
ITID-31113.priority: P1 upon confirmed encryption; P2 for confirmed unauthorized RDP/remote-access logon pending confirmation of payload deployment.
ITID-31113.escalation: Escalate immediately; disable or rotate the compromised remote-access credentials and isolate the access point network-wide.
indicators: Successful logon to RDP/remote-access service from an anomalous geography or after repeated failed attempts
Interactive logon followed shortly by mass file encryption
Remote-access logs showing use of credentials not recently used by the account owner
vectors: Brute-force or credential-stuffing attack against internet-exposed RDP
Use of credentials purchased from an initial access broker
Reused/weak remote-access passwords without MFA
rootCauses: RDP exposed directly to the internet without MFA
Weak or reused remote-access credentials
Absence of account lockout/rate limiting on remote-access logon
controls: MFA on all remote-access services
RDP gateway/VPN in front of direct internet exposure
Account lockout and anomalous-logon alerting
Immutable/offline backups
ITID-31113.detection: Strong signal from remote-access authentication logs and geo/velocity anomaly detection when correlated with subsequent encryption activity.
ITID-31113.response: Disable the compromised account, terminate active remote sessions, isolate the entry host, and restore from backup while hunting for lateral movement performed during the session.
metrics: Number of exposed remote-access endpoints without MFA
Time from anomalous logon to detection
Time from detonation to containment
ITID-31113.notes: Scope excludes the extortion/leak-site publication angle of the same incident, tracked separately under the Public Disclosure/Extortion Threats domain.

playbook.name: Response: Ransomware Delivered via Compromised RDP/Remote Access
playbook.description: For a confirmed encrypting-ransomware incident where access was gained through compromised Remote Desktop Protocol or another remote-access credential/service.

steps.title: Confirm encryption scope across the environment
steps.desc: Identify all hosts and shares showing active or completed file encryption.
steps.outcome: Full scope of encrypted/affected systems established.

steps.title: Identify the compromised RDP/remote-access account and origin
steps.desc: Determine which account(s) and remote-access entry point (RDP, VPN, remote-management tool) were used, and whether credentials were brute-forced, stuffed, or previously stolen.
steps.guidance: Check for logins from unusual source IPs/geographies and off-hours access patterns.
steps.outcome: Compromised account(s) and remote-access vector identified.

steps.title: Check for other accounts or systems accessed via the same remote-access path
steps.desc: Review whether the same exposed remote-access service was used to access other accounts or hosts prior to the ransomware deployment.
steps.outcome: Full scope of remote-access misuse established.

steps.title: Isolate the entire affected network segment immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect affected systems from the network at a segment level given ransomware's rapid lateral-spread nature.
steps.outcome: Further encryption and lateral movement halted.

steps.title: Disable the compromised accounts and remove RDP from direct internet exposure
steps.desc: Disable/reset the compromised credentials and place remote access behind VPN/MFA-gated access, removing any direct internet-facing RDP.
steps.outcome: Attacker's remote-access path closed.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence before any remediation
steps.desc: Image affected systems and preserve authentication/remote-access logs before wiping or rebuilding anything.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for investigation.

steps.title: Remove the ransomware and enforce MFA on all remote access
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts and require MFA on every remote-access path before it is restored to service.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean; remote access hardened.

steps.title: Verify backup integrity before restoring
steps.desc: Confirm backups predate the compromise and are free of the ransomware before restoring.
steps.outcome: Clean, verified backup identified for restore.
steps.abort: If no clean backup exists, escalate rebuild timeline to leadership.

steps.title: Do not pay the ransom; coordinate with Legal and law enforcement if demanded
steps.desc: If a ransom demand is presented, engage Legal and consider law-enforcement referral. Standard guidance is against payment.
steps.outcome: Leadership/Legal engaged; no unilateral payment made.

steps.title: Document the incident and remediate remote-access exposure
steps.desc: Record the timeline and close the gap (exposed RDP, missing MFA, weak password policy) that enabled the compromise.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete remediations tracked to completion.

ITID-31114.def: An encrypting ransomware infection in which the payload was distributed via a trusted third-party software update, build pipeline, or vendor package that had been compromised upstream.
ITID-31114.purpose: Captures ransomware encryption incidents delivered through a compromised software supply chain or update mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Ransomware bundled into a legitimate vendor's software update that was pushed to customers
Ransomware distributed through a compromised build/CI pipeline of a trusted software vendor
scopeExcludes: Ransomware delivered via phishing, exploited vulnerability, or compromised remote access (ITID-31111, 31112, 31113)
Non-ransomware backdoors delivered via compromised software updates (ITID-31214)
ITID-31114.severity: Critical. Supply-chain delivery typically affects many downstream organizations simultaneously.
ITID-31114.priority: P1 immediately upon suspicion of a compromised trusted update, regardless of confirmed encryption.
ITID-31114.escalation: Escalate to IR and vendor-risk management immediately; halt deployment of the affected update fleet-wide and notify the vendor.
indicators: Ransomware detonation shortly after installing a routine vendor update
Vendor advisory confirming a compromised release
Anomalous outbound connections from the updated software immediately post-installation
vectors: Compromise of a software vendor's build or release pipeline
Compromise of a software update/distribution server
rootCauses: Insufficient code-signing/integrity verification of vendor updates
Lack of vendor supply-chain security assessment
No staged/canary rollout of third-party updates
controls: Code-signing verification for third-party software
Staged/canary rollout of vendor updates
Vendor supply-chain risk assessment program
Immutable/offline backups
ITID-31114.detection: Detection depends heavily on EDR behavioral alerting post-installation and vendor disclosure; pre-installation detection is typically weak.
ITID-31114.response: Halt further rollout of the affected update, isolate systems that received it, coordinate with the vendor on remediation, and restore from backup.
metrics: Number of hosts receiving the compromised update
Time from vendor advisory to internal containment
Time from detonation to containment
detections: EDR mass encryption behavior alert following software update
ITID-31114.notes: Scope covers ransomware payloads specifically; a non-ransomware backdoor delivered the same way is tracked under ITID-31214. Extortion/leak-site angle tracked under the Public Disclosure/Extortion Threats domain.

playbook.name: Response: Ransomware Deployed via Compromised Software Supply Chain/Update
playbook.description: For a confirmed encrypting-ransomware incident delivered through a compromised software vendor update or supply-chain component.

steps.title: Confirm encryption scope across the environment
steps.desc: Identify all hosts and shares showing active or completed file encryption, prioritizing every system that received the compromised update.
steps.outcome: Full scope of encrypted/affected systems established.
steps.tool: EDR fleet query / software deployment inventory

steps.title: Identify the compromised software/vendor and affected version
steps.desc: Determine which product, update package, or build was compromised and the distribution window.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the vendor's security advisory if one has been issued.
steps.outcome: Compromised product/version and distribution window identified.

steps.title: Enumerate every system in the org that installed the compromised update
steps.desc: Cross-reference the deployment/patch-management inventory to find every host that pulled the compromised update, not just those already showing encryption.
steps.outcome: Complete list of exposed systems, including those not yet encrypted.

steps.title: Isolate the entire affected network segment immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect affected systems from the network at a segment level given ransomware's rapid lateral-spread nature.
steps.outcome: Further encryption and lateral movement halted.

steps.title: Block further distribution of the compromised update org-wide
steps.desc: Halt the update channel/repository and prevent any remaining exposed systems from installing the malicious package.
steps.outcome: No further systems can receive the compromised update.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence before any remediation
steps.desc: Image affected systems and preserve the compromised installer/update artifact for analysis.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for investigation and vendor coordination.

steps.title: Remove the ransomware and roll back to a known-clean software version
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts and reinstall a verified-clean version of the affected software once the vendor confirms remediation.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean; affected software restored to a trusted version.

steps.title: Verify backup integrity before restoring
steps.desc: Confirm backups predate the compromised update's distribution and are free of the ransomware before restoring.
steps.outcome: Clean, verified backup identified for restore.
steps.abort: If no clean backup exists, escalate rebuild timeline to leadership.

steps.title: Do not pay the ransom; coordinate with Legal and law enforcement if demanded
steps.desc: If a ransom demand is presented, engage Legal and consider law-enforcement referral. Standard guidance is against payment.
steps.outcome: Leadership/Legal engaged; no unilateral payment made.

steps.title: Document the incident and reassess supply-chain trust controls
steps.desc: Record the timeline and evaluate update-signing verification, vendor risk assessment, and staged-rollout controls to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete remediations tracked to completion.

ITID-31115.def: An encrypting ransomware infection deployed by an affiliate using a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) offering, where the payload, leak infrastructure, and negotiation tooling are provided by a separate operator group.
ITID-31115.purpose: Captures ransomware encryption incidents carried out by an affiliate operating under a Ransomware-as-a-Service program.
scopeIncludes: Ransomware payload attributable to a known RaaS family/affiliate program
Incidents where negotiation and leak-site infrastructure is confirmed to be operated by a distinct RaaS group from the deploying affiliate
scopeExcludes: Ransomware developed and operated end-to-end by a single non-affiliate actor (see other leaves in this Type based on delivery vector)
The extortion negotiation/leak-site publication itself (Public Disclosure/Extortion Threats domain)
ITID-31115.severity: High to Critical; RaaS affiliates commonly combine encryption with double extortion.
ITID-31115.priority: P1 upon confirmed encryption or identification of a known RaaS payload/toolkit signature.
ITID-31115.escalation: Escalate immediately to IR; treat as a professionalized, likely double-extortion operation and engage legal/communications early.
indicators: Payload matching a known RaaS family signature/hash
Ransom note referencing a known affiliate program's leak-site branding
Use of affiliate-standard toolkits/utilities alongside the encryptor
vectors: Affiliate-driven intrusion using whatever initial access vector the affiliate obtained (purchased access, phishing, exploited vulnerability)
Deployment of a RaaS-provided encryptor binary following manual hands-on-keyboard staging
rootCauses: Same root causes as the initial access vector used by the affiliate (see sibling leaves)
Lack of threat-intel-informed detection tuned to known RaaS toolkits
controls: Threat-intelligence-informed detection for known RaaS families
Immutable/offline backups
EDR behavioral detection for mass encryption and service-stop activity
ITID-31115.detection: Strong when threat intel provides known indicators for the affiliate's toolkit; otherwise relies on generic mass-encryption behavioral detection.
ITID-31115.response: Treat as a high-sophistication, likely double-extortion incident from the outset; engage full IR, legal, and executive stakeholders and restore from backup rather than pay.
metrics: Number of incidents attributed per known RaaS family
Time from detonation to containment
ITID-31115.notes: This leaf classifies by business model (RaaS affiliate) rather than delivery vector, since a given RaaS affiliate may use any initial access method; where the specific delivery vector is also known, both this leaf and the vector-specific leaf may be relevant context but only one primary classification should be recorded. Extortion/leak-site angle tracked under the Public Disclosure/Extortion Threats domain.

playbook.name: Response: Ransomware Deployed by Affiliate via Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS)
playbook.description: For a confirmed encrypting-ransomware incident where the deployment was carried out by an independent affiliate operating a RaaS platform's payload.

steps.title: Confirm encryption scope across the environment
steps.desc: Identify all hosts and shares showing active or completed file encryption.
steps.outcome: Full scope of encrypted/affected systems established.

steps.title: Identify the RaaS family and affiliate-specific tradecraft
steps.desc: Determine the ransomware-as-a-service brand from the payload/ransom note and note any affiliate-specific tooling observed (varies by affiliate even under the same RaaS brand).
steps.outcome: RaaS family identified; affiliate tradecraft documented.

steps.title: Investigate the full initial-access chain used by the affiliate
steps.desc: Determine how the affiliate gained initial access, which may be entirely independent of the RaaS operator and could involve a purchased access broker foothold, phishing, or exploited vulnerability.
steps.guidance: RaaS affiliates commonly obtain initial access separately from the ransomware payload itself — investigate this as its own timeline, not just the encryption event.
steps.outcome: Initial access vector and timeline established.

steps.title: Isolate the entire affected network segment immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect affected systems from the network at a segment level given ransomware's rapid lateral-spread nature.
steps.outcome: Further encryption and lateral movement halted.

steps.title: Close the full access chain identified, not just the payload's drop point
steps.desc: Remediate every foothold used along the access chain (initial vector, any purchased-access artifacts, lateral-movement tools) to prevent re-entry by the same or a different affiliate.
steps.outcome: All identified access points closed.

steps.title: Engage Legal, Executive leadership, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Notify Legal and executives; consider law-enforcement referral. Do not engage with the extortion demand without Legal involvement.
steps.outcome: Leadership engaged and coordinating the business/legal response track.

steps.title: Remove the ransomware and every persistence/access mechanism found
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts and close the full initial-access chain identified during investigation.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of the ransomware and the affiliate's access.

steps.title: Verify backup integrity before restoring
steps.desc: Confirm backups predate the compromise and are free of the ransomware before restoring.
steps.outcome: Clean, verified backup identified for restore.
steps.abort: If no clean backup exists, escalate rebuild timeline to leadership.

steps.title: Do not pay the ransom; leadership/Legal make the final call
steps.desc: Standard guidance is against payment given no guarantee of data recovery or that stolen data will be deleted.
steps.outcome: Payment decision made deliberately by Legal/Executive, not unilaterally by IR staff.

steps.title: Document the full incident including the access-chain findings
steps.desc: Record the complete timeline from initial access through payload deployment, and remediate the specific gaps that allowed the chain to succeed.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete remediations tracked to completion.

ITID-31116.def: An encrypting ransomware infection not yet attributable to a specific delivery vector (phishing, exploited vulnerability, compromised remote access, supply chain) or business model (RaaS affiliate).
ITID-31116.purpose: Catch-all for encrypting ransomware incidents that do not fit a more specific delivery-vector or business-model leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the initial access vector has been confirmed
Ransomware incidents where the delivery mechanism remains undetermined after initial triage
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID under Encrypting Ransomware
ITID-31116.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High by default given the encryption impact.
ITID-31116.priority: P1 by default given active encryption impact, reclassified once the vector is confirmed.
ITID-31116.escalation: Escalate immediately as with any confirmed encryption event; reclassify to the specific leaf once the initial access vector is determined.
indicators: Mass file encryption/ransom note with initial access vector not yet determined
vectors: Activity of unclear specific initial access vector
rootCauses: Insufficient forensic detail captured at time of detection
controls: Immutable/offline backups
EDR behavioral detection for mass encryption
ITID-31116.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification of the initial access vector.
ITID-31116.response: Contain and restore as with any ransomware incident; investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once the vector is confirmed.
metrics: Count of encrypting ransomware incidents pending vector reclassification
ITID-31116.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Encrypting Ransomware
playbook.description: For a confirmed encrypting-ransomware incident where the specific initial-access vector has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm encryption scope across the environment
steps.desc: Identify all hosts and shares showing active or completed file encryption, not just the first reported system.
steps.outcome: Full scope of encrypted/affected systems established.

steps.title: Determine the initial-access vector
steps.desc: Investigate email, remote-access, vulnerability, and supply-chain vectors to determine how the ransomware entered the environment.
steps.outcome: Initial access vector identified or narrowed to a short list.

steps.title: Identify the ransomware family
steps.desc: Determine the specific ransomware strain via IOC/sample analysis and ransom-note characteristics to inform response.
steps.outcome: Ransomware family identified where possible.

steps.title: Isolate the entire affected network segment immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect affected systems from the network at a segment level, not host-by-host, given ransomware's rapid lateral-spread nature.
steps.outcome: Further encryption and lateral movement halted.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence before any remediation
steps.desc: Image affected systems and preserve logs before wiping or rebuilding anything.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for investigation.

steps.title: Engage Legal and Executive leadership
steps.desc: Notify Legal and executives of the incident and any extortion demand. Do not engage with any ransom demand without Legal involvement.
steps.outcome: Leadership engaged and coordinating the business/legal response track.

steps.title: Remove the ransomware and any persistence mechanisms
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts of the ransomware payload and any dropped persistence artifacts once the access vector is closed.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of the ransomware.

steps.title: Verify backup integrity before restoring
steps.desc: Confirm backups predate the compromise and are free of the ransomware before restoring from them.
steps.outcome: Clean, verified backup identified for restore.
steps.abort: If no clean backup exists, escalate rebuild timeline and options to leadership.

steps.title: Do not pay the ransom; coordinate with Legal and law enforcement if demanded
steps.desc: If a ransom demand is presented, engage Legal and consider law-enforcement referral. Standard guidance is against payment.
steps.outcome: Leadership/Legal engaged; no unilateral payment made.

steps.title: Document the incident and finalize root-cause remediation
steps.desc: Record the full timeline once the access vector is confirmed and track remediation of the specific gap to completion.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete remediations tracked to completion.

ITID-31121.def: Ransomware that locks the user out of the desktop/screen (a full-screen ransom message overlay) on a consumer or standard endpoint, without encrypting underlying files.
ITID-31121.purpose: Captures screen-locking ransomware affecting consumer or standard endpoint devices, without file encryption.
scopeIncludes: Full-screen lock overlay demanding payment on a Windows/macOS/Linux endpoint
Locker malware that disables normal desktop interaction but leaves the file system unencrypted
scopeExcludes: MBR/bootloader-level lockers that prevent the OS from booting at all (ITID-31122)
Mobile-device screen lockers (ITID-31123)
Any ransomware that encrypts files (Encrypting Ransomware leaves under 31111-31116)
ITID-31121.severity: Medium. Disruptive but typically does not destroy data, and is usually straightforward to remediate by rebuilding the endpoint.
ITID-31121.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if propagating across multiple endpoints.
ITID-31121.escalation: Escalate to endpoint security if the lock overlay is observed on more than one host or resists standard removal tooling.
indicators: Full-screen ransom message preventing normal desktop use
EDR/AV detection of known screen-locker family
User report of being unable to access the desktop after a suspicious download or ad-click
vectors: Malicious advertisement or drive-by download bundling a screen-locker
Fake software installer bundling a screen-locker payload
rootCauses: Lack of endpoint protection against known locker families
Users running untrusted downloaded executables with local admin rights
controls: Endpoint protection/AV signature and behavioral detection
Removal of unnecessary local admin rights
Application allowlisting
ITID-31121.detection: Good; screen-lock behavior is a well-known signature/behavioral pattern for most endpoint protection products.
ITID-31121.response: Isolate the host, remove the locker via safe-mode/removal tooling or reimage, and verify no underlying file encryption occurred.
metrics: Number of screen-locker incidents per quarter
Mean time to remediate
ITID-31121.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by target platform/impact layer: this leaf is desktop-screen-level locking on a standard endpoint, distinct from MBR/bootloader-level and mobile-device locking.

playbook.name: Response: Screen Locker Ransomware (Consumer/Endpoint)
playbook.description: For a confirmed screen-locker ransomware incident on a consumer or endpoint device that blocks normal system use without necessarily encrypting files.

steps.title: Confirm the lock is a screen locker, not file-encrypting ransomware
steps.desc: Distinguish between a screen/UI lock and actual file encryption by examining the device offline or via a bootable rescue medium.
steps.guidance: Screen lockers often make false encryption claims to pressure payment; verify actual file state before assuming data loss.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether files are actually encrypted or only UI access is blocked.

steps.title: Identify the delivery vector for the locker
steps.desc: Determine how the locker was installed (malicious download, drive-by, bundled installer) to prevent recurrence on this and other devices.
steps.outcome: Delivery vector identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected device from the network
steps.desc: Disconnect the device from Wi-Fi/network to prevent any command-and-control communication or further activity.
steps.outcome: Device isolated.

steps.title: Preserve the device state before remediation
steps.desc: Capture screenshots/photos of the lock screen and any ransom demand before proceeding with removal.
steps.outcome: Evidence of the lock screen and demand preserved.

steps.title: Remove the locker via safe mode or bootable rescue media
steps.desc: Boot the device into safe mode or from clean rescue media and remove the locker malware and any associated persistence.
steps.guidance: Do not pay to unlock — many lockers can be removed without payment via offline remediation tools.
steps.outcome: Device unlocked and confirmed free of the locker malware.
steps.abort: If removal is not possible, escalate to a full OS reimage.

steps.title: Verify file integrity and restore normal access
steps.desc: Confirm user files are intact (screen lockers typically do not encrypt) and restore the device to normal use.
steps.outcome: Device fully operational with data confirmed intact.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce safe-download practices
steps.desc: Record how the locker was installed and provide guidance/controls to prevent recurrence (e.g., browser protections, download restrictions).
steps.outcome: Finding logged; user guidance or controls updated.

ITID-31122.def: Ransomware that modifies or overwrites the Master Boot Record (MBR) or system bootloader so the affected device cannot boot into its operating system, displaying a ransom demand instead.
ITID-31122.purpose: Captures locker ransomware that overwrites the Master Boot Record or bootloader to prevent the operating system from starting.
scopeIncludes: Malware overwriting the MBR/bootloader with a custom ransom-screen loader
Malware rendering a device unbootable pending payment, independent of file-level encryption
scopeExcludes: Screen lockers operating within a running OS session (ITID-31121)
Mobile-device lockers (ITID-31123)
File-encrypting ransomware that also happens to affect boot recovery options (ITID-31111-31116, with recovery inhibition tracked via T1490 there)
ITID-31122.severity: High. An unbootable device is a hard availability impact requiring hands-on recovery.
ITID-31122.priority: P1 upon confirmation that affected devices cannot boot.
ITID-31122.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT operations/desktop support for physical/remote recovery imaging; treat as a fleet-wide risk if the same loader is seen on multiple hosts.
indicators: Device fails to boot past a custom ransom-screen loader
Pre-boot ransom message referencing payment instructions
EDR/AV pre-execution detection of MBR-modifying behavior on a device shortly before it goes offline
vectors: Malware with direct disk-write access modifying the MBR/bootloader
Delivery via a dropper that gains sufficient privilege to write to raw disk sectors
rootCauses: Endpoints running without boot-integrity protections (e.g., Secure Boot misconfigured/disabled)
Excessive local administrator privileges enabling raw disk access
controls: Secure Boot / boot-integrity enforcement
Restriction of raw disk-write access via least-privilege endpoint accounts
Full-disk encryption with pre-boot authentication as an indirect barrier
ITID-31122.detection: Limited once the boot sector is already overwritten; best detection is pre-execution EDR flagging of MBR-write behavior before the device goes unbootable.
ITID-31122.response: Do not attempt in-place repair without forensic imaging; rebuild/reimage the device from known-good media and restore user data from backup.
metrics: Number of devices rendered unbootable per incident
Mean time to reimage/recover
detections: EDR pre-execution MBR/boot-sector write behavior alert
ITID-31122.notes: Differentiated by target layer: this leaf is boot-level unavailability, distinct from within-OS screen locking and mobile-device locking.

playbook.name: Response: MBR/Bootloader Locker Ransomware
playbook.description: For a confirmed ransomware incident where the Master Boot Record or bootloader has been overwritten to prevent the system from booting normally.

steps.title: Confirm MBR/bootloader compromise
steps.desc: Use a bootable diagnostic/rescue medium to confirm the MBR or bootloader has been modified and determine whether the underlying file system is intact.
steps.outcome: MBR/bootloader compromise confirmed; underlying file-system state assessed.

steps.title: Identify the delivery vector
steps.desc: Determine how the malware achieved the privilege level needed to modify the MBR/bootloader.
steps.outcome: Delivery/privilege-escalation vector identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected device from the network
steps.desc: Physically disconnect the device to prevent any network-based propagation or command-and-control activity.
steps.outcome: Device isolated.

steps.title: Preserve the disk image before remediation
steps.desc: Create a forensic image of the affected disk before attempting boot-record repair, to preserve evidence and allow data-recovery attempts.
steps.outcome: Disk image preserved.

steps.title: Repair or rebuild the boot record from clean media
steps.desc: Use bootable rescue media to restore a clean MBR/bootloader, or rebuild the system from a known-clean image if repair is not reliable.
steps.outcome: System boots normally with the malicious bootloader removed.
steps.abort: If repair is unreliable, escalate to full disk wipe and rebuild.

steps.title: Verify data integrity and restore from backup if needed
steps.desc: Confirm user data on the drive is accessible and intact; restore from backup if the file system was damaged.
steps.outcome: Data confirmed intact or restored; system fully operational.

steps.title: Document the incident and review endpoint hardening
steps.desc: Record the timeline and evaluate boot-integrity protections (Secure Boot, disk encryption with pre-boot authentication) to reduce recurrence risk.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; hardening recommendations tracked.

ITID-31123.def: Ransomware affecting a mobile device (smartphone/tablet) that locks the screen, sets an unauthorized device PIN/password, or otherwise denies normal device use pending payment.
ITID-31123.purpose: Captures locker ransomware targeting mobile devices, locking the device screen or setting a device PIN without consent.
scopeIncludes: Malicious mobile app that sets device admin privileges to lock the screen or reset the PIN
Mobile ransomware displaying a persistent ransom overlay that cannot be dismissed
scopeExcludes: Desktop/laptop screen lockers (ITID-31121)
MBR/bootloader-level lockers (ITID-31122)
Mobile banking trojans that steal credentials rather than lock the device (ITID-31222)
ITID-31123.severity: Medium, higher for corporate-managed (MDM-enrolled) devices holding business data.
ITID-31123.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for corporate-owned or MDM-enrolled devices.
ITID-31123.escalation: Escalate to mobile device management (MDM) administrators to remotely wipe/reset the affected device where enrolled.
indicators: Persistent ransom overlay on a mobile device that cannot be dismissed
Device admin privileges granted to an unrecognized app
MDM alert on an unauthorized device-admin/lock change
vectors: Malicious app installed from outside the official app store (sideloading)
Malicious app abusing device administrator API permissions granted during installation
rootCauses: Sideloading of apps from untrusted sources
Lack of MDM enforcement restricting installation sources on corporate devices
controls: MDM policy restricting app installation to approved stores
Mobile threat defense (MTD) app scanning
Remote wipe/reset capability via MDM
ITID-31123.detection: Moderate; MDM and mobile threat defense tooling can flag unauthorized device-admin grants, but visibility is generally lower than on managed desktop endpoints.
ITID-31123.response: Remotely wipe/reset the device via MDM where enrolled, or guide the user through manufacturer-level factory reset; revoke any corporate access tied to the device pending confirmation it is clean.
metrics: Number of mobile locker incidents per quarter
Percentage of affected devices remediated via MDM remote action
detections: Mobile threat defense malicious app detection
ITID-31123.notes: Differentiated by target platform (mobile) from the desktop/OS-level and boot-level locker leaves.

playbook.name: Response: Mobile Device Locker Ransomware
playbook.description: For a confirmed ransomware incident locking a mobile device's screen or functionality via a malicious app or profile.

steps.title: Confirm the lock mechanism and identify the malicious app/profile
steps.desc: Determine whether the lock was caused by a malicious app, a rogue device-admin/MDM profile, or an over-privileged permission grant.
steps.outcome: Locking mechanism and responsible app/profile identified.

steps.title: Determine whether the device is enrolled in corporate MDM
steps.desc: Check enrollment status so remote remediation options (remote wipe, profile removal) can be assessed.
steps.outcome: MDM enrollment status and available remote options confirmed.

steps.title: Isolate the device from corporate resources
steps.desc: Revoke the device's access to corporate email, VPN, and cloud services pending remediation.
steps.outcome: Device access to corporate resources revoked.

steps.title: Remove the malicious app/profile or perform a factory reset
steps.desc: Where safe-mode/admin removal is not possible, perform a remote or manual factory reset of the device to remove the locker.
steps.guidance: Do not pay any unlock fee — factory reset via recovery mode is generally effective against mobile lockers.
steps.outcome: Device unlocked and free of the malicious app/profile.

steps.title: Restore the device from a known-clean backup
steps.desc: Reprovision the device from MDM policy and restore user data from a clean backup, avoiding the same app source.
steps.outcome: Device fully restored to a trusted, working state.

steps.title: Rotate credentials that were accessible from the device
steps.desc: Reset passwords/tokens for accounts that were logged in on the device while compromised.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Document the incident and reinforce mobile app-installation controls
steps.desc: Record how the malicious app/profile was installed and tighten app-store restrictions or MDM policy accordingly.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; mobile policy updated.

ITID-31124.def: Locker ransomware not yet attributable to a specific target platform (standard endpoint screen lock, MBR/bootloader, or mobile device).
ITID-31124.purpose: Catch-all for locker ransomware incidents that do not fit a more specific target-platform leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the affected platform/layer has been confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID under Locker Ransomware
ITID-31124.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-31124.escalation: Reclassify once the affected platform/layer is clarified.
indicators: Device or system locked with a ransom demand, specific platform not yet determined
vectors: Activity of unclear specific vector or target platform
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: EDR behavioral detection for screen-lock/UI hijack processes
Application allowlisting to block untrusted executables
Offline/immutable backups for rapid recovery
User awareness training on ransomware lures
ITID-31124.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-31124.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-31124.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Locker Ransomware
playbook.description: For a confirmed locker-ransomware incident (device/screen access blocked without confirmed file encryption) where the specific delivery mechanism has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm the nature of the lock and rule out file encryption
steps.desc: Determine whether the incident is a UI/access lock only, or whether files have also been encrypted, using offline inspection where possible.
steps.outcome: Lock type confirmed and file-encryption status established.

steps.title: Determine the delivery vector and platform
steps.desc: Identify whether the affected device is a desktop, server, or mobile device and how the locker was delivered.
steps.outcome: Delivery vector and platform identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected device from the network
steps.desc: Disconnect the device to prevent any command-and-control communication or spread to other systems.
steps.outcome: Device isolated.

steps.title: Preserve evidence before remediation
steps.desc: Capture the lock screen/ransom demand and image the device where feasible before remediation.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved.

steps.title: Remove the locker using appropriate offline/rescue tooling
steps.desc: Use safe mode, rescue media, or a factory reset (as appropriate to the platform) to remove the locker without paying.
steps.outcome: Device unlocked and confirmed clean.
steps.abort: If removal is unreliable, escalate to full rebuild/reimage.

steps.title: Verify data integrity and restore normal operation
steps.desc: Confirm data is intact (or restore from backup if needed) and return the device to normal service.
steps.outcome: Device fully operational with data confirmed intact.

steps.title: Document the incident and close the identified delivery gap
steps.desc: Record the timeline and remediate the specific control gap once the delivery vector is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; remediation tracked.

ITID-31131.def: The data-exfiltration phase of a double extortion ransomware attack, performed using a known/standard affiliate toolkit (e.g., commodity exfiltration or file-transfer utilities associated with a ransomware program), occurring before file encryption.
ITID-31131.purpose: Captures the pre-encryption data exfiltration stage of a double extortion ransomware incident carried out using a standard affiliate exfiltration toolkit.
scopeIncludes: Use of a known affiliate exfiltration tool to stage and transfer data out of the environment ahead of encryption
Bulk data staging (archiving to a single location) preceding a confirmed encryption event
scopeExcludes: Automated/self-orchestrated exfiltration staging with no standard toolkit involved (ITID-31132)
Exfiltration following extended dwell-time reconnaissance as the defining characteristic (ITID-31133)
The extortion demand and leak-site publication of exfiltrated data (Public Disclosure/Extortion Threats domain, e.g. ITID-23115, ITID-23431)
ITID-31131.severity: High to Critical; data exfiltration converts an availability incident into a confidentiality breach as well.
ITID-31131.priority: P1 upon confirmed exfiltration, independent of whether encryption has yet occurred.
ITID-31131.escalation: Escalate to IR, legal, and privacy/compliance immediately upon confirmed exfiltration, as breach notification obligations may apply regardless of the encryption outcome.
indicators: Large outbound data transfer to an unfamiliar cloud storage or file-transfer endpoint
Use of a known affiliate exfiltration binary or utility identified via EDR/network telemetry
Archive files staged in unusual locations shortly before encryption begins
vectors: Use of a known commodity or affiliate-provided exfiltration/file-transfer tool
Abuse of legitimate cloud storage/sync services for exfiltration
rootCauses: Insufficient egress monitoring/DLP on bulk outbound transfers
Lack of network segmentation limiting access to sensitive data stores prior to encryption
controls: Egress traffic monitoring and DLP on bulk outbound transfers
Network segmentation limiting lateral reach to sensitive data
Immutable/offline backups
ITID-31131.detection: Moderate; large outbound transfer volume and destination anomalies are detectable via network/DLP telemetry if egress monitoring is in place.
ITID-31131.response: Confirm scope and sensitivity of exfiltrated data, engage legal/privacy for breach notification assessment, and proceed with standard ransomware containment and recovery.
metrics: Volume of data exfiltrated prior to encryption
Time from exfiltration start to detection
ITID-31131.notes: Scope is limited to the technical exfiltration/staging activity; the extortion demand and any leak-site publication of the stolen data are tracked under the Public Disclosure/Extortion Threats domain to avoid duplicate classification of the same incident.

playbook.name: Response: Pre-Encryption Data Exfiltration via Ransomware Affiliate Toolkit
playbook.description: For a confirmed double-extortion ransomware incident where data was exfiltrated by the affiliate's toolkit before file encryption began.

steps.title: Confirm encryption scope across the environment
steps.desc: Identify every host/share showing signs of encryption, not just the first reported system.
steps.outcome: Full encryption scope established.

steps.title: Investigate the pre-encryption exfiltration separately
steps.desc: Review network/DLP/cloud logs for the days-to-weeks before encryption for signs of bulk data staging and transfer, a distinct activity from the encryption itself.
steps.guidance: Double-extortion affiliates typically exfiltrate well before triggering encryption — investigate this as its own timeline.
steps.outcome: Scope and content of exfiltrated data established.
steps.tool: Network logs / DLP / cloud audit logs

steps.title: Identify the full initial-access chain
steps.desc: Determine how the affiliate initially gained access, which may predate the exfiltration by days or weeks.
steps.outcome: Initial access vector and timeline established.

steps.title: Isolate the entire affected network segment immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect affected systems from the network at a segment level, not host-by-host, given ransomware's lateral-spread speed.
steps.outcome: Further encryption and lateral movement halted.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence before any remediation
steps.desc: Image affected systems and preserve logs before wiping/rebuilding anything.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for investigation and potential law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Engage Legal, Executive leadership, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Notify Legal and executives; consider FBI/law-enforcement referral. Do not engage with the extortion demand without Legal involvement.
steps.guidance: Standard guidance is against paying — Legal/Executive make the final call, not the SOC.
steps.outcome: Leadership engaged and coordinating the business/legal response track.

steps.title: Remove the ransomware and every persistence/access mechanism found
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts and close the full initial-access chain identified during investigation.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of the ransomware and the affiliate's access.

steps.title: Verify backup integrity before restoring
steps.desc: Confirm backups predate the compromise and are themselves free of the ransomware/backdoor before restoring from them.
steps.outcome: Clean, verified backup identified for restore.
steps.abort: If no clean backup exists, escalate rebuild timeline and options to leadership.

steps.title: Assess breach-notification obligations for the exfiltrated data
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Privacy on notification requirements given the confirmed data exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations determined and executed.

steps.title: Document the full incident and remediate root-cause access gaps
steps.desc: Record the full timeline (initial access through exfiltration through encryption) and remediate the specific gaps that allowed it.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete remediations tracked to completion.

ITID-31132.def: A double extortion ransomware incident in which the exfiltration-staging step is performed by automated tooling (e.g., a scripted or built-in exfiltration module in the ransomware toolkit) rather than manual, hands-on selection of data.
ITID-31132.purpose: Captures double extortion ransomware incidents where exfiltration staging is largely automated rather than manually operated.
scopeIncludes: Ransomware toolkits with a built-in automated exfiltration/staging module that runs with minimal operator interaction
Scripted bulk-collection-and-transfer routines executed immediately before or during encryption
scopeExcludes: Manually operated exfiltration using a standard affiliate toolkit (ITID-31131)
Exfiltration following extended manual reconnaissance/dwell time (ITID-31133)
ITID-31132.priority: P1 upon confirmed automated exfiltration activity.
ITID-31132.escalation: Escalate immediately; automated staging can move large volumes of data very quickly, so early containment of egress paths is time-critical.
indicators: Rapid, scripted enumeration and staging of files across multiple systems in a short window
Automated compression/archiving jobs triggered near-simultaneously across hosts
Outbound transfer volume spiking sharply in a short time window
vectors: Ransomware toolkit with an integrated automated data-collection/exfiltration module
Scripted mass file-copy-and-transfer routine deployed alongside the encryptor
rootCauses: Insufficient rate-limiting/anomaly detection on internal file-share access patterns
Lack of egress monitoring capable of detecting rapid automated transfer spikes
controls: Anomaly detection on rapid, broad file-share access patterns
Egress bandwidth/volume alerting
Immutable/offline backups
ITID-31132.detection: Good where behavioral analytics can flag the unusually rapid, broad access pattern characteristic of automated collection.
ITID-31132.response: Cut egress paths immediately upon detection, assess data scope quickly given the speed of automated staging, and proceed with standard containment/recovery.
metrics: Time from automated staging start to egress blocked
Volume of data staged/exfiltrated
detections: Behavioral analytics rapid mass file-access alert
ITID-31132.notes: Extortion demand and leak-site publication tracked separately under the Public Disclosure/Extortion Threats domain.

playbook.name: Response: Double Extortion Ransomware with Automated Exfiltration Staging
playbook.description: For a confirmed double-extortion ransomware incident where the exfiltration was performed by automated tooling that stages and transfers data in bulk ahead of encryption.

steps.title: Confirm encryption scope across the environment
steps.desc: Identify every host/share showing signs of encryption.
steps.outcome: Full encryption scope established.

steps.title: Identify the automated exfiltration tooling and staging locations
steps.desc: Locate archive/staging directories, compression tool usage, and the exfiltration destination (cloud storage, attacker-controlled server) used by the automated toolkit.
steps.guidance: Automated staging tools often leave distinct artifacts (archive files, unusual outbound transfer patterns) separate from the encryption payload — investigate this as its own line.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration mechanism, staged data volume, and destination identified.

steps.title: Determine the scope and sensitivity of exfiltrated data
steps.desc: Review staged archive contents/logs to determine what categories of data (PII, financial, IP) were exfiltrated.
steps.outcome: Data sensitivity and scope established for notification assessment.

steps.title: Isolate the entire affected network segment immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect affected systems at a segment level given ransomware's rapid lateral-spread nature.
steps.outcome: Further encryption and lateral movement halted.

steps.title: Block outbound transfer to the identified exfiltration destination
steps.desc: Block the attacker-controlled cloud storage/server destination at the firewall/proxy to stop any ongoing transfer.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration blocked.

steps.title: Engage Legal, Executive leadership, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Notify Legal and executives; consider law-enforcement referral. Do not engage with the extortion demand without Legal involvement.
steps.outcome: Leadership engaged and coordinating the business/legal response track.

steps.title: Remove the ransomware and the automated exfiltration tooling
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts of both the ransomware payload and any staging/exfiltration scripts or utilities.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of the ransomware and exfiltration tooling.

steps.title: Verify backup integrity before restoring
steps.desc: Confirm backups predate the compromise and are free of the ransomware before restoring.
steps.outcome: Clean, verified backup identified for restore.
steps.abort: If no clean backup exists, escalate rebuild timeline to leadership.

steps.title: Assess breach-notification obligations for the exfiltrated data
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Privacy on notification requirements given the confirmed exfiltration scope and data sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations determined and executed.

steps.title: Document the full incident and remediate data-loss-prevention gaps
steps.desc: Record the full timeline and address the DLP/egress-monitoring gap that allowed bulk staged data to leave undetected.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete remediations tracked to completion.

ITID-31133.def: A double extortion ransomware incident characterized by a prolonged dwell time in which the adversary conducted manual reconnaissance and data discovery within the environment before staging exfiltration and deploying the encryptor.
ITID-31133.purpose: Captures double extortion ransomware incidents preceded by an extended period of manual, hands-on-keyboard reconnaissance before exfiltration and encryption.
scopeIncludes: Incidents where forensic timeline shows adversary presence and manual discovery activity for an extended period (typically weeks or more) prior to exfiltration/encryption
Manual identification and targeting of high-value data repositories prior to exfiltration
scopeExcludes: Rapid, automated exfiltration with no significant dwell time (ITID-31132)
Exfiltration via a standard toolkit without evidence of extended prior reconnaissance (ITID-31131)
ITID-31133.severity: Critical; prolonged dwell time typically correlates with broader data access and more damaging exfiltration.
ITID-31133.priority: P1, with heightened forensic scope given the extended timeline.
ITID-31133.escalation: Escalate to full IR and forensics immediately; scope the entire dwell-time window, not just the final encryption event, to identify all systems and data potentially accessed.
indicators: Authentication and access logs showing adversary activity spanning weeks prior to encryption
Evidence of manual directory/share enumeration well before exfiltration begins
Use of living-off-the-land tools for discovery over an extended period
vectors: Manual, hands-on-keyboard operation following initial access, conducting extended reconnaissance before acting
Use of legitimate administrative tools for prolonged internal discovery to avoid early detection
rootCauses: Insufficient detection coverage for slow, low-and-slow internal reconnaissance
Lack of centralized logging/retention sufficient to reconstruct a multi-week dwell-time timeline
controls: Extended log retention to support long dwell-time investigations
Behavioral analytics tuned to detect low-and-slow internal reconnaissance
Immutable/offline backups
ITID-31133.detection: Weaker in real time due to the low-and-slow nature of the activity; strongest during post-incident forensic reconstruction with adequate log retention.
ITID-31133.response: Conduct a full forensic timeline reconstruction covering the entire dwell period, assume broad data access, and remediate all identified persistence mechanisms before considering the environment clean.
metrics: Measured dwell time from initial access to detonation
Scope of systems/data accessed during dwell time
ITID-31133.notes: Extortion demand and leak-site publication tracked separately under the Public Disclosure/Extortion Threats domain.

playbook.name: Response: Double Extortion Ransomware Following Prolonged Dwell-Time Reconnaissance
playbook.description: For a confirmed double-extortion ransomware incident preceded by an extended period of attacker reconnaissance and data discovery inside the environment before exfiltration and encryption.

steps.title: Confirm encryption scope across the environment
steps.desc: Identify every host/share showing signs of encryption.
steps.outcome: Full encryption scope established.

steps.title: Reconstruct the full dwell-time timeline
steps.desc: Review historical logs to establish how long the attacker was present, what internal reconnaissance and data-discovery activity occurred, and which systems were touched before exfiltration/encryption.
steps.guidance: Prolonged dwell time means standard short-window log retention may not cover the full timeline — extend the log review window accordingly.
steps.outcome: Full attacker timeline established from initial access through encryption.

steps.title: Investigate the exfiltration separately from the encryption event
steps.desc: Determine what data was identified as high-value during reconnaissance and subsequently exfiltrated.
steps.outcome: Scope and content of exfiltrated data established.
steps.tool: Network logs / DLP / cloud audit logs

steps.title: Isolate the entire affected network segment immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect affected systems at a segment level given ransomware's rapid lateral-spread nature.
steps.outcome: Further encryption and lateral movement halted.

steps.title: Rotate credentials for every account touched during the dwell-time period
steps.desc: Given the extended reconnaissance window, assume broader credential exposure than a short-dwell incident and rotate accordingly.
steps.outcome: All potentially exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Engage Legal, Executive leadership, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Notify Legal and executives; consider law-enforcement referral. Do not engage with the extortion demand without Legal involvement.
steps.outcome: Leadership engaged and coordinating the business/legal response track.

steps.title: Remove the ransomware and every persistence mechanism established during dwell time
steps.desc: Given the prolonged access, hunt for and remove all footholds established across the full dwell period, not just those tied to the final encryption event.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of the ransomware and all attacker footholds.

steps.title: Verify backup integrity before restoring
steps.desc: Confirm backups predate the compromise and are free of the ransomware before restoring; given the long dwell time, verify backups further back than usual.
steps.outcome: Clean, verified backup identified for restore.
steps.abort: If no clean backup exists, escalate rebuild timeline to leadership.

steps.title: Assess breach-notification obligations for the exfiltrated data
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Privacy on notification requirements given the confirmed data exfiltration and its scope.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations determined and executed.

steps.title: Document the full incident and address detection gaps that allowed prolonged dwell time
steps.desc: Record the full timeline and remediate the detection/monitoring gaps that allowed the attacker to remain undetected for an extended period.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete remediations tracked to completion.

ITID-31134.def: A double extortion ransomware incident (confirmed encryption plus confirmed or threatened data exfiltration) not yet attributable to a specific exfiltration method (standard toolkit, automated staging, or extended dwell-time reconnaissance).
ITID-31134.purpose: Catch-all for double extortion ransomware incidents that do not fit a more specific exfiltration-method leaf under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before the exfiltration method has been confirmed
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID under Double Extortion Ransomware
ITID-31134.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Critical by default given the confirmed dual impact.
ITID-31134.escalation: Escalate immediately as with any confirmed double extortion incident; reclassify once the exfiltration method is clarified.
indicators: Confirmed encryption plus evidence of data exfiltration, specific method not yet determined
vectors: Activity of unclear specific exfiltration method
rootCauses: Insufficient forensic detail captured at time of detection
controls: Immutable/offline backups
Egress traffic monitoring and DLP
ITID-31134.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-31134.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-31134.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Double Extortion Ransomware Incident
playbook.description: For a confirmed double-extortion ransomware incident (data exfiltration plus encryption) where the specific exfiltration method or dwell-time characteristics have not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm encryption scope across the environment
steps.desc: Identify every host/share showing signs of encryption, not just the first reported system.
steps.outcome: Full encryption scope established.

steps.title: Investigate the pre-encryption exfiltration as its own timeline
steps.desc: Review network/DLP/cloud logs for signs of bulk data staging and transfer prior to encryption, distinct from the encryption event itself.
steps.outcome: Scope and content of exfiltrated data established.
steps.tool: Network logs / DLP / cloud audit logs

steps.title: Identify the initial-access vector and full attacker timeline
steps.desc: Determine how the attacker gained access and reconstruct the timeline through exfiltration and encryption.
steps.outcome: Initial access vector and timeline established.

steps.title: Isolate the entire affected network segment immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect affected systems at a segment level given ransomware's rapid lateral-spread nature.
steps.outcome: Further encryption and lateral movement halted.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence before any remediation
steps.desc: Image affected systems and preserve logs before wiping/rebuilding anything.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for investigation and potential law-enforcement referral.

steps.title: Engage Legal, Executive leadership, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Notify Legal and executives; consider law-enforcement referral. Do not engage with the extortion demand without Legal involvement.
steps.outcome: Leadership engaged and coordinating the business/legal response track.

steps.title: Remove the ransomware and every persistence/access mechanism found
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts and close the full initial-access chain identified during investigation.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of the ransomware and attacker access.

steps.title: Verify backup integrity before restoring
steps.desc: Confirm backups predate the compromise and are free of the ransomware before restoring.
steps.outcome: Clean, verified backup identified for restore.
steps.abort: If no clean backup exists, escalate rebuild timeline to leadership.

steps.title: Assess breach-notification obligations for the exfiltrated data
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Privacy on notification requirements given the confirmed data exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations determined and executed.

steps.title: Document the full incident and remediate root-cause access gaps
steps.desc: Record the full timeline (initial access through exfiltration through encryption) and remediate the specific gaps that allowed it.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; concrete remediations tracked to completion.

ITID-31141.def: A ransomware attack in which a human operator manually navigates the target environment, selects deployment targets, and times execution, rather than relying on a self-propagating or fully automated encryptor.
ITID-31141.purpose: Captures targeted ransomware attacks that are manually operated by a human adversary in real time, rather than automated/commodity deployment.
scopeIncludes: Manual, hands-on-keyboard deployment of the encryptor across selected hosts by an operator inside the environment
Adversary manually disabling specific backup/security tooling on chosen hosts before deploying the encryptor
scopeExcludes: Deployment stemming directly from a purchased initial-access-broker handoff as the defining characteristic (ITID-31142)
Deployment specifically timed to a business-critical event as the defining characteristic (ITID-31143)
ITID-31141.severity: Critical; human operation typically means deliberate targeting of the most damaging systems and backups.
ITID-31141.priority: P1, treat as an active adversary-in-the-environment event.
ITID-31141.escalation: Escalate to full IR immediately; assume an active human operator and prioritize containing lateral movement, not just the encryptor payload.
indicators: Manual, interactive command execution across multiple hosts preceding encryption
Security tooling/backups deliberately and selectively disabled prior to deployment
Encryptor deployed near-simultaneously across many hosts via manual push (e.g., through compromised admin tooling)
vectors: Manual lateral movement using compromised administrative credentials followed by targeted encryptor deployment
Deliberate, manual disabling of backup and security infrastructure before encryption
rootCauses: Excessive standing administrative privilege enabling broad manual lateral movement
Insufficient monitoring of administrative tooling used for mass software deployment
controls: Privileged access management restricting standing admin rights
Monitoring/alerting on backup and security-tool service-stop events
Immutable/offline backups
ITID-31141.detection: Good if administrative tooling and backup infrastructure are monitored for unauthorized service-stop or configuration-change events, which is a strong precursor signal.
ITID-31141.response: Assume an active human operator; contain identity and administrative access paths in addition to isolating hosts, and validate integrity of backup infrastructure before relying on it for recovery.
metrics: Time from lateral movement detection to encryptor deployment
Number of hosts encrypted in the initial deployment wave
ITID-31141.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by attack characteristic (manual human operation) rather than the specific initial-access or timing detail.

playbook.name: Response: Human-Operated Targeted Ransomware Deployment
playbook.description: For a confirmed targeted ransomware incident where an intrusion operator manually navigated the environment, disabled defenses, and deployed the ransomware by hand rather than through automated propagation.

steps.title: Confirm encryption scope across the environment
steps.desc: Identify every host/share showing signs of encryption; human-operated actors often target specific high-value systems first.
steps.outcome: Full encryption scope established.

steps.title: Reconstruct the operator's manual activity and toolset
steps.desc: Review EDR/command-line telemetry for evidence of manual reconnaissance, credential harvesting, defense-disabling (EDR/AV tampering), and lateral movement carried out interactively by the operator.
steps.guidance: Human-operated intrusions leave distinct manual-activity artifacts (interactive shell sessions, admin tool abuse) different from automated malware — investigate accordingly.
steps.outcome: Operator's activity timeline and toolset documented.

steps.title: Identify all accounts and systems the operator gained privileged access to
steps.desc: Determine the full scope of compromised privileged accounts (domain admin, service accounts) the operator used to move and deploy the ransomware.
steps.outcome: Full scope of compromised privileged access established.

steps.title: Isolate the entire affected network segment immediately
steps.desc: Disconnect affected systems at a segment level given the scale a human operator with privileged access can typically reach.
steps.outcome: Further encryption and lateral movement halted.

steps.title: Force reset of all privileged and domain-level credentials
steps.desc: Reset all administrative, domain admin, and service-account credentials the operator may have accessed, not just the ones directly observed.
steps.outcome: Attacker's privileged access fully revoked.

steps.title: Engage Legal, Executive leadership, and law enforcement
steps.desc: Notify Legal and executives; consider law-enforcement referral given the sophistication of a human-operated attack. Do not engage with the extortion demand without Legal involvement.
steps.outcome: Leadership engaged and coordinating the business/legal response track.

steps.title: Remove the ransomware and rebuild trust in the directory/identity infrastructure
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts and, given privileged-account compromise, assess whether the domain/identity infrastructure itself needs rebuilding.
