steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-31911.def: A custom-built malware implant whose code, infrastructure, or tradecraft matches a previously attributed nation-state threat actor's toolset, allowing confident attribution to a known advanced persistent threat group.
ITID-31911.purpose: Captures custom malware implants attributed to a nation-state actor's known toolset, distinct from bespoke one-off tooling with no attribution linkage.
scopeIncludes: Implants matching a known, previously-attributed nation-state toolset via code overlap, shared infrastructure, or TTP fingerprinting
Reuse of a signature nation-state framework/loader across multiple campaigns
scopeExcludes: Bespoke malware built for a single-target campaign with no attribution linkage to a known actor (ITID-31912)
Malware built by reusing leaked/stolen source code from a prior unrelated breach (ITID-31913)
ITID-31911.severity: Critical, given the sophistication and resourcing typically associated with nation-state actors.
ITID-31911.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership and, where applicable, government/sector information-sharing partners given the attribution.
indicators: Code/binary overlap with a previously attributed nation-state toolset
Infrastructure overlap (C2 domains/IPs) with known nation-state campaigns
TTP fingerprint matching a tracked advanced persistent threat group
vectors: Spear-phishing with a nation-state-signature implant
Supply-chain compromise consistent with known nation-state tradecraft
rootCauses: High-value target profile attracting nation-state interest
Gaps in detection for previously-documented nation-state TTPs
controls: Threat-intelligence-driven detection engineering for known nation-state TTPs
Sector-level information sharing (ISAC/ISAO) integration
ITID-31911.detection: Dependent on maintaining current threat intelligence on the attributed actor's evolving toolset and infrastructure.
ITID-31911.response: Engage full incident response and threat intelligence support, assume long-dwell compromise until scoped, and coordinate disclosure per sector/regulatory requirements.
metrics: Count of confirmed nation-state-attributed incidents per year
Dwell time before detection
ITID-31911.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by attribution confidence: this leaf requires a confirmed link to a previously-known nation-state toolset, distinguishing it from unattributed bespoke tooling (ITID-31912).

playbook.name: Response: Nation-State Custom Implant (Attribution-Linked Toolset)
playbook.description: For a confirmed custom implant attributable to a known or suspected nation-state threat actor toolset. Assume a sophisticated, patient adversary throughout.

steps.title: Confirm the implant and correlate against known nation-state toolset indicators
steps.desc: Confirm the implant's presence and correlate its indicators (TTPs, infrastructure, code artifacts) against threat intelligence on known nation-state toolsets.
steps.guidance: Engage threat intelligence resources early — attribution context materially changes the response posture.
steps.outcome: Implant confirmed and attribution context established where possible.

steps.title: Scope the full extent of compromise across the environment
steps.desc: Given the sophistication implied by nation-state tooling, assume the initial finding is not isolated — hunt across the environment for related indicators, lateral movement, and additional implants.
steps.guidance: Do not assume single-host scope; nation-state actors typically establish redundant footholds.
steps.outcome: Full scope of compromise established.

steps.title: Escalate to full incident-response engagement rather than routine endpoint remediation
steps.desc: Engage the organization's full incident response process (leadership, legal, external IR support as needed) rather than treating this as routine endpoint cleanup.
steps.guidance: A sophisticated, patient adversary requires coordinated response, not ad hoc single-analyst remediation.
steps.outcome: Full IR engagement activated.

steps.title: Contain without tipping off the adversary prematurely
steps.desc: Coordinate containment actions carefully — a nation-state actor monitoring for defensive response may accelerate destructive action or shift tactics if alerted too early; balance evidence preservation against the need to stop ongoing access.
steps.outcome: Containment plan executed with coordinated timing across all identified footholds.

steps.title: Remove all identified implants and persistence mechanisms simultaneously
steps.desc: Coordinate simultaneous removal across all identified compromised hosts to prevent the adversary from using a remaining foothold to re-establish access elsewhere.
steps.outcome: All known implants and persistence removed in a coordinated action.

steps.title: Hunt for additional undiscovered footholds before declaring eradication complete
steps.desc: Continue threat hunting after the initial cleanup to identify any remaining, previously undiscovered access the adversary may retain.
steps.guidance: Nation-state actors are known to maintain redundant access; a single cleanup pass is rarely sufficient.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further footholds remain, based on thorough hunting.

steps.title: Rebuild affected systems from known-clean sources and re-credential
steps.desc: Rebuild compromised systems rather than relying solely on in-place cleanup, and rotate all credentials the adversary may have accessed.
steps.outcome: Systems rebuilt and credentials rotated.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review and update threat intelligence
steps.desc: Document the full campaign, attribution assessment, and defensive gaps exploited; update threat intelligence and detection content accordingly.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive report completed and detection content updated.

ITID-31912.def: A malware implant custom-engineered for use against a single specific target organization, with no code, infrastructure, or TTP overlap to a previously attributed threat actor, indicating bespoke development rather than reuse of an established toolset.
ITID-31912.purpose: Captures custom malware built specifically for a single-target campaign, without attribution to a previously-known threat actor's toolset.
scopeIncludes: Implants with unique code showing no overlap with any known/tracked malware family
Malware tailored specifically to the target's environment (e.g. custom protocol evasion, target-specific persistence)
scopeExcludes: Implants matching a known nation-state toolset (ITID-31911)
Malware built by reusing leaked/stolen source code from a prior breach (ITID-31913)
ITID-31912.severity: Critical, given the resourcing implied by bespoke, single-target development.
ITID-31912.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident response; treat attribution as an open question requiring dedicated threat intelligence analysis.
indicators: Implant with no matches against any known malware family in threat intelligence platforms
Malware tailored to specific internal systems/configurations not publicly known
vectors: Highly targeted spear-phishing with a purpose-built implant
Insider knowledge or reconnaissance-informed custom tooling
rootCauses: High-value or unique target profile justifying bespoke development cost
Gaps in detection since no prior signature/behavioral baseline exists
controls: Behavioral/anomaly-based detection independent of known signatures
Enhanced monitoring for high-value targets
ITID-31912.detection: Weak for signature-based tooling since no prior sample exists; behavioral/anomaly detection is the primary available coverage.
ITID-31912.response: Conduct full forensic reverse engineering of the implant, since no existing threat intelligence will describe it, and preserve samples for future attribution efforts.
metrics: Count of confirmed bespoke single-target implants per year
ITID-31912.notes: Differentiated from ITID-31911 by attribution status: no linkage to a known toolset, reflecting either a genuinely new actor or successful operational security by a known one.

playbook.name: Response: Bespoke Malware Built for Single-Target Campaign
playbook.description: For malware custom-built specifically for a single-target campaign against this organization. Assume a sophisticated, patient adversary that has invested significant effort in this specific target.

steps.title: Confirm the malware is bespoke/single-target rather than a known commodity family
steps.desc: Analyze the malware and confirm it does not match known commodity families, and assess indicators (targeting logic, hardcoded organizational references) suggesting it was built specifically for this organization.
steps.guidance: Bespoke, single-target malware implies the adversary invested significant reconnaissance and development effort — treat this as a strong signal of a determined, targeted campaign.
steps.outcome: Confirmed bespoke malware and targeting intent.

steps.title: Scope the full extent of compromise across the environment
steps.desc: Hunt across the environment for related indicators, additional implants, and lateral movement, since single-target campaigns typically involve more than one foothold.
steps.guidance: Do not assume single-host scope.
steps.outcome: Full scope of compromise established.

steps.title: Escalate to full incident-response engagement
steps.desc: Engage the organization's full incident response process rather than treating this as routine endpoint cleanup, given the deliberate targeting of this organization specifically.
steps.outcome: Full IR engagement activated.

steps.title: Contain without tipping off the adversary prematurely
steps.desc: Coordinate containment timing carefully to avoid alerting a patient adversary before all known footholds can be addressed simultaneously.
steps.outcome: Containment plan executed with coordinated timing.

steps.title: Remove all identified implants and persistence mechanisms simultaneously
steps.desc: Coordinate simultaneous removal across all identified compromised hosts.
steps.outcome: All known implants and persistence removed in a coordinated action.

steps.title: Hunt for additional undiscovered footholds before declaring eradication complete
steps.desc: Continue threat hunting after initial cleanup, since a determined single-target adversary is likely to have built in redundant access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further footholds remain.

steps.title: Rebuild affected systems from known-clean sources and re-credential
steps.desc: Rebuild compromised systems and rotate all credentials the adversary may have accessed.
steps.outcome: Systems rebuilt and credentials rotated.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review and assess why this organization was targeted
steps.desc: Document the full campaign and assess what made the organization a specific target, feeding findings into future threat modeling.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive report completed.

ITID-31913.def: A malware implant developed by an actor using source code that was leaked publicly or stolen in a prior, unrelated security breach (e.g. a leaked commercial malware builder or a breached red-team tool), adapted and deployed as the actor's own custom tooling.
ITID-31913.purpose: Captures custom malware built by repurposing source code leaked or stolen from a prior, unrelated breach.
scopeIncludes: Malware built on leaked source code from a publicly-known prior breach (e.g. a leaked malware family's source repository)
Implants derived from stolen legitimate security/red-team tooling repurposed maliciously
scopeExcludes: Malware matching a known nation-state toolset developed in-house by that actor (ITID-31911)
Fully original bespoke development with no traceable source-code lineage (ITID-31912)
ITID-31913.severity: High-Critical, since leaked source code often provides a capable, previously-tested foundation.
ITID-31913.escalation: Escalate immediately, and note the source-code lineage for threat intelligence tracking of who else may be using the same leaked base.
indicators: Code overlap with a publicly-documented leaked malware source repository
Implant capability set matching a known leaked tool's feature list with actor-specific modifications
vectors: Deployment of a modified variant built from a leaked commercial malware builder's source
Repurposing of stolen legitimate offensive security tooling
rootCauses: Prior public leak of malware/red-team tool source code lowering the barrier to entry for building capable implants
Insufficient tracking of derivative malware families stemming from known leaks
controls: Threat intelligence tracking of derivative families from known source leaks
Signature/behavioral detection tuned to the leaked base's known characteristics
ITID-31913.detection: Moderate: detection benefits from the leaked source's public documentation, though actor-specific modifications may evade exact signature matches.
ITID-31913.response: Identify the source-code lineage, apply detection signatures known for the leaked base with adjustment for observed modifications, and report findings to threat intelligence.
metrics: Count of leaked-source-derived implant incidents per year
detections: Signature detection tuned to known leaked source base
ITID-31913.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by origin: built from a traceable prior public/breach leak, rather than an in-house nation-state toolset (ITID-31911) or fully original bespoke code (ITID-31912).

playbook.name: Response: Custom Malware Reusing Leaked/Stolen Source Code from Prior Breach
playbook.description: For custom malware built on leaked or stolen source code from a prior breach (e.g., a leaked commercial malware builder or a competitor group's toolset), adapted for use against this organization. Assume a sophisticated, patient adversary.

steps.title: Confirm the malware's lineage to the leaked/stolen source code
steps.desc: Analyze the malware's code structure and compare against the known leaked/stolen source code base to confirm lineage and identify what the current operator has modified.
steps.guidance: Engage threat intelligence to identify which known leak the code derives from and what other actors have used it.
steps.outcome: Confirmed code lineage and modifications identified.

steps.title: Scope the full extent of compromise across the environment
steps.desc: Hunt across the environment for related indicators and additional footholds, since the operator adapting leaked code may have used it broadly.
steps.outcome: Full scope of compromise established.

steps.title: Escalate to full incident-response engagement
steps.desc: Engage the organization's full incident response process rather than routine endpoint remediation.
steps.outcome: Full IR engagement activated.

steps.title: Contain without tipping off the adversary prematurely
steps.desc: Coordinate containment timing to avoid alerting the adversary before all known footholds can be addressed simultaneously.
steps.outcome: Containment plan executed with coordinated timing.

steps.title: Remove all identified implants and persistence mechanisms simultaneously
steps.desc: Coordinate simultaneous removal across all identified compromised hosts.
steps.outcome: All known implants and persistence removed.

steps.title: Hunt for additional undiscovered footholds before declaring eradication complete
steps.desc: Continue threat hunting after initial cleanup, since the adapted codebase may include capabilities not yet observed in this environment.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further footholds remain.

steps.title: Rebuild affected systems and re-credential
steps.desc: Rebuild compromised systems from known-clean sources and rotate all potentially accessed credentials.
steps.outcome: Systems rebuilt and credentials rotated.

steps.title: Document the code lineage and update threat intelligence
steps.desc: Record the source-code lineage and operator TTPs observed, and share with threat intelligence sources tracking the same leaked codebase.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and threat intelligence updated.

ITID-31914.def: An incident involving custom APT malware, not clearly matching the nation-state-attributed, bespoke single-target, or leaked-source-derived patterns captured by the sibling leaves.
ITID-31914.purpose: Catch-all for cases that do not fit the more specific leaves under Custom Malware.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific Custom Malware leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID under Custom Malware
ITID-31914.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Critical by default given the APT context.
ITID-31914.escalation: Reclassify once attribution/origin detail is clarified.
indicators: Custom APT malware alert of unclear specific origin
vectors: Activity of unclear specific custom-tooling origin
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Threat intelligence-driven hunting for custom malware indicators
EDR with behavioral analytics for anomalous process activity
Network segmentation to limit lateral movement
Egress filtering and C2 detection
ITID-31914.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-31914.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific Custom Malware leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-31914.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Custom APT Malware
playbook.description: General response for custom APT malware that does not fit a more specific sub-category. Assume a sophisticated, patient adversary and escalate to full incident-response engagement.

steps.title: Confirm the custom malware and its capabilities
steps.desc: Confirm the presence of custom (non-commodity) malware and analyze its capabilities.
steps.outcome: Malware confirmed and capabilities understood.

steps.title: Scope the full extent of compromise across the environment
steps.desc: Hunt across the environment for related indicators and additional footholds.
steps.outcome: Full scope of compromise established.

steps.title: Escalate to full incident-response engagement
steps.desc: Engage the organization's full incident response process.
steps.outcome: Full IR engagement activated.

steps.title: Contain without tipping off the adversary prematurely
steps.desc: Coordinate containment timing to avoid premature adversary awareness.
steps.outcome: Containment plan executed with coordinated timing.

steps.title: Remove all identified implants and persistence mechanisms simultaneously
steps.desc: Coordinate simultaneous removal across all compromised hosts.
steps.outcome: All known implants and persistence removed.

steps.title: Hunt for additional undiscovered footholds
steps.desc: Continue threat hunting after initial cleanup to confirm no remaining access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further footholds remain.

steps.title: Rebuild affected systems and re-credential
steps.desc: Rebuild compromised systems and rotate potentially accessed credentials.
steps.outcome: Systems rebuilt and credentials rotated.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the campaign and update detection content.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive report completed.

ITID-31921.def: An advanced persistent threat operating technique in which the actor performs its objectives using only legitimate, pre-installed operating system tools and scripting engines (living off the land), deploying no custom implant binary at all, to avoid leaving any novel artifact for signature-based detection.
ITID-31921.purpose: Captures APT implants that rely entirely on legitimate, pre-installed system tools rather than any custom binary, maximizing stealth.
scopeIncludes: Exclusive use of native OS binaries/scripting engines (e.g. PowerShell, WMI, certutil) to conduct APT objectives with no custom binary present
Persistence, lateral movement, and data collection achieved entirely through built-in administrative tooling
scopeExcludes: Firmware/UEFI-level implants, which do involve a custom low-level artifact (ITID-31922)
Anti-forensic log-wiping activity as the primary finding rather than living-off-the-land execution (ITID-31923)
ITID-31921.severity: Critical, since the complete absence of custom binaries makes this exceptionally difficult to detect.
ITID-31921.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident response; assume extended dwell time given the difficulty of detecting living-off-the-land activity.
indicators: Native admin tools invoked with unusual argument patterns or from unusual parent processes
Correlated sequences of built-in tool usage matching known living-off-the-land APT tradecraft
No malicious binary found despite confirmed unauthorized activity
vectors: Compromised credentials used to drive native tooling for lateral movement and collection
Scripted abuse of WMI/PowerShell/scheduled tasks for full attack lifecycle execution
rootCauses: Insufficient logging/auditing of native administrative tool usage
Lack of behavioral baselining for normal vs. anomalous admin tool use
mitreTechniques: T1059.001 Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
controls: Detailed logging and behavioral analytics on native administrative tool usage
Application control restricting native tool usage to expected administrative contexts
ITID-31921.detection: Requires mature behavioral analytics correlating sequences of native tool usage; signature-based tooling provides essentially no coverage.
ITID-31921.response: Reconstruct the full attack timeline from native tool usage logs, since no binary sample exists to analyze, and assume broad lateral movement until scoped.
metrics: Count of confirmed living-off-the-land APT incidents per year
Dwell time before detection
detections: Behavioral analytics on native tool usage sequences
ITID-31921.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by the complete absence of any custom artifact; firmware implants (ITID-31922) and log-wiping (ITID-31923) both involve a distinct technical artifact/action of their own.

playbook.name: Response: Living-off-the-Land APT Implant (No Custom Binary)
playbook.description: For an APT-level intrusion using only built-in OS tools and legitimate administrative utilities (living off the land) with no custom malware binary deployed. Assume a sophisticated, patient adversary.

steps.title: Confirm malicious use of legitimate tools via behavioral correlation
steps.desc: Since no custom binary exists, confirm malicious activity by correlating unusual sequences/contexts of legitimate tool usage (PowerShell, WMI, PsExec, native admin utilities) against expected administrative baselines.
steps.guidance: AV/signature tools will find nothing — this depends entirely on behavioral baselining and anomaly detection.
steps.outcome: Confirmed malicious living-off-the-land activity and the sequence of abused tools identified.

steps.title: Scope the full extent of compromise across the environment
steps.desc: Hunt across the environment for the same living-off-the-land technique pattern on other hosts, since a patient adversary using this approach typically has multiple footholds.
steps.outcome: Full scope of compromise established.

steps.title: Escalate to full incident-response engagement
steps.desc: Engage the organization's full incident response process.
steps.outcome: Full IR engagement activated.

steps.title: Contain without tipping off the adversary prematurely
steps.desc: Coordinate containment timing carefully, since disabling legitimate tools broadly can both alert the adversary and disrupt business operations.
steps.outcome: Containment plan executed with coordinated timing.

steps.title: Revoke abused credentials/access and remove any scheduled task or script persistence
steps.desc: Since there is no binary to delete, eradication centers on revoking the compromised credentials/access used and removing any persistence implemented via legitimate scripting/scheduling mechanisms.
steps.outcome: Abused access revoked and persistence removed.

steps.title: Hunt for additional undiscovered footholds before declaring eradication complete
steps.desc: Continue threat hunting for the same technique pattern across the environment.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further footholds remain.

steps.title: Rotate all potentially compromised credentials and monitor tool usage baselines
steps.desc: Rotate credentials the adversary may have used and establish tighter behavioral baselines/alerting for the abused legitimate tools.
steps.outcome: Credentials rotated and monitoring improved.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review focused on living-off-the-land detection gaps
steps.desc: Document the technique sequence used and assess detection/logging gaps that allowed it to go unnoticed.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive report completed.

ITID-31922.def: An advanced persistent threat implant embedded in a device's firmware or UEFI layer, executing prior to OS load and surviving operating system reinstallation, disk wipe, or replacement, requiring firmware-level remediation or hardware replacement to fully remove.
ITID-31922.purpose: Captures APT implants planted at the firmware/UEFI level, providing persistence that survives OS reinstallation and most conventional remediation.
scopeIncludes: UEFI/firmware-resident implants confirmed to survive a full OS reinstall
Bootkit-style persistence operating below the OS layer as part of a broader APT campaign
scopeExcludes: Living-off-the-land techniques with no custom firmware/binary artifact (ITID-31921)
Anti-forensic log-wiping malware operating at the OS/application layer (ITID-31923)
Non-APT firmware backdoors tracked under the Trojan/Backdoor ITID branch when no broader APT campaign context applies
ITID-31922.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership and the hardware vendor; plan for hardware replacement given the extreme difficulty of firmware-level remediation.
indicators: Firmware hash mismatch against vendor-known-good baseline
Malicious behavior surviving a full OS reimage or disk replacement
Anomalous pre-boot activity detected via measured/secure boot attestation failures
vectors: Supply-chain implantation of firmware prior to device delivery
Physical or remote firmware-flashing exploit chains used by a well-resourced actor
rootCauses: Lack of firmware integrity/attestation verification
Absence of hardware supply-chain security vetting
controls: Firmware integrity/attestation verification (measured/secure boot)
Hardware supply-chain vetting
Vendor firmware update/validation program
ITID-31922.detection: Weak without specialized firmware attestation tooling or vendor assistance; a genuinely difficult detection surface.
ITID-31922.response: Engage the hardware vendor and specialized firmware forensics; reflash from a verified clean source or replace affected hardware entirely.
metrics: Count of firmware-level APT implants confirmed per year
Number of devices requiring hardware replacement
ITID-31922.notes: Scoped to firmware/UEFI implants occurring within a broader APT campaign context; a standalone firmware backdoor with no wider APT campaign linkage is tracked under the Trojan/Backdoor ITID branch instead, avoiding duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Firmware/UEFI-Level Persistent Implant
playbook.description: For an APT-level implant persisting at the firmware/UEFI level, surviving OS reinstallation and disk replacement. Assume a sophisticated, patient adversary; OS-level cleanup alone will not remove this.

steps.title: Confirm firmware/UEFI-level persistence via specialized firmware analysis
steps.desc: Use firmware integrity scanning tools to confirm the implant resides at the UEFI/firmware level rather than the OS level.
steps.guidance: Standard OS-level EDR cannot see firmware-level implants — dedicated firmware scanning capability is required.
steps.outcome: Confirmed firmware/UEFI-level persistence.
steps.tool: Firmware integrity scanner (e.g., vendor UEFI scanning tool)

steps.title: Scope the full extent of compromise across the environment
steps.desc: Determine whether other devices of the same hardware model/firmware version are similarly affected.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected hardware established.

steps.title: Escalate to full incident-response engagement
steps.desc: Engage the organization's full incident response process, including hardware vendor coordination.
steps.outcome: Full IR engagement activated, vendor engaged.

steps.title: Physically isolate the affected hardware
steps.desc: Remove the affected device from the network and, where feasible, from operational use pending remediation.
steps.outcome: Device isolated.

steps.title: Reflash firmware to a known-clean, vendor-verified version or replace the hardware
steps.desc: OS reinstallation will not remove a firmware-level implant. Reflash the UEFI/firmware to a verified clean version from the vendor, or replace the affected hardware component entirely if clean reflashing cannot be guaranteed.
steps.guidance: Treat OS-level cleanup as explicitly insufficient for this category — hardware-level remediation is mandatory.
steps.outcome: Firmware reflashed to verified-clean state, or hardware replaced.
steps.abort: If firmware integrity cannot be guaranteed after reflashing, replace the hardware rather than return it to service.

steps.title: Verify firmware integrity post-remediation
steps.desc: Re-scan the firmware after reflashing/replacement to confirm no residual implant remains.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean firmware state.

steps.title: Reinstall the OS on the remediated hardware and rotate credentials
steps.desc: Reinstall the operating system on the now firmware-clean hardware and rotate all potentially compromised credentials.
steps.outcome: System restored on clean hardware with rotated credentials.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review and assess firmware security posture
steps.desc: Document the implant and assess organizational firmware integrity monitoring and hardware supply-chain security posture.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive report completed.

ITID-31923.def: Advanced persistent threat tradecraft focused on deleting, altering, or disabling security logs and forensic artifacts (event logs, EDR telemetry, command history) to conceal the actor's activity and impede incident response and root-cause analysis.
ITID-31923.purpose: Captures APT activity centered on anti-forensic techniques — log wiping and evidence destruction — used to conceal the actor's presence and hinder investigation.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate clearing/tampering of Windows Event Logs, EDR telemetry, or command-history artifacts by an APT actor
Disabling of logging/auditing services as part of an intrusion to prevent forensic reconstruction
scopeExcludes: Living-off-the-land technique use where log tampering is not the primary finding (ITID-31921)
Firmware-level persistence where anti-forensics is not the primary activity (ITID-31922)
ITID-31923.severity: Critical, since successful log wiping severely hampers the ability to scope and remediate the broader compromise.
ITID-31923.escalation: Escalate immediately; treat as confirmation of an active, sophisticated compromise requiring full incident response and out-of-band evidence preservation.
indicators: Gaps or discontinuities in event log sequences
Log service disabled or logs cleared around the time of suspected compromise
EDR agent tampering or unexpected telemetry gaps
vectors: Native log-clearing commands (e.g. wevtutil, PowerShell log-clearing cmdlets) executed by the actor
EDR agent tampering/uninstallation as part of the intrusion
rootCauses: Logs stored only locally with no centralized, tamper-resistant forwarding
Insufficient monitoring for log-clearing events or EDR tampering
mitreTechniques: T1070.001 Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
controls: Centralized, tamper-resistant log forwarding (write-once/remote SIEM ingestion)
Alerting on log-clearing events and EDR agent tampering
ITID-31923.detection: Strong when logs are forwarded to a centralized, tamper-resistant SIEM before an actor can clear them locally; weak if logging is local-only.
ITID-31923.response: Preserve all available out-of-band/centralized log copies immediately, treat the log-wiping event itself as a high-confidence compromise indicator, and scope the incident using any surviving telemetry.
metrics: Count of confirmed anti-forensic/log-wiping incidents per year
Percentage of logs preserved via centralized forwarding despite local tampering

playbook.name: Response: Anti-Forensic/Log-Wiping APT Malware
playbook.description: For an APT-level intrusion that includes anti-forensic log-wiping capability. Assume a sophisticated, patient adversary; immediate out-of-band evidence preservation is required before further wiping occurs.

steps.title: Immediately preserve evidence out-of-band before further log wiping can occur
steps.desc: As soon as anti-forensic/log-wiping activity is suspected, immediately export/copy logs, memory, and disk images to an out-of-band, write-protected location before the adversary can wipe further evidence.
steps.guidance: This step takes priority over further investigation — every additional minute risks irrecoverable evidence loss.
steps.outcome: Critical evidence preserved in a location the adversary cannot reach or wipe.
steps.tool: Forensic imaging tools / centralized log forwarding

steps.title: Confirm the log-wiping activity and scope of evidence already lost
steps.desc: Analyze remaining logs and any centrally-forwarded copies to determine what evidence was destroyed and what timeframe/systems are affected.
steps.outcome: Scope of evidence loss and affected timeframe understood.

steps.title: Escalate to full incident-response engagement
steps.desc: Engage the organization's full incident response process immediately, including legal counsel given the evidentiary implications of anti-forensic activity.
steps.outcome: Full IR engagement activated with legal involved.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems without further local log/evidence disruption
steps.desc: Isolate affected hosts using network-level controls where possible rather than local actions that could further disturb remaining forensic evidence.
steps.outcome: Hosts isolated with forensic evidence preserved.

steps.title: Remove all identified implants and persistence mechanisms simultaneously
steps.desc: Coordinate simultaneous removal across all identified compromised hosts once evidence is preserved.
steps.outcome: All known implants and persistence removed.

steps.title: Hunt for additional undiscovered footholds using preserved out-of-band evidence
steps.desc: Use the preserved out-of-band logs/images (rather than potentially-wiped local logs) to hunt for additional footholds.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further footholds remain, based on out-of-band evidence.

steps.title: Rebuild affected systems and re-credential
steps.desc: Rebuild compromised systems from known-clean sources and rotate potentially accessed credentials.
steps.outcome: Systems rebuilt and credentials rotated.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review and improve log resilience
steps.desc: Document the incident, the evidence lost, and improve centralized/immutable log forwarding to reduce future anti-forensic risk.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive report completed and log resilience improved.

ITID-31931.def: An advanced persistent threat intrusion structured as a chain of discrete stages, where an initial small dropper retrieves and executes progressively more capable payloads culminating in the final operational implant, with each stage validating the environment before advancing to reduce exposure of the full toolset.
ITID-31931.purpose: Captures the mechanical dropper-to-payload handoff chain of a multi-stage APT intrusion, distinct from the broader campaign-lifecycle or C2-infrastructure aspects.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed multi-stage execution chains from initial dropper through intermediate loaders to final payload
Stage-gating logic that only advances to the next payload after environment validation
scopeExcludes: The specific C2 infrastructure handoff between stages as the primary finding (ITID-31932)
The broader campaign-level reconnaissance/escalation/exfiltration lifecycle as the classification focus rather than the technical dropper chain itself (ITID-31933)
ITID-31931.escalation: Escalate immediately; assume the full stage chain has not yet been fully recovered until forensic analysis is complete.
indicators: Small initial dropper retrieving a second-stage payload only after passing environment checks
Sequential process/file creation events consistent with a multi-stage loader chain
Distinct payload capability levels observed across stages of the same intrusion
vectors: Phishing-delivered initial dropper as the first stage of a longer chain
Exploit-delivered small stager retrieving a fully-featured implant as a later stage
rootCauses: Lack of visibility into intermediate loader stages, allowing the final payload to go undetected
Insufficient sandboxing of intermediate stages to observe full chain behavior
controls: EDR visibility across the full process/file creation chain, not just initial execution
Sandboxing capable of following multi-stage chains to their final payload
ITID-31931.detection: Moderate: requires EDR/sandbox tooling that tracks the full chain rather than alerting only on the initial stage.
ITID-31931.response: Reconstruct the full stage chain from initial dropper to final payload, and ensure remediation addresses every stage, not just the initially-detected artifact.
metrics: Count of confirmed multi-stage dropper chains per year
Average number of stages observed per chain
ITID-31931.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by focus: the technical dropper-to-payload mechanics, distinct from C2 infrastructure handoff (ITID-31932) or the broader campaign lifecycle (ITID-31933).

playbook.name: Response: Multi-Stage Dropper-to-Final-Payload Chain
playbook.description: For an APT-level intrusion using a multi-stage dropper chain (initial dropper fetches a second-stage loader, which in turn deploys the final payload). Assume a sophisticated, patient adversary.

steps.title: Reconstruct the full dropper chain from initial access to final payload
steps.desc: Trace each stage of the dropper chain — initial access, first-stage dropper, second-stage loader, final payload — to fully understand the attack chain rather than stopping at the first identified stage.
steps.guidance: Stopping remediation at the first-discovered stage risks leaving later stages (or their own persistence) intact.
steps.outcome: Full multi-stage chain reconstructed and understood.

steps.title: Scope the full extent of compromise across the environment
steps.desc: Hunt across the environment for the same dropper chain pattern on other hosts.
steps.outcome: Full scope of compromise established.

steps.title: Escalate to full incident-response engagement
steps.desc: Engage the organization's full incident response process.
steps.outcome: Full IR engagement activated.

steps.title: Block infrastructure associated with every identified stage
steps.desc: Block network indicators (domains/IPs) associated with each stage of the chain, not just the final payload's C2.
steps.outcome: All stage-associated infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Remove every stage's artifacts and persistence mechanisms
steps.desc: Remove the initial dropper, second-stage loader, and final payload along with any persistence each stage independently established.
steps.guidance: Each stage may have its own separate persistence mechanism — removing only the final payload can leave the chain able to re-deploy it.
steps.outcome: All stages and their persistence mechanisms removed.

steps.title: Hunt for additional undiscovered footholds before declaring eradication complete
steps.desc: Continue threat hunting to confirm no stage of the chain remains active anywhere in the environment.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further footholds remain.

steps.title: Rebuild affected systems and re-credential
steps.desc: Rebuild compromised systems from known-clean sources and rotate potentially accessed credentials.
steps.outcome: Systems rebuilt and credentials rotated.

steps.title: Document the full attack chain
steps.desc: Document each stage of the chain and the infrastructure used, for detection content covering the full chain rather than only the final payload.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive report completed.

ITID-31932.def: A multi-stage advanced persistent threat operation in which command-and-control responsibility is deliberately transferred from one piece of infrastructure to another as the intrusion progresses (e.g. a disposable first-stage C2 handing off to a more protected, long-term C2 channel), compartmentalizing the operation so early-stage infrastructure exposure does not compromise the full campaign.
ITID-31932.purpose: Captures multi-stage APT malware where the classification focus is the deliberate handoff of C2 infrastructure between stages, used to compartmentalize and protect the operation.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed handoff from an initial/disposable C2 channel to a distinct, longer-term C2 infrastructure
Deliberate infrastructure segmentation designed to limit the blast radius of early-stage detection
scopeExcludes: The dropper-to-payload execution chain itself when infrastructure handoff is not the primary finding (ITID-31931)
The broader reconnaissance/escalation/exfiltration campaign lifecycle as the classification focus (ITID-31933)
ITID-31932.escalation: Escalate immediately; prioritize identifying and blocking the follow-on C2 infrastructure before the actor completes the handoff.
indicators: Implant communicating with an initial C2 endpoint before pivoting to a distinct, previously-unseen C2 channel
Infrastructure reuse patterns showing a consistent staged-handoff design across multiple intrusions by the same actor
vectors: Disposable first-stage C2 (e.g. commodity infrastructure) used to avoid burning higher-value long-term infrastructure
Deliberate infrastructure segmentation as a standard operational security practice of the actor
rootCauses: Detection tooling that stops monitoring after blocking the initial C2, missing the handoff to follow-on infrastructure
Lack of extended network monitoring across the full intrusion timeline
controls: Extended network monitoring beyond initial C2 blocking to catch follow-on handoffs
Threat intelligence tracking of an actor's staged-infrastructure patterns
ITID-31932.detection: Requires sustained network monitoring across the full intrusion timeline rather than declaring victory after blocking the first-observed C2.
ITID-31932.response: Continue monitoring for follow-on C2 activity after blocking the initial channel, and block all identified infrastructure in the handoff chain.
metrics: Count of confirmed staged C2 handoff incidents per year
detections: Extended post-blocking network monitoring for follow-on C2
ITID-31932.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by focus: the C2 infrastructure compartmentalization strategy itself, distinct from the dropper-to-payload execution mechanics (ITID-31931) or the overall campaign lifecycle (ITID-31933).

playbook.name: Response: Multi-Stage Malware with Staged C2 Infrastructure Handoff
playbook.description: For an APT-level intrusion where C2 responsibility is handed off between different infrastructure at each stage (e.g., initial beacon to redirector, then handoff to a separate long-term C2 server). Assume a sophisticated, patient adversary.

steps.title: Map the full C2 infrastructure handoff chain
steps.desc: Trace C2 communication across each stage to identify every piece of infrastructure involved in the handoff, not just the currently-active C2 destination.
steps.guidance: Blocking only the currently-observed C2 destination will not stop the adversary from using an already-prepared handoff destination.
steps.outcome: Full C2 infrastructure chain mapped.

steps.title: Scope the full extent of compromise across the environment
steps.desc: Hunt across the environment for related indicators and additional footholds.
steps.outcome: Full scope of compromise established.

steps.title: Escalate to full incident-response engagement
steps.desc: Engage the organization's full incident response process.
steps.outcome: Full IR engagement activated.

steps.title: Block all identified infrastructure across the handoff chain simultaneously
steps.desc: Block every domain/IP identified across the full handoff chain at the same time, to prevent the adversary from simply shifting to an already-prepared alternate destination.
steps.outcome: All identified infrastructure blocked simultaneously.

steps.title: Remove all identified implants and persistence mechanisms simultaneously
steps.desc: Coordinate simultaneous removal across all identified compromised hosts.
steps.outcome: All known implants and persistence removed.

steps.title: Hunt for additional undiscovered footholds and unused handoff infrastructure
steps.desc: Continue threat hunting and threat intelligence review to identify any prepared-but-unused handoff infrastructure that should also be tracked/blocked.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further footholds remain and handoff infrastructure fully accounted for.
steps.tool: EDR / SIEM threat hunting / threat intelligence

steps.title: Rebuild affected systems and re-credential
steps.desc: Rebuild compromised systems from known-clean sources and rotate potentially accessed credentials.
steps.outcome: Systems rebuilt and credentials rotated.

steps.title: Document the C2 infrastructure handoff pattern
steps.desc: Document the full infrastructure chain and handoff pattern for ongoing threat intelligence tracking.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive report completed.

ITID-31933.def: A long-dwell advanced persistent threat campaign classified at the level of its overall operational lifecycle — encompassing distinct, temporally separated reconnaissance, privilege-escalation/lateral-movement, and data-exfiltration stages — where the classification concern is the campaign's extended duration and stage progression rather than any single dropper or C2-handoff mechanic.
ITID-31933.purpose: Captures the full campaign-level lifecycle of a long-dwell APT intrusion as the classification focus, spanning distinct reconnaissance, escalation, and exfiltration stages rather than a single technical mechanic.
scopeIncludes: Campaigns confirmed to span weeks-to-months with clearly distinguishable reconnaissance, escalation, and exfiltration phases
Long-dwell intrusions where the primary finding is the extended operational timeline itself
scopeExcludes: The specific dropper-to-payload technical chain as the primary finding (ITID-31931)
The specific C2 infrastructure handoff as the primary finding (ITID-31932)
ITID-31933.escalation: Escalate immediately to full incident response and executive leadership given the extended dwell time and likely broad access already achieved.
indicators: Forensic timeline reconstruction revealing distinct reconnaissance, escalation, and exfiltration phases over an extended period
Evidence of dwell time measured in weeks or months prior to detection
vectors: Initial access followed by patient, low-and-slow reconnaissance before escalation
Staged campaign execution deliberately paced to avoid triggering time-based anomaly detection
rootCauses: Insufficient long-baseline behavioral analytics capable of correlating activity across a long timeline
Lack of retained log history sufficient to reconstruct a multi-month intrusion
controls: Long-baseline behavioral/UEBA analytics
Extended log retention sufficient for multi-month forensic reconstruction
ITID-31933.detection: Requires long-retention logging and behavioral analytics capable of correlating low-and-slow activity across an extended timeline.
ITID-31933.response: Conduct a full campaign-level forensic timeline reconstruction across all affected systems, and assume broad access/exfiltration until conclusively scoped otherwise.
metrics: Count of confirmed long-dwell campaigns per year
Average dwell time from initial access to detection
detections: Long-baseline UEBA correlation across extended timeline
ITID-31933.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by altitude: this leaf classifies at the campaign-lifecycle level, while ITID-31931/31932 classify specific technical mechanics (dropper chain / C2 handoff) within such a campaign.

playbook.name: Response: Long-Dwell APT Campaign with Distinct Reconnaissance/Escalation/Exfiltration Stages
playbook.description: For a long-dwell APT campaign spanning distinct reconnaissance, privilege-escalation, and data-exfiltration phases over an extended period. Assume a sophisticated, patient adversary.

steps.title: Reconstruct the full campaign timeline across all phases
steps.desc: Build a timeline covering the reconnaissance, privilege-escalation, and exfiltration phases of the campaign using all available log retention, since long-dwell campaigns can span months.
steps.guidance: Check log retention limits early — long-dwell activity may predate standard retention windows, requiring extended-retention or archived log sources.
steps.outcome: Full campaign timeline reconstructed across all phases.

steps.title: Determine what data was accessed or exfiltrated across the dwell period
steps.desc: Identify all data accessed, staged, or exfiltrated throughout the campaign's dwell time, not just at the point of detection.
steps.outcome: Full scope of data impact determined.

steps.title: Escalate to full incident-response engagement
steps.desc: Engage the organization's full incident response process, including legal/compliance given the likely data-exposure scope of a long-dwell campaign.
steps.outcome: Full IR engagement activated with legal/compliance involved.

steps.title: Contain without tipping off the adversary prematurely
steps.desc: Coordinate containment timing across all identified footholds established throughout the dwell period.
steps.outcome: Containment plan executed with coordinated timing.

steps.title: Remove all identified implants and persistence mechanisms established across every phase
steps.desc: Coordinate simultaneous removal of all footholds and persistence mechanisms established during reconnaissance, escalation, and exfiltration phases.
steps.guidance: A long dwell time typically means multiple, layered persistence mechanisms accumulated over time.
steps.outcome: All known implants and persistence removed.

steps.title: Hunt for additional undiscovered footholds before declaring eradication complete

steps.outcome: Confirmed no further footholds remain.

steps.title: Rebuild affected systems, re-credential, and address data-exposure obligations
steps.desc: Rebuild compromised systems, rotate all potentially accessed credentials, and address any regulatory/contractual notification obligations arising from the confirmed data impact.
steps.outcome: Systems rebuilt, credentials rotated, and notification obligations addressed.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review covering the entire dwell period
steps.desc: Document the full campaign timeline and assess why the dwell time was so extended, feeding findings into improved detection and log retention policy.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive report completed.

ITID-32111.def: Successful use of a zero-day (no available patch or public advisory at time of use) vulnerability in the Windows kernel or kernel-mode drivers to gain code execution, privilege escalation, or defense evasion.
ITID-32111.purpose: Captures exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched vulnerability in the Windows kernel.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of an undisclosed Windows kernel or kernel-mode driver vulnerability
Confirmed use of a kernel-mode zero-day for local privilege escalation on Windows
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a publicly known/patched Windows kernel CVE (see local exploitation known-CVE leaves)
Zero-day exploitation of a Linux, macOS/iOS, or Android kernel (sibling ITIDs)
ITID-32111.severity: Critical. Kernel-level zero-day exploitation implies full system compromise potential and no vendor patch exists.
ITID-32111.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command, vulnerability management, and the vendor (Microsoft Security Response Center) for coordinated disclosure/patch tracking.
indicators: Anomalous kernel-mode crash or driver fault preceding privilege escalation
EDR alert on unexpected SYSTEM-level code execution with no known CVE match
Kernel callback/API hooking not attributable to known malware
vectors: Malicious driver loaded via signed/unsigned bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver technique
Exploitation delivered via a preceding initial-access foothold to reach kernel attack surface
rootCauses: Memory-safety defects (use-after-free, race conditions) in kernel or driver code
Insufficient kernel attack-surface reduction (unnecessary drivers loaded)
controls: Kernel-mode driver allowlisting / Microsoft vulnerable driver blocklist
Memory-safety mitigations (HVCI, Kernel CFG)
EDR kernel-level telemetry
ITID-32111.detection: Low-to-moderate; kernel telemetry from EDR/HVCI can surface anomalies but true zero-days evade signature-based detection until publicly characterized.
ITID-32111.response: Isolate affected hosts, capture memory/kernel crash dumps, coordinate with Microsoft MSRC, and prioritize compensating controls (HVCI, driver blocklist) pending patch.
metrics: Time from first observed exploitation to vendor patch availability
Number of hosts exposed pending mitigation
ITID-32111.notes: Differentiated from sibling zero-day leaves by target platform (Windows kernel specifically). Excludes any Windows kernel exploitation where a CVE/patch already existed at time of use.

playbook.name: Response: Windows Kernel Zero-Day Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability in the Windows kernel, with no vendor patch or public signature available.

steps.title: Identify anomalous kernel-level behavior via EDR/behavioral telemetry
steps.desc: Since no CVE or signature exists yet, hunt for anomalies rather than known indicators: unexpected kernel-mode crashes/BSODs, driver-load anomalies, unsigned kernel modules, or a process gaining SYSTEM privileges with no legitimate escalation path.
steps.guidance: Focus on behavioral deviation (crash dumps, ETW kernel callbacks, driver signing anomalies) since signature-based tools will not detect this.
steps.outcome: Candidate host(s) and anomalous kernel activity identified.
steps.tool: EDR / Windows crash dump analysis / ETW

steps.title: Capture forensic evidence before the host is altered
steps.desc: Capture full memory image, kernel crash dump, and relevant event logs from the affected host(s) to support vendor and internal analysis.
steps.guidance: Preserve volatile evidence immediately; kernel exploits often leave minimal disk artifacts.
steps.outcome: Forensic evidence preserved for analysis.

steps.title: Determine scope of exposure across the fleet
steps.desc: Identify all systems running the affected Windows build/kernel version to establish potential blast radius.
steps.outcome: List of potentially exposed hosts.

steps.title: Isolate confirmed-compromised hosts
steps.desc: Network-isolate any host with confirmed kernel-level compromise to prevent lateral movement or further exploitation.
steps.outcome: Compromised hosts isolated.

steps.title: Deploy compensating controls while awaiting a patch
steps.desc: Apply vendor-recommended mitigations (e.g., disabling the vulnerable kernel feature/driver, restricting local logon, enhanced ASR rules) across at-risk systems until an official fix is available.
steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced fleet-wide.
steps.tool: Group Policy / EDR attack surface reduction

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure and patch development with Microsoft
steps.desc: Report findings to Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) with forensic evidence to expedite patch development, following responsible disclosure practices.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Rebuild compromised hosts from known-good media
steps.desc: Given kernel-level compromise can undermine OS integrity guarantees, rebuild confirmed-affected hosts from trusted images rather than attempting in-place remediation.
steps.outcome: Hosts rebuilt clean.

steps.title: Apply the vendor patch fleet-wide once released
steps.desc: Deploy the official security update on an emergency basis as soon as Microsoft releases it, prioritizing exposed systems.
steps.outcome: Patch deployed across the environment.

steps.title: Restore rebuilt hosts to service
steps.desc: Return verified-clean, patched hosts to production after validation.
steps.outcome: Hosts restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and update zero-day response playbook
steps.desc: Record the detection method that worked, response timeline, and any gaps in behavioral detection coverage for future kernel-level zero-days.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32112.def: Successful use of a zero-day vulnerability in the Linux kernel or kernel modules to gain code execution, privilege escalation, or defense evasion.
ITID-32112.purpose: Captures exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched vulnerability in the Linux kernel.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of an undisclosed Linux kernel or kernel-module vulnerability
Zero-day container-escape-adjacent kernel exploitation on Linux hosts (where the primary event is the kernel bug, not a container boundary bypass tracked elsewhere)
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a publicly known/patched Linux kernel CVE (see ITID-32331)
Zero-day exploitation of Windows, macOS/iOS, or Android kernels (sibling ITIDs)
ITID-32112.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command and coordinate disclosure with the upstream kernel maintainers / distro security teams.
indicators: Unexpected kernel panic or oops preceding privilege escalation
Loadable kernel module activity inconsistent with baseline
Root-level process spawned from an unprivileged parent with no known technique match
vectors: Local exploitation following an initial unprivileged foothold
Exploitation of kernel network-facing subsystems (e.g., netfilter, io_uring) from a remote or local vector
rootCauses: Memory-safety defects in kernel subsystems
Race conditions in kernel object lifecycle handling
controls: Kernel hardening (seccomp, SELinux/AppArmor, kernel lockdown mode)
Kernel module signing enforcement
Host-based intrusion detection with kernel auditd/eBPF telemetry
ITID-32112.detection: Low-to-moderate; auditd/eBPF-based sensors can surface anomalous root transitions but zero-day-specific signatures are unavailable until public disclosure.
ITID-32112.response: Isolate host, capture kernel crash/core dump, apply available mitigations (lockdown mode, module signing), track distro patch release.
metrics: Time from first observed exploitation to distro patch availability
Number of Linux hosts exposed pending mitigation
ITID-32112.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32111 by target platform (Linux). Local Linux kernel exploitation of a known/patched CVE is tracked separately under ITID-32331.

playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability in the Linux kernel, with no vendor patch or public signature available.

steps.title: Identify anomalous kernel behavior via auditd/EDR telemetry
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies since no signature exists: unexpected kernel panics/oops messages, unauthorized kernel module loads, or a process gaining root with no legitimate escalation path.

steps.title: Capture forensic evidence before the host is altered

steps.guidance: Preserve volatile evidence immediately.
steps.outcome: Forensic evidence preserved.

steps.title: Determine scope of exposure across the fleet

steps.outcome: List of potentially exposed hosts.

steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced fleet-wide.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the kernel maintainers/distro vendor
steps.desc: Report findings through responsible disclosure channels (kernel security list or distro security team) with forensic evidence to expedite a fix.
steps.outcome: Vendor/maintainers engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Rebuild compromised hosts from known-good media
steps.desc: Rebuild confirmed-affected hosts from trusted images rather than attempting in-place remediation, given kernel-level compromise undermines OS integrity guarantees.
steps.outcome: Hosts rebuilt clean.

steps.title: Apply the kernel patch fleet-wide once released
steps.desc: Deploy the official kernel update on an emergency basis, prioritizing exposed systems.
steps.outcome: Patch deployed across the environment.

steps.title: Restore rebuilt hosts to service
steps.desc: Return verified-clean, patched hosts to production after validation.
steps.outcome: Hosts restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and update zero-day response playbook
steps.desc: Record detection method, response timeline, and gaps in kernel-level behavioral detection coverage.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32113.def: Successful use of a zero-day vulnerability in macOS or iOS (kernel, XNU, or platform frameworks) to gain code execution, sandbox escape, or privilege escalation.
ITID-32113.purpose: Captures exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched vulnerability in macOS or iOS.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of an undisclosed macOS/iOS kernel (XNU) vulnerability
Zero-day iOS sandbox-escape or jailbreak-style exploit chain used against a device
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a publicly known/patched macOS/iOS CVE
Zero-day exploitation of Windows, Linux, or Android (sibling ITIDs)
Zero-click messaging-app exploit chains tracked specifically under mercenary spyware deployment (ITID-32143) when spyware attribution is confirmed
ITID-32113.severity: Critical, especially for iOS given mobile device exposure and mercenary-spyware precedent.
ITID-32113.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command; notify Apple Product Security for coordinated disclosure.
indicators: Unexplained device crash logs (panic/backtrace) referencing kernel or WebKit components
Mobile Device Management (MDM) anomaly indicating unauthorized profile or process behavior
Forensic artifact consistent with sandbox escape (e.g., unexpected entitlement usage)
vectors: Exploit chain delivered via malicious link, message, or attachment targeting the device
Exploitation of a platform framework (WebKit, ImageIO) reachable without user interaction
rootCauses: Memory-safety defects in XNU kernel or platform frameworks
Insufficient sandboxing of high-privilege system services
controls: Mobile threat defense (MTD) tooling
Lockdown Mode (iOS) enablement for high-risk users
Rapid OS/security update deployment via MDM
ITID-32113.detection: Low; Apple's closed platform limits third-party telemetry, so detection relies on forensic artifact review (e.g., Mobile Verification Toolkit) and crash-log analysis.
ITID-32113.response: Preserve device forensic artifacts (sysdiagnose, crash logs), engage mobile forensics, coordinate with Apple, and consider Lockdown Mode for at-risk users.
metrics: Time from first observed exploitation to Apple patch availability
Number of devices with confirmed forensic indicators
ITID-32113.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by platform (Apple). Where the exploit is confirmed delivered via commercial mercenary spyware, log under ITID-32143 instead to avoid double-counting.

playbook.name: Response: macOS/iOS Zero-Day Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability affecting macOS or iOS, with no vendor patch or public signature available.

steps.title: Identify anomalous behavior via MDM/EDR telemetry
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies: unexpected process spawns from system daemons, unsigned/unnotarized code execution, sandbox escapes, or unexplained configuration profile changes on managed devices.
steps.guidance: For iOS, also review MDM device compliance drift and unexpected battery/data usage often associated with spyware-class exploits.
steps.outcome: Candidate device(s) and anomalous activity identified.

steps.title: Capture forensic evidence (sysdiagnose / device image)
steps.desc: Collect a sysdiagnose bundle (iOS) or full disk/memory forensic capture (macOS) from affected device(s) before further use or reboot.
steps.guidance: Preserve volatile evidence immediately; iOS exploits often leave minimal persistent artifacts.
steps.outcome: Forensic evidence preserved.

steps.title: Determine scope of exposure across managed devices
steps.desc: Identify all devices running the affected OS version to establish blast radius, prioritizing high-value users (executives, IT admins).
steps.outcome: List of potentially exposed devices.

steps.title: Isolate or remotely restrict confirmed-compromised devices
steps.desc: Revoke network/VPN access and enterprise account tokens for confirmed-compromised devices.
steps.outcome: Compromised devices isolated from corporate resources.

steps.title: Deploy compensating controls while awaiting a fix
steps.desc: Disable the vulnerable feature/service (e.g., iMessage attachment auto-render, a specific system service) via MDM configuration profile until Apple releases a patch.
steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced across managed devices.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with Apple Product Security
steps.desc: Report findings to Apple with forensic evidence to expedite patch development.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Factory-reset and re-provision confirmed-compromised devices
steps.desc: Given the difficulty of confirming full removal of an unknown implant, wipe and re-provision confirmed-compromised devices from a trusted baseline once evidence collection is complete.
steps.outcome: Devices restored to a clean state.

steps.title: Apply the OS update fleet-wide once released
steps.desc: Push the emergency security update to all managed devices as soon as Apple releases it.
steps.outcome: Patch deployed across the fleet.

steps.title: Return re-provisioned devices to users
steps.desc: Restore verified-clean, patched devices to their users after validation.
steps.outcome: Devices restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and assess targeting pattern
steps.desc: Record whether affected users share a role/profile suggesting targeted (rather than opportunistic) delivery, and update mobile threat detection coverage accordingly.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32114.def: Successful use of a zero-day vulnerability in the Android OS (kernel, framework, or bundled components) to gain code execution, privilege escalation, or sandbox escape.
ITID-32114.purpose: Captures exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched vulnerability in Android.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of an undisclosed Android kernel or framework vulnerability
Zero-day exploitation of Android system components (e.g., media/codec libraries) for privilege escalation
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a publicly known/patched Android CVE
Zero-day exploitation of Windows, Linux, or macOS/iOS (sibling ITIDs)
Confirmed mercenary spyware deployment chains (ITID-32143)
ITID-32114.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command; notify Android/OEM security teams and Google's Android Security team for coordinated disclosure.
indicators: Unexplained app or system-service crash preceding elevated-privilege behavior
MDM/EMM anomaly indicating unauthorized system-level access
Forensic artifact consistent with privilege escalation beyond app sandbox
vectors: Malicious application or exploit chain delivered via sideloaded APK or compromised app-store listing
Exploitation of a system component reachable via a malicious message or link (zero-click)
rootCauses: Memory-safety defects in Android kernel or bundled native libraries
Fragmented OEM patch distribution leaving devices exposed post-disclosure
controls: Mobile threat defense (MTD) tooling
Enforced OS/security patch level via MDM/EMM compliance policy
Application allowlisting / disabling sideloading
ITID-32114.detection: Low-to-moderate; MTD and EMM compliance telemetry can flag out-of-date patch levels and anomalous behavior but zero-day-specific detection is limited pre-disclosure.
ITID-32114.response: Preserve device forensic artifacts, engage mobile forensics, coordinate with Google/OEM, and enforce compliance-based device quarantine pending patch.
metrics: Time from first observed exploitation to Android/OEM patch availability
Number of devices non-compliant with patch level post-disclosure
ITID-32114.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by platform (Android). Confirmed mercenary spyware chains are logged under ITID-32143 instead.

playbook.name: Response: Android Zero-Day Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability affecting the Android OS, with no vendor patch or public signature available.

steps.title: Identify anomalous behavior via MDM/mobile threat defense telemetry
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies: unexpected privileged process activity, unexplained permission grants, sideloaded/unsigned APK execution, or sandbox/SELinux policy violations.
steps.outcome: Candidate device(s) and anomalous activity identified.

steps.title: Capture forensic evidence (device logs / bug report)
steps.desc: Collect an Android bug report and, where feasible, a device image from affected device(s) before further use.
steps.guidance: Preserve volatile evidence immediately.
steps.outcome: Forensic evidence preserved.
steps.tool: Android bug report tooling / mobile forensic tooling

steps.title: Determine scope of exposure across managed devices
steps.desc: Identify all devices running the affected Android version/OEM build to establish blast radius.
steps.outcome: List of potentially exposed devices.

steps.title: Isolate or remotely restrict confirmed-compromised devices
steps.desc: Revoke network/VPN access and enterprise account tokens for confirmed-compromised devices.
steps.outcome: Compromised devices isolated from corporate resources.

steps.title: Deploy compensating controls while awaiting a fix
steps.desc: Disable or restrict the vulnerable component/service via MDM policy until Google/OEM releases a patch.
steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced across managed devices.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with Google/OEM security teams
steps.desc: Report findings to Android Security/OEM with forensic evidence to expedite patch development.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Factory-reset and re-provision confirmed-compromised devices
steps.desc: Wipe and re-provision confirmed-compromised devices from a trusted baseline once evidence collection is complete.
steps.outcome: Devices restored to a clean state.

steps.title: Apply the security patch fleet-wide once released
steps.desc: Push the emergency security update to all managed devices as soon as it is released.
steps.outcome: Patch deployed across the fleet.

steps.title: Return re-provisioned devices to users
steps.desc: Restore verified-clean, patched devices to their users after validation.
steps.outcome: Devices restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review mobile patch SLA
steps.desc: Record detection method, response timeline, and OEM patch-lag risk; consider compensating device policy for slow-patching OEMs.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32115.def: An incident involving exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched operating-system vulnerability, not clearly matching a more specific platform leaf.
ITID-32115.purpose: Catch-all for OS zero-day exploitation that does not clearly fit Windows, Linux, macOS/iOS, or Android leaves.
scopeIncludes: Zero-day exploitation of a niche or embedded general-purpose OS (e.g., a minority desktop/server OS) not covered by a specific leaf
Cases logged before the affected OS platform is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Any case where the specific OS platform (Windows, Linux, macOS/iOS, Android) is confirmed — reclassify to the matching sibling leaf
ITID-32115.severity: Critical pending platform confirmation; reassess once specific OS is identified.
ITID-32115.priority: P1 by default given zero-day nature.
ITID-32115.escalation: Escalate immediately; reclassify to a specific platform leaf once confirmed.
indicators: OS-level crash or anomalous privileged process with unclear platform attribution
vectors: Activity of unclear specific OS vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: General OS hardening baselines pending platform-specific control mapping
ITID-32115.detection: Same general telemetry gaps as sibling zero-day leaves, pending finer platform classification.
ITID-32115.response: Investigate and reclassify to a platform-specific leaf once the OS is confirmed.
metrics: Count pending platform reclassification
ITID-32115.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General OS Zero-Day Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability in an operating system not otherwise classified, with no vendor patch or public signature available.

steps.title: Identify anomalous OS-level behavior via available telemetry
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies appropriate to the platform: unexpected privilege gains, crashes, unsigned code execution, or unexplained system state changes with no known IOC to match against.
steps.outcome: Candidate host(s) and anomalous activity identified.

steps.title: Capture forensic evidence before the host is altered
steps.desc: Capture memory/disk image and relevant logs from affected host(s) to support analysis.
steps.outcome: Forensic evidence preserved.

steps.title: Determine scope of exposure across the fleet
steps.desc: Identify all systems running the affected OS/version to establish blast radius.
steps.outcome: List of potentially exposed hosts.

steps.title: Isolate confirmed-compromised hosts
steps.desc: Network-isolate any host with confirmed compromise to prevent lateral movement.
steps.outcome: Compromised hosts isolated.

steps.title: Deploy compensating controls while awaiting a fix
steps.desc: Disable or restrict the vulnerable feature/service and apply available hardening until an official patch is released.
steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced fleet-wide.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the OS vendor
steps.desc: Report findings to the vendor's security team with forensic evidence to expedite patch development.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Rebuild or re-provision compromised hosts
steps.desc: Rebuild confirmed-affected hosts from trusted media rather than attempting in-place remediation.
steps.outcome: Hosts rebuilt clean.

steps.title: Apply the vendor patch fleet-wide once released
steps.desc: Deploy the official security update on an emergency basis, prioritizing exposed systems.
steps.outcome: Patch deployed across the environment.

steps.title: Document the incident and update zero-day response playbook
steps.desc: Record detection method, response timeline, and any gaps in behavioral detection coverage for future OS zero-days.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32121.def: Exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched vulnerability in enterprise software (e.g., file-transfer, collaboration, network-management platforms) that is broadly deployed such that a single vendor flaw creates supply-chain-scale exposure across many organizations.
ITID-32121.purpose: Captures zero-day exploitation of widely-deployed enterprise software where the blast radius extends beyond the initially compromised organization.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of an undisclosed vulnerability in a widely-used enterprise platform (e.g., managed file transfer, collaboration suite, network management tool)
Cases where the same zero-day is being mass-exploited across many organizations, not just this one
scopeExcludes: Zero-day exploitation of custom/in-house applications (ITID-32124)
Zero-day exploitation confined to a browser (ITID-32122) or office document format (ITID-32123)
ITID-32121.severity: Critical; mass-exploitation potential and downstream customer impact elevate severity beyond a typical single-org zero-day.
ITID-32121.priority: P1, immediate, with heightened external-communications coordination.
ITID-32121.escalation: Escalate to incident command, legal/communications (given potential downstream customer notification obligations), and the software vendor.
indicators: Web shell or anomalous process spawned from a known enterprise application's service account
Outbound connections from the application server inconsistent with its function
Vendor advisory or ISAC alert referencing active mass exploitation
vectors: Unauthenticated remote exploitation of an internet-facing enterprise application endpoint
Malicious file upload/deserialization exploiting an undisclosed application flaw
rootCauses: Insecure deserialization or authentication-bypass defects in vendor code
Insufficient network segmentation around internet-facing enterprise applications
controls: Network segmentation isolating internet-facing application servers
Web application firewall with virtual-patching capability
Rapid vendor patch/mitigation deployment process
ITID-32121.detection: Moderate once a public advisory exists (IOCs/detection rules follow quickly given the scale of impact); low prior to disclosure.
ITID-32121.response: Isolate affected application servers, hunt for web shells/persistence, apply vendor mitigations, and assess customer/downstream notification obligations.
metrics: Time from vendor advisory to internal patch/mitigation
Number of internet-facing instances confirmed exploited
detections: Web shell detection on application servers
ITID-32121.notes: Differentiated from sibling application-zero-day leaves by the supply-chain/mass-exploitation scale axis rather than a specific application category.

playbook.name: Response: Zero-Day in Widely-Used Enterprise Software (Supply-Chain Impact)
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability in widely-used enterprise software with potential supply-chain/downstream impact.

steps.title: Identify anomalous behavior via application/EDR telemetry
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies in the affected software: unexpected child processes spawned by the application, unusual outbound connections, or unexplained file writes with no known IOC to match against.
steps.outcome: Candidate host(s)/instance(s) and anomalous activity identified.

steps.title: Determine scope across the environment and downstream customers
steps.desc: Identify all internal deployments of the affected software and, if your organization distributes it downstream, assess supply-chain exposure to customers/partners.
steps.guidance: Given the supply-chain implication, scope must include both internal exposure and any downstream parties relying on this software.
steps.outcome: Full internal and downstream exposure list established.

steps.title: Isolate or restrict the affected software instances
