steps.desc: Network-isolate or restrict access to systems running the vulnerable software, particularly internet-facing instances.
steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced.

steps.title: Deploy vendor-recommended compensating controls
steps.desc: Apply interim mitigations (feature disabling, WAF rules, configuration hardening) published by the vendor while awaiting a patch.
steps.outcome: Interim risk reduction in place.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure and patch tracking with the vendor
steps.desc: Engage the software vendor's security team, and notify downstream customers/partners per supply-chain disclosure obligations if applicable.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged; downstream parties notified as required.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence from compromised instances
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised systems of dropped malware or persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: Systems confirmed clean.

steps.title: Apply the vendor patch across all instances
steps.desc: Deploy the official fix on an emergency basis across all internal deployments.
steps.outcome: Patch deployed.

steps.title: Restore isolated systems to service
steps.desc: Return patched, verified-clean systems to production.
steps.outcome: Systems restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review third-party software risk exposure
steps.desc: Record the incident, assess concentration risk from this software vendor, and evaluate whether downstream notification obligations were met.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32122.def: Exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched vulnerability in a web browser's rendering engine, JavaScript engine, or sandbox to achieve remote code execution or sandbox escape on an endpoint.
ITID-32122.purpose: Captures zero-day exploitation targeting a web browser to achieve client-side code execution.
scopeIncludes: Zero-day exploitation of a browser rendering/JS engine (e.g., V8, WebKit, Gecko)
Zero-day browser sandbox-escape used to achieve code execution outside the browser process
scopeExcludes: Known-CVE browser exploitation delivered via drive-by download (ITID-32413, which specifically tracks drive-by delivery of a browser zero-day — cross-reference when the delivery mechanism, not the vulnerability itself, is the focus)
Zero-day exploitation of a malicious browser extension's own vulnerability (ITID-32423)
ITID-32122.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command and the browser vendor for coordinated disclosure.
indicators: Browser process crash or unexpected child-process spawn (e.g., browser spawning a shell)
EDR alert on renderer-to-broker sandbox escape pattern
Anomalous JavaScript execution preceding native code execution
vectors: User visits an attacker-controlled or compromised web page triggering the exploit
Malicious advertisement serving the exploit (malvertising)
rootCauses: Memory-safety defects in the browser's JavaScript/rendering engine
Sandbox escape defects in inter-process communication
controls: Browser auto-update enforcement
Site isolation / renderer sandboxing
Endpoint detection for anomalous browser child processes
ITID-32122.detection: Low pre-disclosure; moderate post-disclosure once vendor IOCs and detection signatures are published.
ITID-32122.response: Isolate affected endpoints, capture browser/process forensics, apply emergency browser update or mitigation, and hunt for further compromise from the initial foothold.
metrics: Time from disclosure to fleet-wide browser patch
Number of endpoints with confirmed exploitation indicators
ITID-32122.notes: Focuses on the browser vulnerability itself; the drive-by delivery vector of a browser zero-day is separately tracked under ITID-32413 to avoid duplicating the delivery-mechanism angle.

playbook.name: Response: Zero-Day in Web Browser
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability in a web browser, with no vendor patch or public signature available.

steps.title: Identify anomalous browser-related process behavior
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies: browser renderer/sandbox processes spawning unexpected child processes, unexplained outbound connections following a browsing session, or sandbox escape indicators.
steps.outcome: Candidate host(s) and anomalous activity identified.

steps.title: Identify the delivery vector (malicious site/ad/link)
steps.desc: Trace browsing history and network logs to identify the site or link that triggered the exploit, to support blocking and user notification.
steps.outcome: Delivery vector identified.

steps.title: Isolate confirmed-compromised hosts
steps.desc: Network-isolate any host with confirmed post-exploitation activity.
steps.outcome: Compromised hosts isolated.

steps.title: Block the malicious domain/URL organization-wide
steps.desc: Block the identified malicious site at the proxy/DNS layer to prevent further exposure.
steps.outcome: Delivery vector blocked fleet-wide.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the browser vendor
steps.desc: Report findings to the browser vendor's security team with forensic evidence to expedite patch development.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence from compromised hosts
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts of dropped malware or persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: Hosts confirmed clean.

steps.title: Deploy the browser update fleet-wide once released
steps.desc: Push the emergency browser security update to all managed endpoints as soon as it is released.
steps.outcome: Patch deployed across the fleet.

steps.title: Document the incident and review web filtering coverage
steps.desc: Record the delivery vector, detection method, and assess whether web filtering/sandboxing controls could have reduced exposure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32123.def: Exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched vulnerability in an office/productivity application (word processor, spreadsheet, PDF reader) triggered by a specially crafted document opened by the victim.
ITID-32123.purpose: Captures zero-day exploitation delivered through a malicious office/productivity document.
scopeIncludes: Zero-day exploitation of a document-parsing or macro-execution vulnerability in an office suite or PDF reader
Malicious document exploiting an undisclosed vulnerability to achieve code execution on open
scopeExcludes: Known-CVE document exploitation with an available patch
Zero-day exploitation confined to a browser (ITID-32122) or custom in-house application (ITID-32124)
ITID-32123.severity: Critical, particularly given phishing as a common delivery vector for widespread impact.
ITID-32123.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command and the software vendor for coordinated disclosure.
indicators: Office application spawning an unexpected child process (e.g., PowerShell, cmd) on document open
Anomalous memory corruption crash in a document reader application
Endpoint detection of shellcode execution originating from a document-handling process
vectors: Spearphishing email with a malicious document attachment exploiting the zero-day
Malicious document hosted for download and opened by the victim
rootCauses: Memory-safety or macro/embedded-object handling defects in document parsers
Insufficient application sandboxing of untrusted document content
controls: Protected View / sandboxed document rendering
Attachment detonation sandboxing at the email gateway
Application allowlisting to constrain child-process spawning from office apps
ITID-32123.detection: Low pre-disclosure; email gateway detonation sandboxes can catch exploitation behaviorally even without a known signature.
ITID-32123.response: Isolate affected endpoints, retrieve and analyze the malicious document, apply vendor mitigation, and search mail environment for further delivery of the same document.
metrics: Number of recipients of the malicious document
Time from disclosure to patch deployment
ITID-32123.notes: Differentiated from browser and custom-app zero-day siblings by the document-based delivery/exploitation mechanism.

playbook.name: Response: Zero-Day in Office/Productivity Application (Document-Based Exploit)
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability delivered via a malicious document opened in an office/productivity application.

steps.title: Identify anomalous process behavior following document open
steps.desc: Hunt for the office application spawning unexpected child processes (e.g., a script host, command shell) immediately after a document was opened, with no known IOC to match against.
steps.outcome: Candidate host(s) and the triggering document identified.

steps.title: Trace the document's delivery path and recipient list
steps.desc: Determine how the malicious document was delivered (email, shared drive, external site) and identify all recipients who may have received or opened it.
steps.outcome: Full delivery and recipient scope established.

steps.title: Isolate confirmed-compromised hosts
steps.desc: Network-isolate any host where the document was opened and post-exploitation activity is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Compromised hosts isolated.

steps.title: Purge the malicious document from all mailboxes/shares
steps.desc: Remove the identified document from all mailboxes and shared storage to prevent further opens.
steps.outcome: Document removed organization-wide.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the software vendor
steps.desc: Report findings to the application vendor's security team with forensic evidence to expedite patch development.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence from compromised hosts
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts of dropped malware or persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: Hosts confirmed clean.

steps.title: Deploy the application update fleet-wide once released
steps.desc: Push the emergency security update to all managed endpoints as soon as it is released; interim, enable Protected View/macro-blocking hardening.
steps.outcome: Patch deployed and interim hardening applied.

steps.title: Document the incident and review email/document filtering controls
steps.desc: Record the delivery vector and detection method, and assess whether sandboxed document rendering or attachment filtering could reduce future exposure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32124.def: Exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched vulnerability in software developed and maintained internally by the organization (not a commercial or open-source third-party product).
ITID-32124.purpose: Captures zero-day exploitation of an organization's own custom or in-house-developed application.
scopeIncludes: Zero-day exploitation of a bug in internally-authored application code
Exploitation of an undisclosed logic or memory-safety flaw the organization's own developers introduced
scopeExcludes: Zero-day exploitation of a commercial enterprise product (ITID-32121)
Zero-day exploitation of a browser (ITID-32122) or office application (ITID-32123)
ITID-32124.severity: High-Critical, depending on the application's data sensitivity and exposure.
ITID-32124.escalation: Escalate to incident command and the internal engineering/application-owner team; no external vendor exists to coordinate with.
indicators: Application error logs showing unexpected input triggering a crash or unexpected behavior
Anomalous application-layer requests preceding unauthorized data access or code execution
WAF/RASP alert on an unrecognized exploitation pattern
vectors: Direct exploitation of an internet-facing custom application endpoint
Exploitation discovered via bug-bounty or red-team activity later confirmed as actively exploited in the wild
rootCauses: Insecure coding practices not caught by SAST/DAST/code review
Lack of a formal secure-SDLC or dependency-vulnerability-management process for in-house code
controls: Runtime application self-protection (RASP)
Secure SDLC with mandatory SAST/DAST gating
Internal bug-bounty/vulnerability-disclosure program
ITID-32124.detection: Low-to-moderate; detection depends entirely on internal application logging/WAF maturity since no vendor telemetry or public IOC exists.
ITID-32124.response: Engineering team patches the vulnerability directly (no vendor dependency), isolate affected components, and conduct a root-cause code review of related code paths.
metrics: Time from discovery to internal patch deployment (typically faster than vendor-dependent leaves)
Number of related code paths remediated post-incident
detections: WAF/RASP anomaly alerting on custom applications
ITID-32124.notes: Distinguished from ITID-32121 by ownership: this leaf is for the organization's own code, where remediation is internally controlled rather than vendor-dependent.

playbook.name: Response: Zero-Day in Custom/In-House Application
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability in an application developed and maintained in-house.

steps.title: Identify anomalous application behavior via logs/EDR
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies: unexpected process spawns from the application server, unauthorized data access patterns, or unexplained errors/crashes with no known IOC to match against.
steps.outcome: Candidate host(s)/service(s) and anomalous activity identified.

steps.title: Engage the in-house development team to review recent code paths
steps.desc: Since no vendor exists, engage internal developers immediately to review the affected code path, request handling, and any recent changes that may be implicated.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable code path identified.

steps.title: Isolate or take the affected application/endpoint offline
steps.desc: Network-isolate the affected service, or take the specific vulnerable endpoint/feature offline, to halt active exploitation.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Deploy a WAF rule or input-validation hotfix as an interim control
steps.desc: Apply a targeted WAF rule or emergency code hotfix to block the specific exploitation pattern while a full fix is developed.
steps.outcome: Interim risk reduction in place.

steps.title: Develop and deploy a permanent code fix
steps.desc: Have the development team develop, test, and deploy a proper fix for the vulnerability through the normal (accelerated) release pipeline.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated in code.

steps.title: Remove any payload or unauthorized data access resulting from exploitation
steps.desc: Investigate and remediate any data exposure, unauthorized account changes, or backdoors introduced during exploitation.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the application to full service
steps.desc: Re-enable the affected feature/endpoint once the fix is verified in production.
steps.outcome: Application restored to normal operation.

steps.title: Document the incident and conduct a secure code review of related components
steps.desc: Record the vulnerability class and root cause, and schedule a secure code review of related application components to catch similar issues.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and follow-up review scheduled.

ITID-32125.def: An incident involving exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched application-level vulnerability, not clearly matching a more specific application-category leaf.
ITID-32125.purpose: Catch-all for application zero-day exploitation that does not fit enterprise software, browser, office/productivity, or custom-application leaves.
scopeIncludes: Zero-day exploitation of an application category not otherwise enumerated (e.g., a niche commercial utility)
Cases logged before the specific application category is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Any case where the application category (enterprise software, browser, office/productivity, custom in-house) is confirmed — reclassify to the matching sibling leaf
ITID-32125.severity: Critical pending confirmation; reassess once application category is identified.
ITID-32125.priority: P1 by default given zero-day nature.
ITID-32125.escalation: Escalate immediately; reclassify once the application category is clarified.
indicators: Application-level crash or anomalous behavior with unclear category attribution
vectors: Activity of unclear specific application vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: General application-hardening baselines pending category-specific control mapping
ITID-32125.detection: Same general telemetry gaps as sibling zero-day leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32125.response: Investigate and reclassify to a category-specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending category reclassification
ITID-32125.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Application Zero-Day Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability in an application not otherwise classified, with no vendor patch or public signature available.

steps.title: Identify anomalous application behavior via available telemetry
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies in the affected application: unexpected child processes, unusual network activity, or unexplained crashes with no known IOC to match against.
steps.outcome: Candidate host(s)/instance(s) and anomalous activity identified.

steps.title: Determine scope of exposure across the environment
steps.desc: Identify all deployments/instances of the affected application to establish blast radius.
steps.outcome: List of potentially exposed instances.

steps.title: Isolate or restrict the affected application instances
steps.desc: Network-isolate or restrict access to systems running the vulnerable application.
steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced.

steps.title: Deploy available compensating controls
steps.desc: Apply interim mitigations (feature disabling, WAF rules, configuration hardening) while awaiting a patch or fix.
steps.outcome: Interim risk reduction in place.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the vendor or maintainer
steps.desc: Engage the software vendor/maintainer's security contact with forensic evidence to expedite a fix.
steps.outcome: Vendor/maintainer engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence from compromised instances
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised systems of dropped malware or persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: Systems confirmed clean.

steps.title: Apply the fix across all instances once available
steps.desc: Deploy the official patch/fix on an emergency basis across all affected deployments.
steps.outcome: Patch deployed.

steps.title: Document the incident and update zero-day response playbook
steps.desc: Record detection method, response timeline, and any gaps in behavioral detection coverage for future application zero-days.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32131.def: Exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched vulnerability in ICS/SCADA hardware or software (PLCs, HMIs, engineering workstations, historian servers) to achieve unauthorized control or manipulation.
ITID-32131.purpose: Captures zero-day exploitation of industrial control system / SCADA equipment.
scopeIncludes: Zero-day exploitation of a PLC, HMI, or SCADA historian/engineering-workstation vulnerability
Exploitation of an undisclosed OT protocol implementation flaw
scopeExcludes: Zero-day exploitation of general-purpose IoT devices (ITID-32132)
Zero-day exploitation of network appliances/firmware such as routers or VPN gateways (ITID-32133)
ITID-32131.severity: Critical; potential for physical/safety impact elevates severity beyond typical IT zero-days.
ITID-32131.escalation: Escalate immediately to OT/ICS security team, safety officers, and the equipment vendor.
indicators: Unexpected PLC logic change or HMI command not issued by an authorized operator
OT network traffic anomaly on engineering-protocol ports
Historian data inconsistency suggesting manipulated readings
vectors: Exploitation via an IT/OT network bridge point
Exploitation of an internet-exposed OT management interface
rootCauses: Legacy OT protocols lacking authentication/encryption by design
Insufficient IT/OT network segmentation
controls: IT/OT network segmentation with unidirectional gateways where feasible
OT-specific intrusion detection (protocol-aware)
Vendor patch/compensating-control tracking for OT assets
ITID-32131.detection: Low; OT environments typically have limited security telemetry compared to IT, and zero-day signatures are unavailable pre-disclosure.
ITID-32131.response: Engage OT safety and engineering teams before any containment action (to avoid unsafe process states), isolate at the IT/OT boundary, and coordinate with the equipment vendor.
metrics: Time from disclosure to compensating control deployment on OT assets
Number of OT assets confirmed exposed
ITID-32131.notes: Scoped specifically to control-system/OT equipment to avoid overlap with general IoT (ITID-32132) and network-appliance (ITID-32133) siblings.

playbook.name: Response: Industrial Control System (ICS/SCADA) Zero-Day Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability in an ICS/SCADA component, with no vendor patch available and potential safety/physical-process impact.

steps.title: Identify anomalous behavior via OT monitoring/EDR
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies in OT network traffic and controller state (unexpected PLC logic changes, unusual engineering-workstation-to-controller traffic, abnormal process values) with no known IOC to match against.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with OT/control engineers who understand normal process baselines.
steps.outcome: Candidate ICS asset(s) and anomalous activity identified.

steps.title: Assess safety and physical-process impact
steps.desc: Immediately engage plant/OT engineering to determine whether the anomaly poses a safety risk or has altered a physical process, given ICS exploitation can have real-world consequences beyond data compromise.
steps.guidance: Safety takes priority over evidence preservation if a hazardous condition is possible.
steps.outcome: Safety impact assessed and communicated to operations leadership.

steps.title: Isolate the affected ICS segment from IT networks
steps.desc: Enforce or tighten the IT/OT network boundary (firewall, data diode) to prevent the exploit from spreading from/to the affected segment.
steps.guidance: Avoid abrupt shutdown of live physical processes without OT engineering sign-off.
steps.outcome: OT segment isolated with minimal process disruption.
steps.abort: Coordinate any isolation timing with plant operations to avoid unsafe shutdown.

steps.title: Switch to manual/backup control procedures if warranted
steps.desc: If controller integrity cannot be verified, transition the affected process to manual control or a verified backup controller per site safety procedures.
steps.outcome: Process continuity/safety maintained during response.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the ICS vendor and CISA/ICS-CERT
steps.desc: Report findings to the equipment vendor and relevant national ICS security authority (e.g., CISA) with forensic evidence to expedite a fix and industry-wide alerting.
steps.outcome: Vendor and authorities engaged.

steps.title: Verify and restore controller firmware/logic integrity
steps.desc: Reflash or restore affected controllers from a verified known-good firmware/logic backup.
steps.outcome: Controller integrity restored.

steps.title: Return the ICS segment to automated control after validation
steps.desc: Restore normal automated control only after engineering has validated controller logic and safety systems.
steps.outcome: Process restored to normal, verified-safe operation.

steps.title: Document the incident and review IT/OT segmentation
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether IT/OT network segmentation and OT-specific monitoring require strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32132.def: Exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched vulnerability in a consumer or enterprise IoT device (cameras, sensors, smart building/office equipment) to achieve code execution or device takeover.
ITID-32132.purpose: Captures zero-day exploitation of general-purpose IoT devices.
scopeIncludes: Zero-day exploitation of an IoT device's firmware or embedded web-management interface
Exploitation used to recruit the device into a botnet or as a network foothold
scopeExcludes: Zero-day exploitation of ICS/SCADA equipment (ITID-32131)
Zero-day exploitation of network appliances/firmware such as routers, firewalls, or VPN gateways (ITID-32133)
ITID-32132.severity: Medium-High; severity depends on device criticality and network position.
ITID-32132.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the device provides a pivot into a sensitive network segment.
ITID-32132.escalation: Escalate to network security team; isolate the device segment pending vendor patch.
indicators: Unexpected outbound connections from an IoT device to unfamiliar infrastructure
Device firmware checksum mismatch from known-good baseline
Device joining a known botnet C2 pattern
vectors: Exploitation of an exposed device management web interface
Exploitation via a device's exposed network service (e.g., UPnP, Telnet)
rootCauses: Weak or absent secure-boot/firmware-integrity verification
Devices exposed directly to the internet without network segmentation
controls: IoT network segmentation (dedicated VLAN, no direct internet exposure)
Firmware integrity monitoring where supported
Device inventory and lifecycle/patch management program
ITID-32132.detection: Low-to-moderate; network-based anomaly detection (unexpected outbound traffic) is often the most reliable signal given limited on-device telemetry.
ITID-32132.response: Isolate the device network segment, capture available firmware/logs, and apply vendor patch or replace the device if unsupported.
metrics: Number of IoT devices on unsegmented networks
Time from disclosure to patch/replacement
detections: Network anomaly detection for IoT segments
ITID-32132.notes: Scoped to general-purpose/consumer-style IoT to avoid overlap with OT/ICS (ITID-32131) and network infrastructure appliances (ITID-32133).

playbook.name: Response: IoT Device Zero-Day Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability in an IoT device, with no vendor patch available.

steps.title: Identify anomalous device behavior via network monitoring
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies such as unexpected outbound connections, unusual traffic volume, or command-and-control-like beaconing from IoT devices, since most IoT devices lack host-based logging.
steps.guidance: Rely on network-level detection (NetFlow, IDS) as the primary visibility source for these devices.
steps.outcome: Candidate device(s) and anomalous activity identified.

steps.title: Determine scope across the IoT fleet
steps.desc: Identify all devices of the same make/model/firmware version to establish blast radius.
steps.outcome: List of potentially exposed devices.

steps.title: Isolate affected devices to a restricted network segment
steps.desc: Move confirmed/suspected-compromised devices to a quarantined VLAN with no access to sensitive internal resources.
steps.outcome: Compromised devices isolated.

steps.title: Block malicious C2 destinations and restrict unnecessary connectivity
steps.desc: Block identified command-and-control destinations at the firewall and restrict the device class to only the minimum required connectivity.
steps.outcome: Outbound exploitation channel blocked.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the device vendor
steps.desc: Report findings to the device manufacturer with forensic evidence to expedite a firmware fix.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Factory-reset or replace compromised devices
steps.desc: Given limited forensic visibility on most IoT devices, factory-reset (or physically replace, if reset cannot be trusted) confirmed-compromised units.
steps.outcome: Devices restored to a clean state.

steps.title: Apply firmware update fleet-wide once released and restore devices
steps.desc: Update firmware on all devices of the affected model once the vendor releases a fix, then return devices to normal network segmentation.
steps.outcome: Fleet patched and restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review IoT network segmentation policy
steps.desc: Record the incident and assess whether IoT devices are adequately segmented and monitored given their limited native security controls.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32133.def: Exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched vulnerability in the firmware or management software of a network appliance (router, firewall, VPN gateway, load balancer) to achieve code execution or unauthorized administrative access.
ITID-32133.purpose: Captures zero-day exploitation of network infrastructure appliances such as routers, firewalls, and VPN gateways.
scopeIncludes: Zero-day exploitation of a router, firewall, or VPN gateway's firmware/web-admin interface
Exploitation used to establish a persistent foothold on network perimeter infrastructure
scopeExcludes: Zero-day exploitation of general-purpose consumer/enterprise IoT devices (ITID-32132)
Known-CVE VPN gateway exploitation with an available patch (ITID-32221)
ITID-32133.severity: Critical; perimeter network appliances are high-value footholds with broad downstream access.
ITID-32133.escalation: Escalate immediately to network security team, incident command, and the appliance vendor.
indicators: Unauthorized configuration change on a firewall/router/VPN gateway
Anomalous administrative session or new admin account creation on the appliance
Outbound C2-style traffic originating from the appliance itself
vectors: Exploitation of an internet-exposed appliance management interface
Exploitation of the appliance's VPN/SSL termination component
rootCauses: Memory-safety or authentication-bypass defects in vendor firmware
Management interfaces exposed to the internet unnecessarily
controls: Restrict appliance management interfaces to trusted networks only
Appliance firmware integrity verification and rapid patch process
Network traffic monitoring for anomalous appliance behavior
ITID-32133.detection: Low pre-disclosure; appliances often lack robust host-based telemetry, so network-layer anomaly detection is the primary signal.
ITID-32133.response: Assume full compromise of the appliance and any credentials/certificates it held; rebuild/reimage from trusted firmware, rotate all secrets, and apply vendor patch.
metrics: Time from disclosure to firmware patch across the fleet
Number of appliances confirmed compromised
detections: Network traffic anomaly detection at the perimeter
ITID-32133.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32221 (known-CVE VPN exploitation) by the zero-day/no-patch-available condition, and from ITID-32132 by targeting network infrastructure rather than general IoT.

playbook.name: Response: Network Appliance/Firmware Zero-Day Exploit (Router/Firewall/VPN Gateway)
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability in network appliance firmware (router, firewall, or VPN gateway), with no vendor patch available. These devices sit at the network perimeter, so compromise represents a severe, high-privilege foothold.

steps.title: Identify anomalous appliance behavior via management-plane and traffic review
steps.desc: Hunt for unexpected configuration changes, unauthorized administrative logins, unexplained new accounts, or anomalous traffic patterns traversing the appliance, since no signature exists yet.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference appliance syslog/management-plane audit logs against change-management records.
steps.outcome: Candidate appliance(s) and anomalous activity identified.
steps.tool: Appliance syslog / SIEM / network traffic analysis

steps.title: Assess the severity of perimeter compromise
steps.desc: Given this device's position at the network boundary, determine whether attacker access extends beyond the appliance into the internal network (lateral movement, credential harvesting from transiting traffic).
steps.guidance: Treat perimeter appliance compromise as a potential full-network compromise until proven otherwise.
steps.outcome: Scope of downstream compromise established.

steps.title: Isolate or fail over the affected appliance
steps.desc: Take the affected appliance out of production traffic flow — failing over to a redundant unit or standby configuration — while investigation proceeds.
steps.outcome: Malicious appliance removed from the traffic path.
steps.abort: Ensure failover does not itself route through compromised infrastructure.

steps.title: Force credential and certificate rotation for anything transiting the appliance
steps.desc: Rotate VPN/administrative credentials and any certificates/keys that may have transited or been stored on the compromised appliance.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the appliance vendor
steps.desc: Report findings to the vendor's security team with forensic evidence to expedite firmware patch development.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Factory-reset and rebuild the appliance configuration from a trusted baseline
steps.desc: Given firmware-level compromise can survive a simple reboot, factory-reset the appliance and rebuild its configuration from a verified trusted backup, not the potentially compromised running config.
steps.outcome: Appliance restored to a clean, trusted state.

steps.title: Apply the firmware patch and return the appliance to production
steps.desc: Apply the vendor's emergency firmware update once released, verify configuration integrity, and restore the appliance to production traffic.
steps.outcome: Appliance patched and restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review perimeter appliance hardening/monitoring
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate management-plane exposure, monitoring coverage, and redundancy for perimeter appliances.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32134.def: An incident involving exploitation of a previously unknown, unpatched embedded-system vulnerability, not clearly matching a more specific embedded-category leaf.
ITID-32134.purpose: Catch-all for embedded-system zero-day exploitation that does not fit ICS/SCADA, IoT, or network-appliance leaves.
scopeIncludes: Zero-day exploitation of an embedded device category not otherwise enumerated
Cases logged before the specific embedded device category is confirmed
scopeExcludes: Any case where the embedded category (ICS/SCADA, IoT, network appliance) is confirmed — reclassify to the matching sibling leaf
ITID-32134.priority: P1 by default given zero-day nature.
ITID-32134.escalation: Escalate immediately; reclassify once the embedded device category is clarified.
indicators: Embedded device anomaly with unclear category attribution
vectors: Activity of unclear specific embedded-device vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: General embedded-device hardening baselines pending category-specific control mapping
ITID-32134.detection: Same general telemetry gaps as sibling zero-day leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32134.response: Investigate and reclassify to a category-specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending category reclassification
ITID-32134.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Embedded System Zero-Day Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exploitation of a previously unknown (zero-day) vulnerability in an embedded system not otherwise classified, with no vendor patch available.

steps.title: Identify anomalous device behavior via available telemetry
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies (unexpected network activity, unexplained device state changes) using whatever network- or device-level visibility exists, since no signature is available.
steps.outcome: Candidate device(s) and anomalous activity identified.
steps.tool: Network traffic analysis / device logging (if available)

steps.title: Determine scope across similar devices
steps.desc: Identify all devices of the same make/model/firmware to establish blast radius.
steps.outcome: List of potentially exposed devices.

steps.title: Isolate affected devices to a restricted network segment
steps.desc: Move confirmed/suspected-compromised devices to a quarantined segment with minimal access to other resources.
steps.outcome: Compromised devices isolated.

steps.title: Restrict device connectivity to the minimum required
steps.desc: Restrict the device class to only essential connectivity as a compensating control.
steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the device vendor
steps.desc: Report findings to the manufacturer with forensic evidence to expedite a fix.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Factory-reset or replace compromised devices
steps.desc: Reset confirmed-compromised devices to a known-good state, or physically replace them if reset cannot be trusted.
steps.outcome: Devices restored to a clean state.

steps.title: Apply firmware update and restore devices once released
steps.desc: Update firmware fleet-wide once available, then return devices to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Fleet patched and restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review embedded-device monitoring coverage
steps.desc: Record the incident and assess whether visibility and segmentation for this device class need improvement.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32141.def: A confirmed or attributed nation-state (or nation-state-aligned) intrusion using two or more chained zero-day vulnerabilities to achieve initial access, privilege escalation, and/or sandbox escape against a specific, targeted victim.
ITID-32141.purpose: Captures use of a chained sequence of zero-day exploits as part of a targeted nation-state campaign.
scopeIncludes: A multi-stage zero-day exploit chain attributed to a nation-state or nation-state-aligned actor
Targeted (not opportunistic/mass) use of zero-days against a specific organization or individual
scopeExcludes: A single zero-day used opportunistically without nation-state attribution (see the specific platform/application leaf instead)
Zero-day acquired and used via a commercial exploit broker without confirmed nation-state operational control (ITID-32142)
Zero-day used specifically within confirmed mercenary spyware tooling (ITID-32143)
ITID-32141.severity: Critical; nation-state attribution implies sophisticated, well-resourced, and likely persistent adversary intent.
ITID-32141.priority: P1, immediate, with executive and legal/government-liaison notification.
ITID-32141.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command, executive leadership, legal, and relevant government/ISAC liaison channels.
indicators: Multiple distinct zero-day exploitation stages observed in a single intrusion timeline
Tradecraft (infrastructure, tooling, TTPs) consistent with a known or suspected APT group
Targeting pattern consistent with strategic/geopolitical rather than financial motive
vectors: Spearphishing or watering-hole delivery of the initial-stage zero-day
Chained exploitation moving from initial access zero-day to privilege-escalation zero-day
rootCauses: High-value target profile attracting well-resourced adversary investment in exploit development
Insufficient defense-in-depth to contain a determined, well-funded actor
controls: Threat-intelligence-driven hunting for known APT tradecraft
Executive/high-value-target protective monitoring program
Rapid cross-team incident response coordination
ITID-32141.detection: Low pre-disclosure; improves substantially with threat-intelligence sharing once any stage of the chain is publicly attributed.
ITID-32141.response: Full incident response with threat-intel-informed scoping, assume long-dwell-time persistence, and engage government/ISAC partners as appropriate.
metrics: Number of exploit-chain stages identified
Dwell time from initial access to detection
detections: Threat-intel IOC/TTP matching for known APT groups
ITID-32141.notes: Attribution to a nation-state actor and evidence of a multi-stage chain are the differentiators from single-exploit or broker/spyware-sourced siblings.

playbook.name: Response: Zero-Day Exploit Chain Used in Targeted Nation-State Campaign
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected use of a zero-day exploit chain as part of a targeted, sophisticated campaign attributed or suspected to be linked to a nation-state actor.

steps.title: Identify anomalous behavior indicative of a sophisticated multi-stage intrusion
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies across the exploit chain: initial access, privilege escalation, and persistence stages, given nation-state actors typically chain multiple novel techniques.
steps.guidance: Assume high operational sophistication; look for anti-forensic behavior and minimal footprint.
steps.outcome: Full exploit chain and affected host(s) identified.

steps.title: Preserve comprehensive forensic evidence with chain-of-custody
steps.desc: Capture memory, disk, and network evidence with strict chain-of-custody given likely legal/intelligence community interest.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and defensible.

steps.title: Assess targeting pattern and likely objective
steps.desc: Determine why this organization/individual was targeted (data of interest, access to third parties, geopolitical relevance) to inform scope and escalation.
steps.outcome: Targeting rationale assessed.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems without tipping off the actor prematurely
steps.desc: Contain compromised systems using methods that minimize signaling to the actor if broader investigation/monitoring is still needed, in coordination with leadership.
steps.guidance: Balance immediate containment against intelligence value of continued (monitored) access.
steps.outcome: Systems contained per an agreed strategy.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and legal/national authorities
steps.desc: Given the nation-state attribution, immediately escalate to executive leadership, legal counsel, and relevant national cybersecurity authorities (e.g., CISA/national CERT) per policy.
steps.outcome: Leadership and authorities briefed.

steps.title: Coordinate multi-vendor disclosure for each exploit in the chain
steps.desc: Report each zero-day in the chain to its respective vendor with forensic evidence to expedite fixes.
steps.outcome: All relevant vendors engaged.

steps.title: Rebuild all compromised systems and rotate all potentially exposed credentials
steps.desc: Rebuild affected systems from trusted media and rotate all credentials/secrets the actor may have accessed, given the sophistication of persistence techniques used.
steps.outcome: Environment rebuilt clean; credentials rotated.

steps.title: Restore systems and implement enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Return rebuilt, patched systems to service with heightened monitoring given the risk of re-targeting by a persistent, well-resourced actor.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with enhanced monitoring in place.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review with legal and executive stakeholders
steps.desc: Document the full campaign, attribution assessment, and strategic implications; review with legal and executive leadership.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and briefed to leadership.

ITID-32142.def: Exploitation of a zero-day vulnerability where the exploit itself was acquired via purchase from a commercial exploit-development/brokerage vendor, rather than developed by the using actor.
ITID-32142.purpose: Captures use of a zero-day acquired through a commercial exploit broker or vendor.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation attributed to an exploit purchased from a known commercial broker/vendor (e.g., an exploit-acquisition marketplace or vendor)
Cases where procurement/acquisition evidence (not just technical exploit characteristics) points to a commercial source
scopeExcludes: A zero-day chain developed and operated end-to-end by a nation-state's own capability (ITID-32141)
Zero-day used within confirmed mercenary spyware product deployment specifically (ITID-32143)
ITID-32142.escalation: Escalate to incident command and threat intelligence for broker/vendor attribution research; consider legal/policy engagement given commercial-exploit-market implications.
indicators: Exploit code/tooling matching known commercial broker product signatures
Threat-intel reporting linking the observed exploit to a specific brokerage vendor
vectors: Exploit deployed via the purchasing actor's own delivery infrastructure after acquisition
Combined use of a purchased exploit with off-the-shelf or custom implants
rootCauses: Existence of a commercial market that lowers the barrier to zero-day capability acquisition
Insufficient defenses against well-funded but not necessarily technically sophisticated actors
controls: Threat-intelligence tracking of known commercial exploit-broker tooling and infrastructure
Standard zero-day containment controls (isolation, patching, hunting)
ITID-32142.detection: Low-to-moderate; commercial broker exploits are sometimes reused across multiple customers, so cross-incident threat-intel correlation can surface patterns.
ITID-32142.response: Treat as a standard zero-day incident technically, while separately tracking the acquisition-source angle for threat-intelligence and policy reporting.
metrics: Number of incidents attributed to a specific known broker
Time from disclosure to patch
detections: Threat-intel signature matching for known broker tooling
ITID-32142.notes: The differentiator is the acquisition/procurement angle (commercially purchased exploit), not the technical exploitation mechanism, which is documented under the relevant platform/application leaf as well when both angles are known.

playbook.name: Response: Zero-Day Purchased from Commercial Exploit Broker/Vendor
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected use of a zero-day exploit sourced from a commercial exploit broker/vendor (rather than independently developed) against the organization.

steps.title: Identify anomalous behavior and characteristics consistent with commercial exploit tooling
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies; commercial broker exploit chains often show distinctive polish/modularity (clean anti-forensic behavior, professional-grade obfuscation) that can hint at their origin.
steps.outcome: Candidate host(s) and exploit characteristics identified.

steps.title: Preserve forensic evidence and engage threat intelligence for attribution
steps.desc: Capture forensic evidence and engage threat intelligence resources/vendors who track known commercial exploit brokers to aid attribution.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; attribution assessment underway.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems
steps.desc: Network-isolate confirmed-compromised systems to halt further exploitation.
steps.outcome: Compromised systems isolated.

steps.title: Assess whether targeting suggests use against a specific individual (spyware-style)
steps.desc: Determine whether the target profile (executive, journalist-adjacent role, legal/HR access) suggests deliberate targeted surveillance rather than opportunistic compromise, escalating to legal/executive review if so.
steps.outcome: Targeting assessment complete.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the affected software vendor
steps.desc: Report findings to the affected software vendor with forensic evidence to expedite a patch.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged and tracking the issue.

steps.title: Rebuild compromised systems and rotate exposed credentials
steps.desc: Rebuild affected systems from trusted media and rotate credentials the actor may have accessed.
steps.outcome: Environment rebuilt clean; credentials rotated.

steps.title: Restore systems and apply the vendor patch once released
steps.desc: Return rebuilt systems to service and apply the emergency patch fleet-wide as soon as it is available.
steps.outcome: Systems restored and patched.

steps.title: Document the incident and brief legal/executive leadership on the commercial spyware market threat
steps.desc: Record the incident, attribution assessment, and implications of commercial exploit markets for the organization's threat model.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and briefed.

ITID-32143.def: Exploitation of a zero-day vulnerability as part of a confirmed commercial mercenary spyware product (e.g., surveillance-ware sold to government or private clients) deployed against a specific individual or organization.
ITID-32143.purpose: Captures use of a zero-day within a confirmed commercial mercenary spyware product deployed against a target.
scopeIncludes: Zero-click or one-click exploit chain attributed to a known mercenary spyware product
Forensic confirmation (e.g., via mobile forensic toolkits) of spyware indicators tied to a zero-day exploit chain
scopeExcludes: A zero-day chain attributed to direct nation-state operational tooling rather than a commercial spyware product (ITID-32141)
Generic commercial exploit-broker use without spyware-product attribution (ITID-32142)
ITID-32143.severity: Critical; typically targets high-risk individuals (journalists, activists, executives, government officials) with sophisticated, hard-to-detect tooling.
ITID-32143.priority: P1, immediate, with careful handling given sensitive/high-profile targeting.
ITID-32143.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command, executive protection/legal, and specialist mobile-forensics support; consider notifying the individual's personal security team if targeting a specific person.
indicators: Mobile forensic artifacts matching known mercenary spyware indicators (e.g., process names, file paths, network infrastructure)
Zero-click exploitation via messaging or media-parsing components with no user interaction required
vectors: Zero-click exploit delivered via a messaging application
One-click exploit delivered via a malicious link sent to the target
rootCauses: High-value/high-risk individual profile attracting commercial surveillance targeting
Reliance on default mobile OS security posture without enhanced protections (e.g., Lockdown Mode) for at-risk individuals
controls: Mobile Lockdown Mode / enhanced protection settings for at-risk individuals
Mobile forensic monitoring (e.g., periodic MVT scans) for high-risk personnel
Threat-intel subscription for mercenary spyware indicators
ITID-32143.detection: Low; mercenary spyware is specifically engineered to evade standard EDR/MTD detection, requiring specialist forensic tooling.
ITID-32143.response: Engage specialist mobile forensics immediately, preserve the device without factory-resetting, and coordinate with the individual on physical/personal security implications.
metrics: Number of at-risk individuals enrolled in enhanced mobile protection
Time to forensic confirmation
detections: Mobile forensic artifact review (MVT) for known spyware indicators
ITID-32143.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32113/32114 (generic platform zero-days) by confirmed commercial spyware-product attribution and targeted, high-risk-individual context.

playbook.name: Response: Zero-Day Used in Mercenary Spyware Deployment
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected deployment of mercenary/commercial spyware (e.g., targeting a mobile device or messaging application) against an individual within the organization via a zero-day exploit.

steps.title: Identify anomalous device/application behavior consistent with spyware implantation
steps.desc: Hunt for indicators such as zero-click message artifacts, unexpected process activity in messaging apps, unusual data/battery usage, or configuration profile anomalies on the targeted individual's device(s).
steps.guidance: Use specialized mobile forensic tooling designed to detect known spyware families where available.
steps.outcome: Confirmed or suspected spyware implant identified.
steps.tool: Mobile Verification Toolkit (MVT) / mobile threat defense / MDM

steps.title: Preserve device forensic evidence without tipping off the operator
steps.desc: Capture a full device forensic image/sysdiagnose discreetly, avoiding actions (factory reset, obvious security app installs) that could alert the spyware operator before evidence is secured.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved.

steps.title: Immediately escalate to executive leadership and legal counsel
steps.desc: Given the targeted, high-sophistication nature of mercenary spyware, escalate immediately to executive leadership and legal counsel — the target is likely a high-value individual and legal/reputational/safety implications may follow.
steps.outcome: Leadership and legal briefed.

steps.title: Isolate the device from corporate resources
steps.desc: Revoke the device's access to corporate accounts, VPN, and email while investigation proceeds.
steps.outcome: Device isolated from corporate resources.

steps.title: Advise the individual on personal safety and communication precautions
steps.desc: Brief the targeted individual (with legal/HR involvement) on communication hygiene and personal safety considerations, given spyware of this class often targets individuals for surveillance beyond corporate espionage.
steps.outcome: Individual briefed and supported.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the platform vendor and specialist researchers
steps.desc: Report findings to the affected platform vendor (e.g., Apple, WhatsApp) and, where appropriate, specialist digital-rights/forensic organizations that track mercenary spyware.
steps.outcome: Vendor and specialists engaged.

steps.title: Factory-reset and re-provision the device from a trusted baseline
steps.desc: Wipe and re-provision the device once forensic evidence collection is complete.
steps.outcome: Device restored to a clean state.

steps.title: Return the device to the individual with the platform patch applied
steps.desc: Restore the re-provisioned, patched device to the individual once the vendor's fix is confirmed installed.
steps.outcome: Device restored.

steps.title: Conduct an executive/legal post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the incident and review with legal and executive leadership, including any notification obligations and whether additional protective measures are warranted for high-risk individuals.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and briefed to leadership.

ITID-32144.def: An incident involving zero-day exploitation attributed to a sophisticated/advanced threat actor, not clearly matching a more specific advanced-threat-category leaf.
ITID-32144.purpose: Catch-all for advanced-threat zero-day exploitation that does not fit nation-state campaign, broker-purchased, or mercenary-spyware leaves.
scopeIncludes: Advanced zero-day exploitation of unclear sourcing/attribution (nation-state vs. broker vs. spyware not yet determined)
Cases logged before attribution research is complete
scopeExcludes: Any case where the advanced-threat category (nation-state campaign, commercial broker, mercenary spyware) is confirmed — reclassify to the matching sibling leaf
ITID-32144.priority: P1 by default given zero-day and advanced-threat context.
ITID-32144.escalation: Escalate immediately; reclassify once attribution research clarifies the specific category.
indicators: Sophisticated exploitation tradecraft with unclear attribution
vectors: Activity of unclear specific advanced-threat vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail/attribution captured at time of detection
controls: Threat-intelligence-driven hunting pending attribution
ITID-32144.detection: Same general telemetry gaps as sibling zero-day leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32144.response: Investigate and reclassify to a category-specific leaf once attribution is confirmed.
metrics: Count pending attribution/reclassification
ITID-32144.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Advanced Threat Zero-Day Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected use of a zero-day exploit by an advanced/sophisticated threat actor not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Identify anomalous behavior indicative of sophisticated intrusion
steps.desc: Hunt for behavioral anomalies across the intrusion lifecycle, given advanced actors typically use novel techniques with minimal footprint and no available signature.
steps.outcome: Affected host(s) and anomalous activity identified.

steps.title: Preserve comprehensive forensic evidence
steps.desc: Capture memory, disk, and network evidence with proper chain-of-custody given the likely sophistication and possible legal interest.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems
steps.desc: Network-isolate compromised systems while balancing intelligence value of continued monitored access, in coordination with leadership.
steps.outcome: Systems contained per an agreed strategy.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership
steps.desc: Brief executive leadership given the advanced nature of the actor and potential broader implications.
steps.outcome: Leadership briefed.

steps.title: Coordinate disclosure with the affected vendor(s)
steps.desc: Report findings to the relevant software/hardware vendor(s) with forensic evidence to expedite fixes.
steps.outcome: Vendor(s) engaged.

steps.title: Rebuild compromised systems and rotate exposed credentials
steps.desc: Rebuild affected systems from trusted media and rotate all potentially exposed credentials/secrets.
steps.outcome: Environment rebuilt clean; credentials rotated.

steps.title: Restore systems with enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Return rebuilt, patched systems to service with heightened monitoring given the risk of re-targeting.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with enhanced monitoring.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the incident, attribution assessment (if any), and strategic implications for the organization's threat model.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32211.def: Remote exploitation of a publicly known RDP-related CVE (e.g., a remote code execution or authentication flaw in the RDP service) against a system for which a vendor patch was available but not applied.
ITID-32211.purpose: Captures remote exploitation of a known, patchable RDP vulnerability on a system that was not patched.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a known-CVE RDP service vulnerability where a patch existed at time of exploitation
RDP-exposed system compromised via an unpatched, publicly disclosed flaw
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a protocol-level flaw that bypasses Network Level Authentication regardless of patch status (ITID-32212)
Exploitation of RDP gateway/broker software specifically, as opposed to the RDP service itself (ITID-32213)
RDP compromise via credential-based access (brute force/valid accounts) with no vulnerability exploited — tracked under a credential-access ITID elsewhere
ITID-32211.severity: High; RDP compromise typically yields direct interactive remote access.
ITID-32211.priority: P1 if internet-facing and unpatched at time of exploitation, else P2.
ITID-32211.escalation: Escalate to incident command; treat as an active intrusion path requiring immediate isolation of the exposed host.
indicators: RDP service crash preceding unauthorized session establishment
EDR/IDS signature match for a known RDP CVE exploit (e.g., BlueKeep-class patterns)
Unexpected interactive logon session with no corresponding valid credential use
vectors: Direct exploitation of an internet-exposed RDP port (3389) running an unpatched service version
Exploitation reached via internal lateral movement to an unpatched internal RDP host
rootCauses: Missing patch management/vulnerability remediation SLA compliance
RDP exposed directly to the internet without a gateway or VPN in front of it
mitreTechniques: T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
controls: Patch management SLA enforcement for RDP-hosting systems
Placing RDP behind a VPN/gateway rather than direct internet exposure
Network Level Authentication (NLA) enforcement
ITID-32211.detection: Moderate-high; known-CVE exploitation typically has published IDS/EDR signatures once disclosed.
ITID-32211.response: Isolate the host, apply the missing patch, and hunt for lateral movement originating from the compromised RDP host.
metrics: Number of RDP hosts exceeding patch SLA
Time from patch availability to exploitation (patch gap)
detections: IDS/EDR signatures for known RDP CVEs
ITID-32211.notes: Scoped specifically to known-CVE, patch-available exploitation; protocol-level NLA-bypass and gateway/broker-specific exploitation are tracked under sibling leaves.

playbook.name: Response: Known-CVE RDP Vulnerability Exploitation (Unpatched System)
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a known, documented RDP vulnerability against an unpatched system exposing Remote Desktop Protocol.

steps.title: Confirm the exploited CVE and affected host(s) via RDP/event logs
steps.desc: Correlate RDP connection logs, Windows Security event logs (4624/4625/4648), and EDR/IDS alerts against the known CVE to confirm which hosts were exploited.
steps.outcome: Confirmed CVE and affected host list.
steps.tool: Windows Event Logs / EDR / network IDS

steps.title: Check whether RDP was internet-facing without compensating controls
steps.desc: Determine whether the exposed RDP service was directly reachable from the internet without network-level authentication (NLA), VPN, or MFA — a common root cause for this exploit class.
steps.outcome: Exposure configuration documented for root-cause analysis.
steps.tool: Firewall rule review / external attack surface scan

steps.title: Isolate affected hosts and restrict RDP exposure
steps.desc: Network-isolate confirmed-compromised hosts and immediately restrict or disable internet-facing RDP access organization-wide as an emergency measure.
steps.outcome: Further exploitation halted; RDP exposure minimized.

steps.title: Force credential rotation for accounts used on affected hosts
steps.desc: Rotate passwords for any accounts that authenticated to or were accessible from the compromised host(s).
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Patch the vulnerability on all affected/at-risk systems
steps.desc: Apply the vendor security patch fixing this CVE across all systems exposing RDP on an emergency basis.
steps.outcome: Patch applied fleet-wide.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence delivered by the exploit
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts of any dropped malware or persistence mechanism.
steps.outcome: Hosts confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore hosts with NLA, MFA, and VPN-gated RDP access enforced
steps.desc: Return patched, verified-clean hosts to service, ensuring RDP is only reachable via VPN with MFA and NLA enabled going forward.
steps.outcome: Hosts restored with hardened access controls.

steps.title: Document the incident and review remote access exposure policy
steps.desc: Record why RDP was exposed without compensating controls and recommend policy changes to prevent direct internet exposure of remote access services.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32212.def: Exploitation of a flaw in the RDP protocol or its implementation that allows an attacker to bypass Network Level Authentication (NLA) and reach the RDP session/logon stage without valid credentials.
ITID-32212.purpose: Captures exploitation of an RDP protocol-level flaw that bypasses Network Level Authentication.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation that circumvents NLA's pre-authentication requirement
Protocol-downgrade or implementation-flaw attacks against the RDP handshake itself
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a known-CVE RDP service defect unrelated to NLA bypass (ITID-32211)
Exploitation of RDP gateway/broker software (ITID-32213)
ITID-32212.severity: High-Critical; NLA is a primary compensating control for RDP exposure, so bypassing it removes a key defense layer.
ITID-32212.escalation: Escalate immediately; treat NLA as compromised as a control and reassess all RDP exposure relying on it.
indicators: RDP connection reaching the logon screen despite NLA being enabled and enforced
Protocol-level anomaly in RDP handshake captured via network monitoring
vectors: Protocol downgrade forcing a weaker authentication negotiation
Exploitation of an implementation-specific flaw in the NLA/CredSSP negotiation
rootCauses: CredSSP/NLA implementation defects
Legacy RDP client/server versions still permitting downgrade negotiation
controls: Enforce minimum RDP/CredSSP protocol versions (disable downgrade negotiation)
Layer RDP access behind an additional authentication factor beyond NLA (VPN + MFA)
ITID-32212.detection: Low-moderate; requires network-level protocol inspection to distinguish from normal NLA-protected sessions.
ITID-32212.response: Isolate affected hosts, disable RDP exposure pending mitigation, and verify no other systems share the vulnerable implementation.
metrics: Number of RDP hosts using outdated protocol versions permitting downgrade
detections: Network protocol inspection for RDP handshake anomalies
ITID-32212.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32211 by targeting the authentication/protocol layer itself rather than the RDP service's general code.

playbook.name: Response: RDP Protocol-Level Exploit Bypassing Network Level Authentication
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of an RDP protocol-level vulnerability that bypasses Network Level Authentication (NLA), allowing pre-authentication compromise.

steps.title: Confirm NLA bypass and affected host(s) via RDP/EDR logs
steps.desc: Review RDP connection sequencing and EDR telemetry to confirm the exploit achieved code execution or session access prior to successful NLA authentication.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploit method and affected host list.
steps.tool: EDR / Windows Event Logs / network capture

steps.title: Assess whether internet-facing exposure enabled the attack
steps.desc: Determine whether the affected RDP service was reachable from the internet without VPN gating, as this is a key root-cause consideration for pre-authentication exploits.
steps.outcome: Exposure configuration documented.

steps.title: Disable or restrict RDP access immediately
steps.desc: Disable RDP on affected hosts or restrict it to VPN-only access as an emergency compensating control, since NLA itself cannot be relied upon.
steps.outcome: Exploitation vector removed.

steps.title: Isolate confirmed-compromised hosts
steps.desc: Network-isolate any host with confirmed post-exploitation activity.
steps.outcome: Compromised hosts isolated.

steps.title: Apply the vendor patch addressing the protocol-level flaw
steps.desc: Deploy the security update fixing the underlying RDP protocol vulnerability across all affected systems.
steps.outcome: Patch applied fleet-wide.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence delivered by the exploit
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts of dropped malware or persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: Hosts confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore RDP access behind VPN with MFA enforced
steps.desc: Re-enable RDP only for VPN-connected, MFA-authenticated sessions once systems are patched and verified clean.
steps.outcome: Hosts restored with hardened access controls.

steps.title: Document the incident and reassess reliance on NLA as a sole control
steps.desc: Record the finding that NLA alone was insufficient and recommend defense-in-depth (VPN gating, MFA) for all remote access services.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32213.def: Exploitation of a vulnerability in RDP gateway, connection-broker, or session-management software (the internet-facing intermediary that brokers RDP sessions) to gain unauthorized access or code execution.
ITID-32213.purpose: Captures exploitation of RDP gateway or connection-broker software rather than the RDP endpoint itself.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of an RDP gateway/broker product's web-facing or session-management component
Vulnerability in the intermediary system that fronts RDP access for an organization
scopeExcludes: Direct exploitation of the RDP service on the target endpoint itself (ITID-32211, ITID-32212)
ITID-32213.severity: Critical; gateway compromise typically grants access to the entire pool of systems it brokers.
ITID-32213.escalation: Escalate immediately; treat as compromise of a centralized access-control point requiring fleet-wide credential rotation review.
indicators: Anomalous administrative activity on the RDP gateway/broker appliance
Unexpected session-broker log entries for users/hosts with no corresponding legitimate request
Gateway process crash preceding unauthorized access
vectors: Exploitation of the gateway's internet-facing web-management or authentication component
Exploitation of a session-broker API vulnerability
rootCauses: Gateway/broker software patch lag
Gateway management interface exposed beyond what is operationally necessary
controls: Restrict gateway management interface exposure
Patch management SLA specific to gateway/broker software
Segregation of the gateway from the broader internal network
ITID-32213.detection: Moderate once a public advisory exists for the gateway product; low pre-disclosure.
ITID-32213.response: Isolate the gateway, assume compromise of all sessions it brokered, rotate credentials/certificates, and apply vendor patch.
metrics: Time from gateway vendor advisory to patch
Number of sessions/hosts potentially exposed via the gateway
ITID-32213.notes: Scoped to the intermediary gateway/broker layer specifically, distinct from direct RDP endpoint exploitation covered by ITID-32211/32212.

playbook.name: Response: RDP Gateway/Broker Software Vulnerability Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a vulnerability in RDP gateway or connection broker software (e.g., Remote Desktop Gateway, third-party RDP brokers) that mediates remote desktop access.

steps.title: Confirm the exploited vulnerability and affected gateway/broker instance
steps.desc: Review gateway/broker application logs and EDR/IDS alerts to confirm exploitation and identify the specific instance(s) affected.
steps.outcome: Confirmed vulnerability and affected instance(s).

steps.title: Determine downstream session/host exposure
steps.desc: Since the gateway mediates access to multiple internal hosts, identify every backend host and session the compromised gateway had access to.
steps.outcome: Full downstream exposure list established.

steps.title: Take the gateway/broker offline or fail over
steps.desc: Remove the affected gateway/broker from production traffic flow, failing over to a redundant instance if available, to prevent further exploitation.
steps.outcome: Malicious access path removed.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and terminate active sessions for all downstream hosts
steps.desc: Force logoff of all active RDP sessions brokered through the compromised gateway and rotate credentials for affected accounts.
steps.outcome: Potentially compromised sessions terminated; credentials invalidated.
steps.tool: Identity provider / Remote Desktop Session Host management

steps.title: Patch the gateway/broker software
steps.desc: Apply the vendor security patch fixing the vulnerability to the gateway/broker software.
steps.outcome: Patch applied.

steps.title: Investigate and remediate downstream hosts for compromise
steps.desc: Check every backend host reachable through the compromised gateway for signs of unauthorized access or lateral movement.
steps.outcome: Downstream hosts confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the gateway to service with hardened configuration
steps.desc: Return the patched gateway/broker to production with MFA and NLA enforced for all brokered sessions.
steps.outcome: Gateway restored with hardened access controls.

steps.title: Document the incident and review gateway architecture resilience
steps.desc: Record the incident and assess whether redundancy and patch cadence for gateway/broker infrastructure need improvement given its centralized access role.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32214.def: An incident involving remote exploitation of RDP, not clearly matching a more specific RDP-exploit leaf.
ITID-32214.purpose: Catch-all for RDP exploitation that does not fit known-CVE, NLA-bypass, or gateway/broker leaves.
scopeIncludes: RDP exploitation of unclear specific mechanism
Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling RDP leaf
ITID-32214.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending classification.
ITID-32214.priority: P2 by default, escalate to P1 if internet-facing.
ITID-32214.escalation: Reclassify once the specific exploitation mechanism is clarified.
indicators: RDP-related alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific RDP vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32214.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32214.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32214.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General RDP Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of an RDP-related vulnerability not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the exploit and affected host(s) via RDP/EDR logs
steps.desc: Correlate RDP connection logs, Windows Security event logs, and EDR/IDS alerts to confirm exploitation and identify affected host(s).
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploit and affected host list.
steps.tool: Windows Event Logs / EDR / network IDS

steps.title: Check whether RDP was internet-facing without compensating controls
steps.desc: Determine whether the exposed RDP service was reachable from the internet without network-level authentication, VPN, or MFA.
steps.outcome: Exposure configuration documented.

steps.title: Isolate affected hosts and restrict RDP exposure
steps.desc: Network-isolate confirmed-compromised hosts and restrict internet-facing RDP access as an emergency measure.
steps.outcome: Further exploitation halted.

steps.title: Force credential rotation for exposed accounts
steps.desc: Rotate passwords for accounts accessible from the compromised host(s).
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Patch or reconfigure the vulnerable RDP component
steps.desc: Apply the applicable vendor patch or configuration fix addressing the vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence delivered by the exploit
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts of dropped malware or persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: Hosts confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore hosts with hardened RDP access controls
steps.desc: Return patched, verified-clean hosts to service with VPN gating, MFA, and NLA enforced.
steps.outcome: Hosts restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review remote access exposure policy
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend policy changes preventing direct internet exposure of remote access services.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32221.def: Remote exploitation of a publicly known CVE in a VPN gateway/concentrator appliance for which a vendor patch was available but not applied.
ITID-32221.purpose: Captures remote exploitation of a known, patchable VPN gateway vulnerability on an unpatched appliance.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a known-CVE VPN appliance vulnerability where a patch existed at time of exploitation
scopeExcludes: Zero-day exploitation of a VPN/network appliance with no patch available (ITID-32133)
VPN authentication-bypass exploitation not tied to a specific known-CVE patch gap (ITID-32222)
VPN session/token exploitation not involving a patchable appliance vulnerability (ITID-32223)
ITID-32221.severity: Critical; VPN gateways sit at the network perimeter and typically grant broad internal access once compromised.
ITID-32221.escalation: Escalate immediately; assume full appliance compromise and potential internal network access.
indicators: Appliance log gap or tampering consistent with known exploitation tooling for the CVE
Unexpected configuration or account changes on the VPN gateway
Outbound connections from the appliance itself inconsistent with normal operation
vectors: Direct exploitation of the internet-facing VPN gateway's known vulnerable component
Exploitation via a publicly available proof-of-concept for the CVE
rootCauses: Missed patch management SLA for perimeter/VPN appliances
Delayed emergency patching despite active-exploitation advisories
controls: Expedited emergency-patch process for perimeter VPN appliances
Network segmentation limiting blast radius from a compromised VPN gateway
Credential rotation and re-issuance of certificates post-compromise
ITID-32221.detection: Moderate-high once public advisory/IOCs exist; many VPN CVEs have published detection signatures given their high-value target status.
ITID-32221.response: Isolate and rebuild the appliance from trusted firmware, rotate all credentials/certificates it held, patch, and hunt for lateral movement.
metrics: Number of VPN appliances exceeding patch SLA
Time from patch availability to exploitation
detections: Vendor/IDS signatures for known VPN CVEs
ITID-32221.notes: Cross-references ITID-32133 (zero-day network appliance exploitation): this leaf applies only when a patch was available and not applied at time of exploitation.

playbook.name: Response: Known-CVE VPN Gateway Vulnerability Exploitation (Unpatched Appliance)
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a known, documented vulnerability in a VPN gateway appliance that had not been patched.

steps.title: Confirm the exploited CVE and affected appliance
steps.desc: Correlate VPN appliance logs, authentication logs, and EDR/IDS alerts against the known CVE to confirm exploitation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed CVE and affected appliance(s).
steps.tool: VPN appliance logs / SIEM / network IDS

steps.title: Check whether the appliance lacked MFA/network-level compensating controls
steps.desc: Determine whether the exposed VPN gateway required only single-factor authentication and had no additional network-level restrictions — a common root cause for this exploit class.
steps.outcome: Exposure/authentication configuration documented for root-cause analysis.

steps.title: Assess scope of downstream network access granted by the appliance
steps.desc: Since VPN compromise grants internal network access, determine the full scope of internal resources reachable through the compromised gateway.
steps.outcome: Downstream exposure scope established.

steps.title: Take the appliance offline or restrict to emergency access only
