steps.desc: Disable the affected VPN gateway or restrict it to break-glass emergency access while investigation and patching proceed.
steps.outcome: Exploitation vector removed.
steps.abort: Coordinate downtime with business stakeholders needing remote access.

steps.title: Force credential and session rotation for all VPN users
steps.desc: Terminate all active VPN sessions and rotate credentials for all users of the compromised gateway.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed sessions and credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Patch the VPN appliance
steps.desc: Apply the vendor's emergency security patch fixing the CVE.
steps.outcome: Patch applied.

steps.title: Investigate internal network for lateral movement from the compromised gateway
steps.desc: Check internal hosts reachable through the compromised VPN for signs of unauthorized access.
steps.outcome: Internal environment confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore VPN access with MFA enforced
steps.desc: Return the patched gateway to service, enforcing MFA for all VPN authentication going forward.
steps.outcome: Gateway restored with hardened access controls.

steps.title: Document the incident and review VPN patch-management SLA
steps.desc: Record why the patch was not applied before exploitation and recommend faster emergency-patch processes for internet-facing VPN infrastructure, plus mandatory MFA policy.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32222.def: Exploitation of a vulnerability that allows an attacker to bypass VPN authentication entirely (e.g., via a logic flaw, default-credential-adjacent flaw, or authentication-check omission) rather than exploiting memory-safety code execution.
ITID-32222.purpose: Captures exploitation of a VPN authentication-bypass vulnerability.
scopeIncludes: Authentication-check bypass allowing VPN session establishment without valid credentials
Logic-flaw exploitation in the VPN's authentication workflow
scopeExcludes: Memory-safety/code-execution exploitation of the VPN gateway generally (ITID-32221)
Session/token-based exploitation after authentication has already occurred (ITID-32223)
ITID-32222.escalation: Escalate immediately; force re-authentication of all active sessions and review for unauthorized access granted via the bypass.
indicators: Successful VPN session establishment with no corresponding valid authentication log entry
Anomalous authentication log gaps around the time of the bypass
vectors: Direct exploitation of the authentication-bypass logic flaw against the internet-facing VPN portal
rootCauses: Authentication logic flaw in vendor code (e.g., improper handling of a specific request parameter)
Insufficient vendor security testing of the authentication workflow
controls: Emergency patch deployment for known authentication-bypass CVEs
Multi-factor authentication layered in front of/independent from the vulnerable component where feasible
Session anomaly monitoring correlating VPN sessions to authentication logs
ITID-32222.detection: Moderate once public advisory exists; look for VPN sessions with no matching authentication log entry.
ITID-32222.response: Force logout of all sessions, patch immediately, and audit access performed during the exposure window.
metrics: Number of sessions established without matching authentication logs during exposure window
ITID-32222.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32221 by the specific mechanism (authentication logic bypass, not general code execution) and from ITID-32223 by occurring pre-authentication rather than against an already-issued session/token.

playbook.name: Response: VPN Authentication Bypass Vulnerability Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a vulnerability allowing an attacker to bypass VPN authentication entirely.

steps.title: Confirm the authentication bypass and affected sessions
steps.desc: Review VPN authentication logs for sessions established without a corresponding successful authentication event, correlating with the known bypass technique.
steps.outcome: Confirmed bypass instances and affected accounts/sessions.

steps.title: Check whether the VPN was internet-facing without MFA as a compensating control
steps.desc: Determine whether MFA was enforced independently of the bypassed authentication mechanism, which could have limited impact.
steps.outcome: Compensating control gap documented.

steps.title: Disable the vulnerable authentication path
steps.desc: Disable or restrict the specific authentication mechanism/endpoint that allows the bypass while a fix is developed.
steps.outcome: Bypass vector closed.

steps.title: Terminate all active sessions and force re-authentication
steps.desc: Terminate all current VPN sessions and require all users to re-authenticate under hardened conditions.
steps.outcome: Potentially unauthorized sessions terminated.

steps.title: Patch the VPN software/appliance
steps.desc: Apply the vendor's fix addressing the authentication bypass.
steps.outcome: Patch applied.

steps.title: Investigate internal network for unauthorized access resulting from the bypass
steps.desc: Check internal hosts and accounts for signs of unauthorized activity originating from bypassed sessions.
steps.outcome: Internal environment confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore VPN access with MFA mandatory and independent of the patched mechanism
steps.desc: Return the patched VPN to service, ensuring MFA is enforced as a layered control independent of any single authentication mechanism.
steps.outcome: VPN restored with hardened, layered access controls.

steps.title: Document the incident and review authentication architecture for single points of failure
steps.desc: Record the incident and assess whether authentication relies on a single control that, if bypassed, grants full access.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32223.def: Exploitation of a flaw in how a VPN gateway issues, validates, or manages session tokens (e.g., session fixation, predictable token generation, improper token invalidation) to hijack or reuse a session without ever possessing valid credentials.
ITID-32223.purpose: Captures exploitation of a VPN session or token handling vulnerability that does not involve stealing or guessing credentials.
scopeIncludes: Session fixation or session-token prediction against a VPN gateway
Reuse of an improperly invalidated VPN session token
scopeExcludes: Authentication-bypass exploitation occurring before any session/token is issued (ITID-32222)
Credential theft/phishing-based session takeover (tracked under a credential-access ITID elsewhere)
ITID-32223.severity: High-Critical, depending on the privilege level of the hijacked session.
ITID-32223.escalation: Escalate immediately; invalidate all active sessions and review the token-generation/validation implementation.
indicators: Same session token observed in use from two geographically inconsistent source IPs
Token reuse after an expected invalidation event (e.g., password change, logout)
vectors: Prediction or brute-forcing of a weakly-random session token
Reuse of a token that was not properly invalidated after logout or timeout
rootCauses: Weak session-token entropy/generation in vendor code
Improper session-invalidation logic on logout/timeout
mitreTechniques: T1550.001 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token
controls: Strong cryptographically random session-token generation
Strict session-invalidation enforcement on logout/timeout/password change
Session anomaly detection (impossible-travel / concurrent-session alerting)
ITID-32223.detection: Moderate; impossible-travel and concurrent-session detection on VPN sessions can surface token reuse.
ITID-32223.response: Force invalidation of all active sessions, patch the token-handling defect, and audit access performed via the hijacked session.
metrics: Number of concurrent-session anomalies detected on VPN infrastructure
ITID-32223.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32222 by occurring against an already-issued session/token rather than the pre-authentication check, and explicitly excludes credential-based takeover.

playbook.name: Response: VPN Session/Token Vulnerability Exploitation (Non-Credential-Based)
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a vulnerability in VPN session handling or token management (e.g., session fixation, token replay, insufficient session expiry) that does not involve stolen credentials.

steps.title: Confirm the session/token exploitation technique and affected sessions
steps.desc: Review VPN session logs for anomalies such as reused/replayed session tokens, session continuation from unexpected source IPs, or sessions outliving normal expiry.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation technique and affected session(s).

steps.title: Identify the legitimate user(s) whose sessions were hijacked/replayed
steps.desc: Determine which legitimate accounts had sessions affected, to scope notification and further investigation.
steps.outcome: Affected user accounts identified.

steps.title: Invalidate all active sessions and tokens
steps.desc: Force termination of all active VPN sessions and invalidate outstanding session tokens organization-wide.
steps.outcome: Exploitable sessions/tokens invalidated.

steps.title: Restrict the vulnerable session-handling mechanism
steps.desc: Apply an interim configuration change (shorter session expiry, IP-binding, disabling the vulnerable feature) while a permanent fix is developed.
steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced.

steps.title: Patch the VPN software addressing the session/token flaw
steps.desc: Apply the vendor's fix correcting the session/token handling vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Patch applied.

steps.title: Investigate for unauthorized activity under hijacked sessions
steps.desc: Review activity conducted under affected sessions/tokens for signs of unauthorized data access or changes.
steps.outcome: Scope of unauthorized activity established and remediated.

steps.title: Restore VPN access with hardened session management
steps.desc: Return the patched VPN to service with shortened session lifetimes and additional session-binding controls.
steps.outcome: VPN restored with hardened session controls.

steps.title: Document the incident and notify affected users
steps.desc: Record the incident, notify users whose sessions were affected, and review session-management design across remote access infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and users notified.

ITID-32224.def: An incident involving remote exploitation of VPN infrastructure, not clearly matching a more specific VPN-exploit leaf.
ITID-32224.purpose: Catch-all for VPN exploitation that does not fit known-CVE, authentication-bypass, or session/token leaves.
scopeIncludes: VPN exploitation of unclear specific mechanism
Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling VPN leaf
ITID-32224.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Critical pending classification given perimeter exposure.
ITID-32224.escalation: Reclassify once the specific exploitation mechanism is clarified.
indicators: VPN-related alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific VPN vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32224.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32224.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32224.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General VPN Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a VPN-related vulnerability not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the exploit and affected appliance/sessions
steps.desc: Correlate VPN logs and EDR/IDS alerts to confirm exploitation and identify affected appliance(s) and session(s).
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploit and affected scope.

steps.title: Check whether the exposed access point lacked MFA/compensating controls
steps.desc: Determine whether the VPN was internet-facing without MFA or other compensating controls as a root-cause consideration.
steps.outcome: Exposure configuration documented.

steps.title: Restrict or disable the affected VPN service
steps.desc: Take the affected VPN gateway offline or restrict access while the vulnerability is addressed.
steps.outcome: Exploitation vector removed.

steps.title: Terminate active sessions and rotate credentials
steps.desc: Force logoff of active sessions and rotate credentials for affected accounts.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed sessions/credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Patch or reconfigure the vulnerable VPN component
steps.desc: Apply the applicable vendor patch or configuration fix.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated.

steps.title: Investigate internal network for downstream compromise
steps.desc: Check internal hosts reachable through the compromised VPN for signs of unauthorized access.
steps.outcome: Internal environment confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore VPN access with MFA enforced
steps.desc: Return the patched VPN to service, enforcing MFA for all authentication going forward.
steps.outcome: VPN restored with hardened access controls.

steps.title: Document the incident and review VPN exposure policy
steps.desc: Record findings and recommend policy changes for internet-facing VPN infrastructure, including mandatory MFA.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32231.def: Remote exploitation of a publicly known CVE in web server software (e.g., the HTTP server daemon or its modules) for which a vendor/project patch was available but not applied.
ITID-32231.purpose: Captures remote exploitation of a known, patchable web server software vulnerability on an unpatched server.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a known-CVE web server daemon or module vulnerability where a patch existed at time of exploitation
scopeExcludes: WAF bypass techniques used to reach an otherwise-mitigated vulnerability (ITID-32232)
Server-Side Request Forgery specifically (ITID-32233)
Directory traversal/path manipulation specifically (ITID-32234)
ITID-32231.priority: P1 if internet-facing and unpatched, else P2.
ITID-32231.escalation: Escalate to incident command; isolate the affected server pending patch.
indicators: Web server process crash or unexpected child-process spawn (e.g., web shell drop)
IDS/WAF signature match for a known web-server CVE exploit
vectors: Direct exploitation of an internet-facing web server's known vulnerable component or module
rootCauses: Missed patch management SLA for internet-facing web infrastructure
Delayed patching despite active-exploitation advisories
controls: Patch management SLA enforcement for internet-facing web servers
Web application firewall virtual-patching pending permanent fix
Web shell detection tooling
ITID-32231.response: Isolate the server, hunt for web shells/persistence, patch, and review logs for the exploitation window.
metrics: Number of web servers exceeding patch SLA
Time from patch availability to exploitation
detections: IDS/WAF signatures for known web-server CVEs
ITID-32231.notes: Scoped to known-CVE server-software defects generally; SSRF and directory traversal are broken out as their own leaves given their distinct exploitation mechanism and detection profile.

playbook.name: Response: Known-CVE Web Server Software Vulnerability Exploitation (Unpatched)
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a known, documented vulnerability in web server software (e.g., Apache, IIS, nginx) that had not been patched.

steps.title: Confirm the exploited CVE and affected server(s) via web server logs
steps.desc: Correlate web server access/error logs, WAF alerts, and EDR telemetry against the known CVE to confirm exploitation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed CVE and affected server(s).

steps.title: Determine whether the server was internet-facing without compensating controls
steps.desc: Confirm the server's internet exposure and whether a WAF or other compensating control was in place ahead of patching.
steps.outcome: Exposure configuration documented for root-cause analysis.

steps.title: Isolate or take the affected server offline
steps.desc: Remove the affected server from production traffic or isolate it from the network to halt active exploitation.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.
steps.abort: Coordinate with business owners on service impact.

steps.title: Deploy a virtual patch/WAF rule as an interim control
steps.desc: Apply a WAF rule targeting the specific exploitation pattern while the official patch is applied.
steps.outcome: Interim risk reduction in place.

steps.title: Patch the web server software
steps.desc: Apply the vendor security patch fixing the CVE on an emergency basis.
steps.outcome: Patch applied.

steps.title: Remove any web shell or persistence delivered by the exploit
steps.desc: Scan and clean the server of any web shells, backdoors, or unauthorized file modifications resulting from exploitation.
steps.outcome: Server confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the server to production after verification
steps.desc: Return the patched, verified-clean server to production traffic.
steps.outcome: Server restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review patch-management SLA for internet-facing servers
steps.desc: Record why the patch wasn't applied before exploitation and recommend a faster emergency-patch process for internet-facing web infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32232.def: Use of an evasion or obfuscation technique to bypass web application firewall (WAF) filtering rules, allowing an otherwise-blocked exploitation attempt to reach the underlying vulnerable web server or application.
ITID-32232.purpose: Captures successful bypass of a web application firewall to reach an underlying vulnerability.
scopeIncludes: Payload obfuscation/encoding specifically crafted to evade known WAF signature rules
Exploitation confirmed to have bypassed an active WAF rule that should have blocked it
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a web server vulnerability where no WAF was in place or engaged (ITID-32231)
ITID-32232.severity: High; WAF bypass indicates a compensating control failure in addition to the underlying vulnerability.
ITID-32232.escalation: Escalate to incident command and the WAF rule-management team to close the evasion gap.
indicators: Malicious request pattern reaching the origin server despite an active WAF rule intended to block it
WAF logs showing a request classified as benign that later correlates with exploitation
vectors: Encoding/obfuscation of exploit payloads (e.g., alternate encodings, case manipulation, comment injection)
HTTP request smuggling used to desynchronize WAF and origin server parsing
rootCauses: WAF signature rules not covering known evasion/obfuscation variants
Parsing inconsistency between the WAF and the origin web server
controls: Regular WAF rule-set tuning against known evasion techniques
Consistent HTTP parsing configuration between WAF and origin server (to prevent smuggling)
Positive-security-model (allowlist) WAF rules where feasible
ITID-32232.detection: Moderate; requires correlating WAF logs with origin server logs to spot requests that should have been blocked.
ITID-32232.response: Patch the underlying vulnerability, update WAF rules to close the evasion gap, and audit for other requests using the same evasion pattern.
metrics: Number of WAF bypass events detected
WAF rule coverage gap closure time
ITID-32232.notes: This leaf tracks the WAF-evasion angle specifically; the underlying server/application vulnerability being exploited is the same class of issue as ITID-32231 but the compensating-control failure is the focus here.

playbook.name: Response: Web Application Firewall (WAF) Bypass Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a technique that bypasses Web Application Firewall (WAF) protections to deliver a malicious payload to the underlying web application.

steps.title: Confirm the WAF bypass technique and affected requests
steps.desc: Review WAF logs alongside backend application logs to identify requests that should have been blocked but reached the application, confirming the bypass technique used.
steps.outcome: Confirmed bypass technique and affected request/host list.

steps.title: Assess impact of the payload that reached the application
steps.desc: Determine what the bypassing payload achieved (e.g., injection, RCE) once it reached the unprotected backend.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed.

steps.title: Apply an updated WAF rule closing the bypass
steps.desc: Deploy a corrected WAF rule set that accounts for the bypass technique (e.g., encoding variant, HTTP parameter pollution).
steps.outcome: Bypass technique blocked.

steps.title: Isolate or restrict the affected application if impact is severe
steps.desc: If significant compromise occurred, take the affected application offline or restrict access while remediation proceeds.
steps.outcome: Further exploitation halted.

steps.title: Fix the underlying application vulnerability the WAF was compensating for
steps.desc: Address the root-cause vulnerability in the application itself rather than relying solely on the WAF as a permanent control.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated at the source.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence delivered through the bypass
steps.desc: Clean the application/server of any malicious code or unauthorized changes introduced via the bypassing payload.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore full service after verification
steps.desc: Return the application to normal service once the vulnerability is fixed and the WAF rule is verified effective.
steps.outcome: Application restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review WAF rule-testing process
steps.desc: Record the bypass technique and recommend improved WAF rule testing/tuning to catch similar bypasses proactively.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32233.def: Exploitation of a web application flaw that allows an attacker to induce the server to make unintended requests to internal or otherwise-restricted resources (e.g., cloud metadata services, internal-only APIs) on the attacker's behalf.
ITID-32233.purpose: Captures exploitation of a Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability.
scopeIncludes: SSRF used to reach internal-only network resources not otherwise internet-accessible
SSRF used to reach cloud instance metadata services for credential theft
scopeExcludes: General known-CVE web server software exploitation not involving induced server-side requests (ITID-32231)
Directory traversal/path manipulation exploitation (ITID-32234)
ITID-32233.severity: High-Critical; SSRF frequently provides a pivot from an internet-facing application into otherwise-unreachable internal infrastructure or cloud credentials.
ITID-32233.priority: P1 if cloud metadata or internal admin interfaces are reachable, else P2.
ITID-32233.escalation: Escalate to incident command; treat any cloud credentials reachable via SSRF as compromised and rotate immediately.
indicators: Application logs showing outbound requests to internal IP ranges or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., 169.254.169.254) initiated by the application itself
Unexpected internal API calls originating from the web application's own service identity
vectors: User-supplied URL/parameter used unsanitized in a server-side outbound request
Exploitation of a webhook, PDF-generation, or URL-preview feature that fetches attacker-controlled URLs
rootCauses: Insufficient input validation/allowlisting on server-side outbound request destinations
Cloud instance metadata service reachable without additional authentication (e.g., IMDSv1)
mitreTechniques: T1552.005 Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API
controls: Enforce IMDSv2 (or equivalent) requiring token-based metadata access
Allowlist server-side outbound request destinations
Network segmentation limiting what internal resources the application can reach
ITID-32233.detection: Moderate; outbound-request logging from application servers to internal/metadata ranges is a strong detection signal when instrumented.
ITID-32233.response: Patch the input-validation flaw, rotate any credentials retrievable via the SSRF path (especially cloud instance credentials), and review what internal resources were reachable.
metrics: Number of applications with unrestricted server-side outbound request capability
Time to credential rotation post-SSRF confirmation
detections: Outbound request monitoring to internal/metadata IP ranges
ITID-32233.notes: Broken out as its own leaf given SSRF's distinct exploitation mechanism (induced server-side requests) and cloud-credential-theft consequence, separate from general web server CVE exploitation.

playbook.name: Response: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability, where an attacker induced the server to make unauthorized requests on their behalf, potentially reaching internal resources or cloud metadata services.

steps.title: Confirm the SSRF vulnerability and the requests it generated
steps.desc: Review application and network logs for outbound requests initiated by the server to unexpected internal addresses or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., 169.254.169.254) matching the SSRF pattern.
steps.outcome: Confirmed SSRF instances and target destinations.

steps.title: Assess whether cloud credentials or internal service data were exposed
steps.desc: Determine whether the SSRF reached cloud instance metadata services or internal-only APIs, which could have exposed credentials or sensitive data.
steps.guidance: Treat any successful metadata-service access as a probable credential compromise.
steps.outcome: Scope of potential data/credential exposure established.

steps.title: Disable or restrict the vulnerable request-generating feature
steps.desc: Disable the specific application feature that issues outbound requests based on user input, or restrict it via WAF rule, until fixed.
steps.outcome: SSRF vector closed.

steps.title: Rotate any cloud/internal credentials that may have been exposed
steps.desc: Immediately rotate cloud instance credentials, API keys, or tokens accessible via the reached metadata/internal service.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Fix the SSRF vulnerability with proper input validation/allow-listing
steps.desc: Remediate the vulnerable code with strict URL/destination allow-listing and disabling of redirects to internal address ranges.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated in code.

steps.title: Investigate reached internal systems for further compromise
steps.desc: Check any internal system reached via the SSRF for unauthorized access or data exposure resulting from the exploited trust relationship.
steps.outcome: Internal systems confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the application feature after verification
steps.desc: Re-enable the fixed feature once the code change and credential rotation are verified.
steps.outcome: Application restored to normal operation.

steps.title: Document the incident and review cloud metadata service protections
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend metadata service hardening (e.g., IMDSv2 enforcement) and network-level egress restrictions for application servers.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32234.def: Exploitation of a web application/server flaw that allows an attacker to manipulate file-path input (e.g., using ../ sequences or absolute paths) to read, write, or execute files outside the intended directory scope.
ITID-32234.purpose: Captures exploitation of a directory traversal or path manipulation vulnerability.
scopeIncludes: Path traversal used to read sensitive files outside the web root (e.g., configuration files, credentials)
Path traversal used to write a file (e.g., a web shell) outside the intended upload directory
scopeExcludes: SSRF exploitation (induced server-side network requests rather than file-path manipulation) (ITID-32233)
General known-CVE web server software exploitation unrelated to path handling (ITID-32231)
ITID-32234.severity: High-Critical, especially when traversal enables arbitrary file write leading to code execution.
ITID-32234.priority: P1 if file write/code execution is achieved, else P2 for read-only disclosure.
ITID-32234.escalation: Escalate to incident command; treat as active compromise if a file write was achieved.
indicators: Web server access logs showing traversal sequences (../, encoded variants) in request parameters
Unexpected file appearing outside the intended upload/storage directory
vectors: Unsanitized file-path parameter in a file-download or file-upload feature
Archive extraction ('zip slip') writing files outside the intended extraction directory
rootCauses: Insufficient input validation/canonicalization of user-supplied file paths
Missing sandboxing of file-upload/extraction functionality
controls: Canonicalize and validate all user-supplied file paths against an allowlisted base directory
Sandbox archive-extraction functionality
Least-privilege file-system permissions for the web application process
ITID-32234.detection: Moderate-high; traversal sequences in access logs are a well-known, reliably detectable pattern.
ITID-32234.response: Patch the input-validation flaw, remove any files written outside the intended directory (including web shells), and review logs for the exploitation window.
metrics: Number of traversal attempts blocked vs. successful
ITID-32234.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32233 (SSRF) by the mechanism being file-path manipulation rather than induced network requests.

playbook.name: Response: Directory Traversal/Path Manipulation Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a directory traversal or path manipulation vulnerability allowing an attacker to read or write files outside the intended application directory.

steps.title: Confirm the traversal exploitation and files accessed
steps.desc: Review web server/application logs for traversal sequences (e.g., ../ patterns, encoded variants) and identify which files outside the intended directory were accessed or modified.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation and list of accessed/modified files.

steps.title: Assess sensitivity of exposed or modified files
steps.desc: Determine whether configuration files, credentials, or source code were read, or whether files were written (indicating potential webshell upload) outside the intended directory.
steps.outcome: Impact of the exposure/modification assessed.

steps.title: Isolate or restrict the affected application
steps.desc: Take the vulnerable endpoint/application offline or restrict access via WAF rule to halt further exploitation.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Rotate any credentials found in exposed configuration files
steps.desc: If configuration files or secrets were read via the traversal, immediately rotate any exposed credentials.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Fix the path validation vulnerability
steps.desc: Remediate the vulnerable code to properly canonicalize and validate file paths against an allow-listed base directory.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated in code.

steps.title: Remove any webshell or unauthorized file written via the traversal
steps.desc: Locate and remove any malicious file written outside the intended directory during exploitation.
steps.outcome: Server confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the application after verification
steps.desc: Return the fixed application to normal service after verification.
steps.outcome: Application restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review secure coding practices for file-handling code
steps.desc: Record the finding and recommend a targeted secure code review of other file-handling endpoints for similar path-validation gaps.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32235.def: An incident involving remote exploitation of a web server, not clearly matching a more specific web-server-exploit leaf.
ITID-32235.purpose: Catch-all for web server exploitation that does not fit known-CVE, WAF-bypass, SSRF, or directory-traversal leaves.
scopeIncludes: Web server exploitation of unclear specific mechanism
Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling web server leaf
ITID-32235.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending classification.
ITID-32235.priority: P2 by default, escalate to P1 if code execution or data exposure is confirmed.
ITID-32235.escalation: Reclassify once the specific exploitation mechanism is clarified.
indicators: Web server-related alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific web server vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32235.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32235.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32235.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Web Server Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a web server vulnerability not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the exploit and affected server(s) via web server/WAF logs
steps.desc: Correlate web server access/error logs, WAF alerts, and EDR telemetry to confirm exploitation and identify affected server(s).
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploit and affected server(s).

steps.title: Determine whether the server was internet-facing without adequate compensating controls
steps.desc: Confirm the server's internet exposure and existing protections (WAF, network restrictions).
steps.outcome: Exposure configuration documented.

steps.title: Isolate or take the affected server offline
steps.desc: Remove the affected server from production traffic or isolate it from the network to halt active exploitation.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Deploy an interim WAF rule or configuration mitigation
steps.desc: Apply a targeted WAF rule or configuration change addressing the specific exploitation pattern while a permanent fix is developed.
steps.outcome: Interim risk reduction in place.

steps.title: Patch or fix the underlying vulnerability
steps.desc: Apply the applicable vendor patch or code fix addressing the vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated.

steps.title: Remove any webshell or persistence delivered by the exploit
steps.desc: Scan and clean the server of any web shells, backdoors, or unauthorized file modifications.
steps.outcome: Server confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the server to production after verification
steps.desc: Return the patched, verified-clean server to production traffic.
steps.outcome: Server restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review web infrastructure hardening
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend improvements to patch cadence and WAF coverage for internet-facing web infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32311.def: Local exploitation of a memory-safety or logic vulnerability in a privileged local service/daemon (running as SYSTEM/root) to escalate an unprivileged local session to elevated privileges.
ITID-32311.purpose: Captures local privilege escalation achieved by exploiting a vulnerable local service or daemon.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a code-level vulnerability (buffer overflow, race condition, insecure IPC handling) in a privileged local service binary
Local exploit against a third-party agent/service running with elevated privileges (e.g., an EDR agent, backup agent)
scopeExcludes: Privilege escalation achieved via broken access-control/authorization logic rather than binary exploitation — see ITID-33223/ITID-33224/ITID-33214 under the Unauthorized Access > Privilege Escalation Tier-3 branch, which cover misconfigured role assignment and horizontal/vertical access-control failures rather than vulnerability exploitation
SUID/SGID-specific binary exploitation on Linux/Unix (ITID-32312)
UAC-bypass-specific technique (ITID-32313)
Scheduled task/service hijacking specifically (ITID-32314)
ITID-32311.severity: High-Critical; local privilege escalation is typically a post-initial-access step toward full system compromise.
ITID-32311.priority: P1 if paired with confirmed initial access, else P2.
ITID-32311.escalation: Escalate to incident command; assume the escalating actor already has some foothold requiring full-chain investigation.
indicators: Unprivileged process spawning a SYSTEM/root-level child process via a vulnerable service
Service crash/restart immediately preceding a privilege-escalation event
EDR alert on exploitation of a known vulnerable local service
vectors: Local exploitation of a vulnerable privileged service after initial unprivileged access
Exploitation of a third-party privileged agent installed on the endpoint
rootCauses: Memory-safety or insecure IPC-handling defects in privileged local service code
Unpatched third-party agents running with excessive privilege
controls: Patch management for privileged local services and third-party agents
Principle of least privilege for service accounts
EDR local-exploitation behavioral detection
ITID-32311.detection: Moderate; EDR can often detect the resulting anomalous privileged child-process behavior even without a signature for the specific exploit.
ITID-32311.response: Isolate the host, patch/update the vulnerable service, and investigate the initial-access vector that preceded the escalation.
metrics: Number of privileged services/agents exceeding patch SLA
ITID-32311.notes: This branch (Local Exploitation) is scoped to the vulnerability/exploit-code mechanism itself. Broken-access-control or authorization-logic privilege escalation (e.g., insecure default role assignment, horizontal/vertical access-control failures) is a distinct mechanism tracked under ITID-33214/33223/33224 in the Unauthorized Access domain's Privilege Escalation Tier-3 branch — cross-reference to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Vulnerable Service/Daemon Privilege Escalation Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a vulnerability in a locally-running service or daemon to escalate privileges from an unprivileged user to SYSTEM/root.

steps.title: Identify the new SYSTEM/root process spawned from an unprivileged parent
steps.desc: Review EDR/process-creation telemetry for a privileged (SYSTEM/root) process unexpectedly spawned by, or with a parent/lineage of, an unprivileged user process — the primary signal of local privilege escalation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed privilege escalation event and affected host.

steps.title: Identify the vulnerable service/daemon exploited
steps.desc: Determine which locally-running service/daemon was exploited (e.g., insecure service permissions, unquoted service path, vulnerable daemon version) to achieve the escalation.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable service/daemon identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host to prevent the now-privileged attacker from moving laterally or expanding access.
steps.outcome: Host isolated.

steps.title: Terminate the malicious privileged process and disable the vulnerable service
steps.desc: Kill the escalated process and stop/disable the exploited service to prevent re-exploitation.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Patch or reconfigure the vulnerable service/daemon
steps.desc: Apply the vendor patch, or correct the insecure permission/configuration, that allowed the escalation.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated.

steps.title: Remove any persistence established with elevated privileges
steps.desc: Check for and remove new privileged accounts, scheduled tasks, or services created during the elevated-access window.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean of privileged persistence.

steps.title: Restore the host to service after verification
steps.desc: Return the patched, verified-clean host to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Host restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and audit similar services fleet-wide
steps.desc: Record the vulnerability class and audit other hosts for the same insecure service configuration.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and fleet-wide audit scheduled.

ITID-32312.def: Local privilege escalation on a Linux/Unix system achieved by abusing a binary with the SUID or SGID bit set that is misconfigured (e.g., an unnecessary SUID binary, or one with an exploitable code flaw) to execute code with the file owner's (often root) privileges.
ITID-32312.purpose: Captures Linux/Unix privilege escalation via a misconfigured SUID/SGID binary.
scopeIncludes: Abuse of a misconfigured SUID/SGID binary (unintended shell escape, unnecessary SUID flag) to gain elevated privileges
Exploitation of a code vulnerability specifically within a SUID/SGID-flagged binary
scopeExcludes: Windows UAC bypass techniques (ITID-32313, platform-specific mechanism)
Privilege escalation via a vulnerable service/daemon not related to the SUID/SGID mechanism (ITID-32311)
ITID-32312.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if paired with confirmed initial access.
ITID-32312.escalation: Escalate to incident command upon confirmation; audit the system for other unnecessary SUID/SGID binaries.
indicators: Root-owned shell spawned from a non-root user session via a known SUID-abusable binary (e.g., via GTFOBins-documented technique)
Auditd log showing execution of a SUID binary followed immediately by privilege change
vectors: Execution of a SUID binary with a known privilege-escalation gadget (documented in tools like GTFOBins)
Exploitation of a custom/in-house SUID binary with an unreviewed code flaw
rootCauses: Unnecessary SUID/SGID bits left on binaries not requiring elevated execution
Lack of periodic SUID/SGID binary auditing
mitreTechniques: T1548.001 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid
controls: Periodic SUID/SGID binary auditing and removal of unnecessary flags
Mandatory access control (SELinux/AppArmor) constraining SUID binary behavior
Auditd monitoring of SUID/SGID binary execution
ITID-32312.detection: Moderate-high; auditd/eBPF-based monitoring reliably captures SUID/SGID execution events for correlation.
ITID-32312.response: Remove or fix the misconfigured binary, audit for other instances across the fleet, and investigate for follow-on activity.
metrics: Number of unnecessary SUID/SGID binaries identified and remediated per audit cycle
ITID-32312.notes: Platform-specific (Linux/Unix) sibling to ITID-32313 (Windows UAC bypass); both are local binary-exploitation privilege-escalation mechanisms differentiated by OS.

playbook.name: Response: Misconfigured SUID/SGID Binary Privilege Escalation (Linux/Unix)
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a misconfigured SUID/SGID binary on a Linux/Unix system to escalate privileges from an unprivileged user to root.

steps.title: Identify the root process spawned from an unprivileged user's shell
steps.desc: Review auditd/EDR process telemetry for a root-owned process or shell spawned via execution of a SUID/SGID binary by an unprivileged user — the primary signal of this escalation technique.
steps.outcome: Confirmed privilege escalation event and affected host.

steps.title: Identify the exploited SUID/SGID binary and its misconfiguration
steps.desc: Determine which binary was exploited (e.g., unnecessary SUID bit, exploitable functionality within a legitimate SUID binary) and how it was misconfigured.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable binary and misconfiguration identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host to prevent the now-root attacker from moving laterally or expanding access.
steps.outcome: Host isolated.

steps.title: Remove the SUID/SGID bit from the exploited binary
steps.desc: Immediately strip the unnecessary SUID/SGID permission from the exploited binary to close the escalation path.
steps.outcome: Escalation path closed.

steps.title: Audit and remediate similar misconfigurations fleet-wide
steps.desc: Scan all hosts for the same or similarly unnecessary SUID/SGID binaries and remediate.
steps.outcome: Misconfiguration remediated organization-wide.

steps.title: Remove any persistence established with root privileges
steps.desc: Check for and remove new privileged accounts, cron jobs, or SSH keys created during the elevated-access window.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean of privileged persistence.

steps.title: Restore the host to service after verification
steps.desc: Return the remediated, verified-clean host to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Host restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and establish a baseline SUID/SGID audit process
steps.desc: Record the finding and recommend periodic auditing of SUID/SGID binaries as a standard hardening practice.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32313.def: Local privilege escalation on Windows achieved by exploiting a technique that circumvents the UAC elevation prompt, allowing a process to gain administrative privileges without user consent.
ITID-32313.purpose: Captures Windows privilege escalation via a User Account Control (UAC) bypass technique.
scopeIncludes: Use of a known UAC-bypass technique (e.g., abusing an auto-elevating binary, DLL hijacking of an auto-elevate component)
Exploitation of a UAC design/implementation flaw to silently elevate privileges
scopeExcludes: Linux/Unix SUID/SGID abuse (ITID-32312, platform-specific mechanism)
DLL hijacking used purely for code execution/persistence rather than UAC elevation specifically (ITID-32321)
ITID-32313.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if paired with confirmed initial access.
ITID-32313.escalation: Escalate to incident command upon confirmation.
indicators: Administrative-level process spawned without a corresponding UAC consent prompt event in the Windows event log
Known auto-elevating binary (e.g., a signed Microsoft binary in the UAC allowlist) executed with anomalous parent process or loaded module
vectors: Abuse of an auto-elevating Windows binary combined with DLL hijacking to run attacker code with elevated privileges
Use of a public UAC-bypass tool/technique (e.g., fodhelper, eventvwr-class techniques)
rootCauses: Windows' auto-elevate allowlist trusting binaries that can be manipulated via DLL search-order or registry hijacking
UAC configured at a lower-than-default security setting
mitreTechniques: T1548.002 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Bypass User Account Control
controls: UAC set to 'Always Notify' rather than a reduced-prompt setting
Application allowlisting to prevent abuse of auto-elevating binaries
EDR detection of known UAC-bypass technique patterns
ITID-32313.detection: Moderate; EDR vendors maintain detections for well-known public UAC-bypass techniques, though novel techniques may evade signature-based detection.
ITID-32313.response: Isolate the host, identify the specific bypass technique used, and audit for other hosts vulnerable to the same technique.
metrics: Number of hosts with UAC configured below 'Always Notify'
ITID-32313.notes: Platform-specific (Windows) sibling to ITID-32312 (Linux SUID/SGID abuse). Where DLL hijacking is the mechanism but the goal is general code execution/persistence rather than UAC elevation, use ITID-32321 instead.

playbook.name: Response: UAC Bypass Privilege Escalation Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a technique that bypasses Windows User Account Control (UAC) to execute code with elevated (administrator) privileges without user consent.

steps.title: Identify the elevated process spawned without a corresponding UAC consent prompt
steps.desc: Review EDR/process telemetry for a process running with an elevated integrity level whose parent process lineage shows no legitimate UAC consent event — the primary signal of a bypass.
steps.outcome: Confirmed bypass event and affected host.

steps.title: Identify the specific UAC bypass technique used
steps.desc: Determine which known bypass technique (e.g., abuse of an auto-elevating binary, DLL hijacking of a trusted elevated process, registry manipulation) was used.
steps.outcome: Bypass technique identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host to prevent the now-elevated attacker from moving laterally or expanding access.
steps.outcome: Host isolated.

steps.title: Terminate the malicious elevated process
steps.desc: Kill the process that achieved unauthorized elevation.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Apply hardening to prevent the specific bypass technique
steps.desc: Apply the relevant Group Policy/registry hardening (e.g., raising UAC prompt behavior, restricting the abused auto-elevating binary) to close the bypass path.
steps.outcome: Bypass path closed fleet-wide.

steps.title: Remove any persistence established with elevated privileges
steps.desc: Check for and remove new administrator accounts, scheduled tasks, or services created during the elevated-access window.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean of privileged persistence.

steps.title: Restore the host to service after verification
steps.desc: Return the remediated, verified-clean host to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Host restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and audit endpoint hardening baseline
steps.desc: Record the bypass technique and verify the endpoint hardening baseline (UAC settings, ASR rules) is applied fleet-wide.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32314.def: Local privilege escalation achieved by modifying or hijacking a scheduled task or service that runs with elevated privileges, causing attacker-controlled code to execute in that elevated context.
ITID-32314.purpose: Captures privilege escalation achieved by hijacking a scheduled task or service configuration.
scopeIncludes: Modification of an existing privileged scheduled task's action/binary path to run attacker code
Exploitation of weak file/folder permissions on a service binary path allowing binary replacement (service hijacking)
scopeExcludes: UAC-bypass-specific technique (ITID-32313)
SUID/SGID binary abuse (ITID-32312)
DLL hijacking/sideloading targeting an application rather than a scheduled task/service configuration (ITID-32321)
ITID-32314.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if paired with confirmed initial access.
ITID-32314.escalation: Escalate to incident command upon confirmation; audit all scheduled tasks/services for similar weak-permission conditions.
indicators: Scheduled task or service configuration change immediately preceding a privileged process execution not matching its documented purpose
Weak ACL identified on a service binary or scheduled task action path allowing non-privileged write access
vectors: Modifying a scheduled task's action to point to attacker-controlled code, relying on the task's elevated run-as context
Replacing a service binary at a writable path due to weak file-system permissions
rootCauses: Weak file/folder permissions on scheduled task or service binary paths
Scheduled tasks/services configured to run with excessive privilege relative to their function
controls: Least-privilege run-as accounts for scheduled tasks/services
Periodic ACL auditing on scheduled task and service binary paths
Change monitoring on scheduled task/service configuration
ITID-32314.detection: Moderate-high; scheduled task/service configuration change monitoring is a well-instrumented telemetry source in most EDR/SIEM deployments.
ITID-32314.response: Revert the malicious task/service modification, remediate the underlying weak-permission condition, and audit for similar misconfigurations elsewhere.
metrics: Number of scheduled tasks/services identified with weak-permission paths per audit cycle
ITID-32314.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32313 (UAC-specific) and ITID-32312 (SUID/SGID-specific) by the scheduled task/service hijacking mechanism, which can occur on either Windows or Linux/Unix.

playbook.name: Response: Scheduled Task/Service Hijacking Privilege Escalation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a misconfigured scheduled task or service (e.g., writable binary path, weak permissions, unquoted path) that runs with elevated privileges, allowing an unprivileged user to hijack its execution.

steps.title: Identify the privileged process resulting from the hijacked task/service
steps.desc: Review EDR/process telemetry for a SYSTEM/root-level process executing attacker-controlled code at the next scheduled run or service start — the primary signal of this technique.
steps.outcome: Confirmed hijack event and affected host.
steps.tool: EDR / Task Scheduler or cron logs

steps.title: Identify the hijacked task/service and the misconfiguration exploited
steps.desc: Determine which scheduled task or service was hijacked and what misconfiguration (writable path, weak ACL, unquoted path) enabled it.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable task/service and misconfiguration identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host to prevent the now-privileged attacker from moving laterally or expanding access.
steps.outcome: Host isolated.

steps.title: Disable the hijacked task/service and restore the legitimate binary
steps.desc: Disable the affected scheduled task/service and remove the attacker-planted binary from the hijacked path.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Correct the underlying permission misconfiguration
steps.desc: Fix the file/folder ACLs or path quoting that allowed the unprivileged write, on the affected host and any others sharing the same configuration.
steps.outcome: Misconfiguration remediated fleet-wide.

steps.title: Remove any persistence established with elevated privileges
steps.desc: Check for and remove new privileged accounts or additional scheduled tasks/services created during the elevated-access window.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean of privileged persistence.

steps.title: Restore the host to service after verification
steps.desc: Return the remediated, verified-clean host to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Host restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and audit scheduled tasks/services fleet-wide
steps.desc: Record the finding and scan for similarly misconfigured scheduled tasks/services across the environment.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and fleet-wide audit scheduled.

ITID-32315.def: An incident involving local privilege escalation via exploit-code mechanisms, not clearly matching a more specific privilege-escalation leaf.
ITID-32315.purpose: Catch-all for local privilege-escalation exploitation that does not fit vulnerable-service, SUID/SGID, UAC-bypass, or scheduled-task leaves.
scopeIncludes: Local privilege escalation of unclear specific mechanism
Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf
Broken access-control/authorization-logic privilege escalation (tracked under ITID-33214/33223/33224 in the Unauthorized Access domain, not here)
ITID-32315.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as High pending classification.
ITID-32315.escalation: Reclassify once the specific exploitation mechanism is clarified.
indicators: Privilege-escalation alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific local-exploitation vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32315.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32315.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32315.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one. Also serves as the cross-reference point noting that authorization-logic privilege escalation belongs under ITID-33214/33223/33224 instead.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Privilege Escalation Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a local privilege escalation technique not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Identify the new privileged process spawned from an unprivileged parent
steps.desc: Review EDR/process-creation telemetry for a SYSTEM/root-level process unexpectedly spawned by an unprivileged user process — the primary signal of local privilege escalation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed privilege escalation event and affected host.

steps.title: Identify the escalation technique/vulnerability exploited
steps.desc: Determine the specific mechanism used to escalate privileges on this host.
steps.outcome: Escalation technique identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host to prevent the now-privileged attacker from moving laterally or expanding access.
steps.outcome: Host isolated.

steps.title: Terminate the malicious privileged process
steps.desc: Kill the escalated process to halt active exploitation.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Remediate the underlying vulnerability/misconfiguration
steps.desc: Apply a patch or configuration fix addressing the specific weakness that enabled escalation.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated.

steps.title: Remove any persistence established with elevated privileges
steps.desc: Check for and remove new privileged accounts, scheduled tasks, or services created during the elevated-access window.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean of privileged persistence.

steps.title: Restore the host to service after verification
steps.desc: Return the patched, verified-clean host to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Host restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review privilege-escalation detection coverage
steps.desc: Record the technique used and assess whether detection rules cover this escalation class fleet-wide.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32321.def: Local exploitation in which an attacker places a malicious DLL where a legitimate application will load it in place of (or alongside) the intended library, due to search-order weaknesses or an application's insecure loading behavior, achieving code execution in that application's context.
ITID-32321.purpose: Captures local code execution achieved via DLL hijacking or DLL sideloading.
scopeIncludes: DLL search-order hijacking exploiting an application's insecure library-loading path
DLL sideloading abusing a legitimate signed application to load a malicious DLL alongside it
scopeExcludes: DLL hijacking used specifically as a UAC-bypass mechanism against an auto-elevating binary (ITID-32313)
Malicious file association/handler abuse (ITID-32322)
ITID-32321.severity: High, particularly when the hijacked application runs with elevated privileges or is a trusted/signed process used for defense evasion.
ITID-32321.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the target application runs with elevated privileges.
ITID-32321.escalation: Escalate to incident command upon confirmation; identify and remediate all vulnerable application installations.
indicators: Legitimate signed application loading a DLL from an unexpected/writable directory
Unsigned or newly-created DLL present in an application's directory alongside a signed executable
vectors: Dropping a malicious DLL into a directory earlier in the search order than the legitimate library location
Sideloading a malicious DLL alongside a legitimate signed binary copied to an attacker-writable directory
rootCauses: Application referencing a DLL without a fully-qualified path, relying on default search order
Writable application directories allowing DLL placement by a non-privileged user
mitreTechniques: T1574.001 Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Search Order Hijacking
T1574.002 Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Side-Loading
controls: Application directory permission hardening (no user-writable application folders)
Safe DLL search mode / fully-qualified library loading in application code
EDR detection of unsigned DLLs loaded by signed processes
ITID-32321.detection: Moderate-high; EDR image-load monitoring for unsigned DLLs loaded by known signed processes is a well-established detection pattern.
ITID-32321.response: Remove the malicious DLL, identify the loading application and its search-order weakness, and patch or reconfigure to load from a fully-qualified path.
metrics: Number of applications identified with insecure DLL loading behavior
ITID-32321.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32313 by purpose: this leaf is for general code execution/persistence, while UAC-specific DLL hijacking is tracked under ITID-32313.

playbook.name: Response: DLL Hijacking/Sideloading Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of DLL hijacking or sideloading, where a malicious DLL was loaded by a legitimate application due to insecure library search order or path handling.

steps.title: Identify the legitimate process loading an unexpected/unsigned DLL
steps.desc: Review EDR/DLL-load telemetry for a trusted application loading a DLL from an unexpected location or an unsigned/mismatched DLL — the primary signal of this technique.
steps.outcome: Confirmed hijack event, affected host, and malicious DLL identified.

steps.title: Determine the delivery method of the malicious DLL
steps.desc: Trace how the malicious DLL was placed in the search path (e.g., dropped by another payload, delivered via a compromised software package).
steps.outcome: Delivery vector identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host to prevent further exploitation or lateral movement.
steps.outcome: Host isolated.

steps.title: Terminate the affected process and quarantine the malicious DLL
steps.desc: Kill the process that loaded the malicious DLL and quarantine the file to prevent reload.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Remove the malicious DLL and any dropped persistence
steps.desc: Delete the malicious DLL and any additional payloads or persistence mechanisms established.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean.

steps.title: Harden the vulnerable application's DLL search behavior where possible
steps.desc: Apply vendor patches or safe DLL search mode settings to the affected application to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Application hardened against future hijacking.

steps.title: Restore the host to service after verification
steps.desc: Return the remediated, verified-clean host to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Host restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and audit software installation sources
steps.desc: Record the delivery vector and review controls on software installation sources to prevent future DLL planting.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32322.def: Local exploitation in which an attacker modifies a file-type association or default handler so that opening a file of that type (or triggering an event associated with it) executes attacker-controlled code.
ITID-32322.purpose: Captures local code execution achieved by abusing a malicious file association or default file handler.
scopeIncludes: Modification of a Windows registry file-association key to point at attacker-controlled code
Abuse of a default handler/protocol association to trigger code execution on a routine user action
scopeExcludes: DLL hijacking/sideloading (ITID-32321)
LOLBin abuse where no file-association change is involved (ITID-32323)
ITID-32322.severity: High, particularly for persistence combined with routine user activity triggering re-execution.
ITID-32322.escalation: Escalate to incident command upon confirmation; revert the malicious association and audit for persistence mechanisms.
indicators: Registry/system configuration change to a file-type association or default handler key inconsistent with legitimate software installation
Unexpected process execution correlated with a routine file-open or protocol-handler event
vectors: Registry modification of a common file-type association (e.g., .txt, .lnk) to launch a malicious payload
Hijacking a URL protocol handler to launch attacker code when a specific link type is clicked
rootCauses: Insufficient monitoring of registry keys controlling file associations and default handlers
Excessive local write privileges allowing non-administrative modification of association keys
mitreTechniques: T1546.001 Event Triggered Execution: Change Default File Association
controls: Registry monitoring of file-association and protocol-handler keys
Least-privilege enforcement preventing non-administrative modification of system-wide associations
EDR detection of file-association tampering
ITID-32322.detection: Moderate-high; registry-key monitoring for association changes is a well-instrumented detection surface.
ITID-32322.response: Revert the malicious association, identify how the modification was made, and audit for related persistence artifacts.
metrics: Number of unauthorized file-association changes detected
ITID-32322.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32321 (library-loading mechanism) and ITID-32323 (native-binary-abuse mechanism) by the file-association/handler configuration being the specific exploited component.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious File Association/Handler Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a file association or handler abuse technique, where opening a file of a given type triggers execution of attacker-controlled code via a hijacked or malicious handler.

steps.title: Identify the process launched via the file association/handler at the time of file open
steps.desc: Review EDR telemetry correlating a file-open event with an unexpected process launch through a hijacked or malicious file handler.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation event and affected host.

steps.title: Identify the malicious/hijacked handler and affected file type
steps.desc: Determine which file type association or handler registration was abused or maliciously registered.
steps.outcome: Malicious handler and file type identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host to prevent further exploitation or lateral movement.
steps.outcome: Host isolated.

steps.title: Remove or restore the malicious file association/handler
steps.desc: Revert the hijacked file association to its legitimate handler and remove any malicious handler registration.
steps.outcome: Exploitation vector closed.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence delivered via the handler
steps.desc: Clean the host of any malware or persistence mechanism established through the abused handler.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the host to service after verification
steps.desc: Return the remediated, verified-clean host to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Host restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and audit file association integrity fleet-wide
steps.desc: Record the finding and consider monitoring for unauthorized file association changes across the environment.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32323.def: Local exploitation in which an attacker abuses a legitimate, signed, pre-installed system binary's built-in functionality (e.g., script execution, download, or proxy-execution capability) to execute arbitrary code or commands while evading detection tools that trust signed binaries.
ITID-32323.purpose: Captures local code execution achieved by abusing a legitimate, pre-installed system binary (a Living-off-the-Land Binary).
scopeIncludes: Use of a native OS binary's documented functionality to execute attacker-supplied code or scripts (e.g., proxy-execution via a signed system utility)
Abuse of a built-in scripting/interpreter binary to run an attacker payload disguised as legitimate activity
scopeExcludes: DLL hijacking/sideloading of a legitimate binary (ITID-32321, a distinct mechanism — malicious library injection rather than abusing the binary's own documented functionality)
Malicious file-association abuse (ITID-32322)
ITID-32323.severity: Medium-High; LOLBin abuse is frequently a defense-evasion/execution technique rather than the initial compromise vector itself.
ITID-32323.escalation: Escalate to incident command upon confirmation; determine what payload/command the LOLBin was used to execute.
indicators: Native system binary observed executing with unusual command-line arguments inconsistent with normal administrative use
Signed system utility making outbound network connections or spawning unusual child processes
vectors: Abuse of a signed system utility's documented download/execute capability to fetch and run a payload
Use of a native scripting engine to execute an attacker-supplied script while evading application-allowlisting controls
rootCauses: Application allowlisting policies that trust signed system binaries unconditionally without command-line/behavioral scrutiny
Insufficient logging of native binary command-line arguments
controls: Command-line argument logging and behavioral analytics for commonly-abused native binaries
Application-control policies that restrict LOLBin usage patterns beyond simple binary-path allowlisting
EDR detections tuned to known LOLBin abuse techniques
ITID-32323.detection: Moderate; command-line/behavioral analytics can catch known abuse patterns, but attackers continuously discover new LOLBin techniques (living-off-the-land is inherently evasive against signature-based tools).
ITID-32323.response: Identify the payload/command executed via the LOLBin, isolate the host, and tune detection rules for the specific technique observed.
metrics: Number of distinct LOLBin abuse techniques observed per period
detections: Command-line behavioral analytics for known LOLBins
ITID-32323.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32321 by mechanism: this leaf covers abuse of a binary's own legitimate functionality, not injection of a malicious library into it.

playbook.name: Response: Living-off-the-Land Binary (LOLBin) Abuse for Local Execution
playbook.description: For confirmed abuse of a legitimate, pre-installed system binary (LOLBin) to execute malicious code or evade detection during local execution.

steps.title: Identify anomalous use of a legitimate system binary
steps.desc: Review EDR/command-line telemetry for a legitimate binary (e.g., a scripting host, admin utility) being invoked with unusual arguments or parent process lineage consistent with LOLBin abuse rather than normal administrative use.
steps.guidance: Focus on command-line arguments and parent/child process relationships, since the binary itself is legitimate and will not be flagged as malicious.
steps.outcome: Confirmed abuse event, binary, and affected host identified.

steps.title: Determine what the LOLBin was used to achieve
steps.desc: Establish whether the binary was used for download/execution, defense evasion, persistence, or lateral movement.
steps.outcome: Objective of the abuse established.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host to prevent further exploitation or lateral movement.
steps.outcome: Host isolated.

steps.title: Terminate the malicious process chain
steps.desc: Kill the process(es) involved in the LOLBin abuse chain.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence delivered via the LOLBin
steps.desc: Clean the host of any malware or persistence mechanism established through the abused binary.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean.

steps.title: Tune detection rules/attack surface reduction for the abused binary
steps.desc: Deploy or tighten ASR rules or application control policies restricting the abused binary's use to expected administrative contexts.
steps.outcome: Detection/prevention coverage improved for this technique.
steps.tool: EDR attack surface reduction / application allow-listing

steps.title: Restore the host to service after verification
steps.desc: Return the remediated, verified-clean host to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Host restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review LOLBin detection coverage fleet-wide
steps.desc: Record the technique used and assess whether detection rules and application control policies cover this LOLBin abuse pattern organization-wide.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32324.def: An incident involving local code execution via file/execution-mechanism exploitation, not clearly matching a more specific file-execution-exploit leaf.
ITID-32324.purpose: Catch-all for local file-execution exploitation that does not fit DLL hijacking, file-association abuse, or LOLBin leaves.
scopeIncludes: Local file-execution exploitation of unclear specific mechanism
Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf

ITID-32324.escalation: Reclassify once the specific exploitation mechanism is clarified.
indicators: Local execution alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific local file-execution vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32324.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32324.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32324.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General File Execution Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a local file execution technique not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Identify the anomalous execution event via EDR telemetry
steps.desc: Review EDR/process-creation telemetry for the unexpected execution event and identify the affected host.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation event and affected host.

steps.title: Identify the execution technique/mechanism exploited
steps.desc: Determine the specific mechanism used to achieve unauthorized local execution.
steps.outcome: Execution technique identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host to prevent further exploitation or lateral movement.
steps.outcome: Host isolated.

steps.title: Terminate the malicious process
steps.desc: Kill the process(es) involved in the exploitation.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence delivered by the exploit

steps.desc: Return the remediated, verified-clean host to normal operation.

steps.title: Document the incident and review local execution detection coverage

ITID-32331.def: Local exploitation of a publicly known kernel CVE (Windows, Linux, or other OS) for which a vendor/project patch was available but not applied, used to escalate an unprivileged local session to kernel-level or SYSTEM/root privileges.
ITID-32331.purpose: Captures local exploitation of a known, patchable kernel vulnerability for privilege escalation.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a known-CVE kernel vulnerability where a patch existed at time of exploitation, used for local privilege escalation
scopeExcludes: Zero-day kernel exploitation with no patch available (ITID-32111 Windows, ITID-32112 Linux)
Sandbox/container-escape-specific kernel exploitation (ITID-32332)
Hypervisor/VM-escape-specific kernel exploitation (ITID-32333)
ITID-32331.priority: P1 if paired with confirmed initial access, else P2.
ITID-32331.escalation: Escalate to incident command; assume full host compromise given kernel-level access.
indicators: Kernel crash/panic immediately preceding a privilege-escalation event
EDR/IDS signature match for a known kernel-exploitation CVE
vectors: Local exploitation of an unpatched kernel vulnerability following initial unprivileged access
rootCauses: Missed patch management SLA for OS/kernel updates
Legacy or end-of-life kernel versions no longer receiving vendor patches
controls: Patch management SLA enforcement for OS/kernel updates
Kernel hardening mitigations (KASLR, SMEP/SMAP, kernel lockdown)
EDR kernel-level exploitation detection
ITID-32331.detection: Moderate-high once public advisory/IOCs exist for the specific CVE.
ITID-32331.response: Isolate the host, patch the kernel, and investigate the initial-access vector that preceded the local escalation.
metrics: Number of hosts exceeding kernel patch SLA
ITID-32331.notes: Differentiated from the zero-day kernel leaves (ITID-32111/32112) by patch availability at time of exploitation, and from ITID-32332/32333 by not involving a sandbox/container or hypervisor boundary.

playbook.name: Response: Known-CVE Kernel Vulnerability Exploitation (Local Privilege Escalation)
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a known, documented kernel vulnerability on an unpatched system to achieve local privilege escalation.

steps.title: Confirm the exploited CVE via crash/panic and process telemetry
steps.desc: Correlate kernel crash/panic logs, EDR process telemetry showing a SYSTEM/root process spawned from an unprivileged parent, and any available exploit signatures against the known CVE.
steps.outcome: Confirmed CVE and affected host(s).

steps.title: Determine scope of unpatched systems fleet-wide
steps.desc: Identify all systems running the vulnerable kernel version to establish the full at-risk population.
steps.outcome: List of unpatched, at-risk hosts.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host to prevent the now-privileged attacker from moving laterally or expanding access.
steps.outcome: Host isolated.

steps.title: Apply available compensating mitigations to at-risk hosts
steps.desc: Apply any vendor-published workaround (disabling the vulnerable kernel feature/module) to unpatched hosts pending emergency patching.
steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced fleet-wide.

steps.title: Patch the kernel vulnerability fleet-wide
steps.desc: Apply the vendor security patch fixing this CVE across all affected systems on an emergency basis.
steps.outcome: Patch applied fleet-wide.

steps.title: Remove any persistence established with elevated privileges
steps.desc: Check for and remove new privileged accounts, scheduled tasks, or services created during the elevated-access window.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean of privileged persistence.

steps.title: Restore the host to service after verification
steps.desc: Return the patched, verified-clean host to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Host restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review patch-management SLA for kernel updates
steps.desc: Record why the patch wasn't applied before exploitation and recommend a faster emergency-patch process for kernel-level CVEs.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32332.def: Local exploitation of a kernel vulnerability specifically to break out of a sandbox or container isolation boundary, gaining code execution on the underlying host operating system.
ITID-32332.purpose: Captures escape from a sandbox or container to the underlying host via a kernel exploit.
scopeIncludes: Container-escape exploitation of a kernel namespace/cgroup vulnerability
