Application-sandbox escape (e.g., a browser or document-reader sandbox) that pivots through a kernel vulnerability to reach the host OS
scopeExcludes: General known-CVE kernel exploitation not involving a container/sandbox boundary (ITID-32331)
Hypervisor/VM-escape-specific kernel exploitation (ITID-32333, a distinct isolation boundary — virtualization rather than OS-level containment)
ITID-32332.severity: Critical; escape compromises the isolation boundary the environment was specifically designed to rely on.
ITID-32332.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command; assume the host and any co-located containers/tenants are compromised.
indicators: Container runtime logs showing a process escaping its assigned namespace/cgroup boundary
Host-level process activity attributable to a container that should not have host access
Kernel audit log anomaly correlating with a container-escape technique signature
vectors: Exploitation of a kernel namespace isolation vulnerability from within a compromised container
Exploitation of a shared kernel resource (e.g., a device driver exposed to containers) to break isolation
rootCauses: Kernel version running with a known container-escape vulnerability unpatched
Containers granted excessive capabilities/privileges reducing the isolation boundary's effective strength
controls: Least-privilege container capability configuration (avoid privileged containers)
Kernel patch management specific to container-escape CVEs
Runtime container security monitoring (e.g., seccomp/AppArmor profile enforcement and violation alerting)
ITID-32332.detection: Moderate; container runtime security tooling can detect namespace-boundary violations and unexpected host-level activity originating from a container.
ITID-32332.response: Isolate the affected host, assume compromise of all co-located containers, patch the kernel, and audit container capability configurations.
metrics: Number of privileged/excessive-capability containers identified per audit
Time from CVE disclosure to kernel patch on container hosts
ITID-32332.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32333 by isolation boundary type: this leaf is OS-level containment (sandbox/container), while ITID-32333 covers virtualization/hypervisor boundaries.

playbook.name: Response: Sandbox/Container Escape via Kernel Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a kernel vulnerability to escape an application sandbox or container, gaining access to the underlying host beyond the intended isolation boundary.

steps.title: Confirm the escape via host-level telemetry outside the container/sandbox boundary
steps.desc: Review host-level EDR/kernel telemetry for process or file activity originating from a containerized workload but executing outside its expected namespace/cgroup boundary — the primary signal of an escape.
steps.outcome: Confirmed escape event and affected host.

steps.title: Assess broader host and co-located workload exposure
steps.desc: Since escape implies host-level compromise, determine what other containers/workloads share the compromised host and whether they may be affected.
steps.guidance: Treat this as host-level compromise, not container-level — investigate broader than the single escaped container.
steps.outcome: Full host and co-located workload exposure scope established.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host from the cluster/infrastructure
steps.desc: Cordon and isolate the compromised host at the orchestration and network level to prevent lateral movement to other hosts or workloads.
steps.outcome: Host isolated from the broader infrastructure.
steps.tool: Container orchestration platform / network access control

steps.title: Terminate and evacuate co-located workloads
steps.desc: Drain and reschedule other workloads from the compromised host to unaffected infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Co-located workloads relocated to trusted infrastructure.

steps.title: Patch the kernel vulnerability across the infrastructure fleet
steps.desc: Apply the vendor security patch fixing this CVE across all hosts in the fleet on an emergency basis, given the broader infrastructure risk.
steps.outcome: Patch applied fleet-wide.

steps.title: Rebuild the compromised host from a known-good image
steps.desc: Rebuild the affected host from trusted media rather than attempting in-place remediation, given kernel-level compromise undermines host integrity guarantees.
steps.outcome: Host rebuilt clean.

steps.title: Return the rebuilt host to the cluster after verification
steps.desc: Uncordon and reintroduce the patched, verified-clean host to production once validated.
steps.outcome: Host restored to the cluster.

steps.title: Document the incident and review container isolation hardening
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate additional isolation controls (gVisor/Kata, seccomp profiles, kernel hardening) to reduce escape risk.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32333.def: Local exploitation of a hypervisor or virtualization-stack vulnerability to break out of a guest virtual machine's isolation boundary, gaining code execution on the host hypervisor or other co-located guest VMs.
ITID-32333.purpose: Captures escape from a virtual machine to the underlying hypervisor/host via a kernel or hypervisor exploit.
scopeIncludes: Guest-to-host VM escape exploiting a hypervisor vulnerability
Exploitation of a virtual device/driver emulation flaw to break the VM isolation boundary
scopeExcludes: Container/sandbox-escape-specific kernel exploitation (ITID-32332, a distinct isolation boundary — OS-level containment rather than virtualization)
General known-CVE kernel exploitation confined within a single guest OS (ITID-32331)
ITID-32333.severity: Critical; VM escape is one of the most severe possible virtualization security failures, potentially compromising the entire host and all co-located tenants.
ITID-32333.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command and infrastructure/virtualization platform team; treat as a multi-tenant incident requiring assessment of all co-located workloads.
indicators: Hypervisor-level logs showing anomalous guest-to-host boundary activity
Unexpected process execution on the host hypervisor attributable to a specific guest VM
Cross-VM side effects (e.g., one tenant's VM affecting another's) with no legitimate shared-resource explanation
vectors: Exploitation of a virtual device emulation (e.g., virtual NIC, disk controller) vulnerability from within the guest
Exploitation of a hypervisor management-interface vulnerability reachable from a guest VM
rootCauses: Hypervisor/virtualization platform patch lag on a known VM-escape CVE
Overly permissive virtual hardware configuration exposing unnecessary emulated devices to guests
controls: Hypervisor patch management SLA specific to VM-escape CVEs
Minimize emulated virtual hardware/device exposure to guest VMs
Hypervisor-level security monitoring for guest-to-host boundary anomalies
ITID-32333.detection: Low-moderate; hypervisor-level telemetry is often more limited than guest-OS telemetry, making cross-boundary escape harder to detect directly.
ITID-32333.response: Isolate the affected hypervisor host, assume compromise of all co-located guest VMs, patch the virtualization platform, and notify affected tenants if a multi-tenant environment.
metrics: Time from hypervisor CVE disclosure to patch
Number of co-located tenants/workloads assessed post-incident
ITID-32333.notes: ATT&CK does not define a hypervisor-specific escape technique distinct from container escape; T1611 Escape to Host is the closest applicable mapping and is used here to represent the virtualization boundary, differentiated in the definition text and notes from ITID-32332's OS-level container/sandbox scope.

playbook.name: Response: Hypervisor/VM Escape Kernel Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a kernel/hypervisor vulnerability allowing a guest VM to escape isolation and access the underlying hypervisor host. This implies host-level compromise from a guest and requires investigation across the entire virtualization infrastructure, not just the originating VM.

steps.title: Confirm the escape via hypervisor-level telemetry
steps.desc: Review hypervisor management-plane logs and host-level EDR (where deployable) for anomalous activity originating from the guest VM's hypervisor process on the host, or unexpected hypervisor management API calls.
steps.outcome: Confirmed escape event and affected hypervisor host.

steps.title: Assess exposure across the entire virtualization infrastructure
steps.desc: Given VM escape implies host-level compromise, immediately determine every other VM hosted on the same physical host, and every host managed by the same hypervisor management plane, that may be at risk — this is broader than a single-VM incident.
steps.guidance: Do not scope this as a single-VM incident — hypervisor compromise can expose the entire virtualization cluster.
steps.outcome: Full infrastructure-wide exposure scope established.

steps.title: Isolate the affected physical host from the management network and other hosts
steps.desc: Isolate the compromised hypervisor host from the management network and cluster fabric to prevent spread to other hosts or the management plane.
steps.outcome: Compromised host isolated from the broader virtualization infrastructure.
steps.abort: Coordinate migration of unaffected guest VMs before full isolation if feasible.

steps.title: Migrate unaffected VMs and rotate hypervisor management credentials
steps.desc: Live-migrate unaffected guest VMs to verified-clean hosts where possible, and rotate all hypervisor/management-plane credentials given the risk of credential harvesting.
steps.outcome: Unaffected workloads relocated; management credentials rotated.

steps.title: Coordinate with the hypervisor vendor and patch the vulnerability fleet-wide
steps.desc: Engage the hypervisor vendor's security team and apply the emergency patch across the entire virtualization fleet, not just the affected host.
steps.outcome: Vendor engaged; patch applied infrastructure-wide.

steps.title: Rebuild the compromised physical host from trusted media
steps.desc: Reinstall the hypervisor on the affected physical host from verified trusted media, given host-level compromise cannot be reliably remediated in place.
steps.outcome: Host rebuilt clean.

steps.title: Restore the rebuilt host and migrated VMs after verification
steps.desc: Reintroduce the patched, rebuilt host into the cluster and restore normal VM placement once validated.
steps.outcome: Infrastructure restored to normal operation.

steps.title: Conduct an infrastructure-wide post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the incident and review virtualization infrastructure hardening, hypervisor patch cadence, and management-plane segmentation given the severity of this compromise class.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and briefed to infrastructure leadership.

ITID-32334.def: An incident involving local kernel exploitation, not clearly matching a more specific kernel-exploit leaf.
ITID-32334.purpose: Catch-all for kernel exploitation that does not fit known-CVE, container-escape, or hypervisor-escape leaves.
scopeIncludes: Kernel exploitation of unclear specific mechanism
Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf
ITID-32334.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Critical pending classification.
ITID-32334.priority: P1 by default given kernel-level exposure.
ITID-32334.escalation: Reclassify once the specific exploitation mechanism is clarified.
indicators: Kernel-level alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific kernel-exploitation vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32334.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32334.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32334.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Kernel Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a kernel-level vulnerability not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the exploitation via crash/process telemetry
steps.desc: Correlate kernel crash/panic logs and EDR process telemetry showing anomalous privileged activity to confirm exploitation and affected host(s).
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation event and affected host(s).

steps.title: Determine scope across the fleet
steps.desc: Identify all systems running the affected kernel version to establish blast radius.
steps.outcome: List of at-risk hosts.

steps.title: Isolate the affected host(s)
steps.desc: Network-isolate compromised hosts to prevent lateral movement or further exploitation.
steps.outcome: Hosts isolated.

steps.title: Apply available compensating mitigations
steps.desc: Apply any available workaround pending a full patch.
steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced.

steps.title: Patch the kernel vulnerability fleet-wide
steps.desc: Apply the vendor security patch across all affected systems on an emergency basis.
steps.outcome: Patch applied fleet-wide.

steps.title: Rebuild compromised hosts from trusted media if integrity is in question
steps.desc: Given kernel-level compromise can undermine OS integrity guarantees, rebuild confirmed-affected hosts rather than remediating in place.
steps.outcome: Hosts rebuilt clean.

steps.title: Restore hosts to service after verification
steps.desc: Return patched, verified-clean hosts to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Hosts restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review kernel patch-management SLA
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend improvements to kernel patch cadence and detection coverage.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32411.def: A drive-by download in which the malicious exploit payload is served via an advertisement placed through a legitimate ad network — either a compromised legitimate advertiser account or a malicious ad purchased directly — so that visitors to unrelated, otherwise-trustworthy sites are exposed.
ITID-32411.purpose: Captures drive-by download exploitation delivered through a malicious or compromised advertising network.
scopeIncludes: Exploit served via a malicious/compromised ad creative rendered on a third-party publisher's page
Malvertising redirect chain leading to an exploit landing page
scopeExcludes: Drive-by download via direct compromise of the visited website's own content (ITID-32412)
Drive-by download specifically attributable to a browser zero-day where the delivery mechanism (malvertising vs. compromised site) is not the focus (ITID-32413)
ITID-32411.severity: Medium-High; broad, opportunistic reach across many unrelated sites elevates population-level risk even when individual payloads are commodity malware.
ITID-32411.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if a targeted or high-value host is confirmed compromised.
ITID-32411.escalation: Escalate to incident command upon confirmed exploitation; notify the ad network/publisher if internally-owned advertising surfaces are implicated.
indicators: Browser navigating to a known malvertising redirect chain/domain immediately before exploit delivery
EDR/network alert on a known exploit-kit landing page signature
Unusual outbound connection to ad-network infrastructure followed by a secondary payload download
vectors: Malicious ad creative purchased through a legitimate ad exchange to reach broad, untargeted victim traffic
Compromise of a legitimate advertiser's account to inject a malicious ad into an existing campaign
rootCauses: Ad network vetting/verification gaps allowing malicious creatives to be served
Lack of ad-network domain reputation filtering at the network egress layer
controls: Web/DNS filtering blocking known malvertising and exploit-kit domains
Browser exploit mitigation (site isolation, sandboxing)
Ad-blocking/script-blocking browser extensions on managed endpoints
ITID-32411.detection: Moderate; malvertising redirect chains and exploit-kit domains are commonly tracked in threat-intel feeds, enabling web/DNS filtering detection.
ITID-32411.response: Isolate affected endpoints, block the malvertising domain chain, and confirm whether any payload executed successfully.
metrics: Number of malvertising domains blocked at the web/DNS filter per period
detections: Web/DNS filtering alerts on known malvertising infrastructure
ITID-32411.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32412 by delivery channel: this leaf is the ad-network vector specifically, as opposed to direct compromise of the visited site's own content.

playbook.name: Response: Drive-By Download via Malicious/Compromised Ad Network (Malvertising)
playbook.description: For a confirmed drive-by download delivered through a malicious or compromised advertising creative/ad network served on an otherwise trusted page.

steps.title: Confirm the drive-by download and identify the delivering ad creative
steps.desc: Review EDR/browser telemetry to confirm a payload executed and trace the browsing session back to the specific ad tag, ad network, or redirect chain that served it.
steps.guidance: Check referrer chains and ad-slot metadata captured by web proxy logs.
steps.outcome: Payload and delivering ad creative/network identified.
steps.abort: If the ad was blocked or the payload failed to execute, downgrade to a near-miss and skip containment.

steps.title: Identify all users exposed to the same ad campaign
steps.desc: Query proxy/DNS logs for other users who loaded the same malicious ad creative or redirect domain in the relevant time window.
steps.outcome: Full scope of exposed endpoints identified.

steps.title: Isolate all affected endpoints
steps.desc: Network-isolate every endpoint confirmed to have executed the payload.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Block the malicious ad network/redirect domains organization-wide
steps.desc: Add the ad network's serving domains and the full redirect/exploit-kit chain to web-filtering and DNS blocklists.
steps.outcome: Malicious ad infrastructure blocked for all users.

steps.title: Notify the hosting site and ad exchange
steps.desc: Where the legitimate site/ad exchange can be identified, notify them so the malicious creative can be pulled from rotation.
steps.outcome: Site/exchange notified.

steps.title: Remove the payload and check for persistence
steps.desc: Remove the delivered malware from each affected endpoint and verify no persistence mechanism (scheduled task, run key, browser extension) was installed.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and monitor
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review ad-blocking/script-blocking policy
steps.desc: Record the malvertising delivery chain and assess whether stricter ad-blocking, script-blocking, or browser isolation would reduce future exposure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32412.def: A drive-by download in which an attacker has compromised a legitimate website's own infrastructure or content (not an ad network) and silently injected exploit code, so that ordinary visitors are exposed without any visible sign the site was altered.
ITID-32412.purpose: Captures drive-by download exploitation delivered via a silently compromised legitimate website, without visible defacement.
scopeIncludes: Silent injection of exploit/redirect code into a legitimate site's pages, CMS templates, or included scripts
Watering-hole-style compromise where the site itself, not an ad, delivers the exploit
scopeExcludes: Drive-by download via a malicious ad served through an ad network (ITID-32411)
Website defacement incidents with visible content alteration (tracked under a separate website-integrity ITID, not this branch)
ITID-32412.severity: High; silent, non-defacing compromise implies a deliberate and often targeted (watering-hole) intent, and reduces the odds of quick detection via visible symptoms.
ITID-32412.priority: P1 if the compromised site is used for targeted/watering-hole purposes, else P2.
ITID-32412.escalation: Escalate to incident command; if the compromised site belongs to the organization, treat as a website-integrity incident in parallel with the drive-by exposure to visitors.
indicators: Unexpected script tag or iframe injected into a legitimate site's page source not present in the source-controlled version
File integrity monitoring alert on web server content files
Visitors' endpoint security flagging exploitation immediately after visiting a known-legitimate site
vectors: Exploitation of a CMS or plugin vulnerability to inject malicious script into page templates
Compromise of a shared/included third-party JavaScript library referenced by the site
rootCauses: Unpatched CMS/plugin software on the compromised website
Lack of file-integrity monitoring or content-security-policy enforcement on the web property
controls: File integrity monitoring on web server content
Content Security Policy (CSP) restricting script sources
Regular CMS/plugin patch management
ITID-32412.detection: Moderate; file-integrity monitoring and CSP violation reporting are effective when deployed, but detection can lag when neither control is in place.
ITID-32412.response: Remediate the compromised website (identify and remove injected code, patch the underlying vulnerability) and separately assess exposure to visitors who loaded the malicious content.
metrics: Time from injection to detection/removal
Number of visitor sessions exposed during the compromise window
detections: File integrity monitoring on web content
ITID-32412.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32411 by delivery channel (compromised site content vs. ad network) and explicitly excludes visible-defacement incidents, which are a website-integrity concern tracked elsewhere.

playbook.name: Response: Drive-By Download via Compromised Legitimate Website (Non-Defacement Silent Injection)
playbook.description: For a confirmed case of malware delivered via a silent drive-by download on a compromised but otherwise legitimate website the user visited, where the site itself shows no visible defacement.

steps.title: Identify the affected endpoint and confirm the download occurred
steps.desc: Review EDR/browser telemetry to confirm the drive-by download executed and what payload was delivered.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromise with the payload identified.
steps.abort: If the download was blocked/quarantined before execution, downgrade to a near-miss and skip containment.

steps.title: Identify the compromised website and injected script
steps.desc: Determine which legitimate site served the malicious content, locate the injected script/iframe, and notify the site owner/host where feasible.
steps.outcome: Source site and injection point identified; owner notified if reasonably possible.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Network-isolate the endpoint pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated.

steps.title: Block the malicious script source/redirect chain organization-wide
steps.desc: Add the compromised site's malicious script source and redirect chain to the web-filtering blocklist without necessarily blocking the entire legitimate site.
steps.outcome: Malicious payload path blocked for all users.

steps.title: Remove the payload and check for persistence
steps.desc: Remove the delivered malware and verify no persistence mechanism (scheduled task, registry run key, browser extension) was installed.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the endpoint and monitor
steps.desc: Return the endpoint to service and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Endpoint restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review web-filtering coverage
steps.desc: Record the delivery mechanism and assess whether browser-isolation or stricter script-blocking policy would reduce future risk.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32413.def: A drive-by download whose exploit payload leverages a previously unknown, unpatched browser vulnerability, focusing on the delivery-mechanism angle of a browser zero-day already characterized under the Zero-day Exploits branch.
ITID-32413.purpose: Captures drive-by download exploitation where the underlying browser vulnerability is itself a zero-day.
scopeIncludes: Confirmed drive-by delivery (via any site or ad channel) of an exploit chain using an undisclosed browser vulnerability
Cases where the delivery/campaign characteristics (targeting, scale, infrastructure) are the primary investigative focus alongside the underlying zero-day
scopeExcludes: The underlying browser zero-day vulnerability's technical characterization, which is the primary focus of ITID-32122 — this leaf should be used alongside, not instead of, ITID-32122 when both the delivery campaign and the vulnerability itself need tracking
Drive-by download using a known/patched browser CVE (see ITID-32411/32412 depending on delivery channel)
ITID-32413.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command and the browser vendor; coordinate with ITID-32122 tracking for the vulnerability-disclosure angle.
indicators: Browser crash/anomaly with no known CVE match, observed across multiple drive-by delivery campaigns
Exploit-kit infrastructure serving a payload that fails to match any known-CVE signature
vectors: Watering-hole or malvertising delivery of a browser zero-day exploit chain
Targeted delivery of a browser zero-day via a crafted link
rootCauses: Memory-safety defects in the browser's rendering/JS engine (same root cause as ITID-32122)
Delivery infrastructure (compromised site or malvertising) providing the exposure surface
controls: Browser auto-update enforcement
Site isolation / renderer sandboxing
Web/DNS filtering for known delivery infrastructure once identified
ITID-32413.detection: Low pre-disclosure; improves once the vulnerability is publicly characterized and IOCs for the delivery campaign are shared.
ITID-32413.response: Isolate affected endpoints, coordinate with the parallel zero-day vulnerability record (ITID-32122), and hunt for the same delivery infrastructure across the environment.
metrics: Number of endpoints exposed to the same delivery campaign
Time from disclosure to fleet-wide patch
detections: Threat-intel IOC matching for the delivery campaign
ITID-32413.notes: This leaf intentionally overlaps in subject matter with ITID-32122 (Zero-Day in Web Browser) by design: ITID-32122 documents the vulnerability itself, while this leaf documents the drive-by delivery/campaign angle. Log both when both aspects are relevant, to avoid losing either the vulnerability or the campaign context.

playbook.name: Response: Drive-By Download via Browser Zero-Day Exploit
playbook.description: For a confirmed drive-by download that exploited a previously unknown (zero-day) browser vulnerability, where no vendor patch may yet exist.

steps.title: Confirm exploitation of an unpatched browser vulnerability
steps.desc: Review EDR/browser crash and exploitation telemetry, and work with the reverse-engineering/threat-intel function to confirm the technique does not match any known, patched CVE.
steps.guidance: Capture memory artifacts and the exploit payload for analysis before the endpoint is remediated.
steps.outcome: Zero-day exploitation confirmed and technical details captured.
steps.abort: If the technique matches a known patched CVE, reclassify and follow the standard drive-by playbook instead.

steps.title: Identify the vulnerable browser/component and version scope
steps.desc: Determine the exact browser, engine version, and plugin/component exploited, and identify all other endpoints running the same vulnerable version.
steps.outcome: Full population of at-risk endpoints identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint(s)
steps.desc: Network-isolate all endpoints confirmed to have been exploited.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Apply interim mitigation to at-risk endpoints
steps.desc: Where no patch exists, apply compensating controls to the vulnerable population: disable the affected browser feature/plugin, force an alternate browser, or enforce browser isolation for untrusted sites.
steps.outcome: Interim mitigation applied fleet-wide pending a vendor fix.

steps.title: Escalate to the browser vendor and track patch availability
steps.desc: Report the zero-day to the browser vendor (or via coordinated disclosure channel) and open an urgent internal tracking item for the forthcoming patch; treat as a standing risk until resolved.
steps.guidance: This is time-sensitive: no patch may exist yet, so containment must be maintained until one ships.
steps.outcome: Vendor notified; patch-tracking ticket opened with an owner.

steps.title: Remove the payload and check for persistence
steps.desc: Remove the delivered malware and verify no persistence mechanism was installed on each affected endpoint.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore endpoints once patched or mitigated
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service only after the interim mitigation is verified in place or the vendor patch is deployed; apply elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored with mitigation/patch confirmed.

steps.title: Document the zero-day and update patch/mitigation tracking
steps.desc: Record the exploitation technique, mitigation applied, and vendor patch timeline for future reference; confirm patch deployment once released.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and patch deployment tracked to closure.

ITID-32414.def: An incident involving drive-by download exploitation, not clearly matching a more specific drive-by-download leaf.
ITID-32414.purpose: Catch-all for drive-by download exploitation that does not fit malvertising, compromised-website, or browser-zero-day leaves.
scopeIncludes: Drive-by download exploitation of unclear specific delivery mechanism
Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf
ITID-32414.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium-High pending classification.
ITID-32414.escalation: Reclassify once the specific delivery mechanism is clarified.
indicators: Drive-by-download alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific drive-by-download vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32414.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32414.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32414.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Drive-By Download
playbook.description: For a confirmed drive-by download that does not fit a more specific malvertising, compromised-website, or zero-day classification, or where the delivery mechanism has not yet been determined.

steps.title: Confirm the drive-by download and identify the payload
steps.desc: Review EDR/browser telemetry to confirm a download occurred without user-initiated action and identify the delivered payload.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed and payload identified.
steps.abort: If the download was blocked/quarantined before execution, downgrade to a near-miss and skip containment.

steps.title: Determine the delivery source
steps.desc: Trace the browsing session to determine whether the source was a malicious ad, a compromised legitimate site, or another vector, and reclassify to a more specific playbook if one becomes clear.
steps.outcome: Delivery vector identified or confirmed as genuinely unclear.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint
steps.desc: Network-isolate the endpoint pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated.

steps.title: Block the identified malicious domain(s)
steps.desc: Add any identified malicious hosting or redirect domains to the web-filtering blocklist.
steps.outcome: Known-bad domains blocked.

steps.title: Remove the payload and check for persistence
steps.desc: Remove the delivered malware and verify no persistence mechanism was installed.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore the endpoint and monitor
steps.desc: Return the endpoint to service and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Endpoint restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record what is known about the delivery mechanism and payload for future correlation, noting any gaps that prevented more specific classification.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32421.def: A browser extension, installed with legitimate-appearing permissions, that uses those permissions (e.g., broad host access, tab/history read access) beyond its stated purpose to collect and exfiltrate user browsing data, form input, or credentials.
ITID-32421.purpose: Captures a malicious browser extension abusing overly broad permissions to exfiltrate user data.
scopeIncludes: Extension exfiltrating browsing history, form data, or session data to an external server without disclosed purpose
Extension whose stated functionality does not require the scope of data it is observed collecting
scopeExcludes: Extension used specifically as a remote code execution/C2 channel (ITID-32422)
Extension exploiting a cross-origin or sandbox vulnerability rather than abusing its own granted permissions (ITID-32423)
ITID-32421.severity: Medium-High, depending on the sensitivity of exfiltrated data and scale of installation.
ITID-32421.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials or sensitive business data are confirmed exfiltrated.
ITID-32421.escalation: Escalate to incident command upon confirmation; force removal via browser management policy across affected endpoints.
indicators: Extension making outbound network connections to infrastructure unrelated to its stated function
Browser network log showing tab/history/form data transmitted to an external domain
Extension permission scope inconsistent with its documented feature set
vectors: Extension published with legitimate functionality that is later updated (post-installation) to add malicious data-collection behavior
Extension acquired by a new owner who repurposes its existing user base for data harvesting
rootCauses: Insufficient enterprise extension vetting/allowlisting policy
Browser extension auto-update behavior allowing malicious functionality to be pushed after initial vetting
controls: Enterprise browser extension allowlisting policy
Network egress monitoring for anomalous extension-originated traffic
Periodic re-review of previously-approved extensions for permission/behavior drift
ITID-32421.detection: Moderate; network egress monitoring can surface anomalous extension traffic, though attribution to a specific extension requires browser-level telemetry.
ITID-32421.response: Force-remove the extension via browser management policy, assess scope of data already exfiltrated, and notify affected users if sensitive data was involved.
metrics: Number of endpoints with the malicious extension installed at time of discovery
detections: Network egress monitoring for extension-originated traffic
ITID-32421.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32422/32423 by mechanism: this leaf covers abuse of the extension's own granted permissions rather than use as a C2 channel or exploitation of a technical vulnerability.

playbook.name: Response: Browser Extension Abusing Overly Broad Permissions for Data Exfiltration
playbook.description: For a browser extension confirmed to be exfiltrating data (browsing history, form data, session content) via permissions broader than its stated function requires.

steps.title: Confirm the extension and the data being exfiltrated
steps.desc: Review browser/EDR telemetry to identify the extension, its granted permissions, and the destination(s) receiving exfiltrated data.
steps.guidance: Check extension manifest permissions against its stated purpose.
steps.outcome: Extension identified, exfiltrated data types and destination confirmed.
steps.abort: If the extension is confirmed legitimate with justified permissions, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Identify all users with the extension installed
steps.desc: Query the browser/endpoint management console for the full population of users with the extension installed and active.
steps.outcome: Full affected-user population identified.

steps.title: Force-remove or disable the extension fleet-wide
steps.desc: Push a policy to disable and remove the extension across all managed browsers, and add it to a blocklist to prevent reinstallation.
steps.outcome: Extension removed and blocked organization-wide.

steps.title: Block the exfiltration destination
steps.desc: Block the C2/exfiltration domain or endpoint at the network/DNS layer.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration channel blocked.

steps.title: Invalidate exposed sessions and credentials
steps.desc: Determine what session tokens, cookies, or form data were exposed and force-expire affected sessions; require password resets where credentials may have been captured.
steps.outcome: Exposed sessions/credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Restore normal browsing and monitor for reinstallation
steps.desc: Confirm affected endpoints are clean and monitor for attempted reinstallation of the extension or use of a rebranded clone.
steps.outcome: No recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review extension governance policy
steps.desc: Record findings and assess whether extension allow-listing or stricter permission review would prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32422.def: A browser extension that provides an attacker with a persistent remote-control channel — receiving commands from and sending results to an external server — effectively functioning as a lightweight C2 implant running inside the browser.
ITID-32422.purpose: Captures a malicious browser extension used as a remote code execution or command-and-control channel.
scopeIncludes: Extension polling an external server for commands and executing them within or via the browser
Extension used to proxy attacker traffic or execute arbitrary script on attacker instruction
scopeExcludes: Extension abusing broad permissions purely for passive data exfiltration without a command channel (ITID-32421)
Extension exploiting a cross-origin/sandbox vulnerability as its primary mechanism (ITID-32423)
ITID-32422.severity: Critical; a persistent, interactively-controlled C2 channel inside the browser represents an active, ongoing compromise.
ITID-32422.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command; treat as an active intrusion requiring full incident response, not just extension removal.
indicators: Extension establishing periodic beaconing connections to an external command server
Extension executing dynamically-fetched script content (eval-style execution) inconsistent with its stated function
Browser process behavior consistent with remote-command execution (e.g., unexpected tab manipulation, form submission)
vectors: Extension deliberately designed and distributed as a C2 implant disguised as a useful tool
Legitimate extension compromised/updated by an attacker to add C2 beaconing functionality
rootCauses: Insufficient enterprise extension vetting/allowlisting policy
Lack of monitoring for anomalous extension network beaconing behavior
mitreTechniques: T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
controls: Enterprise browser extension allowlisting policy
Network egress monitoring/beaconing detection for extension-originated traffic
EDR/browser telemetry for extension-driven script execution
ITID-32422.detection: Moderate; beaconing-pattern network detection is effective once the C2 infrastructure is identified or matches known patterns.
ITID-32422.response: Treat as an active C2 compromise: isolate affected endpoints, force-remove the extension, block the C2 infrastructure, and investigate for further attacker activity conducted via the channel.
metrics: Number of endpoints with confirmed C2 beaconing via the extension
Dwell time before detection
detections: Network beaconing detection for extension-originated traffic
ITID-32422.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32421 by the presence of an active, interactive command channel rather than passive data collection.

playbook.name: Response: Browser Extension Used as Remote Code Execution/C2 Channel
playbook.description: For a browser extension confirmed to be executing attacker-supplied code or acting as a command-and-control channel on the host.

steps.title: Confirm the extension is executing remote code or acting as a C2 channel
steps.desc: Review EDR telemetry for unusual process activity spawned from the browser process and correlate with the suspect extension; identify the C2 infrastructure being contacted.
steps.outcome: Extension confirmed as an active RCE/C2 vector with C2 infrastructure identified.
steps.abort: If no code execution or C2 traffic is observed, downgrade to the broad-permissions exfiltration playbook.

steps.title: Determine scope of compromise on the host and network
steps.desc: Determine whether the extension achieved persistence beyond the browser, moved laterally, or granted further access, and identify all endpoints with the extension installed.
steps.outcome: Full scope of host and network impact established.

steps.title: Isolate all affected endpoints immediately
steps.desc: Network-isolate every endpoint with the extension installed or showing related C2 activity.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Block the C2 infrastructure and remove the extension fleet-wide
steps.desc: Block the C2 domains/IPs at the network layer and push a policy to disable/remove the extension across all managed browsers.
steps.outcome: C2 blocked; extension removed organization-wide.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate any credentials/tokens exposed on affected hosts
steps.desc: Given the RCE capability, treat the host as fully compromised and rotate any credentials, tokens, or session cookies accessible from it.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Remove all persistence and rebuild affected endpoints
steps.desc: Given confirmed code execution, remove any secondary persistence mechanisms found and rebuild/reimage affected endpoints rather than relying solely on cleanup.
steps.outcome: Endpoints rebuilt or confirmed fully clean.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and apply elevated monitoring
steps.desc: Return rebuilt endpoints to service and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review extension vetting/allow-listing
steps.desc: Record the full attack chain and assess whether extension allow-listing, code-signing requirements, or browser isolation would prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32423.def: Exploitation of a technical vulnerability in a browser extension's implementation (e.g., a content-script injection flaw or improper origin isolation) that allows the extension — or a malicious web page abusing the extension — to bypass the browser's same-origin or sandbox boundaries.
ITID-32423.purpose: Captures exploitation of a cross-origin isolation or sandbox-bypass vulnerability within a browser extension.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a vulnerable (not necessarily malicious-by-design) extension's content-script isolation flaw to escalate access across origins
A malicious web page abusing a legitimate but vulnerable extension's exposed messaging interface to bypass sandbox restrictions
scopeExcludes: An extension that is malicious by design and abusing its own granted permissions (ITID-32421) or acting as a C2 channel (ITID-32422), where the extension itself is the threat rather than a vulnerability being exploited within it
ITID-32423.severity: High-Critical, depending on what cross-origin access or sandbox escape is achieved.
ITID-32423.priority: P1 if sandbox escape to the underlying OS is achieved, else P2 for cross-origin-only impact.
ITID-32423.escalation: Escalate to incident command and the extension developer/browser vendor for coordinated disclosure.
indicators: Browser console/security errors indicating cross-origin access outside the extension's declared permissions
EDR alert on an extension-mediated process achieving unexpected privilege beyond the browser sandbox
vectors: Malicious web page sending crafted messages to a vulnerable extension's content script to trigger the isolation flaw
Exploitation of an extension's native-messaging host to reach outside the browser sandbox entirely
rootCauses: Insecure content-script message-handling logic failing to validate the origin of incoming messages
Overly permissive native-messaging host configuration bridging the browser sandbox to the OS
controls: Extension code review/vetting for content-script message-origin validation
Restricting or disabling native-messaging host capability for enterprise-deployed extensions
Browser site-isolation enforcement
ITID-32423.detection: Low-moderate; requires browser-level security telemetry or vendor disclosure to identify the specific flaw being exploited.
ITID-32423.response: Disable the vulnerable extension pending a fix, report the flaw to the developer/vendor, and audit for evidence of exploitation.
metrics: Number of extensions identified with content-script isolation weaknesses per review cycle
ITID-32423.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32421/32422 by mechanism: this leaf is a technical vulnerability being exploited within (or via) an extension, rather than an extension that is itself malicious by design.

playbook.name: Response: Browser Extension Exploiting Cross-Origin/Sandbox Bypass Vulnerability
playbook.description: For a browser extension confirmed to be exploiting a cross-origin isolation or browser sandbox bypass vulnerability to access data or capabilities outside its intended scope.

steps.title: Confirm the sandbox/cross-origin bypass and affected scope
steps.desc: Review browser security telemetry and extension behavior to confirm the extension accessed data or origins outside its declared permission boundary via a sandbox or cross-origin isolation bypass.
steps.outcome: Bypass confirmed with the specific vulnerability and accessed scope identified.
steps.abort: If the behavior is within the extension's declared permissions, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Identify what cross-origin data was accessed
steps.desc: Determine which sites, sessions, or origin-isolated data the extension was able to read or manipulate as a result of the bypass.
steps.outcome: Scope of exposed data determined.

steps.title: Force-remove the extension fleet-wide
steps.desc: Push a policy to disable and remove the extension across all managed browsers and blocklist it to prevent reinstallation.
steps.outcome: Extension removed and blocked organization-wide.

steps.title: Invalidate sessions for any cross-origin data exposed
steps.desc: Force-expire sessions or tokens for any site/service whose isolation was bypassed.
steps.outcome: Exposed sessions invalidated.

steps.title: Confirm the underlying browser vulnerability status
steps.desc: Determine whether the sandbox/cross-origin bypass exploits a known, patchable browser vulnerability and confirm the patch level of affected endpoints.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability identified and patch status confirmed.

steps.title: Restore normal browsing after patching
steps.desc: Confirm affected endpoints are patched or mitigated before returning to normal browsing, and monitor for related activity.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored with vulnerability addressed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review extension vetting policy
steps.desc: Record the bypass technique and assess whether extension allow-listing, stricter sandboxing policy, or browser patching cadence would prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32424.def: An incident involving a malicious or vulnerable browser extension exploited for security-relevant impact, not clearly matching a more specific extension-exploit leaf.
ITID-32424.purpose: Catch-all for malicious browser extension security exploits that do not fit permission-abuse, C2-channel, or sandbox-bypass leaves.
scopeIncludes: Browser extension security exploitation of unclear specific mechanism
Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf
ITID-32424.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium-High pending classification.
ITID-32424.escalation: Reclassify once the specific exploitation mechanism is clarified.
indicators: Browser extension alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific extension vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32424.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32424.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32424.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Malicious Browser Extension (Security Exploit)
playbook.description: For a browser extension confirmed to be malicious or exploiting a security vulnerability, that does not fit a more specific broad-permissions-exfiltration, RCE/C2, or sandbox-bypass classification.

steps.title: Confirm the extension's malicious behavior
steps.desc: Review browser/EDR telemetry to confirm the extension is behaving maliciously and characterize the behavior (data access, network activity, code execution).
steps.outcome: Malicious behavior confirmed and characterized; reclassify to a more specific playbook if the behavior becomes clear.
steps.abort: If the extension is confirmed benign, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Identify all users with the extension installed
steps.desc: Query the browser/endpoint management console for the full population of users with the extension installed.
steps.outcome: Full affected-user population identified.

steps.title: Force-remove the extension fleet-wide
steps.desc: Push a policy to disable and remove the extension across all managed browsers and blocklist it to prevent reinstallation.
steps.outcome: Extension removed and blocked organization-wide.

steps.title: Block any identified malicious network destinations
steps.desc: Block any C2 or exfiltration domains/IPs associated with the extension.
steps.outcome: Malicious infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Assess and remediate any residual impact
steps.desc: Determine whether any data was exposed or persistence achieved beyond the extension itself, and remediate accordingly.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore normal browsing and monitor
steps.desc: Confirm affected endpoints are clean and monitor for reinstallation attempts.
steps.outcome: No recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review extension governance policy
steps.desc: Record findings and assess whether extension allow-listing would reduce future risk.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32431.def: Exploitation of a web application flaw that reflects unsanitized user input back into an immediate HTTP response, causing attacker-supplied script to execute in the victim's browser when they follow a crafted link or submit a crafted request.
ITID-32431.purpose: Captures exploitation of a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a reflected XSS vulnerability via a crafted URL or form submission delivered to the victim
Confirmed script execution in a victim's browser session resulting from unsanitized request-parameter reflection
scopeExcludes: Stored/persistent XSS where the payload is saved server-side and served to subsequent visitors (ITID-32432)
DOM-based XSS where the vulnerability is purely client-side script logic, with no server round-trip of the payload (ITID-32433)
Cases where the sole confirmed impact is session-token/cookie theft — track under ITID-32434 in addition when that is the specific outcome
ITID-32431.severity: Medium-High; requires victim interaction (following a crafted link), limiting but not eliminating real-world impact.
ITID-32431.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if used against high-value/privileged users or paired with credential/session theft.
ITID-32431.escalation: Escalate to the application owner and incident command upon confirmation of successful exploitation (not just a vulnerability finding).
indicators: Web server access logs showing script-tag/event-handler payloads in request parameters
WAF alert on a reflected-XSS signature pattern
Victim report of unexpected browser behavior after following a link from an untrusted source
vectors: Phishing email or message containing a crafted link with an embedded XSS payload targeting a vulnerable application endpoint
Malicious link posted in a public forum or comment referencing the vulnerable application
rootCauses: Insufficient output encoding of user-supplied input reflected into HTML responses
Lack of a Content Security Policy mitigating script execution impact
mitreTechniques: T1059.007 Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
controls: Context-aware output encoding on all reflected user input
Content Security Policy (CSP) restricting inline script execution
WAF rules for common XSS payload patterns
ITID-32431.detection: Moderate; WAF and access-log pattern matching for known XSS payload structures is well-established, though novel encoding/obfuscation can evade signatures.
ITID-32431.response: Patch the output-encoding flaw, assess whether any victims were confirmed exploited (not just targeted), and review for session/data impact.
metrics: Number of confirmed reflected-XSS exploitation events vs. blocked attempts
ITID-32431.notes: Differentiated from stored (ITID-32432) and DOM-based (ITID-32433) siblings by the payload being reflected in an immediate server response rather than stored or purely client-side.

playbook.name: Response: Reflected XSS Exploitation
playbook.description: For a confirmed exploitation of a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability against a user, typically delivered via a crafted link.

steps.title: Confirm the reflected XSS payload and delivery vector
steps.desc: Review web application/WAF logs and the crafted URL/link to confirm the reflected XSS payload executed in the victim's browser and identify the vulnerable parameter.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable parameter and payload confirmed.
steps.abort: If the payload was blocked by the WAF/browser XSS filter, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Determine what the payload accomplished
steps.desc: Determine whether the payload achieved session/cookie theft, credential harvesting, or another action, and identify all users who clicked the malicious link.
steps.outcome: Impact and affected-user population determined.

steps.title: Invalidate affected sessions
steps.desc: Force-expire sessions/cookies for any user confirmed to have been exposed to the payload.
steps.outcome: Affected sessions invalidated.

steps.title: Block the malicious link/domain and add a WAF rule
steps.desc: Block the distribution domain/link at the email or web gateway and deploy a virtual patch/WAF rule for the vulnerable parameter.
steps.outcome: Distribution vector blocked; interim WAF mitigation in place.

steps.title: Remediate the vulnerable code
steps.desc: Work with the application owner to patch the vulnerable parameter with proper output encoding/input validation.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability patched and verified.

steps.title: Verify the fix and remove interim mitigations
steps.desc: Confirm the patched application is no longer vulnerable to the payload, then remove the temporary WAF rule if no longer needed.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability confirmed remediated.

steps.title: Document the incident and review secure-coding practices
steps.desc: Record the vulnerability and assess whether broader input-validation/output-encoding review across the application is warranted.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32432.def: Exploitation of a web application flaw that permanently stores unsanitized user input (e.g., in a comment, profile field, or message) which is later served to other users, causing attacker-supplied script to execute in every subsequent visitor's browser without requiring a crafted link.
ITID-32432.purpose: Captures exploitation of a stored/persistent cross-site scripting vulnerability.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a stored XSS vulnerability via a malicious submission (comment, profile, upload metadata) later rendered to other users
Persistent payload confirmed to have executed in the browser sessions of multiple subsequent visitors
scopeExcludes: Reflected XSS requiring a crafted link/request per victim (ITID-32431)
DOM-based XSS with no server-side storage of the payload (ITID-32433)
ITID-32432.severity: High-Critical; no per-victim interaction with a crafted link is required, so impact scales to every visitor of the affected page until remediated.
ITID-32432.priority: P1 given the self-propagating, broad-reach exposure to all visitors.
ITID-32432.escalation: Escalate immediately to the application owner and incident command; remove the stored payload as the first containment action.
indicators: Malicious script payload found stored in application data (database record, uploaded file metadata)
Multiple distinct users reporting unexpected browser behavior when viewing the same page/content
Application logs showing the same payload rendered across many distinct user sessions
vectors: Submission of a malicious payload into a public-facing input field that is stored and rendered to other users without sanitization
Upload of a file whose metadata (filename, embedded fields) is rendered unsanitized elsewhere in the application
rootCauses: Insufficient input validation/output encoding at both the storage and rendering points
Lack of a Content Security Policy mitigating script execution impact
mitreTechniques: T1059.007 Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
controls: Input validation and context-aware output encoding at both storage and render points
Content Security Policy (CSP) restricting inline script execution
Regular content/audit scanning of user-generated content stores for embedded script payloads
ITID-32432.detection: Moderate; scanning stored content for script-payload patterns and monitoring for widespread identical browser-side symptoms across users is effective once instrumented.
ITID-32432.response: Remove the stored payload immediately, patch the input-validation/output-encoding flaw, and assess the number of visitors exposed during the exposure window.
metrics: Number of visitors exposed to the stored payload before removal
Time from payload storage to detection/removal
ITID-32432.notes: Differentiated from reflected (ITID-32431) and DOM-based (ITID-32433) siblings by the payload being persistently stored server-side and served to multiple subsequent visitors.

playbook.name: Response: Stored/Persistent XSS Exploitation
playbook.description: For a confirmed exploitation of a stored/persistent cross-site scripting vulnerability, where a malicious script was saved server-side and executes for any user viewing the affected content.

steps.title: Confirm the stored payload and locate where it persists
steps.desc: Confirm the malicious script is stored server-side (e.g. in a comment, profile field, or record) and identify every location/page where it renders.
steps.outcome: Stored payload located and rendering scope determined.
steps.abort: If the payload was sanitized on output and never executed, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify all users exposed to the stored payload
steps.desc: Determine which users viewed the affected content while the payload was live, since stored XSS affects every viewer, not just the original submitter.
steps.outcome: Full affected-user population identified.

steps.title: Remove or neutralize the stored payload immediately
steps.desc: Delete or sanitize the malicious stored content at the database/application layer to stop further execution against new viewers.
steps.outcome: Payload no longer renders for any user.

steps.title: Invalidate sessions for all exposed users
steps.desc: Force-expire sessions/cookies for every user who viewed the affected content while the payload was active.
steps.outcome: Exposed sessions invalidated.

steps.title: Remediate the vulnerable input/output handling
steps.desc: Work with the application owner to patch the input validation and output encoding at the point where the payload was originally stored.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability patched and verified.

steps.title: Audit for additional stored payloads
steps.desc: Search other user-generated content fields for similar injected payloads that may not yet have triggered.
steps.outcome: No further malicious stored content found, or additional instances remediated.

steps.title: Verify the fix and restore normal operation
steps.desc: Confirm the patched application rejects/sanitizes the payload and restore full functionality.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability confirmed remediated.

steps.title: Document the incident and review content-sanitization practices
steps.desc: Record the vulnerability and assess whether broader review of user-generated-content handling is warranted across the application.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32433.def: Exploitation of a client-side JavaScript flaw in which unsanitized data (e.g., from the URL fragment, document.referrer, or local storage) is written into the DOM in an unsafe way entirely within the browser, without the payload ever being sent to or reflected by the server.
ITID-32433.purpose: Captures exploitation of a DOM-based cross-site scripting vulnerability.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a client-side sink (e.g., innerHTML, document.write) processing unsanitized data from a client-side source (URL fragment, window.name)
Payloads that never appear in server access logs because the vulnerable code path is entirely client-side
scopeExcludes: Reflected XSS where the server processes and reflects the payload in its response (ITID-32431)
Stored XSS where the payload is persisted server-side (ITID-32432)
ITID-32433.severity: Medium-High; requires victim interaction similar to reflected XSS, but server-side logs/WAF may not observe the payload at all.
ITID-32433.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if used against high-value/privileged users.
ITID-32433.escalation: Escalate to the application owner and incident command upon confirmation of successful exploitation.
indicators: Browser-side JavaScript error/console log referencing an unsafe DOM sink
Victim report of unexpected browser behavior after following a crafted link, with no corresponding server access-log evidence of the payload
Client-side security scanning tool flagging an unsafe source-to-sink data flow
vectors: Crafted URL fragment (after the #) processed unsafely by client-side JavaScript and written into the DOM
Malicious value in window.name or local/session storage processed unsafely by client-side code
rootCauses: Client-side JavaScript writing untrusted data into the DOM via unsafe sinks without sanitization
Lack of client-side security code review/SAST coverage for DOM-manipulation code paths
mitreTechniques: T1059.007 Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
controls: Client-side input sanitization before any DOM-sink write
Content Security Policy (CSP) restricting inline script execution
Client-side SAST/DAST scanning for unsafe source-to-sink data flows
ITID-32433.detection: Low; because the payload does not necessarily traverse the server, traditional WAF/access-log detection is ineffective — detection depends on client-side security tooling or victim-reported symptoms.
ITID-32433.response: Patch the client-side JavaScript sanitization flaw, and note that server-side WAF logs are unlikely to show direct evidence — rely on browser-side telemetry where available.
metrics: Number of confirmed DOM-XSS exploitation events identified via client-side telemetry
ITID-32433.notes: Differentiated from reflected (ITID-32431) and stored (ITID-32432) siblings specifically by the vulnerability existing entirely in client-side code, with no server round-trip of the payload — this materially changes the detection approach (client-side tooling vs. WAF/access logs).

playbook.name: Response: DOM-Based XSS Exploitation
playbook.description: For a confirmed exploitation of a DOM-based cross-site scripting vulnerability, where the malicious payload never reaches the server and executes entirely client-side via unsafe DOM manipulation.

steps.title: Confirm the DOM-based payload and vulnerable client-side code
steps.desc: Review browser telemetry and the affected page's client-side JavaScript to confirm the payload executed via unsafe DOM sink (e.g. innerHTML, document.write, eval) rather than server-side reflection or storage.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable sink and payload confirmed.
steps.abort: If the payload was neutralized by the browser or a CSP, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify affected users and delivery mechanism
steps.desc: Determine how the malicious URL/fragment reached victims (link, redirect) and identify all users who loaded it.
steps.outcome: Affected-user population and delivery vector identified.

steps.title: Invalidate affected sessions
steps.desc: Force-expire sessions/cookies for users confirmed exposed to the payload.
steps.outcome: Affected sessions invalidated.

steps.title: Deploy an interim CSP or block the malicious link
steps.desc: Tighten Content-Security-Policy to block inline script execution as a stopgap, and block the distribution link/domain at the gateway.
steps.outcome: Interim mitigation in place; distribution vector blocked.

steps.title: Remediate the unsafe DOM sink
steps.desc: Work with the application owner to replace the unsafe DOM sink with safe DOM APIs and proper sanitization of untrusted input.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability patched and verified.

steps.title: Verify the fix and restore normal operation
steps.desc: Confirm the patched page no longer executes the payload and restore full functionality.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability confirmed remediated.

steps.title: Document the incident and review client-side coding practices
steps.desc: Record the vulnerability and assess whether a stricter CSP or DOM-sink audit across the application is warranted.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32434.def: Cross-site scripting exploitation (of any injection type — reflected, stored, or DOM-based) whose specific, confirmed outcome is the theft of a victim's session token or cookie, enabling session hijacking distinct from the general script-execution event itself.
ITID-32434.purpose: Captures cross-site scripting exploitation whose confirmed impact is theft of a session token or cookie.
scopeIncludes: XSS payload specifically designed to read and exfiltrate document.cookie or an application session token to an attacker-controlled endpoint
Confirmed session hijacking (attacker using the stolen token/cookie to access the victim's account) following XSS exploitation
scopeExcludes: XSS exploitation where no session/cookie theft is confirmed (log under the applicable injection-type leaf — ITID-32431/32432/32433 — instead)
Session/cookie theft achieved via a mechanism other than XSS (e.g., network interception, malware) — out of scope for this branch entirely
ITID-32434.severity: Critical; direct account-takeover impact via stolen session credentials.
ITID-32434.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident command; invalidate the stolen session/token and force victim re-authentication.
indicators: XSS payload containing document.cookie or session-storage read logic followed by an exfiltration request
Application session used from a source IP/device inconsistent with the legitimate user immediately after XSS exploitation
Application logs showing session-token reuse from an unexpected location
vectors: XSS payload that reads the session cookie/token and sends it to an attacker-controlled collection endpoint
XSS payload that directly performs authenticated actions on the victim's behalf (session riding) rather than exfiltrating the token itself
rootCauses: Session cookies not flagged HttpOnly, allowing JavaScript access
Lack of secondary session-binding controls (e.g., IP/device fingerprint checks) that would limit the value of a stolen token
mitreTechniques: T1059.007 Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
controls: HttpOnly and Secure flags on all session cookies
Session binding to additional signals (IP/device fingerprint) with re-authentication on mismatch
Content Security Policy (CSP) restricting script execution/exfiltration destinations
ITID-32434.detection: Moderate; session-anomaly detection (impossible travel, device mismatch) can catch the resulting hijacking even if the originating XSS payload itself evades detection.
ITID-32434.response: Invalidate the stolen session/token immediately, force re-authentication, patch the underlying XSS vulnerability, and audit actions taken during the hijacked session.
metrics: Number of confirmed session hijackings via XSS per period
Time from theft to session invalidation
detections: Session anomaly detection (impossible travel, device mismatch)
ITID-32434.notes: This leaf is an outcome-based cross-cut of the injection-type leaves (ITID-32431/32432/32433): log the injection-type leaf for the vulnerability class, and additionally log this leaf when session/cookie theft is the confirmed specific impact, to avoid losing either dimension.

playbook.name: Response: XSS Used for Session Token/Cookie Theft
playbook.description: For an XSS exploit (of any variant) confirmed to have been used specifically to steal session tokens or cookies, enabling account/session takeover.

steps.title: Confirm token/cookie theft and identify the exfiltration destination
steps.desc: Review application and network logs to confirm the XSS payload exfiltrated session tokens/cookies and identify the destination that received them.
steps.outcome: Confirmed theft with destination and stolen token scope identified.

steps.title: Identify accounts with stolen sessions and check for takeover activity
steps.desc: Determine which accounts had tokens/cookies stolen and check for evidence the attacker already used them (logins from new locations/devices, unauthorized actions).
steps.outcome: Affected accounts identified; any takeover activity scoped.

steps.title: Force-expire all stolen sessions immediately
steps.desc: Revoke the stolen session tokens/cookies at the identity provider or application session store without delay, given the risk of active account takeover.
steps.outcome: Stolen sessions invalidated.

steps.title: Force password reset and re-authentication (including MFA) for affected accounts
steps.desc: Require affected users to reset credentials and re-enroll/re-verify MFA before regaining access.
steps.outcome: Affected accounts secured with new credentials.

steps.title: Block the exfiltration destination
steps.desc: Block the domain/endpoint that received the stolen tokens at the network layer.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration channel blocked.

steps.title: Remediate the underlying XSS vulnerability
steps.desc: Patch the XSS vulnerability that enabled the theft (reflected, stored, or DOM-based) at its source.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability patched and verified.

steps.title: Review any unauthorized actions taken with stolen sessions
steps.desc: Audit affected accounts for unauthorized changes or data access made during the exposure window and revert/remediate as needed.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized actions identified and remediated.

steps.title: Restore accounts and apply elevated monitoring
steps.desc: Return accounts to normal use and monitor for further suspicious activity for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Accounts restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review session-security controls
steps.desc: Record findings and assess whether HttpOnly/Secure cookie flags, shorter session lifetimes, or additional CSP hardening would reduce future risk.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32435.def: An incident involving cross-site scripting exploitation, not clearly matching a more specific XSS-type leaf.
ITID-32435.purpose: Catch-all for XSS exploitation that does not fit reflected, stored, DOM-based, or session-theft leaves.
scopeIncludes: XSS exploitation of unclear specific injection type
Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling leaf
ITID-32435.severity: Reassess once more detail is available; treat as Medium-High pending classification.
ITID-32435.escalation: Reclassify once the specific injection type is clarified.
indicators: XSS alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Activity of unclear specific XSS vector
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
mitreTechniques: T1059.007 Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
controls: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32435.detection: Same general telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32435.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32435.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General XSS Exploit
playbook.description: For a confirmed cross-site scripting exploit that does not fit a more specific reflected, stored, DOM-based, or session-theft classification.

steps.title: Confirm the XSS exploit and its variant
steps.desc: Review application/WAF logs and browser telemetry to confirm the payload executed and determine which XSS variant is involved; reclassify to a more specific playbook if it becomes clear.
steps.outcome: Exploit confirmed; variant identified or confirmed as genuinely unclear.
steps.abort: If the payload was blocked, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Determine impact and affected users
steps.desc: Determine what the payload accomplished and identify all affected users.
steps.outcome: Impact and affected-user population determined.

steps.title: Invalidate affected sessions
steps.desc: Force-expire sessions/cookies for any exposed user as a precaution.
steps.outcome: Affected sessions invalidated.

steps.title: Apply an interim WAF rule or CSP mitigation
steps.desc: Deploy a virtual patch or tighten CSP to prevent further exploitation while root cause is investigated.
steps.outcome: Interim mitigation in place.

steps.title: Remediate the underlying vulnerability
steps.desc: Work with the application owner to patch the input validation/output encoding weakness.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability patched and verified.

steps.title: Verify the fix and restore normal operation
steps.desc: Confirm the patched application is no longer vulnerable and restore full functionality.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability confirmed remediated.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings and assess whether broader secure-coding review is warranted.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32511.def: Exploitation of weaknesses in DNS response validation (e.g., predictable transaction IDs, lack of DNSSEC, race-condition response injection) to insert a forged record into a resolver's cache, causing subsequent lookups for a legitimate domain to resolve to an attacker-controlled IP.
ITID-32511.purpose: Captures an adversary forging DNS responses or poisoning a resolver's cache to redirect victims to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
scopeIncludes: Forged DNS response injection exploiting weak transaction-ID randomization
Cache-poisoning attacks against recursive resolvers lacking DNSSEC validation
Birthday-attack style flooding of a resolver with forged responses
scopeExcludes: DNS tunneling for exfiltration/C2 (ITID-32513)
DNS amplification DDoS abuse (ITID-32514)
Zone transfer information disclosure (ITID-32512)
ITID-32511.severity: High — successful poisoning silently redirects victim traffic, enabling credential theft or malware delivery.
ITID-32511.priority: P1 if a production resolver is confirmed poisoned; P2 for detected but unsuccessful attempts.
ITID-32511.escalation: Escalate immediately to network/DNS admins to flush cache and to SOC to assess downstream redirection impact.
indicators: Unexpected TTL or IP change for a well-known internal or external domain
Resolver logs showing an anomalous spike in query responses for one domain from an unexpected source
Client connections to a known-legitimate hostname resolving to an unfamiliar IP range
vectors: Flooding a resolver with spoofed UDP responses guessing the query ID
Exploiting a resolver without source-port randomization
Man-in-the-middle position injecting forged responses on the wire
rootCauses: Resolver lacking DNSSEC validation
Predictable or non-randomized DNS transaction IDs/source ports
Resolver accepting glue records from untrusted authoritative servers
controls: DNSSEC validation on all recursive resolvers
Source port and transaction ID randomization
DNS response rate limiting
ITID-32511.detection: Resolver query/response logs and TTL-anomaly monitoring provide a strong technical signal; DNSSEC failures are directly loggable.
ITID-32511.response: Flush the poisoned cache entry, isolate the resolver, and identify any client traffic already redirected during the exposure window.
metrics: Count of confirmed cache-poisoning events per quarter
Mean time to cache flush after detection
ITID-32511.notes: Scoped to cache/response-forgery attacks against the DNS resolution mechanism itself. DNS tunneling (data channel abuse) is ITID-32513; volumetric amplification abuse is ITID-32514.

playbook.name: Response: DNS Cache Poisoning Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a DNS cache poisoning attack, where a resolver's cache was populated with forged DNS responses to redirect traffic to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

steps.title: Confirm poisoned cache entries via DNS resolver logs
steps.desc: Review DNS resolver query/response logs for records that resolve to unexpected or known-malicious IP addresses, and confirm the entries do not match authoritative records.
steps.outcome: Confirmed poisoned records and affected resolver(s).

steps.title: Identify clients that queried the poisoned records
steps.desc: Determine which internal clients resolved and connected to the malicious IP addresses via the poisoned cache entries, to scope downstream compromise.
steps.outcome: List of affected clients.
steps.tool: DNS query logs / network flow logs

steps.title: Flush the poisoned cache entries
steps.desc: Immediately flush the affected DNS resolver's cache to remove the forged records.
