steps.outcome: Poisoned entries removed.

steps.title: Isolate clients that connected to malicious infrastructure
steps.desc: Network-isolate any client confirmed to have connected to the attacker-controlled IP address for further investigation.
steps.outcome: Potentially compromised clients isolated.

steps.title: Enable DNSSEC and/or source port/transaction ID randomization
steps.desc: Deploy DNSSEC validation and ensure the resolver uses proper query source port and transaction ID randomization to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Resolver hardened against cache poisoning.

steps.title: Investigate and remediate affected clients
steps.desc: Check clients that connected to the malicious infrastructure for signs of compromise and remediate as needed.
steps.outcome: Affected clients confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore normal DNS resolution and client access
steps.desc: Confirm the resolver returns correct, authoritative responses and restore isolated clients to service.
steps.outcome: DNS resolution and client connectivity restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review DNS infrastructure hardening
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend DNSSEC deployment and resolver hardening as standing controls.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32512.def: Abuse of an authoritative DNS server that permits unrestricted AXFR/IXFR zone transfers to an unauthorized host, disclosing the full set of hostnames, internal IPs, and infrastructure naming conventions within a zone.
ITID-32512.purpose: Captures exploitation of misconfigured DNS zone transfers to enumerate an organization's internal DNS records.
scopeIncludes: Unauthenticated AXFR request against a misconfigured authoritative nameserver
Bulk enumeration of internal hostnames via successful zone transfer
scopeExcludes: Cache poisoning of a resolver (ITID-32511)
DNS tunneling (ITID-32513)
ITID-32512.severity: Medium-High — depends on sensitivity of infrastructure disclosed (e.g., exposing internal-only hosts).
ITID-32512.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if disclosed records reveal unpatched or high-value internal systems.
ITID-32512.escalation: Escalate to network/DNS admins to restrict transfer ACLs immediately upon confirmation.
indicators: Authoritative nameserver logs showing an AXFR/IXFR request from an untrusted external IP
Full zone record set observed leaving the network to an unrecognized host
vectors: Direct `dig axfr` style query against an exposed authoritative server
Automated internet-wide scanning tools probing for open zone transfer
rootCauses: Authoritative DNS server configured to allow transfers to any host
Missing or overly broad `allow-transfer` ACL
mitreTechniques: T1590.002 Gather Victim Network Information: DNS
controls: Restrict zone transfers to explicitly authorized secondary nameservers
TSIG authentication for zone transfers
ITID-32512.detection: Authoritative nameserver query logs directly capture AXFR/IXFR requests and source IPs.
ITID-32512.response: Restrict the transfer ACL, rotate any credentials or hostnames now considered exposed, and assess follow-on reconnaissance.
metrics: Count of unauthorized zone-transfer attempts detected per quarter
detections: AXFR/IXFR request from unauthorized source alerting
ITID-32512.notes: Scoped strictly to information disclosure via zone transfer, distinct from cache poisoning and tunneling leaves in this Type.

playbook.name: Response: DNS Zone Transfer Vulnerability Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a misconfigured DNS server allowing unauthorized zone transfer (AXFR), exposing the organization's full DNS zone data to an unauthorized party.

steps.title: Confirm the unauthorized zone transfer via DNS server logs
steps.desc: Review authoritative DNS server logs for AXFR/IXFR requests from unauthorized/unexpected source IP addresses.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized transfer and source IP.

steps.title: Assess what internal information was exposed via the zone data
steps.desc: Review the transferred zone contents for sensitive internal hostnames, IP ranges, or infrastructure details that could aid further reconnaissance/attacks.
steps.outcome: Exposure impact assessed.

steps.title: Restrict zone transfer to authorized secondary servers only
steps.desc: Immediately reconfigure the DNS server to allow AXFR/IXFR only from explicitly authorized secondary name server IP addresses.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized zone transfer capability closed.

steps.title: Monitor for follow-on reconnaissance or attacks against exposed hosts
steps.desc: Increase monitoring on internal hosts/services revealed by the leaked zone data, anticipating targeted follow-on activity.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring in place for exposed assets.

steps.title: Audit all authoritative DNS servers for the same misconfiguration
steps.desc: Check all other DNS servers in the environment for the same overly-permissive zone transfer configuration and remediate.
steps.outcome: Misconfiguration remediated organization-wide.

steps.title: Verify DNS service integrity and restore normal operation
steps.desc: Confirm DNS resolution continues to function correctly for authorized secondaries and clients after the configuration change.
steps.outcome: DNS service verified and restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and add zone transfer restriction to hardening baseline
steps.desc: Record the incident and add DNS zone transfer restriction checks to the standard server hardening/configuration baseline.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32513.def: Abuse of DNS query/response fields (subdomain labels, TXT/NULL records) as a general-purpose covert channel, encoding arbitrary data or command traffic inside DNS lookups to bypass network egress controls that do not inspect DNS content.
ITID-32513.purpose: Captures the technical exploitation of the DNS protocol itself as a covert transport channel, independent of what data is ultimately moved.
scopeIncludes: Encoding arbitrary payloads in DNS query subdomains to establish a covert channel
Use of DNS as a C2 beaconing transport
Exploitation of the DNS protocol's low-inspection status by network security tooling
scopeExcludes: The exfiltration-outcome use case of DNS tunneling — classified as ITID-34123 (commodity tool) / ITID-34124 (unclassified) under the Data Exfiltration domain's dedicated DNS Tunneling Tier-4
General/unclassified DNS tunneling logged purely in a protocol-exploitation context without a confirmed exfiltration or C2 outcome — ITID-43111
General/unclassified DNS tunneling logged purely in a C2 context — ITID-44221
DNS cache poisoning (ITID-32511) and DNS amplification DDoS (ITID-32514)
ITID-32513.severity: High — indicates an established covert channel bypassing egress controls.
ITID-32513.priority: P1 upon confirmation of active tunneling traffic.
ITID-32513.escalation: Escalate to SOC/IR immediately; treat as an active C2 or exfiltration channel pending scope determination.
indicators: High volume of DNS queries to a single or small set of unusual domains
Abnormally long or high-entropy subdomain labels
TXT/NULL record queries at a rate inconsistent with normal application use
vectors: Malware embedding a DNS tunneling client (e.g., iodine, dnscat2-style protocol)
Custom C2 frameworks using DNS as a fallback channel
rootCauses: Egress filtering that permits DNS (port 53) without content inspection
Lack of DNS query volume/entropy baselining
mitreTechniques: T1048.003 Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted/Obfuscated Non-C2 Protocol
controls: DNS query entropy/volume anomaly detection
Restricting recursive DNS to approved internal resolvers only
DNS payload/content inspection at the egress resolver
ITID-32513.detection: DNS query logs with entropy and volume analytics provide a strong technical signal; this is the primary detection surface for this leaf.
ITID-32513.response: Block the tunneling domain(s), isolate affected hosts, and determine whether the channel was used for C2, exfiltration, or both before final classification.
metrics: Count of DNS tunneling channels detected and blocked per quarter
Mean time to detection from first anomalous query
ITID-32513.notes: SCOPE DECISION: this leaf covers the protocol-exploitation mechanism of DNS tunneling itself (how the covert channel is built and abused). Where the investigation confirms the tunnel was used specifically to exfiltrate data, reclassify/cross-reference to ITID-34123 (commodity tool) or ITID-34124 (unclassified) under the Data Exfiltration domain's DNS Tunneling Tier-4, which are scoped to the exfiltration outcome rather than the protocol mechanic. Also distinct from the general-context catch-alls ITID-43111 (protocol exploitation context) and ITID-44221 (C2 context), which exist for incidents too underspecified to attribute to a specific technique.

playbook.name: Response: DNS Tunneling for Covert Data Exfiltration/C2
playbook.description: For confirmed use of DNS tunneling to covertly exfiltrate data or establish command-and-control communications by encoding data within DNS queries/responses.

steps.title: Confirm DNS tunneling via query pattern analysis
steps.desc: Review DNS query logs for indicators of tunneling: high query volume to a single domain, unusually long/high-entropy subdomain labels, or abnormal query types (TXT, NULL) inconsistent with legitimate use.
steps.outcome: Confirmed tunneling activity, source host(s), and destination domain.
steps.tool: DNS query logs / DNS security analytics

steps.title: Assess what data was exfiltrated or what C2 commands were exchanged
steps.desc: Where possible, decode captured tunnel traffic to determine the nature and volume of exfiltrated data or C2 activity.
steps.outcome: Scope and content of exfiltration/C2 activity assessed.

steps.title: Block the malicious domain at the DNS/firewall layer
steps.desc: Block the tunneling domain organization-wide to sever the covert channel.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration/C2 channel severed.

steps.title: Isolate the source host(s)
steps.desc: Network-isolate hosts confirmed to be conducting DNS tunneling for further investigation.
steps.outcome: Source hosts isolated.

steps.title: Remove the malware/agent responsible for the tunneling
steps.desc: Identify and remove the malicious process or implant generating the tunneled traffic from affected hosts.
steps.outcome: Hosts confirmed clean.

steps.title: Deploy DNS traffic analytics to detect tunneling patterns going forward
steps.desc: Implement or tune DNS security analytics capable of detecting tunneling indicators (query entropy, volume anomalies) for ongoing detection.
steps.outcome: Improved detection coverage in place.

steps.title: Restore affected hosts to service after verification
steps.desc: Return remediated, verified-clean hosts to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Hosts restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and assess data exfiltration impact
steps.desc: Record the volume/nature of data exfiltrated and evaluate whether data loss prevention notification obligations apply.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32514.def: Exploitation of DNS's response-size amplification characteristics — sending small spoofed-source queries to open recursive resolvers so that large responses are reflected onto a spoofed victim IP — to conduct a volumetric denial-of-service attack.
ITID-32514.purpose: Captures abuse of open or misconfigured DNS resolvers to amplify traffic volume against a third-party DDoS target.
scopeIncludes: Use of an organization's open recursive resolver as an unwitting amplifier/reflector
Detection of the organization's own resolvers being abused to attack a third party
Large ANY/TXT record responses used to maximize amplification factor
scopeExcludes: Cache poisoning (ITID-32511)
DNS tunneling for C2/exfiltration (ITID-32513)
ITID-32514.severity: Medium for outbound-only abuse (own resolver misused against a third party); High if the organization is the amplification target and suffering denial of service.
ITID-32514.priority: P2 for outbound misuse; P1 if the organization's own services are being denied.
ITID-32514.escalation: Escalate to network engineering to close open resolvers or apply response rate limiting immediately.
indicators: Sudden spike in outbound DNS response traffic to a single external IP
Resolver logs showing high volumes of ANY-type queries from spoofed-looking sources
Inbound flood of large DNS responses the organization never queried for
vectors: Internet-wide scanning to identify open recursive resolvers
Spoofed-source UDP queries directing amplified responses at a victim
rootCauses: Resolver configured for open recursion accessible from the internet
Lack of response rate limiting (RRL) on authoritative/recursive servers
mitreTechniques: T1498.002 Network Denial of Service: Reflection Amplification
controls: Disable open recursion on internet-facing resolvers
DNS Response Rate Limiting (RRL)
Egress/ingress filtering against source-address spoofing (BCP 38)
ITID-32514.detection: Network flow and resolver query-volume monitoring provide strong technical detection for both outbound misuse and inbound reflected-flood impact.
ITID-32514.response: Disable open recursion or apply RRL, and if inbound-targeted, engage upstream DDoS scrubbing/mitigation.
metrics: Count of resolvers identified as open/abusable per scan cycle
Volume of amplification traffic observed per incident
detections: Anomalous outbound DNS response volume alerting
ITID-32514.notes: Scoped to DNS's role as a volumetric amplification vector, distinct from the covert-channel and cache-integrity leaves in this Type.

playbook.name: Response: DNS Amplification Vulnerability Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed abuse of an organization's DNS server as a reflector/amplifier in a DNS amplification denial-of-service attack against a third party.

steps.title: Confirm the DNS server is being used as a reflector via traffic analysis
steps.desc: Review DNS server logs and network traffic for a high volume of spoofed-source queries generating disproportionately large responses directed at a third-party victim IP.
steps.outcome: Confirmed reflector abuse and identification of the affected DNS server(s).
steps.tool: DNS server logs / network flow analysis

steps.title: Assess impact on the organization's own DNS service availability
steps.desc: Determine whether the amplification traffic volume is degrading the organization's own DNS resolution capacity.
steps.outcome: Internal service impact assessed.

steps.title: Rate-limit or disable open recursive resolution
steps.desc: Apply response rate limiting (RRL) and disable open recursive DNS resolution for external/unauthenticated queries to stop the abuse.
steps.outcome: Reflector abuse stopped.

steps.title: Coordinate with upstream ISP/DDoS mitigation provider if own service is impacted
steps.desc: Engage upstream network provider or DDoS mitigation service if the amplification traffic is impacting the organization's own network capacity.
steps.outcome: Traffic mitigated upstream if needed.

steps.title: Harden DNS server configuration against amplification abuse
steps.desc: Apply permanent configuration changes (recursion restriction, RRL, BCP38 source-address validation) to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Server hardened against amplification abuse.

steps.title: Verify normal DNS service and confirm abuse has stopped
steps.desc: Confirm the DNS server no longer generates amplified responses to spoofed queries and normal service is restored.
steps.outcome: Service verified and restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and add amplification hardening to DNS server baseline
steps.desc: Record the incident and add recursion-restriction and rate-limiting checks to the standard DNS server hardening baseline.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32515.def: An incident involving exploitation of the DNS protocol, not clearly matching cache poisoning, zone transfer disclosure, tunneling, or amplification.
ITID-32515.purpose: Catch-all for DNS protocol exploitation incidents that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific DNS exploit leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (32511-32514)
ITID-32515.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-32515.escalation: Reclassify once the specific DNS exploitation pattern is clarified.
indicators: DNS-related alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: DNS protocol abuse of unclear specific mechanism
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
mitreTechniques: T1590.002 Gather Victim Network Information: DNS
controls: DNSSEC validation
DNS traffic monitoring and anomaly detection
Response rate limiting on authoritative DNS servers
Patch management for DNS server software
ITID-32515.detection: Same general DNS telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32515.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32515.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General DNS Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a DNS-related vulnerability not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the exploitation via DNS server/resolver logs
steps.desc: Review DNS server and resolver logs to confirm the exploitation and identify the affected DNS infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation and affected DNS infrastructure.

steps.title: Assess downstream client/service impact
steps.desc: Determine which clients or services relied on the affected DNS infrastructure and may have been impacted.
steps.outcome: Downstream impact scope established.

steps.title: Restrict or reconfigure the affected DNS service
steps.desc: Apply an immediate configuration change or access restriction to halt active exploitation.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Isolate affected clients if downstream compromise is suspected
steps.desc: Network-isolate any client suspected of compromise as a result of the DNS exploitation.
steps.outcome: Potentially compromised clients isolated.

steps.title: Patch or harden the vulnerable DNS component
steps.desc: Apply the applicable vendor patch or configuration hardening addressing the vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated.

steps.title: Verify and restore normal DNS service
steps.desc: Confirm DNS resolution functions correctly and restore any isolated clients to service.
steps.outcome: Service verified and restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review DNS infrastructure hardening baseline
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend improvements to DNS infrastructure hardening and monitoring coverage.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32521.def: Exploitation of a documented CVE in the SMB protocol implementation (e.g., an EternalBlue-class buffer overflow) to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution, characteristic of vulnerabilities capable of worm-like self-propagation across a network.
ITID-32521.purpose: Captures exploitation of a known, publicly disclosed SMB memory-corruption vulnerability that enables remote code execution and can self-propagate.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a specific, named SMB RCE CVE against an unpatched host
Wormable propagation behavior following successful SMB exploitation
scopeExcludes: Authentication relay attacks (ITID-32522)
Anonymous/null session enumeration without code execution (ITID-32523)
ITID-32521.severity: Critical — remote code execution with potential for self-propagation across the environment.
ITID-32521.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmed exploitation attempt or success.
ITID-32521.escalation: Escalate to IR and patch management leadership immediately; treat as a potential network-wide outbreak.
indicators: SMB traffic matching known exploit packet signatures
Unexpected process spawned by the SMB service (lsass.exe/svchost.exe anomalies)
Rapid lateral SMB connection attempts from a single host
vectors: Direct exploitation of unpatched SMBv1/v2 service exposed on the network
Worm payload scanning and exploiting the vulnerability across subnets
rootCauses: Missing critical security patches on SMB services
SMBv1 left enabled where not required
controls: Timely critical patch deployment (CVE-based)
Disable SMBv1
Network segmentation limiting SMB exposure between subnets
ITID-32521.detection: IDS/IPS signatures for known exploit patterns and EDR process-anomaly detection on SMB-facing hosts provide strong coverage.
ITID-32521.response: Isolate affected hosts immediately, patch across the environment, and hunt for lateral spread.
metrics: Count of hosts exploited before patch/isolation
Mean time to patch after CVE disclosure
ITID-32521.notes: Scoped to memory-corruption RCE via a known CVE, distinguishing it from the credential/authentication-abuse leaves (relay, null session) in this Type.

playbook.name: Response: Known-CVE SMB Remote Code Execution Exploit (Wormable Vulnerability Class)
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a known, wormable-class SMB remote code execution vulnerability against an unpatched system.

steps.title: Confirm the exploited CVE and affected host(s)
steps.desc: Correlate exploitation indicators (crash logs, EDR alerts, network IDS signatures) against the known CVE to confirm which hosts were hit.
steps.outcome: Confirmed CVE and affected host list.

steps.title: Assess for worm-like lateral spread
steps.desc: Given the wormable nature of this vulnerability class, immediately check for signs of automated propagation to other internal hosts.
steps.guidance: Do not assume single-host scope — this vulnerability class is specifically designed to self-propagate.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected/at-risk hosts established.
steps.tool: Network traffic analysis / EDR fleet query

steps.title: Isolate all confirmed and at-risk hosts
steps.desc: Network-isolate affected hosts and any unpatched host reachable on the same SMB-exposed segment.
steps.outcome: Further spread halted.

steps.title: Block SMB traffic at network boundaries where not required
steps.desc: Restrict SMB (port 445) traffic across network segments/internet-facing boundaries as an immediate compensating control.
steps.outcome: SMB exposure minimized organization-wide.

steps.title: Patch the vulnerability on all affected/at-risk systems
steps.desc: Apply the vendor security patch fixing this CVE across the environment on an emergency basis.
steps.outcome: Patch applied fleet-wide.

steps.title: Remove any payload/persistence delivered by the exploit
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts of any dropped malware or persistence mechanism.
steps.outcome: Hosts confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore isolated hosts to service after verification
steps.desc: Return patched, confirmed-clean hosts to the network.
steps.outcome: Hosts restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review patch-management SLAs
steps.desc: Record why the patch wasn't applied before exploitation and recommend a faster emergency-patch process for wormable-class CVEs.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32522.def: Exploitation of SMB/NTLM authentication flow weaknesses to capture a victim's authentication attempt and relay it in real time to a different target, granting the attacker access as the victim without ever obtaining the plaintext credential.
ITID-32522.purpose: Captures exploitation of SMB authentication design to relay captured credentials to another host without cracking them.
scopeIncludes: NTLM relay attacks leveraging captured SMB authentication
Coercion of a victim host into authenticating to an attacker-controlled listener for relay
scopeExcludes: Direct RCE via a known SMB CVE (ITID-32521)
Anonymous/null session access requiring no credential relay (ITID-32523)
ITID-32522.severity: High — successful relay grants attacker-controlled access as a legitimate account, often with elevated privileges.
ITID-32522.priority: P1 upon confirmed successful relay to a sensitive target.
ITID-32522.escalation: Escalate to IR and identity/AD teams immediately to assess scope of relayed access.
indicators: Authentication events showing a single account authenticating from an unexpected source host
SMB signing disabled on hosts targeted for relay
Coercion technique traffic (e.g., forced authentication via printer bug-class calls) preceding a relay
vectors: Man-in-the-middle interception of SMB authentication traffic on the local network
Forced authentication coercion techniques directing a victim to authenticate to an attacker listener
rootCauses: SMB signing not enforced across the environment
Lack of network segmentation permitting attacker positioning between client and server
controls: Enforce SMB signing on all hosts
Disable NTLM in favor of Kerberos where feasible
Network segmentation limiting attacker MitM positioning
ITID-32522.detection: Authentication log correlation (source-host mismatch) and SMB-signing-disabled inventory provide a strong technical signal.
ITID-32522.response: Disable the relayed account, enforce SMB signing environment-wide, and hunt for downstream access gained via the relay.
metrics: Count of confirmed relay incidents per quarter
Percentage of hosts with SMB signing enforced
ITID-32522.notes: Scoped to authentication-relay exploitation of the SMB protocol, distinguishing it from direct RCE and passive enumeration leaves in this Type.

playbook.name: Response: SMB Relay Attack Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of an SMB relay attack, where captured authentication traffic (e.g., via NTLM) was relayed to another host to gain unauthorized access without cracking credentials.

steps.title: Confirm the relay attack via authentication log correlation
steps.desc: Correlate authentication logs across the source and destination hosts for an NTLM authentication that appears to originate from an unexpected relaying host rather than the legitimate client.
steps.outcome: Confirmed relay attack and affected hosts/accounts.

steps.title: Determine what access the relayed authentication granted
steps.desc: Establish what actions were performed using the relayed session (e.g., file access, remote code execution) to scope impact.
steps.outcome: Impact of the relayed access established.

steps.title: Isolate the relaying and target hosts
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host used to capture/relay traffic and the target host that accepted the relayed authentication.
steps.outcome: Hosts isolated.

steps.title: Enable SMB signing and disable NTLM where feasible
steps.desc: Enforce SMB signing organization-wide as an immediate compensating control to prevent further relay attacks, and disable NTLM in favor of Kerberos where feasible.
steps.outcome: Relay technique blocked fleet-wide.

steps.title: Rotate credentials for accounts involved in the relayed session
steps.desc: Rotate passwords for any account whose authentication was relayed.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials invalidated.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence resulting from the relayed access
steps.desc: Clean the target host of any unauthorized changes, files, or persistence introduced via the relayed session.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore hosts to service after verification
steps.desc: Return remediated, verified-clean hosts to normal operation with SMB signing enforced.
steps.outcome: Hosts restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and audit SMB signing enforcement fleet-wide
steps.desc: Record the incident and verify SMB signing/NTLM relay mitigations are consistently enforced across the environment.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32523.def: Abuse of legacy SMB support for null or anonymous sessions to enumerate shares, usernames, groups, or system information from a target host without providing valid credentials.
ITID-32523.purpose: Captures exploitation of SMB null/anonymous session support to enumerate system and account information without authentication.
scopeIncludes: Anonymous SMB session used to enumerate shares/users via IPC$
Automated tooling walking a host's SMB null session for reconnaissance data
scopeExcludes: RCE via a known CVE (ITID-32521)
Authentication relay attacks (ITID-32522)
ITID-32523.severity: Low-Medium — primarily an information-disclosure/reconnaissance precursor rather than direct compromise.
ITID-32523.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if enumerated data is used to support a follow-on attack.
ITID-32523.escalation: Escalate to SOC if enumeration is followed by targeted authentication attempts against enumerated accounts.
indicators: SMB session established with no authentication (null session) followed by IPC$ or share enumeration
Repeated anonymous connection attempts from a single source across many hosts
vectors: Legacy null-session support left enabled on Windows hosts
Automated internal reconnaissance tooling (e.g., enum4linux-style) targeting exposed SMB services
rootCauses: Null session/anonymous access not disabled via security policy
Legacy compatibility settings retained past their need
controls: Disable null session/anonymous SMB access via group policy
Restrict IPC$ enumeration
Network segmentation limiting internal SMB exposure
ITID-32523.detection: SMB authentication logs showing anonymous/null logon type provide a direct technical signal.
ITID-32523.response: Disable null session support on affected hosts and review what was enumerated for follow-on risk.
metrics: Count of hosts with null session enabled per scan cycle
Count of anonymous enumeration events per quarter
ITID-32523.notes: Scoped to unauthenticated enumeration, the lowest-severity of the three specific SMB leaves; distinguished from RCE and relay by absence of code execution or credential relay.

playbook.name: Response: SMB Null Session/Anonymous Access Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a misconfigured SMB service allowing null session or anonymous access, exposing shares, user lists, or system information without authentication.

steps.title: Confirm anonymous/null session access via SMB logs
steps.desc: Review SMB/file server logs for successful connections using null/anonymous credentials and identify what shares or information were accessed.
steps.outcome: Confirmed null session access and affected host(s).

steps.title: Assess what information was enumerated or exposed
steps.desc: Determine what user lists, share contents, or system information were retrieved via the anonymous access, since this often supports follow-on reconnaissance or credential attacks.
steps.outcome: Exposure impact assessed.

steps.title: Disable null session/anonymous access
steps.desc: Immediately reconfigure the affected system(s) to disable anonymous SMB access and restrict share permissions.
steps.outcome: Anonymous access vector closed.

steps.title: Monitor for follow-on attacks using enumerated information
steps.desc: Increase monitoring for credential attacks or targeted access attempts against accounts/systems revealed via the anonymous enumeration.
steps.outcome: Heightened monitoring in place.

steps.title: Audit all SMB hosts fleet-wide for the same misconfiguration
steps.desc: Scan the environment for other systems permitting null session/anonymous SMB access and remediate.
steps.outcome: Misconfiguration remediated organization-wide.

steps.title: Verify SMB service integrity and restore normal operation
steps.desc: Confirm legitimate SMB access continues to function correctly after the configuration change.
steps.outcome: Service verified and restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and add null-session checks to the hardening baseline
steps.desc: Record the incident and add anonymous SMB access checks to the standard server hardening baseline.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32524.def: An incident involving exploitation of the SMB protocol, not clearly matching known-CVE RCE, relay, or null-session enumeration.
ITID-32524.purpose: Catch-all for SMB protocol exploitation incidents that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific SMB exploit leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (32521-32523)
ITID-32524.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-32524.escalation: Reclassify once the specific SMB exploitation pattern is clarified.
indicators: SMB-related alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: SMB protocol abuse of unclear specific mechanism
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: SMB signing enforcement
Disabling SMBv1 and restricting SMB to trusted network segments
Network segmentation limiting lateral movement
Timely patching of SMB vulnerabilities (e.g., EternalBlue-class)
ITID-32524.detection: Same general SMB telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32524.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32524.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General SMB Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of an SMB-related vulnerability not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the exploitation via SMB/EDR logs
steps.desc: Review SMB server logs, EDR alerts, and network IDS to confirm exploitation and identify affected host(s).
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation and affected host(s).
steps.tool: SMB server logs / EDR / network IDS

steps.title: Determine scope across the fleet
steps.desc: Identify all systems exposing the same vulnerable SMB configuration/version to establish blast radius.
steps.outcome: List of at-risk hosts.

steps.title: Isolate affected hosts
steps.desc: Network-isolate compromised hosts to halt further exploitation or spread.
steps.outcome: Hosts isolated.

steps.title: Restrict SMB exposure as an interim control
steps.desc: Restrict SMB traffic at network boundaries where not strictly required, pending a full fix.
steps.outcome: Exploitation surface reduced.

steps.title: Patch or reconfigure the vulnerable SMB component
steps.desc: Apply the applicable vendor patch or configuration fix.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated.

steps.title: Remove any payload or persistence delivered by the exploit
steps.desc: Clean confirmed-compromised hosts of dropped malware or persistence mechanisms.
steps.outcome: Hosts confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore hosts to service after verification
steps.desc: Return patched, verified-clean hosts to normal operation.
steps.outcome: Hosts restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review SMB hardening/patch cadence
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend improvements to SMB configuration hardening and patch management.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32531.def: Active manipulation of the TLS handshake (e.g., stripping cipher suite offers, blocking version-negotiation extensions) to coerce a client and server into negotiating a legacy, weaker TLS/SSL version than either would otherwise use, exposing the session to further exploitation.
ITID-32531.purpose: Captures an adversary forcing a TLS negotiation to fall back to a weaker, exploitable protocol version.
scopeIncludes: Active manipulation of handshake negotiation to force fallback to SSLv3/TLS 1.0
SSL-stripping style attacks removing upgrade signals in transit
scopeExcludes: Exploiting a protocol version/cipher that was already configured weak without active downgrade manipulation (ITID-32532)
Certificate trust-chain bypass (ITID-32533)
Implementation memory-safety bugs like Heartbleed (ITID-32534)
ITID-32531.severity: High — successful downgrade exposes the session to well-known weaknesses in legacy protocol versions.
ITID-32531.priority: P1 upon confirmation of an active downgrade attack against production traffic.
ITID-32531.escalation: Escalate to network/security engineering immediately to identify the MitM position and remediate.
indicators: TLS handshake logs showing negotiated protocol version lower than the server's configured minimum
Client connections unexpectedly falling back to SSLv3/TLS 1.0 mid-session
vectors: Man-in-the-middle interception stripping version-negotiation extensions
Exploiting servers that still accept legacy protocol versions as a fallback
rootCauses: Server configuration still permitting legacy TLS/SSL versions
Lack of enforcement of TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV or equivalent anti-downgrade mechanisms
controls: Disable legacy TLS/SSL versions server-side
Enforce TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV
HSTS enforcement for web services
ITID-32531.detection: TLS handshake/version logging at the server or network boundary provides a direct technical signal.
ITID-32531.response: Disable legacy protocol support, identify the MitM vector, and assess data exposed during downgraded sessions.
metrics: Count of downgrade attempts detected per quarter
Percentage of endpoints with legacy TLS disabled
ITID-32531.notes: Scoped to active handshake-manipulation downgrade attacks; a server already configured with weak ciphers/versions with no active manipulation is ITID-32532.

playbook.name: Response: TLS Downgrade Attack Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a TLS downgrade attack, where an attacker forced a connection to negotiate a weaker, vulnerable protocol version or cipher than intended.

steps.title: Confirm the downgrade via connection/TLS handshake logs
steps.desc: Review server and network TLS handshake logs for connections that negotiated an unexpectedly weak protocol version/cipher inconsistent with the client's actual capability, and correlate with a likely on-path attacker position.
steps.outcome: Confirmed downgrade instances and affected connections/hosts.

steps.title: Assess what data may have been exposed via the weakened connection
steps.desc: Determine what data traversed the downgraded connection and whether it could have been intercepted or decrypted.
steps.outcome: Data exposure impact assessed.

steps.title: Isolate the affected network segment if an on-path attacker is suspected
steps.desc: If the downgrade indicates an active on-path attacker (e.g., rogue access point, compromised network device), isolate the affected network segment to remove the interception capability.
steps.outcome: Interception capability removed.

steps.title: Terminate and force re-establishment of affected sessions
steps.desc: Terminate sessions that negotiated the weak protocol/cipher and require re-connection under corrected configuration.
steps.outcome: Weakened sessions terminated.

steps.title: Disable weak TLS protocol versions and cipher suites
steps.desc: Reconfigure affected servers/services to disable outdated TLS versions (e.g., TLS 1.0/1.1) and weak cipher suites, closing the downgrade path at the source. This cryptographic-configuration remediation is required alongside the incident response.
steps.outcome: Downgrade path closed across affected services.

steps.title: Investigate and remediate the on-path attack vector if identified
steps.desc: If a rogue device or compromised network component enabled the downgrade, remove or remediate it.
steps.outcome: Attack vector removed.

steps.title: Verify hardened TLS configuration and restore service
steps.desc: Confirm connections now negotiate only strong protocol versions/ciphers and restore normal service.
steps.outcome: Service verified and restored with hardened TLS configuration.

steps.title: Document the incident and add TLS configuration checks to the hardening baseline
steps.desc: Record the incident and add periodic TLS configuration scanning to the standard hardening/compliance baseline.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32532.def: Exploitation of an endpoint's existing (non-downgraded) TLS/SSL configuration that permits weak cipher suites (e.g., RC4, export-grade ciphers) or outdated protocol versions, allowing an attacker to decrypt or manipulate traffic without needing to force a handshake downgrade.
ITID-32532.purpose: Captures exploitation of a server or client that is already configured to accept weak cipher suites or outdated protocol versions.
scopeIncludes: Exploiting a server statically configured to offer RC4 or export-grade ciphers
Passive decryption of traffic secured only by a known-weak cipher suite
scopeExcludes: Active handshake manipulation forcing a fallback (ITID-32531)
Certificate validation bypass (ITID-32533)
Implementation bugs like Heartbleed (ITID-32534)
ITID-32532.severity: Medium-High depending on data sensitivity and cipher weakness exploited.
ITID-32532.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if actively exploited against sensitive traffic.
ITID-32532.escalation: Escalate to system owners to remediate the cipher configuration immediately upon confirmation.
indicators: Vulnerability scan flagging weak cipher suites/protocol versions in use
Traffic captures showing sessions negotiated with a deprecated cipher
vectors: Passive traffic capture and offline decryption exploiting a known-weak cipher
Active exploitation tools targeting a specific weak-cipher vulnerability class
rootCauses: Legacy configuration never hardened to modern cipher suite baselines
Backward-compatibility requirements retained past their need
controls: Cipher suite hardening baseline enforced via configuration management
Regular TLS configuration scanning
ITID-32532.detection: TLS configuration/vulnerability scanning provides strong, direct coverage of this exposure.
ITID-32532.response: Remediate the cipher/protocol configuration and assess whether traffic was actively intercepted.
metrics: Count of endpoints with weak cipher configuration per scan cycle
ITID-32532.notes: Scoped to exploitation of a static, pre-existing weak configuration, distinct from the active-manipulation downgrade leaf (ITID-32531).

playbook.name: Response: Weak Cipher Suite/Protocol Version Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a weak, deprecated cipher suite or TLS/SSL protocol version still enabled on a service, allowing an attacker to compromise the confidentiality/integrity of a connection.

steps.title: Confirm the weak cipher/protocol was exploited via connection logs
steps.desc: Review server TLS logs for connections established using known-weak cipher suites or deprecated protocol versions, and correlate with signs of exploitation (e.g., traffic decryption, data manipulation).
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation and affected service(s).

steps.title: Assess what data was exposed through the weak connection
steps.desc: Determine what sensitive data traversed connections using the weak cipher/protocol and may have been compromised.
steps.outcome: Data exposure impact assessed.

steps.title: Disable the weak cipher suite/protocol version immediately
steps.desc: Reconfigure the affected service to remove the weak cipher suite and/or deprecated protocol version from its supported list. This cryptographic-configuration remediation is required alongside the incident response.
steps.outcome: Weak cryptography disabled.

steps.title: Terminate and force re-establishment of affected sessions
steps.desc: Terminate any active session using the weak configuration and require reconnection under the hardened settings.
steps.outcome: Weakened sessions terminated.

steps.title: Audit all services fleet-wide for the same weak configuration
steps.desc: Scan the environment for other services still supporting the same weak cipher suite/protocol version and remediate.
steps.outcome: Weak cryptography remediated organization-wide.

steps.title: Rotate any credentials/keys potentially exposed via the weak connection
steps.desc: Rotate any credentials or session keys that may have been intercepted or compromised due to the weak cryptography.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials/keys invalidated.

steps.title: Verify hardened configuration and restore service
steps.desc: Confirm the service now supports only strong cipher suites/protocol versions and restore normal operation.
steps.outcome: Service verified and restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and add cipher/protocol scanning to the hardening baseline
steps.desc: Record the incident and add periodic TLS cipher/protocol version scanning to the standard hardening/compliance baseline.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32533.def: Exploitation of a bug or design flaw in certificate validation logic (e.g., improper hostname checking, chain-of-trust bypass, acceptance of self-signed or expired certificates) that allows an attacker to present a fraudulent certificate as trusted.
ITID-32533.purpose: Captures exploitation of flaws in certificate validation logic to defeat TLS trust verification.
scopeIncludes: Exploiting an application that fails to validate certificate chain-of-trust correctly
Hostname-verification bypass allowing a mismatched certificate to be accepted
Installation of a rogue root CA to enable trusted interception
scopeExcludes: Handshake downgrade attacks (ITID-32531)
Weak cipher exploitation with a validly-trusted certificate (ITID-32532)
Implementation memory-safety bugs like Heartbleed (ITID-32534)
ITID-32533.severity: High — successful bypass enables undetected interception of traffic believed to be secure.
ITID-32533.priority: P1 upon confirmation of active exploitation against production traffic.
ITID-32533.escalation: Escalate to PKI/security engineering immediately; revoke and reissue affected certificates as needed.
indicators: Application logs showing acceptance of a certificate that should have failed validation
Unexpected root CA present in a client's trust store
Certificate transparency log entries for an unauthorized certificate matching an internal domain
vectors: Rogue root certificate installed on a victim device to enable trusted MitM
Application code with flawed or disabled certificate validation logic
rootCauses: Custom TLS validation code with logic errors
Certificate pinning not implemented for high-value applications
Endpoint trust store not adequately controlled
mitreTechniques: T1553.004 Subvert Trust Controls: Install Root Certificate
controls: Certificate pinning for critical applications
Endpoint trust-store management and monitoring
Certificate transparency log monitoring
ITID-32533.detection: Certificate transparency monitoring and endpoint trust-store auditing provide meaningful technical signal.
ITID-32533.response: Revoke affected certificates, remove rogue root CAs from endpoints, and assess scope of intercepted traffic.
metrics: Count of unauthorized root CA installs detected per quarter
Count of certificate validation bypass incidents
ITID-32533.notes: Scoped to trust-validation logic exploitation, distinct from protocol-negotiation and implementation-bug leaves in this Type.

playbook.name: Response: Certificate Validation Bypass Exploitation
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a certificate validation bypass, allowing a man-in-the-middle attack via an invalid, self-signed, or spoofed certificate that a client/service accepted without proper validation.

steps.title: Confirm the bypass via certificate chain/log analysis
steps.desc: Review connection logs and certificate details for connections that accepted an invalid, mismatched, or untrusted certificate, confirming the specific validation bypass (e.g., missing hostname check, disabled chain validation).
steps.outcome: Confirmed bypass mechanism and affected connections/host(s).

steps.title: Assess for an active man-in-the-middle position
steps.desc: Determine whether an attacker is actively positioned on the network path (e.g., rogue access point, ARP spoofing) intercepting traffic using the accepted spoofed certificate.
steps.outcome: MITM position assessed and located if active.

steps.title: Isolate the affected network segment if an active MITM is confirmed
steps.desc: Remove the rogue device or interception point from the network if an active man-in-the-middle position is confirmed.
steps.outcome: Interception capability removed.

steps.title: Disable or patch the vulnerable certificate validation logic
steps.desc: Fix the application/client code or configuration performing the flawed certificate validation as an immediate compensating measure.
steps.outcome: Validation bypass closed.

steps.title: Deploy the code/configuration fix fleet-wide
steps.desc: Roll out the corrected certificate validation logic to all affected clients/services.
steps.outcome: Fix deployed organization-wide.

steps.title: Rotate credentials/data potentially exposed via the intercepted connection
steps.desc: Rotate any credentials or sensitive data that may have transited the intercepted, improperly-validated connection.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials/data invalidated.

steps.title: Verify correct certificate validation and restore service
steps.desc: Confirm the fixed client/service correctly rejects invalid certificates and restore normal operation.
steps.outcome: Service verified and restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and add certificate validation testing to the release process
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend certificate-pinning/validation testing be added to the standard application security testing process.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32534.def: Exploitation of a specific implementation-level vulnerability in a TLS/SSL library (e.g., a Heartbleed-class out-of-bounds memory read) allowing disclosure of sensitive in-memory data such as private keys, session tokens, or credentials, rather than an attack on the protocol design or configuration.
ITID-32534.purpose: Captures exploitation of a memory-safety vulnerability in a TLS library implementation itself.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a known-CVE TLS library memory-disclosure or memory-corruption bug
Extraction of private keys or session data from an affected service's memory via a library-level flaw
scopeExcludes: Configuration-level weak cipher exploitation (ITID-32532)
Handshake downgrade attacks (ITID-32531)
Certificate trust bypass (ITID-32533)
ITID-32534.severity: Critical — can directly expose private keys and long-term credential material.
ITID-32534.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of exploitation.
ITID-32534.escalation: Escalate to IR and PKI teams immediately; treat private keys on the affected service as compromised.
indicators: Vulnerability scan flagging a specific known-CVE TLS library version
Anomalous heartbeat/extension traffic matching a known exploit pattern
Unexplained memory-read patterns on the TLS-terminating service
vectors: Direct exploitation of an unpatched vulnerable TLS library version exposed on the network
rootCauses: Delayed patching of a TLS library following public CVE disclosure
controls: Timely patching of TLS library dependencies
Certificate/key rotation following any suspected exposure
Vulnerability scanning for known TLS library CVEs
ITID-32534.detection: IDS/IPS signatures for known exploit traffic patterns and vulnerability scanning provide strong coverage.
ITID-32534.response: Patch immediately, rotate all private keys and sessions on the affected service, and assess what data may have been disclosed from memory.
metrics: Mean time to patch after CVE disclosure
Count of services confirmed exploited
detections: Known TLS CVE exploit signature IDS/IPS alerting
ITID-32534.notes: Scoped to implementation-level memory-safety bugs in the TLS library code itself, distinct from configuration, negotiation, and trust-validation leaves in this Type.

playbook.name: Response: TLS Implementation Vulnerability Exploitation (Heartbleed-Class)
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a memory-disclosure or similar implementation-level vulnerability in a TLS library (Heartbleed-class), allowing an attacker to extract sensitive data (private keys, session data, credentials) from server memory.

steps.title: Confirm exploitation via TLS library logs/version and traffic analysis
steps.desc: Confirm the affected server runs the vulnerable TLS library version and review network/IDS logs for the distinctive malformed request pattern associated with the exploit.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation and affected server(s).
steps.tool: Network IDS / TLS library version audit

steps.title: Assume private key and session data compromise pending proof otherwise
steps.desc: Given this vulnerability class can leak arbitrary process memory, treat the server's private key, active session tokens, and any in-memory credentials as compromised until forensic analysis proves otherwise.
steps.guidance: Do not wait for confirmed key theft before beginning key rotation — the exposure window alone warrants treating the key as compromised.
steps.outcome: Compromise assumption documented and rotation initiated.

steps.title: Take the affected service offline or apply a vendor hotfix immediately
steps.desc: Remove the vulnerable service from production or apply an emergency configuration change (disabling the vulnerable extension/feature) while the library is patched.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Revoke and reissue the TLS certificate and private key
steps.desc: Revoke the potentially-compromised certificate with the CA and generate/deploy a new private key and certificate.
steps.outcome: Compromised key invalidated; new certificate issued.

steps.title: Patch the TLS library to a fixed version
steps.desc: Update the vulnerable TLS library to the patched version across all affected systems.
steps.outcome: Patch applied fleet-wide.

steps.title: Force password/session reset for accounts that may have been exposed
steps.desc: Given session tokens and credentials may have been leaked from server memory, force a credential/session reset for potentially affected user accounts.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed credentials/sessions invalidated.

steps.title: Restore the service with the patched library and new certificate
steps.desc: Return the patched service, using the newly issued certificate/key, to production.
steps.outcome: Service restored with hardened cryptographic material.

steps.title: Document the incident and notify affected users/customers as required
steps.desc: Record the incident, assess data exposure scope, and notify affected users/customers and regulators per applicable breach notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and notifications completed as required.

ITID-32535.def: An incident involving exploitation of TLS/SSL, not clearly matching downgrade, weak-cipher, certificate-validation, or implementation-bug leaves.
ITID-32535.purpose: Catch-all for TLS/SSL protocol exploitation incidents that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific TLS/SSL exploit leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (32531-32534)
ITID-32535.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-32535.escalation: Reclassify once the specific TLS/SSL exploitation pattern is clarified.
indicators: TLS/SSL-related alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: TLS/SSL protocol abuse of unclear specific mechanism
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: TLS certificate pinning
Disabling deprecated/weak cipher suites and protocol versions
Certificate transparency monitoring
Network intrusion detection for AitM/downgrade attempts
ITID-32535.detection: Same general TLS telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32535.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32535.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General TLS/SSL Exploit
playbook.description: For confirmed exploitation of a TLS/SSL-related vulnerability not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the exploitation via TLS/server logs
steps.desc: Review TLS handshake logs, server logs, and network captures to confirm exploitation and identify affected service(s).
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation and affected service(s).

steps.title: Assess data exposure/impact from the exploited connection
steps.desc: Determine what data or cryptographic material may have been exposed or compromised as a result.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed.

steps.title: Apply an immediate configuration mitigation
steps.desc: Disable the vulnerable feature/configuration or take the affected service offline to halt active exploitation.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation halted.

steps.title: Rotate any potentially exposed cryptographic material or credentials
steps.desc: Rotate certificates, keys, or credentials that may have been exposed as a precaution.
steps.outcome: Potentially exposed material invalidated.

steps.title: Patch or reconfigure the vulnerable TLS component
steps.desc: Apply the applicable vendor patch or the necessary cryptographic-configuration remediation (disabling weak ciphers/protocol versions) alongside the incident response.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated.

steps.title: Verify the fix and restore service
steps.desc: Confirm the vulnerability is remediated and restore normal service.
steps.outcome: Service verified and restored.

steps.title: Document the incident and review TLS configuration hardening baseline
steps.desc: Record the incident and recommend improvements to TLS configuration hardening and scanning coverage.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32611.def: A weaponized document (e.g., Word/Excel/RTF) crafted to trigger a memory-corruption or parsing vulnerability in the host Office application itself, achieving code execution purely through the exploit payload rather than through scripting features.
ITID-32611.purpose: Captures a malicious document that exploits a memory-corruption or parser vulnerability in an Office application, without relying on macros.
scopeIncludes: Documents exploiting a known-CVE Office application memory-corruption bug
OLE object or embedded-object exploits achieving execution without macro code
scopeExcludes: Macro-based execution (Embedded Macros Type, ITID-32631-32634)
PDF reader exploits (ITID-32612)
Human-targeted phishing-attachment social engineering under the ITID-10000 domain (e.g., ITID-11112/11122), which is scoped to the delivery/lure rather than the exploit-code mechanics captured here
ITID-32611.severity: Critical — often achieves remote code execution on open with no further user action.
ITID-32611.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately; treat the opening host as compromised.
indicators: Office application spawning an unexpected child process immediately after opening a document
EDR detection of exploit-shellcode execution patterns from an Office process
Email gateway sandbox detonation flagging the document as exploitative
vectors: Email attachment delivering a crafted document exploiting an unpatched Office CVE
Malformed OLE/embedded objects triggering a parser vulnerability
rootCauses: Unpatched Office application version
Lack of sandboxed document handling (e.g., Protected View disabled)
controls: Timely Office application patching
Protected View / sandboxed document opening enforced by policy
Email attachment sandboxing/detonation
ITID-32611.detection: EDR process-lineage detection (Office spawning unexpected children) provides strong technical coverage.
ITID-32611.response: Isolate the affected host, patch the Office application environment-wide, and hunt for further exploitation attempts.
metrics: Count of exploit-document detections per quarter
Mean time to patch after CVE disclosure
ITID-32611.notes: SCOPE DECISION: this leaf covers the technical exploit-code mechanics of a weaponized document (a memory-corruption/parser bug in the application). The ITID-10000 domain's phishing-attachment leaves (e.g., ITID-11112) cover the human-targeted social-engineering delivery vector regardless of whether the attachment contains an actual exploit; use both codes together when a phishing lure delivers a document that also contains a technical exploit.

ITID-32612.def: A weaponized PDF document crafted to exploit a vulnerability in the parsing or JavaScript engine of a PDF reader application, achieving code execution when the file is opened.
ITID-32612.purpose: Captures a malicious PDF file that exploits a vulnerability in a PDF reader application.
scopeIncludes: PDF exploiting a known-CVE reader application memory-corruption or JavaScript-engine vulnerability
Malicious embedded JavaScript within a PDF triggering reader-side code execution
scopeExcludes: Office document exploits (ITID-32611)
Human-targeted phishing-attachment social engineering under the ITID-10000 domain, scoped to the lure rather than exploit-code mechanics
ITID-32612.severity: Critical — can achieve remote code execution on open.
ITID-32612.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately; treat the opening host as compromised.
indicators: PDF reader spawning an unexpected child process on open
EDR detection of shellcode execution originating from the reader process
Sandbox detonation flagging embedded JavaScript with exploit behavior
vectors: Email attachment delivering a crafted PDF exploiting an unpatched reader CVE
Malicious embedded JavaScript triggering a reader engine vulnerability
rootCauses: Unpatched PDF reader application
JavaScript execution enabled by default within the reader
controls: Timely PDF reader patching
Disable JavaScript execution in PDF readers by policy
Email attachment sandboxing/detonation
ITID-32612.detection: EDR process-lineage detection on the PDF reader process provides strong technical coverage.
ITID-32612.response: Isolate the affected host, patch the reader application environment-wide, and hunt for further exploitation.
metrics: Count of exploit-PDF detections per quarter
Mean time to patch after CVE disclosure
ITID-32612.notes: Sibling to ITID-32611, differentiated by the specific application/file format targeted (PDF reader vs. Office suite).

steps.outcome: Full recipient population identified.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints

ITID-32613.def: A weaponized ZIP/RAR (or similar) archive that either exploits a vulnerability in the extraction utility itself, or abuses archive-format features (path traversal, nested/encrypted archives, malformed headers) to conceal a malicious payload from security scanning.
ITID-32613.purpose: Captures a malicious archive file that exploits an extraction-utility vulnerability or uses the archive format to hide a payload from scanning.
scopeIncludes: Archive exploiting a known-CVE extraction utility vulnerability (e.g., path traversal on extraction)
Password-protected or nested archives used specifically to evade attachment scanning
Malformed archive headers designed to break scanner parsing while remaining extractable by common tools
scopeExcludes: Document/PDF exploits contained within an otherwise-benign archive (classify the contained file under ITID-32611/32612 if the archive itself is not the exploit vector)
Polyglot file-type disguise techniques (ITID-32614)
ITID-32613.severity: High — frequently used specifically to bypass detection ahead of a further payload.
ITID-32613.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the archive is confirmed to have evaded gateway scanning and reached a user.
ITID-32613.escalation: Escalate to email security engineering to close the scanning gap and to SOC to assess payload impact.
indicators: Password-protected archive attachment with the password included in the email body
Archive extraction producing an unexpected file type or path outside the intended directory
Gateway logs showing the archive was not fully scanned due to encryption/nesting
vectors: Email delivery of a password-protected archive to bypass content scanning
Nested/recursive archives ('archive bombs') designed to exhaust or evade scanners
rootCauses: Email gateway unable to scan encrypted or deeply nested archive contents
Extraction utility vulnerable to path traversal or malformed-header exploitation
controls: Block or quarantine password-protected archive attachments by policy
Extraction utility patching
Sandbox detonation of extracted archive contents
ITID-32613.detection: Email gateway scanning gaps for encrypted archives are a known blind spot; endpoint-side detonation of extracted content is the more reliable technical signal.
ITID-32613.response: Quarantine the archive, extract and analyze contents in a sandbox, and assess whether it reached and was opened by a user.
metrics: Count of scanning-evasive archives detected per quarter
detections: Endpoint sandbox detonation of extracted content
ITID-32613.notes: Scoped to the archive format/extraction-utility mechanics used to hide or exploit; the contained payload itself, if a document/PDF exploit, is additionally classified under the relevant sibling leaf.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious Archive File (ZIP/RAR) Exploiting Extraction Vulnerability or Hiding Payload
playbook.description: For a confirmed malicious archive attachment (ZIP/RAR) that either exploited an extraction/archive-handling vulnerability or used the archive format to conceal a malicious payload from scanning.

steps.title: Confirm the archive contents and evasion/exploitation technique
steps.desc: Extract and analyze the archive in a controlled environment to confirm the concealed payload or exploited extraction vulnerability, and determine why it evaded initial scanning (e.g. password-protection, nested archives, path traversal).
steps.outcome: Payload and evasion/exploitation technique confirmed.
steps.abort: If the archive was quarantined before extraction, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify the sender and other recipients
steps.desc: Identify the sending address/domain and search mail logs for all other recipients of the same or similar attachment.
steps.outcome: Full recipient population identified.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints
steps.desc: Network-isolate all endpoints where the archive was extracted and/or the payload executed.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Purge the message from all mailboxes and block the sender
steps.desc: Remove the malicious email from all recipient mailboxes and block the sending address/domain.
steps.outcome: Message purged; sender blocked.

steps.title: Remove the payload and check for persistence
steps.desc: Remove the extracted malware and verify no persistence mechanism was installed.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Review gateway scanning policy for archive handling
steps.desc: Assess whether the gateway should extract and scan nested/password-protected archives, or block them outright, to prevent recurrence of the same evasion.
steps.outcome: Scanning policy gap identified and remediated.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and monitor
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and update gateway archive policy
steps.desc: Record the evasion technique used and confirm the gateway policy change is deployed.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32614.def: An email attachment engineered as a polyglot (valid as more than one file format) or disguised via extension/icon/MIME-type spoofing to evade file-type filtering and mislead the recipient about its true nature.
ITID-32614.purpose: Captures an attachment crafted to disguise its true file type or function as a valid file of two formats simultaneously, evading type-based filtering.
scopeIncludes: Polyglot files valid as two distinct formats (e.g., a file that is simultaneously a valid JPEG and a valid executable/script)
Double-extension or extension-spoofing attachments (e.g., 'invoice.pdf.exe')
MIME-type spoofing to bypass gateway content-type filtering
scopeExcludes: Archive-based scanning evasion (ITID-32613)
Straightforward document/PDF exploits with no type-disguise element (ITID-32611/32612)
ITID-32614.severity: High — specifically designed to defeat filtering and mislead the recipient.
ITID-32614.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if confirmed opened/executed by a user.
ITID-32614.escalation: Escalate to email security engineering to close the specific filtering gap exploited.
indicators: Attachment with a mismatched file extension and detected MIME/magic-byte type
File that parses successfully as two different formats under different tools
Gateway logs showing content-type filtering was bypassed by a spoofed header
vectors: Double-extension naming exploiting default OS behavior of hiding known extensions
Crafting valid polyglot byte structures to pass filters keyed on file signature
rootCauses: Gateway/endpoint filtering relying solely on extension or declared MIME type rather than true content inspection
OS default configuration hiding file extensions from users
controls: True content/magic-byte inspection at the email gateway rather than extension-based filtering alone
Display of full file extensions by OS policy
ITID-32614.detection: Magic-byte/content-type inspection at the gateway is the direct technical control for this specific evasion technique.
ITID-32614.response: Quarantine the attachment, verify true file type, and assess whether it was opened or executed by the recipient.
metrics: Count of polyglot/disguised-type attachments detected per quarter
detections: File-type mismatch (extension vs. magic byte) alerting
ITID-32614.notes: Scoped to the file-type disguise/masquerading technique itself, distinct from the archive-mechanics leaf (ITID-32613) and the direct exploit leaves (ITID-32611/32612).

playbook.name: Response: Polyglot/Disguised File-Type Attachment Exploit
playbook.description: For a confirmed malicious attachment that used a polyglot file structure or disguised file-type/extension (e.g. an executable disguised as an image, or a file valid as two formats simultaneously) to bypass filtering and execute.

steps.title: Confirm the true file type and disguise/polyglot technique
steps.desc: Analyze the file's actual structure/magic bytes versus its apparent extension/MIME type to confirm the disguise or polyglot technique used to bypass filtering.
steps.outcome: True file type and disguise technique confirmed.
steps.abort: If the file was blocked before execution, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify the sender, other recipients, and execution scope
steps.desc: Identify the sending address/domain, search for all other recipients, and confirm which endpoints actually executed/opened the file.
steps.outcome: Full recipient and execution scope identified.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints
steps.desc: Network-isolate all endpoints where the file was executed.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Purge the message from all mailboxes and block the sender
steps.desc: Remove the malicious email from all recipient mailboxes and block the sending address/domain.
steps.outcome: Message purged; sender blocked.

steps.title: Remove the payload and check for persistence
steps.desc: Remove the payload and verify no persistence mechanism was installed.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Close the filtering gap that allowed the disguise to pass
steps.desc: Update the email/attachment filtering policy to inspect true file content/type rather than relying on extension or declared MIME type.
steps.outcome: Filtering gap remediated.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and monitor
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and confirm filtering policy update
steps.desc: Record the disguise technique used and confirm the filtering policy fix is deployed and effective.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32615.def: An incident involving a malicious email attachment exploiting a technical vulnerability or evasion mechanism, not clearly matching document, PDF, archive, or polyglot leaves.
ITID-32615.purpose: Catch-all for malicious email attachment exploitation incidents that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific malicious attachment leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (32611-32614)
ITID-32615.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-32615.escalation: Reclassify once the specific attachment exploitation pattern is clarified.
indicators: Attachment-related alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Attachment-based exploit of unclear specific mechanism
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Email gateway attachment sandboxing
Macro execution blocking via group policy
Endpoint detection for exploit-triggered process anomalies
User awareness training on phishing attachments
ITID-32615.detection: Same general email/attachment telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32615.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32615.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Malicious Attachment Exploit
playbook.description: For a confirmed malicious email attachment exploit that does not fit a more specific document, PDF, archive, or polyglot classification.

steps.title: Confirm the attachment exploit and payload
steps.desc: Review EDR/email gateway telemetry to confirm the attachment executed maliciously and identify the payload; reclassify to a more specific playbook if the attachment type becomes clear.
steps.outcome: Exploitation confirmed and payload identified.
steps.abort: If the attachment was quarantined/blocked before execution, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.desc: Remove any dropped malware and verify no persistence mechanism was installed.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.
