steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings about the attachment type and delivery for future correlation.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32621.def: A link embedded in an email that routes through a sequence of intermediate redirects (legitimate URL shorteners, compromised benign sites, conditional redirect logic) before reaching the final malicious destination, designed so automated scanners following the first hop see only benign content.
ITID-32621.purpose: Captures a malicious email link engineered with a multi-hop redirect chain specifically to defeat automated URL and sandbox scanning.
scopeIncludes: Multi-hop redirect chains using legitimate shorteners or compromised sites as intermediate hops
Conditional/time-delayed or geofenced redirects that serve benign content to scanners and malicious content to real users
scopeExcludes: Zero-click browser exploitation once the final destination is reached (ITID-32622)
Abuse of a vendor's own safe-link rewriting service (ITID-32623)
ITID-32621.severity: High — specifically engineered to defeat existing security controls.
ITID-32621.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if confirmed clicked by a user.
ITID-32621.escalation: Escalate to email security engineering to identify and block the redirect chain infrastructure.
indicators: URL analysis revealing multiple sequential redirects before final landing page
Sandbox detonation showing benign content while user reports differ from scanned result
Time-of-click analysis showing the destination changed after initial scanning
vectors: Chaining public URL shorteners to obscure the final malicious domain
Conditional redirect logic keyed on user-agent or IP to differentiate scanners from real users
rootCauses: URL scanning performed only at time of delivery rather than at time of click
Lack of full redirect-chain resolution in gateway scanning
controls: Time-of-click URL rewriting and re-scanning
Full redirect-chain resolution in gateway analysis
Blocklisting known abused redirector domains
ITID-32621.detection: Time-of-click scanning provides the strongest technical detection surface; delivery-time-only scanning has a known blind spot here.
ITID-32621.response: Block the redirect chain across all hops, and determine whether any user reached the final malicious destination.
metrics: Count of redirect-chain evasions detected per quarter
Percentage of links protected by time-of-click rewriting
ITID-32621.notes: Scoped to the redirect-chain evasion mechanism itself, distinct from what happens once the final destination is reached (browser exploitation, ITID-32622).

playbook.name: Response: Email Link Redirect Chain Evading URL/Sandbox Scanning
playbook.description: For a confirmed malicious email link that used a multi-hop redirect chain (URL shorteners, open redirects, delayed redirects) to evade URL reputation and sandbox scanning before landing the victim on an exploit or credential-harvesting page.

steps.title: Confirm the click and trace the full redirect chain
steps.desc: Review web proxy/browser telemetry to confirm the user clicked the link and reconstruct every hop in the redirect chain to the final landing page and payload.
steps.outcome: Full redirect chain and final payload/landing page identified.
steps.abort: If the link was blocked before the final hop, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify other recipients of the same link
steps.desc: Search mail logs for all other recipients of the email containing the same redirect link.
steps.outcome: Full recipient population identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint if a payload executed
steps.desc: Network-isolate the endpoint if the redirect chain resulted in code execution or credential entry.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated if applicable.

steps.title: Block every hop in the redirect chain and purge the message
steps.desc: Block each domain in the redirect chain (not just the initial shortener) at the web/email gateway and purge the message from all mailboxes.
steps.outcome: Full redirect chain blocked; message purged.

steps.title: Remediate any compromise from the landing page
steps.desc: Remove any payload delivered and reset any credentials entered on a harvesting page.
steps.outcome: Endpoint/account confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore endpoint/account and monitor
steps.desc: Return the endpoint or account to normal use and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: No recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review URL-scanning depth
steps.desc: Record the redirect chain technique and assess whether the email/URL scanning solution needs to follow deeper redirect chains before rendering a verdict.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32622.def: A malicious link that, once clicked, delivers an exploit targeting a browser or browser-plugin vulnerability, achieving code execution or compromise with no additional user action (no download confirmation, no macro enablement) required.
ITID-32622.purpose: Captures an email link that exploits a browser vulnerability requiring no further user interaction beyond the click itself.
scopeIncludes: Links exploiting a known-CVE browser rendering-engine or plugin vulnerability on click
Drive-by-style compromise reached via an email-delivered link
scopeExcludes: Multi-hop redirect evasion mechanics preceding the exploit (ITID-32621, though both may be present in one incident)
Safe-link rewriting abuse (ITID-32623)
Browser exploitation via a general web-based exploit kit landing page with no email delivery vector (ITID-32711-32714)
ITID-32622.severity: Critical — achieves code execution with minimal user interaction.
ITID-32622.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately; treat the clicking host as compromised.
indicators: Browser process spawning an unexpected child process immediately after navigation
EDR detection of exploit-shellcode execution from the browser process
Sandbox detonation flagging the destination page as exploitative
vectors: Email link to an exploit-kit-style landing page targeting an unpatched browser CVE
Malvertising-adjacent exploit delivery reached via an email link
rootCauses: Unpatched browser or browser plugin
Lack of browser isolation for links from untrusted email sources
controls: Timely browser and plugin patching
Remote browser isolation for links from external email
EDR process-lineage monitoring on browser processes
ITID-32622.detection: EDR process-lineage detection on the browser process provides strong technical coverage.
ITID-32622.response: Isolate the affected host, patch the browser environment-wide, and hunt for further exploitation.
metrics: Count of zero-click browser exploit detections per quarter
ITID-32622.notes: Scoped to the browser-exploitation outcome of an email-delivered link; email delivery is the required differentiator from the equivalent generic web exploit kit leaves in the Exploit Kits Type.

playbook.name: Response: Email Link Exploiting Zero-Click Browser Vulnerability
playbook.description: For a confirmed malicious email link that exploited a zero-click (or near-zero-interaction) browser vulnerability, compromising the endpoint with little or no further user action beyond the click, where no vendor patch may yet exist.

steps.title: Confirm zero-click exploitation and capture forensic artifacts
steps.desc: Review EDR/browser crash telemetry to confirm compromise occurred with minimal user interaction and capture memory/exploit artifacts for analysis before remediation.
steps.outcome: Zero-click exploitation confirmed and artifacts preserved.
steps.abort: If the link was blocked before rendering, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Determine whether the technique is a known or unpatched (zero-day) vulnerability
steps.desc: Work with threat intelligence/reverse engineering to determine if the exploited vulnerability is a known patched CVE or an unpatched zero-day, and identify other recipients of the same link.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability status determined; recipient population identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint(s)
steps.desc: Network-isolate all endpoints confirmed to have been exploited.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Purge the message and block the link organization-wide
steps.desc: Remove the message from all mailboxes and block the malicious URL/domain at the web and email gateway.
steps.outcome: Message purged; link blocked.

steps.title: Escalate to the browser/OS vendor if a zero-day is confirmed
steps.desc: If no patch exists, report the vulnerability to the affected vendor and open an urgent internal tracking item; apply interim mitigations (browser isolation, feature disablement) fleet-wide until a patch ships.
steps.guidance: This is time-sensitive given the zero-click nature and lack of a patch.
steps.outcome: Vendor notified; interim mitigation applied; patch tracked to closure.

steps.title: Rebuild affected endpoints and rotate exposed credentials
steps.desc: Given the zero-click, low-visibility nature of the compromise, rebuild/reimage affected endpoints rather than relying solely on cleanup, and rotate any credentials/tokens accessible from them.
steps.outcome: Endpoints rebuilt; exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Restore endpoints once patched or mitigated
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service only after the interim mitigation or vendor patch is confirmed in place, with elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored with mitigation/patch confirmed.

steps.title: Document the zero-click exploit and track patch deployment
steps.desc: Record the exploitation technique, vendor response, and patch timeline; confirm patch deployment once released.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and patch deployment tracked to closure.

ITID-32623.def: Exploitation of an email security vendor's link-rewriting ('safe link') feature — which proxies clicks through the vendor's domain for time-of-click checking — to disguise a malicious final destination behind a trusted vendor domain, or to exploit a re-scan gap in that service.
ITID-32623.purpose: Captures abuse of a security vendor's own URL rewriting/safe-link service to smuggle a malicious destination past its own protection.
scopeIncludes: Malicious links wrapped in a legitimate safe-link rewriting domain to inherit its trust
Exploitation of a re-scanning gap or logic flaw in a specific safe-link vendor's implementation
scopeExcludes: General multi-hop redirect chains not specifically abusing a safe-link vendor's own domain (ITID-32621)
Zero-click browser exploitation at the final destination (ITID-32622)
ITID-32623.severity: High — inherits the trust of a recognized security vendor domain, increasing click-through likelihood.
ITID-32623.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if confirmed clicked by a user.
ITID-32623.escalation: Escalate to the email security vendor and internal email security engineering to report the bypass.
indicators: Malicious final destination reached via a link hosted on a recognized safe-link/rewriting domain
User reports of a 'trusted-looking' link leading to a credential harvesting or exploit page
vectors: Registering a domain that passes initial vendor reputation checks, then swapping content post-scan
Chaining a safe-link wrapper in front of an otherwise-flagged malicious URL
rootCauses: Vendor safe-link service not re-scanning at time of click, or re-scanning with insufficient frequency
Over-trust placed on the rewritten domain by users and downstream filters
controls: Time-of-click re-scanning by the safe-link vendor
Reporting confirmed bypasses to the vendor for signature/logic updates
ITID-32623.detection: Detection relies on downstream outcome monitoring (credential harvest/exploit detonation) since the wrapping domain itself appears trusted.
ITID-32623.response: Report the bypass to the vendor, block the underlying destination, and assess user impact.
metrics: Count of safe-link bypass incidents reported to vendor per quarter
ITID-32623.notes: Scoped specifically to abuse of a security vendor's own rewriting/proxy trust mechanism, distinct from generic redirect-chain evasion (ITID-32621).

playbook.name: Response: Email Link Abusing URL Rewriting/Safe-Link Bypass
playbook.description: For a confirmed malicious email link that abused the organization's own URL-rewriting/safe-link protection service (e.g. time-of-click re-scan gaps, or wrapping a malicious URL so it inherits the rewriter's trusted domain reputation) to reach the victim.

steps.title: Confirm the bypass technique against the safe-link service
steps.desc: Review email security gateway logs to confirm the malicious URL was wrapped/rewritten by the safe-link service and determine how it evaded time-of-click re-scanning (e.g. payload swapped after initial scan, scan-then-serve-malicious behavior).
steps.outcome: Bypass technique confirmed.
steps.abort: If the safe-link service correctly blocked the click at time-of-click, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify all users who clicked the wrapped link
steps.desc: Query safe-link click logs for every user who clicked the wrapped URL, since the rewriter itself logs each click.
steps.outcome: Full affected-user population identified.

steps.title: Isolate any endpoint where the final payload executed
steps.desc: Network-isolate endpoints confirmed to have reached the malicious final destination and executed a payload.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Block the final destination domain and purge the message
steps.desc: Block the true malicious destination domain (not just the rewriter wrapper) at the web/email gateway, and purge the message from all mailboxes.
steps.outcome: Malicious destination blocked; message purged.

steps.title: Remediate any endpoint/account compromise
steps.desc: Remove any payload delivered and reset any credentials entered on a harvesting page reached via the bypass.
steps.outcome: Endpoint/account confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore endpoint/account and monitor
steps.desc: Return the endpoint or account to normal use and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: No recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and escalate the safe-link vendor gap
steps.desc: Record the bypass technique and raise the gap with the safe-link vendor; assess whether re-scan frequency or wrapper configuration needs adjustment.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and vendor gap raised.

ITID-32624.def: An incident involving a malicious email link exploiting a technical vulnerability or evasion mechanism, not clearly matching redirect-chain, zero-click browser, or safe-link-bypass leaves.
ITID-32624.purpose: Catch-all for email exploit-link incidents that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific exploit link leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (32621-32623)
ITID-32624.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-32624.escalation: Reclassify once the specific link exploitation pattern is clarified.
indicators: Link-related alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Email link exploit of unclear specific mechanism
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: URL rewriting and time-of-click link scanning
Web proxy/DNS filtering of malicious domains
Browser isolation for email-borne links
User awareness training on phishing links
ITID-32624.detection: Same general email/link telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32624.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32624.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Email Exploit Link
playbook.description: For a confirmed malicious email link exploit that does not fit a more specific redirect-chain, zero-click, or safe-link-bypass classification.

steps.title: Confirm the click and the resulting exploit/impact
steps.desc: Review web proxy/EDR telemetry to confirm the user clicked the malicious link and determine what it delivered or accomplished; reclassify to a more specific playbook if the technique becomes clear.
steps.outcome: Impact confirmed and characterized.
steps.abort: If the link was blocked before landing, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify other recipients of the same link
steps.desc: Search mail logs for all other recipients of the email containing the malicious link.
steps.outcome: Full recipient population identified.

steps.title: Isolate the affected endpoint if applicable
steps.desc: Network-isolate the endpoint if a payload executed or code ran as a result of the click.
steps.outcome: Endpoint isolated if applicable.

steps.title: Block the malicious link and purge the message
steps.desc: Block the domain/URL at the web/email gateway and purge the message from all mailboxes.
steps.outcome: Link blocked; message purged.

steps.title: Remediate any resulting compromise
steps.desc: Remove any payload delivered and reset any credentials exposed.
steps.outcome: Endpoint/account confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore and monitor
steps.desc: Return the endpoint/account to normal use and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: No recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings about the link and delivery mechanism for future correlation.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32631.def: A VBA macro embedded in an Office document configured with an auto-execute trigger (e.g., AutoOpen, Document_Open, Workbook_Open) that runs malicious code as soon as the document is opened and macros are enabled, without requiring any additional interaction.
ITID-32631.purpose: Captures a malicious VBA macro engineered to execute automatically the moment a document is opened, without further user action.
scopeIncludes: VBA macros using AutoOpen/Document_Open/Workbook_Open or equivalent auto-execute event handlers
Macros that execute immediately upon macro enablement with no further user interaction
scopeExcludes: Macro acting purely as a downloader for a second-stage payload (ITID-32632, though the two are often combined — classify by the primary characteristic under investigation)
Non-VBA legacy feature abuse such as DDE or XLM 4.0 macros (ITID-32633)
ITID-32631.severity: High — auto-execution removes the need for any further victim interaction beyond enabling macros.
ITID-32631.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately; treat the host as compromised upon confirmed macro execution.
indicators: Office application spawning a child process (e.g., powershell.exe, cmd.exe, wscript.exe) immediately after document open
Document metadata/static analysis revealing an AutoOpen/Document_Open macro subroutine
Macro-enablement telemetry correlated with immediate anomalous process activity
vectors: Email attachment prompting the user to 'Enable Content' to trigger the auto-execute macro
Templates or add-ins with embedded auto-execute macros
rootCauses: Macros enabled by default or insufficiently restricted by policy
Users trained to click 'Enable Content' without scrutiny
controls: Block macros from the internet by default (Group Policy)
Macro execution logging and alerting
Application allowlisting for macro-spawned child processes
ITID-32631.detection: EDR process-lineage detection (Office spawning script interpreters/shells) provides strong, direct technical coverage.
ITID-32631.response: Isolate the affected host, block the malicious document/sender, and hunt for further spread from the initial execution.
metrics: Count of auto-execute macro detections per quarter
Percentage of endpoints with internet macros blocked by policy
ITID-32631.notes: Differentiated from sibling leaves by the auto-execute trigger mechanism itself; downstream payload behavior (dropper) is captured separately in ITID-32632 when that is the primary characteristic.

playbook.name: Response: Malicious VBA Macro with Auto-Execute Trigger
playbook.description: For a confirmed malicious Office document containing a VBA macro that executed automatically on open (AutoOpen/Document_Open) without requiring further user interaction beyond enabling content.

steps.title: Confirm macro execution and reconstruct the process tree
steps.desc: Review EDR telemetry to confirm the macro auto-executed and reconstruct the full process tree spawned from the Office application to identify any living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) invoked.
steps.guidance: Macros frequently chain into legitimate system binaries (e.g. mshta, wscript, powershell, rundll32) — trace every child process.
steps.outcome: Macro execution confirmed and full process/execution chain mapped.
steps.abort: If the document was quarantined or the macro was blocked by policy before execution, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify the sender and other recipients
steps.desc: Identify the sending address/domain and search mail logs for all other recipients of the same or similar document.
steps.outcome: Full recipient population identified.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints
steps.desc: Network-isolate all endpoints where the macro executed.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Purge the message from all mailboxes and block the sender
steps.desc: Remove the malicious email from all recipient mailboxes and block the sending address/domain.
steps.outcome: Message purged; sender blocked.

steps.title: Remove the payload and any LOLBin-based persistence
steps.desc: Remove the dropped/downloaded payload and any persistence established via the LOLBin chain (scheduled tasks, run keys, WMI subscriptions).
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Confirm macro-execution policy is enforced fleet-wide
steps.desc: Verify that macros from the internet are blocked or require explicit approval fleet-wide (e.g. via Office group policy), and remediate any gaps.
steps.outcome: Macro policy confirmed enforced across the fleet.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and monitor
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review macro-blocking policy
steps.desc: Record the full execution chain and confirm macro-blocking policy coverage across the organization.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32632.def: A malicious Office macro that acts primarily as a lightweight downloader, reaching out to attacker-controlled infrastructure to retrieve and execute a second-stage payload (e.g., a commodity loader or ransomware precursor) rather than embedding the final payload directly.
ITID-32632.purpose: Captures a macro whose primary function is to retrieve and execute a second-stage payload from external infrastructure.
scopeIncludes: Macros making an outbound connection to fetch and execute a second-stage binary or script
Macro-launched living-off-the-land downloaders (e.g., invoking certutil, bitsadmin, PowerShell download cradles)
scopeExcludes: Macro auto-execute trigger mechanics as the primary classification focus (ITID-32631)
Non-VBA legacy feature abuse (DDE/XLM 4.0) as the delivery mechanism (ITID-32633)
ITID-32632.severity: Critical — typically the first stage of a broader compromise chain (loader, ransomware, or RAT deployment).
ITID-32632.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately; block the download infrastructure and assess what second-stage payload was retrieved.
indicators: Macro-spawned process making an outbound HTTP/HTTPS connection to fetch a file
PowerShell or script-interpreter download-cradle syntax launched from an Office process
Newly written executable/script on disk immediately following document open
vectors: Macro launching a PowerShell download cradle to retrieve a loader
Macro invoking a living-off-the-land binary to fetch the second stage
rootCauses: Macros enabled by default
Lack of egress filtering/monitoring on script-interpreter-initiated connections
controls: Block macros from the internet by default
Egress filtering/monitoring on script-interpreter network connections
Application control blocking unauthorized LOLBins from network access
ITID-32632.detection: EDR network-connection-by-process monitoring on Office and script-interpreter processes provides strong, direct coverage.
ITID-32632.response: Isolate the host, block the download infrastructure, and identify/eradicate the retrieved second-stage payload.
metrics: Count of macro-downloader detections per quarter
Mean time to block download infrastructure after detection
ITID-32632.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32631 by focus on the downloader/dropper function rather than the auto-execute trigger mechanism; an incident may warrant both codes if both characteristics are prominent, in which case classify by the dominant investigative finding.

playbook.name: Response: Macro Downloading Second-Stage Payload (Macro Dropper)
playbook.description: For a confirmed malicious macro that functioned as a dropper, reaching out to download and execute a second-stage payload (loader, RAT, ransomware precursor) after initial execution.

steps.title: Confirm the dropper behavior and identify the second-stage payload
steps.desc: Review EDR telemetry and reconstruct the process tree to confirm the macro downloaded and executed a second-stage payload, and identify what that payload was and did.
steps.guidance: Trace network connections made by the Office process/child processes to identify the staging server.
steps.outcome: Second-stage payload identified and its capability/impact determined.
steps.abort: If the download was blocked before completion, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify the staging server and other recipients
steps.desc: Identify the staging server that hosted the second-stage payload and search mail logs for all other recipients of the same document.
steps.outcome: Staging infrastructure and full recipient population identified.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints immediately
steps.desc: Network-isolate all endpoints where the second-stage payload executed, given the elevated risk of further staged capability (e.g. ransomware).
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Block the staging server and purge the message
steps.desc: Block the staging/C2 domain at the network layer and purge the message from all mailboxes.
steps.outcome: Staging infrastructure blocked; message purged.

steps.title: Remove the second-stage payload and any persistence
steps.desc: Remove the second-stage payload and verify no persistence mechanism was established; consider rebuilding the endpoint if the payload had ransomware or credential-theft capability.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean or rebuilt.

steps.title: Rotate any credentials accessible from the compromised endpoint
steps.desc: Given the second-stage payload's capability, rotate credentials/tokens accessible from the endpoint as a precaution.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and apply elevated monitoring
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review macro/dropper detection coverage
steps.desc: Record the full dropper chain and assess whether macro-blocking or network egress controls should be strengthened.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32633.def: Abuse of legitimate, non-VBA Office application features — such as Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) fields or Excel 4.0 (XLM) macros — as a living-off-the-land execution mechanism, avoiding VBA-specific macro detection controls entirely.
ITID-32633.purpose: Captures exploitation of legacy Office application features other than VBA macros to achieve code execution.
scopeIncludes: Malicious DDE field code embedded in a document to launch a command on open
XLM 4.0 macro sheets (as opposed to VBA) used to execute malicious code
scopeExcludes: Standard VBA auto-execute macros (ITID-32631)
VBA macro acting as a downloader (ITID-32632)
ITID-32633.severity: High — specifically chosen to evade VBA-macro-focused detection and blocking controls.
ITID-32633.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately; treat the host as compromised upon confirmed execution.
indicators: Document containing DDE field codes referencing an external command
XLM 4.0 macro sheet present in a workbook with obfuscated formula-based execution
Office process spawning a child process without a corresponding VBA macro project
vectors: Email attachment with DDE-based command execution requiring only a benign-looking prompt to enable
XLM 4.0 macro workbook distributed to bypass VBA-specific blocking policies
rootCauses: DDE and legacy XLM macro execution not disabled or restricted by policy
Detection tooling tuned specifically for VBA macros, missing legacy feature abuse
mitreTechniques: T1559.002 Inter-Process Communication: Dynamic Data Exchange
controls: Disable DDE and legacy XLM 4.0 macro execution via Office policy
EDR detection tuned to non-VBA Office execution paths
ITID-32633.detection: Requires detection tooling specifically tuned to non-VBA execution paths (DDE/XLM4); standard VBA-macro-focused scanning has a known blind spot here.
ITID-32633.response: Isolate the host, disable the legacy feature environment-wide, and hunt for further exploitation using the same technique.
metrics: Count of DDE/XLM4 abuse detections per quarter
Percentage of endpoints with legacy features disabled
ITID-32633.notes: Scoped specifically to non-VBA legacy feature abuse, the key differentiating axis from the two VBA-macro leaves in this Type.

playbook.name: Response: Macro Exploiting Living-off-the-Land Office Application Features (DDE/XLM 4.0 Macros)
playbook.description: For a confirmed malicious document that used legacy Office living-off-the-land features — Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) fields or Excel 4.0 (XLM) macros — to execute code without a traditional VBA macro, often chaining directly into system binaries.

steps.title: Confirm the DDE/XLM4 technique and reconstruct the full process tree
steps.desc: Review EDR telemetry to confirm the DDE field or XLM 4.0 macro executed and reconstruct the complete process tree, since these techniques characteristically chain directly into living-off-the-land binaries (mshta, cmd, powershell, regsvr32) with no traditional VBA macro present.
steps.guidance: Standard macro-scanning tools that only inspect VBA project streams will miss DDE fields and XLM4 macros — confirm the document was analyzed with tooling that covers both.
steps.outcome: Technique confirmed and full execution chain mapped, including any LOLBin abuse.
steps.abort: If the field/macro was stripped or blocked before execution, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify the sender, other recipients, and payload
steps.desc: Identify the sending address/domain, search for all other recipients of the same document, and determine the ultimate payload delivered via the LOLBin chain.
steps.outcome: Recipient population and payload identified.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints
steps.desc: Network-isolate all endpoints where the technique executed.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Purge the message from all mailboxes and block the sender
steps.desc: Remove the malicious email from all recipient mailboxes and block the sending address/domain.
steps.outcome: Message purged; sender blocked.

steps.title: Remove the payload and any LOLBin-based persistence
steps.desc: Remove the payload and any persistence established via the abused system binaries.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Disable DDE and restrict XLM4 macro execution fleet-wide
steps.desc: Apply Office group policy to disable automatic DDE updates and restrict/disable XLM 4.0 macro execution across the fleet, since these legacy features are rarely required for legitimate business use.
steps.outcome: Legacy feature disabled/restricted fleet-wide.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and monitor
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and confirm legacy-feature hardening
steps.desc: Record the full LOLBin chain and confirm the DDE/XLM4 hardening policy is deployed and effective; assess detection coverage for these legacy techniques.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32634.def: An incident involving a malicious embedded macro or macro-adjacent feature abuse, not clearly matching auto-execute, downloader, or legacy non-VBA feature leaves.
ITID-32634.purpose: Catch-all for embedded macro exploitation incidents that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific embedded macro leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (32631-32633)
ITID-32634.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-32634.escalation: Reclassify once the specific macro exploitation pattern is clarified.
indicators: Macro-related alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Macro-based exploit of unclear specific mechanism

mitreTechniques: T1059.005 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
controls: Macro execution blocking via group policy
Email gateway attachment sandboxing
Application allowlisting
Endpoint detection for macro-spawned process anomalies

metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32634.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Embedded Macro Exploit
playbook.description: For a confirmed malicious embedded macro exploit that does not fit a more specific auto-execute-VBA, dropper, or DDE/XLM4 classification.

steps.title: Confirm macro execution and reconstruct the process tree
steps.desc: Review EDR telemetry to confirm the macro executed and reconstruct the process tree spawned from the Office application; reclassify to a more specific playbook if the technique becomes clear.
steps.guidance: Macros often chain into living-off-the-land binaries — trace every child process.
steps.outcome: Macro execution confirmed and execution chain mapped.
steps.abort: If the macro was blocked before execution, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify the sender and other recipients
steps.desc: Identify the sending address/domain and search mail logs for all other recipients of the same document.
steps.outcome: Full recipient population identified.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints
steps.desc: Network-isolate all endpoints where the macro executed.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Purge the message from all mailboxes and block the sender
steps.desc: Remove the malicious email from all recipient mailboxes and block the sending address/domain.
steps.outcome: Message purged; sender blocked.

steps.title: Remove the payload and check for persistence
steps.desc: Remove any dropped payload and verify no persistence mechanism was installed.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and monitor
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service and apply elevated monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review macro-blocking policy
steps.desc: Record the execution chain observed and confirm macro-blocking policy coverage.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32711.def: A web page hosting a commercially traded or freely circulated commodity exploit kit (e.g., a known kit family with a recognizable landing-page structure) that automatically attempts a battery of known browser/plugin exploits against any visitor, without victim-specific targeting or fingerprinting sophistication.
ITID-32711.purpose: Captures encounters with an off-the-shelf, widely circulated commodity exploit kit landing page.
scopeIncludes: Landing pages matching a known, named commodity exploit kit signature
Mass, indiscriminate drive-by exploitation attempts against any visiting browser
scopeExcludes: Exploit kits with automated victim fingerprinting/payload selection logic (ITID-32712)
Distribution specifically via a compromised ad network (ITID-32713)
Custom, single-target exploit chains (Targeted Exploit Kits Type, ITID-32721-32723)
ITID-32711.severity: High if a vulnerable browser reaches the page and is exploited; Medium if blocked prior to exploitation.
ITID-32711.priority: P2, escalating to P1 upon confirmed successful exploitation.
ITID-32711.escalation: Escalate to IR upon confirmed exploitation; escalate to web/proxy security engineering to block the landing page domain regardless.
indicators: Proxy/IDS signature match for a known commodity exploit kit landing page
Browser exploitation attempt logged against a visiting endpoint
Sandbox detonation confirming known exploit kit behavior
vectors: Compromised legitimate website redirecting visitors to the kit's landing page
Malicious search-engine-optimized pages leading users to the kit
rootCauses: Unpatched browser/plugin population within the organization
Lack of web/proxy filtering against known exploit kit indicators
controls: Web/proxy filtering against known exploit kit domains and signatures
Timely browser/plugin patching
Remote browser isolation for higher-risk browsing categories
ITID-32711.detection: IDS/proxy signature detection for known commodity kits provides strong, direct coverage; sandbox detonation confirms behavior for unknowns.
ITID-32711.response: Block the landing page domain, isolate any exploited host, and verify patch status across the affected browser population.
metrics: Count of commodity exploit kit encounters per quarter
Percentage blocked prior to exploitation
detections: Known exploit kit landing page signature alerting
ITID-32711.notes: Scoped to generic, off-the-shelf kits with no victim-specific targeting; targeted variants belong under the Targeted Exploit Kits Type.

playbook.name: Response: Commodity Exploit Kit Landing Page (Off-the-Shelf Kit)
playbook.description: For a confirmed encounter with a commodity, off-the-shelf web-based exploit kit landing page, typically opportunistic and part of a high-volume, non-targeted campaign.

steps.title: Confirm the exploit kit family and payload delivered
steps.desc: Review EDR/web proxy telemetry and, where available, threat-intel signatures to identify the specific commodity exploit kit family and the payload it attempted or succeeded in delivering.
steps.guidance: Correlate against known exploit kit fingerprints/IOCs.
steps.outcome: Kit family and payload identified.
steps.abort: If the kit was blocked before payload delivery, downgrade to a near-miss.
steps.tool: EDR / web proxy / threat intelligence platform

steps.title: Identify other users who encountered the same kit
steps.desc: Query proxy/DNS logs for other users who hit the same landing page or associated infrastructure in the relevant time window, since commodity kits are typically high-volume.
steps.outcome: Full scope of exposed endpoints identified.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints and block the kit infrastructure
steps.desc: Network-isolate any endpoint that received a payload, and block the landing page domain and known kit infrastructure at the web/DNS layer.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated; kit infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Remove the payload and check for persistence
steps.desc: Remove the delivered payload and verify no persistence mechanism was installed.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Correlate against the known kit family's threat intelligence
steps.desc: Submit IOCs to threat intelligence for correlation against the known kit family to identify any additional related infrastructure to block.
steps.outcome: Related infrastructure identified and blocked.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and monitor
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service and apply standard monitoring, given the opportunistic nature of the campaign.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and confirm patch coverage for the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Record the kit family and confirm patch coverage for whatever vulnerability it targeted, since commodity kits typically exploit known, patchable issues.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32712.def: An exploit kit landing page that first fingerprints the visiting browser, plugins, and OS to identify known vulnerabilities present in that specific environment, then dynamically serves only the matching exploit — increasing success rate and reducing detectable noise compared to a commodity kit firing all exploits at once.
ITID-32712.purpose: Captures an exploit kit that automatically profiles a visitor's environment to select the most effective exploit rather than attempting all exploits indiscriminately.
scopeIncludes: Landing pages performing browser/plugin/OS fingerprinting prior to exploit selection
Dynamic, victim-environment-specific exploit payload delivery
scopeExcludes: Generic commodity kits firing a fixed exploit battery with no fingerprinting (ITID-32711)
Ad-network distribution as the primary characteristic (ITID-32713)
ITID-32712.severity: High — increased success rate due to targeted exploit selection.
ITID-32712.priority: P1 upon confirmed successful exploitation; P2 for detected fingerprinting without confirmed exploitation.
ITID-32712.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately upon confirmed exploitation.
indicators: JavaScript fingerprinting code enumerating installed plugins/versions prior to any exploit delivery
Different exploit payloads served to different visitors from the same landing page
Sandbox analysis showing conditional exploit logic based on reported environment
vectors: Client-side fingerprinting scripts run before the actual exploit payload is served
Server-side environment analysis based on User-Agent and plugin enumeration requests
rootCauses: Unpatched or outdated browser/plugin versions detectable via fingerprinting
Lack of browser fingerprinting-resistance controls
mitreTechniques: T1592.001 Gather Victim Host Information: Hardware
T1592.002 Gather Victim Host Information: Software
controls: Browser fingerprinting-resistance settings/extensions
Timely browser/plugin patching to reduce the fingerprintable attack surface
Web/proxy filtering against known fingerprinting script signatures
ITID-32712.detection: Requires content-level analysis to detect fingerprinting scripts (a lighter-weight signal than a full exploit payload); sandbox detonation with realistic environment simulation improves coverage.
ITID-32712.response: Block the landing page, isolate any exploited host, and identify what environment data was fingerprinted for use in the attack.
metrics: Count of fingerprinting-driven exploit kit encounters per quarter
ITID-32712.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32711 specifically by the presence of automated victim fingerprinting driving payload selection.

playbook.name: Response: Exploit Kit with Automated Vulnerability Fingerprinting/Payload Selection
playbook.description: For a confirmed encounter with a web-based exploit kit that automatically fingerprinted the visiting browser/plugin environment and selected an appropriate exploit/payload combination, still generally opportunistic/high-volume in nature.

steps.title: Confirm the fingerprinting behavior and selected exploit/payload
steps.desc: Review EDR/web proxy telemetry to confirm the kit profiled the browser/plugin environment before serving a tailored exploit, and identify which exploit and payload were ultimately selected and delivered.
steps.outcome: Fingerprinting technique and delivered exploit/payload confirmed.
steps.abort: If the kit was blocked before payload selection completed, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify other users who encountered the same kit
steps.desc: Query proxy/DNS logs for other users who hit the same landing page or infrastructure, since this remains a high-volume commodity technique despite the fingerprinting sophistication.
steps.outcome: Full scope of exposed endpoints identified.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints and block the kit infrastructure
steps.desc: Network-isolate any endpoint that received a payload, and block the landing page domain and fingerprinting/exploit-serving infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated; kit infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Remove the payload and check for persistence
steps.desc: Remove the delivered payload and verify no persistence mechanism was installed.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Confirm patch coverage for the fingerprinted vulnerability
steps.desc: Identify the specific browser/plugin vulnerability the kit selected for this environment and confirm patch coverage fleet-wide.
steps.outcome: Patch status confirmed and remediated where needed.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and monitor
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service and apply standard monitoring.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and correlate with the known kit family
steps.desc: Record the fingerprinting technique and correlate with threat intelligence on the known kit family for broader detection coverage.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32713.def: An exploit kit delivered to victims via malicious advertisements (malvertising) served through a legitimate ad exchange or network — either a compromised ad slot on a trusted site, or a malicious ad that passed initial ad-network vetting — rather than via a compromised website or direct link.
ITID-32713.purpose: Captures an exploit kit reaching victims specifically through a compromised or abused online advertising network.
scopeIncludes: Malicious ad creative on a legitimate, high-traffic site redirecting to an exploit kit landing page
Ad-network-served content passing initial review, then swapped to serve exploit kit redirects post-approval
scopeExcludes: Generic commodity landing pages reached via a compromised website rather than an ad network (ITID-32711)
Fingerprinting-driven exploit selection as the primary characteristic (ITID-32712, though malvertising campaigns often also fingerprint — classify by the dominant characteristic)
ITID-32713.severity: High — leverages the trust of a legitimate, high-traffic site to reach a broad victim population.
ITID-32713.priority: P1 upon confirmed successful exploitation via a malvertising chain.
ITID-32713.escalation: Escalate to IR and to the ad network/publisher to have the malicious creative removed immediately.
indicators: Redirect chain originating from an ad-serving domain leading to a known exploit kit landing page
User browsing a legitimate, trusted site immediately prior to exploitation with no other suspicious navigation
vectors: Malicious creative submitted to an ad exchange that passes initial vetting
Compromise of a legitimate advertiser's account to inject malicious redirects
rootCauses: Ad network vetting insufficient to detect delayed-activation malicious redirects
Lack of ad-content isolation/sandboxing on the browsing side
controls: Ad-blocking/script-blocking browser extensions on managed endpoints
Web/proxy filtering against known malicious ad-network redirect chains
Reporting malicious creatives to the ad network for takedown
ITID-32713.detection: Proxy logs showing ad-domain-to-exploit-kit redirect chains provide a strong technical signal distinguishing this from other delivery vectors.
ITID-32713.response: Block the ad-network redirect domain, report the malicious creative for takedown, and isolate any exploited host.
metrics: Count of malvertising-sourced exploit encounters per quarter
ITID-32713.notes: Differentiated from siblings by the distribution vector (compromised/abused ad network) rather than the kit's internal exploit-selection logic.

playbook.name: Response: Exploit Kit Distributed via Compromised Ad Network
playbook.description: For a confirmed web-based exploit kit encountered via a compromised or malicious advertising network (malvertising-driven distribution), generally opportunistic and high-volume.

steps.title: Confirm the exploit kit and the delivering ad creative
steps.desc: Review EDR/web proxy telemetry to confirm the kit's landing page and trace the browsing session back to the specific ad tag, ad network, or redirect chain that served it.
steps.outcome: Kit and delivering ad creative/network identified.
steps.abort: If the kit was blocked before payload delivery, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify all users exposed to the same ad campaign
steps.desc: Query proxy/DNS logs for other users who loaded the same malicious ad creative or redirect domain, given the high-volume nature of malvertising-driven kits.
steps.outcome: Full scope of exposed endpoints identified.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints and block the ad/kit infrastructure
steps.desc: Network-isolate any endpoint that received a payload, and block the ad network's serving domains and the full redirect/kit chain at the web/DNS layer.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated; malicious ad and kit infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Notify the ad exchange of the malicious creative
steps.desc: Where the ad exchange/network can be identified, notify them so the malicious creative can be pulled from rotation.
steps.outcome: Ad exchange notified.

steps.title: Remove the payload and check for persistence
steps.desc: Remove the delivered payload and verify no persistence mechanism was installed.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and monitor
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service and apply standard monitoring.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review ad-blocking/script-blocking policy
steps.desc: Record the malvertising delivery chain and assess whether stricter ad-blocking or browser isolation would reduce future exposure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32714.def: An incident involving a web-based exploit kit, not clearly matching commodity landing page, automated fingerprinting, or malvertising distribution leaves.
ITID-32714.purpose: Catch-all for web-based exploit kit incidents that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific web-based exploit kit leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (32711-32713)
ITID-32714.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-32714.escalation: Reclassify once the specific exploit kit pattern is clarified.
indicators: Exploit-kit-related alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Web-based exploit delivery of unclear specific mechanism
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Web proxy filtering with exploit-kit signature detection
Browser and plugin patching automation
Browser isolation for high-risk browsing
Network egress filtering for post-exploit callbacks
ITID-32714.detection: Same general web/proxy telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32714.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32714.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Web-Based Exploit Kit
playbook.description: For a confirmed encounter with a web-based exploit kit that does not fit a more specific commodity-landing-page, fingerprinting, or malvertising-distribution classification.

steps.title: Confirm the exploit kit encounter and payload
steps.desc: Review EDR/web proxy telemetry to confirm the kit's landing page was reached and identify any payload delivered; reclassify to a more specific playbook if the distribution mechanism becomes clear.
steps.outcome: Encounter confirmed and payload identified.
steps.abort: If the kit was blocked before payload delivery, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify other users who encountered the same kit
steps.desc: Query proxy/DNS logs for other users who hit the same landing page or infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Full scope of exposed endpoints identified.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints and block the kit infrastructure
steps.desc: Network-isolate any endpoint that received a payload, and block the landing page domain and known kit infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated; kit infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Determine the distribution vector and block it
steps.desc: Determine how users reached the landing page (malvertising, compromised site, phishing link) and block that specific distribution channel.
steps.outcome: Distribution channel blocked.

steps.title: Remove the payload and check for persistence
steps.desc: Remove the delivered payload and verify no persistence mechanism was installed.
steps.outcome: Endpoints confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and monitor
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service and apply standard monitoring.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident
steps.desc: Record findings about the kit and delivery mechanism for future correlation.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32721.def: A custom-built sequence of exploits, developed or assembled specifically for one target organization or victim population, deployed by compromising a website that the intended victims are known to frequent (a watering hole) rather than through broad, indiscriminate distribution.
ITID-32721.purpose: Captures a bespoke exploit chain built and deployed against a single specific target via a watering-hole compromise.
scopeIncludes: Compromise of a site known to be frequented by a specific target organization's employees, seeded with a custom exploit chain
Exploit chains built or assembled specifically for one campaign rather than reused as a commodity kit
scopeExcludes: Broad, indiscriminate commodity exploit kit distribution (ITID-32711-32714)
Environment fingerprinting as the primary characteristic where the campaign is not watering-hole-specific (ITID-32722)
ITID-32721.severity: Critical — indicates a deliberate, resourced campaign against a specific organization.
ITID-32721.escalation: Escalate to IR and executive security leadership immediately given the targeted nature of the campaign.
indicators: A site known to be frequented by the organization's staff found serving exploit code only to visitors from the target's IP ranges
Exploit chain components not previously observed in any commodity kit tracking
Narrow, low-volume visitor targeting inconsistent with mass exploitation
vectors: Compromise of a trusted third-party or industry-specific website frequented by the target population
IP-range or organizational fingerprint gating limiting exploit delivery to the intended victims only
rootCauses: Third-party site relied upon by staff lacking adequate security hardening
Insufficient threat intelligence sharing on watering-hole campaigns within the target's sector
mitreTechniques: T1591.001 Gather Victim Org Information: Determine Physical Locations
controls: Threat intelligence monitoring for watering-hole activity in frequently-visited third-party sites
Web/proxy filtering with behavioral anomaly detection
Remote browser isolation for high-risk or high-value user populations
ITID-32721.detection: Requires threat-intelligence-driven and behavioral detection since indicators are novel and low-volume by design; commodity signature detection has limited coverage here.
ITID-32721.response: Isolate any exploited host, notify the compromised third-party site owner, and assess the full scope of the targeted campaign.
metrics: Count of confirmed watering-hole campaigns per year
ITID-32721.notes: Scoped to the watering-hole delivery mechanism against a specific target; distinct from environment-fingerprinting-focused targeting (ITID-32722) which may or may not use a watering hole.

playbook.name: Response: Custom Exploit Chain Built for Single-Target Watering-Hole Campaign
playbook.description: For a confirmed custom-built exploit chain deployed via a watering-hole compromise targeted specifically at this organization or its personnel, indicating a resourced, motivated adversary who conducted real reconnaissance on the org.

steps.title: Confirm targeting and escalate to full incident investigation
steps.desc: Confirm the exploit chain is custom-built and specifically targeted (e.g. tailored to internal tooling, employee-specific watering-hole site) rather than commodity, and immediately escalate to a full incident investigation given the implied reconnaissance and adversary sophistication.
steps.guidance: Custom targeting implies the adversary has studied this organization specifically — treat as a high-severity incident from the outset, not a routine endpoint cleanup.
steps.outcome: Targeted nature confirmed; full incident response engaged with appropriate leadership visibility.
steps.abort: If further analysis shows the kit is actually a known commodity chain, downgrade to the standard exploit-kit playbook.
steps.tool: EDR / threat intelligence / incident response team

steps.title: Reconstruct the full exploit chain and identify all affected personnel
steps.desc: Reverse-engineer the exploit chain to understand every stage and capability, and identify every employee/system that visited the watering-hole site.
steps.outcome: Full exploit chain and affected population mapped.

steps.title: Determine what reconnaissance informed the targeting
steps.desc: Assess what information about the organization (org chart, internal tools, employee habits) the adversary likely used to craft this targeted watering-hole, to understand the broader exposure.
steps.outcome: Likely reconnaissance sources identified.

steps.title: Isolate all affected endpoints immediately
steps.desc: Network-isolate every endpoint confirmed or suspected to have been exploited.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Block the watering-hole site and exploit chain infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the compromised watering-hole domain and every stage of infrastructure in the exploit chain (C2, staging, exfiltration).
steps.outcome: Full adversary infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials and tokens accessible from affected endpoints
steps.desc: Given the sophistication implied, treat every affected endpoint as fully compromised and rotate all accessible credentials, tokens, and keys.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Rebuild affected endpoints and hunt for lateral movement
steps.desc: Rebuild/reimage affected endpoints rather than relying on cleanup, and conduct a threat hunt across the environment for evidence of lateral movement or additional footholds established by this adversary.
steps.outcome: Endpoints rebuilt; no additional footholds found, or additional compromise remediated.

steps.title: Restore endpoints with elevated, sustained monitoring
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service only after full remediation, with sustained elevated monitoring given the targeted nature of the campaign and likelihood of repeat attempts.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed over an extended monitoring window.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review and threat-actor attribution assessment
steps.desc: Document the complete campaign, assess likely attribution/motive, and brief leadership on the implication that the organization has been specifically targeted for reconnaissance and exploitation.
steps.outcome: Full report completed; leadership briefed; long-term monitoring plan established.

ITID-32722.def: An exploit kit built for a targeted campaign that performs deep, victim-specific environment fingerprinting (organizational network indicators, specific software builds, internal hostnames) and only deploys its payload when the fingerprint matches the intended victim, refusing to fire against any other visitor to reduce exposure and evade broad detection.
ITID-32722.purpose: Captures a targeted exploit kit that fingerprints a specific victim's environment before deciding whether and how to deploy its payload.
scopeIncludes: Exploit logic gated on organization-specific network or environment fingerprints
Payloads that refuse to execute or self-delete when the fingerprint does not match the intended target
scopeExcludes: Watering-hole delivery mechanism as the primary characteristic (ITID-32721, though the two frequently co-occur — classify by the dominant investigative finding)
Broad automated fingerprinting used by a non-targeted commodity kit for exploit selection only (ITID-32712)
ITID-32722.severity: Critical — deliberate targeting combined with anti-analysis fingerprinting indicates a highly resourced, evasive campaign.
ITID-32722.escalation: Escalate to IR and executive security leadership immediately.
indicators: Payload sample exhibiting conditional execution logic gated on specific organizational indicators
Payload observed refusing to execute or self-deleting in sandbox/non-target environments
Fingerprint checks referencing internal-only naming conventions or IP ranges
vectors: Custom loader performing environment checks before deploying the final payload
Staged delivery where only fingerprint-matched targets receive the exploit
rootCauses: Leaked or reconnaissance-derived internal environment details enabling precise fingerprint gating
Sandbox/analysis environments not resembling the real target environment closely enough to trigger the payload
mitreTechniques: T1592.001 Gather Victim Host Information: Hardware
controls: Sandbox environments configured to closely mimic real production environments
Threat intelligence monitoring for targeted campaign indicators
Restricting exposure of internal environment details in reconnaissance-vulnerable channels
ITID-32722.detection: Requires realistic sandbox environments and behavioral analysis to trigger conditional payloads; standard sandboxing has a known blind spot here.
ITID-32722.response: Isolate any exploited host, reverse-engineer the fingerprint-gating logic to understand what internal details were known to the attacker, and assess the full campaign scope.
metrics: Count of confirmed fingerprint-gated targeted campaigns per year
ITID-32722.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32721 by focus on fingerprint-gated conditional deployment logic rather than the watering-hole distribution vector itself.

playbook.name: Response: Targeted Exploit Kit Fingerprinting Specific Victim Environment Before Deployment
playbook.description: For a confirmed targeted exploit kit that fingerprinted this specific victim's environment (internal software versions, network configuration, employee identity) before selectively deploying its exploit, indicating deliberate, org-specific reconnaissance rather than opportunistic targeting.

steps.title: Confirm targeted fingerprinting and escalate to full incident investigation
steps.desc: Confirm the kit fingerprinted characteristics specific to this organization's environment before deploying, and escalate immediately to a full incident investigation given the implied targeting and reconnaissance.
steps.guidance: This differs from commodity fingerprinting (which profiles generic browser/plugin versions) — victim-specific fingerprinting implies the adversary already knows this is the intended target.
steps.outcome: Targeted nature confirmed; full incident response engaged with appropriate leadership visibility.
steps.abort: If the fingerprinting is generic (browser/plugin only) rather than victim-specific, downgrade to the standard exploit-kit playbook.
steps.tool: EDR / threat intelligence / incident response team

steps.title: Reconstruct the fingerprinting logic and identify all affected personnel
steps.desc: Reverse-engineer what victim-specific characteristics the kit checked for and identify every employee/system it was served to.
steps.outcome: Fingerprinting logic and affected population mapped.

steps.title: Assess what reconnaissance informed the fingerprinting criteria
steps.desc: Determine what information about the organization's environment the adversary likely used to build the victim-specific fingerprinting logic.
steps.outcome: Likely reconnaissance sources identified.

steps.title: Isolate all affected endpoints immediately
steps.desc: Network-isolate every endpoint confirmed or suspected to have received the tailored exploit.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Block the delivery and exploit chain infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the delivery vector and every stage of infrastructure in the exploit chain.
steps.outcome: Full adversary infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials and tokens accessible from affected endpoints
steps.desc: Treat every affected endpoint as fully compromised and rotate all accessible credentials, tokens, and keys.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Rebuild affected endpoints and hunt for lateral movement
steps.desc: Rebuild/reimage affected endpoints and conduct a threat hunt across the environment for evidence of lateral movement or additional footholds.
steps.outcome: Endpoints rebuilt; no additional footholds found, or additional compromise remediated.

steps.title: Restore endpoints with elevated, sustained monitoring
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service only after full remediation, with sustained elevated monitoring given the targeted nature of the campaign.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed over an extended monitoring window.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review and threat-actor attribution assessment
steps.desc: Document the complete campaign, assess likely attribution/motive, and brief leadership on the implication that the organization has been specifically targeted.
steps.outcome: Full report completed; leadership briefed; long-term monitoring plan established.

ITID-32723.def: An incident involving a targeted, custom-built exploit kit, not clearly matching watering-hole delivery or fingerprint-gated deployment leaves.
ITID-32723.purpose: Catch-all for targeted exploit kit incidents that do not fit the more specific leaves under this Type.
scopeIncludes: Cases logged before enough detail is available to reclassify to a specific targeted exploit kit leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases clearly matching a more specific sibling ITID (32721-32722)
ITID-32723.severity: Reassess once more detail is available.
ITID-32723.priority: P2 by default given the targeted nature.
ITID-32723.escalation: Reclassify once the specific targeting pattern is clarified.
indicators: Targeted-exploit-related alert of unclear specific pattern
vectors: Targeted exploit delivery of unclear specific mechanism
rootCauses: Insufficient detail captured at time of detection
controls: Web proxy filtering with exploit-kit signature detection
Threat intelligence-driven blocking of targeted campaign infrastructure
Browser and plugin patching automation
EDR detection of exploit-triggered process anomalies
ITID-32723.detection: Same general targeted-campaign telemetry as sibling leaves, pending finer classification.
ITID-32723.response: Investigate and reclassify to a more specific leaf once confirmed.
metrics: Count pending reclassification
ITID-32723.notes: This is an intake/catch-all classification, not a terminal one.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Targeted Exploit Kit
playbook.description: For a confirmed targeted exploit kit that does not fit a more specific watering-hole or victim-fingerprinting classification, but where the kit is confirmed custom/tailored rather than commodity, implying a resourced, motivated adversary.

steps.title: Confirm targeted nature and escalate to full incident investigation
steps.desc: Confirm the kit is custom-built/tailored to this organization rather than commodity, and escalate immediately to a full incident investigation given the implied reconnaissance and adversary sophistication.
steps.outcome: Targeted nature confirmed; full incident response engaged with appropriate leadership visibility.
steps.abort: If the kit turns out to be commodity, downgrade to the standard exploit-kit playbook.
steps.tool: EDR / threat intelligence / incident response team

steps.title: Reconstruct the full exploit chain and identify all affected personnel
steps.desc: Reverse-engineer the exploit chain and identify every employee/system exposed.
steps.outcome: Full exploit chain and affected population mapped.

steps.title: Isolate all affected endpoints immediately
steps.desc: Network-isolate every endpoint confirmed or suspected to have been exploited.
steps.outcome: Affected endpoints isolated.

steps.title: Block the exploit chain infrastructure
steps.desc: Block every stage of infrastructure in the exploit chain (delivery, C2, staging, exfiltration).
steps.outcome: Full adversary infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials and tokens accessible from affected endpoints
steps.desc: Treat every affected endpoint as fully compromised and rotate all accessible credentials, tokens, and keys.
steps.outcome: Exposed credentials rotated.

steps.title: Rebuild affected endpoints and hunt for lateral movement
steps.desc: Rebuild/reimage affected endpoints and conduct a threat hunt for evidence of lateral movement or additional footholds.
steps.outcome: Endpoints rebuilt; no additional footholds found, or additional compromise remediated.

steps.title: Restore endpoints with elevated, sustained monitoring
steps.desc: Return endpoints to service only after full remediation, with sustained elevated monitoring.
steps.outcome: Endpoints restored; no recurrence observed over an extended monitoring window.

steps.title: Conduct a full post-incident review and attribution assessment
steps.desc: Document the complete campaign, assess likely attribution/motive, and brief leadership on the targeted nature of the incident.
steps.outcome: Full report completed; leadership briefed.

ITID-32731.def: A phishing attack built using a subscription-model 'Phishing-as-a-Service' (PhaaS) commercial product, where the attacker rents access to a maintained kit (with regular template/evasion updates) from an underground provider rather than owning or building the kit themselves.
ITID-32731.purpose: Captures use of a commercial, subscription-based phishing-kit-as-a-service product against the organization.
scopeIncludes: Phishing pages/infrastructure matching a known, tracked PhaaS platform's signature templates or backend
Attacks exhibiting the regularly-updated evasion features characteristic of a maintained subscription service
scopeExcludes: Kits sold as one-time packages bundled with dedicated hosting (ITID-32732)
Free/leaked template reuse with no ongoing vendor relationship (ITID-32733)
ITID-32731.severity: High — subscription kits are professionally maintained and evade detection more effectively than static templates.
ITID-32731.priority: P1 upon confirmed successful credential harvest; P2 for detected-but-blocked attempts.
ITID-32731.escalation: Escalate to IR upon confirmed credential compromise; report the phishing infrastructure for takedown.
indicators: Phishing page matching a tracked PhaaS platform's known template fingerprint
Backend infrastructure exhibiting regularly rotating anti-detection features characteristic of a maintained service
Credential harvesting page with real-time exfiltration to a PhaaS-operator-controlled panel
vectors: Email or SMS lure directing victims to a PhaaS-hosted credential harvesting page
Rented PhaaS infrastructure used for a single organization-targeted campaign
rootCauses: Low barrier to entry from commercial PhaaS offerings lowering the skill required to run an effective phishing campaign
Insufficient anti-phishing/MFA coverage on the targeted accounts
mitreTechniques: T1589.001 Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn)
Threat intelligence tracking of known PhaaS platform indicators
Email/web filtering against tracked PhaaS infrastructure
ITID-32731.detection: Threat-intelligence-informed template/infrastructure fingerprint matching provides a strong technical signal for tracked PhaaS platforms.
ITID-32731.response: Reset compromised credentials, report the phishing infrastructure for takedown, and assess account access gained.
metrics: Count of PhaaS-attributed phishing incidents per quarter
Percentage of accounts protected by phishing-resistant MFA
ITID-32731.notes: Differentiated from siblings by the subscription/rental commercial model, distinct from one-time bundled sales (ITID-32732) or free reused templates (ITID-32733).

playbook.name: Response: Commercial/Subscription Phishing-Kit-as-a-Service Product
playbook.description: For a confirmed phishing attack built using a commercial, subscription-based phishing-kit-as-a-service product, typically identifiable by known kit branding, panel infrastructure, or templates used across many unrelated victim organizations.

steps.title: Confirm the phishing kit family and its capabilities
steps.desc: Analyze the phishing page/infrastructure to identify the specific commercial kit family in use and its known capabilities (credential harvesting, MFA relay/bypass, session-token theft).
steps.guidance: Commercial phishing-as-a-service kits often include real-time credential relay to bypass MFA — check for this specifically.
steps.outcome: Kit family and capability confirmed.
steps.abort: If the page was blocked before any credential entry, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify all recipients and any who submitted credentials
steps.desc: Search mail logs for all recipients of the phishing message and correlate with web/proxy logs to identify who reached the page and who submitted credentials.
steps.outcome: Full affected-user population identified, with credential-submission subset flagged as high priority.

steps.title: Force-reset credentials and sessions for anyone who submitted data
steps.desc: Immediately reset passwords and revoke active sessions/tokens for every user who submitted credentials to the phishing page, given the risk of real-time MFA relay.
steps.outcome: Affected accounts secured.

steps.title: Purge the message and block the phishing infrastructure
steps.desc: Remove the phishing email from all mailboxes and block the phishing page domain and hosting infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Message purged; phishing infrastructure blocked.

steps.title: Review affected accounts for unauthorized activity
steps.desc: Audit affected accounts for unauthorized logins, mail-forwarding rules, or actions taken before containment.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized activity identified and remediated.

steps.title: Restore accounts and apply elevated monitoring
steps.desc: Return accounts to normal use and monitor for further suspicious activity.
steps.outcome: Accounts restored; no recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the incident and correlate the kit family with threat intelligence
steps.desc: Record the kit family used and share IOCs with threat intelligence to improve detection of the same commercial kit in future campaigns.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-32732.def: A phishing attack built using a kit purchased as a discrete package from an underground marketplace, sold together with pre-configured hosting infrastructure (bulletproof hosting, pre-registered lookalike domains), as a one-time transaction rather than an ongoing managed service.
ITID-32732.purpose: Captures use of a phishing kit purchased as a one-time package that includes bundled hosting/infrastructure rather than an ongoing subscription.
scopeIncludes: Phishing kit obtained as a one-time purchase bundled with dedicated bulletproof hosting
Pre-packaged kit-plus-domain bundles sold as a single underground marketplace product
scopeExcludes: Ongoing subscription-model PhaaS with regular updates (ITID-32731)
Free/leaked template reuse with self-sourced hosting (ITID-32733)
ITID-32732.severity: Medium-High — less sophisticated evasion than a maintained subscription service, but often paired with dedicated resilient hosting.
ITID-32732.priority: P2, escalating to P1 upon confirmed successful credential harvest.
ITID-32732.escalation: Escalate to IR upon confirmed credential compromise; report the bundled hosting infrastructure for takedown.
indicators: Phishing infrastructure hosted on known bulletproof-hosting ranges commonly sold with kit bundles
Static kit template with no evidence of ongoing update/evasion improvements over the campaign lifetime
vectors: Email lure directing victims to a bundled-hosting credential harvesting page
Lookalike domain pre-registered as part of the purchased bundle
rootCauses: Underground marketplace availability of low-cost bundled kit-plus-hosting products
Insufficient domain-lookalike monitoring
controls: Domain lookalike/typosquat monitoring
Web/proxy filtering against known bulletproof-hosting ranges
Phishing-resistant MFA
ITID-32732.detection: Bulletproof-hosting range blocklisting and lookalike-domain monitoring provide meaningful technical signal.
ITID-32732.response: Reset compromised credentials, report the hosting infrastructure for takedown, and assess account access gained.
metrics: Count of bundled-kit phishing incidents per quarter
ITID-32732.notes: Differentiated from ITID-32731 by the one-time-purchase, bundled-infrastructure commercial model rather than an ongoing subscription.

playbook.name: Response: Phishing Kit Sold with Bundled Hosting/Infrastructure
playbook.description: For a confirmed phishing attack using a kit sold as a bundle with pre-configured hosting/infrastructure (bulletproof hosting, pre-registered lookalike domains, automated panel deployment), typically enabling rapid, disposable campaign infrastructure.

steps.title: Confirm the bundled infrastructure and its provider characteristics
steps.desc: Analyze the phishing infrastructure to confirm it matches a known bundled hosting/kit offering (e.g. bulletproof hosting provider, templated lookalike domain pattern) and identify its known capabilities.
steps.outcome: Infrastructure bundle and capability confirmed.
steps.abort: If the page was blocked before any credential entry, downgrade to a near-miss.

steps.title: Identify all recipients and any who submitted credentials
steps.desc: Search mail logs for all recipients of the phishing message and correlate with web/proxy logs to identify who reached the page and who submitted credentials.
steps.outcome: Full affected-user population identified.

steps.title: Force-reset credentials and sessions for anyone who submitted data
steps.desc: Immediately reset passwords and revoke active sessions/tokens for every user who submitted credentials.
steps.outcome: Affected accounts secured.

steps.title: Purge the message and block the infrastructure, anticipating rapid re-registration
steps.desc: Remove the phishing email from all mailboxes and block the phishing domain/hosting; monitor for near-identical lookalike domains given the ease of re-deploying bundled infrastructure.
steps.guidance: Bundled kits make it trivial for the attacker to spin up a new domain quickly — proactively watch for variants.
