controls: Mobile application management (MAM) with containerized corporate data isolated from personal backup scope
Data loss prevention/CASB monitoring for corporate data in personal cloud accounts
Copy-paste/screenshot restrictions on corporate mobile apps
ITID-33434.detection: Moderate; CASB/DLP tooling with cloud-account visibility can identify this, but only where such tooling covers personal cloud services.
ITID-33434.response: Request/enforce deletion of the synced corporate content from the personal cloud account where feasible, and implement containerization to prevent recurrence.
metrics: Number of personal-cloud-sync exposure incidents identified
Percentage of BYOD fleet with MAM containerization enforced
sops: Data Loss Prevention Incident Response SOP
detections: CASB personal cloud storage corporate-data detection
ITID-33434.notes: This is a passive/unintentional exposure pattern distinct from deliberate exfiltration or malware-driven theft; it is scoped specifically to backup/sync auto-capture behavior.

playbook.name: Personal Cloud Backup Sync Exposing Corporate Data from BYOD Device
playbook.description: A BYOD device's personal cloud backup/sync service (e.g., iCloud, Google Photos) automatically uploads corporate data to an unmanaged personal cloud account.

steps.title: Identify the personal cloud sync and what corporate data it captured
steps.desc: Confirm via DLP/CASB alerts or user report that corporate data (documents, photos of screens, contact lists) was synced to a personal cloud backup account, and identify the exact data involved.
steps.guidance: Check DLP egress logs for the personal cloud domain and cross-reference file/content classification.
steps.outcome: Confirmed personal cloud account, service, and specific corporate data exposed.

steps.title: Assess sensitivity and breach-notification implications
steps.desc: Classify the exposed data's sensitivity to determine whether legal/compliance notification is required.
steps.outcome: Documented sensitivity classification.

steps.title: Disable auto-sync/backup on the device's corporate container
steps.desc: Work with the user (or via MDM policy) to disable automatic cloud backup/sync for the corporate container or the entire device.
steps.outcome: No further corporate data flows to the personal cloud account.

steps.title: Request deletion of the exposed data from the personal cloud account
steps.desc: Have the user delete the synced corporate data from their personal cloud account and confirm removal from any backup versions/trash.
steps.outcome: Exposed data removed from the unmanaged cloud account.

steps.title: Enforce MDM policy blocking personal cloud sync for corporate data
steps.desc: Implement a managed app/data-loss-prevention policy that prevents corporate app data from being included in personal cloud backups (e.g., disabling backup for managed apps).
steps.outcome: Policy deployed and verified to block corporate-data inclusion in personal backups.

steps.title: Verify policy effectiveness and restore normal BYOD operation
steps.desc: Confirm via testing that corporate data is now excluded from personal cloud sync, and restore the user to normal BYOD operation.
steps.outcome: Policy verified effective.

steps.title: Extend the sync-prevention policy across the full BYOD fleet
steps.desc: Document the incident and apply the corporate-data cloud-sync prevention policy to all enrolled BYOD devices, not just the affected one.
steps.outcome: Fleet-wide policy rollout completed.

ITID-33435.def: Unauthorized or unmanaged access to corporate resources from a personally owned device, achieved or exposed by a mechanism not yet classified into a more specific BYOD Exploits sibling.
ITID-33435.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for BYOD-related unauthorized access cases that do not clearly fit unmanaged-device, jailbreak/root, personal-malware, or cloud-sync classification.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered BYOD exploitation patterns pending triage
Cases with insufficient evidence to distinguish the specific mechanism used
scopeExcludes: Any case classifiable into ITID-33431 through ITID-33434 once evidence is sufficient
ITID-33435.severity: Assess per incident; default Medium-High pending clarification.
ITID-33435.priority: P2 pending triage; reclassify and adjust once root cause is determined.
ITID-33435.escalation: Escalate to mobile security/IAM for triage; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is confirmed.
indicators: Any confirmed BYOD-related unauthorized access or exposure not yet attributable to a specific mechanism
vectors: Varies — placeholder pending classification
rootCauses: Insufficient initial telemetry to determine the specific mechanism
controls: BYOD policy enforcement and MDM/MAM controls
ITID-33435.detection: Varies; this bucket exists because initial detection lacks fidelity to classify further.
ITID-33435.response: Triage promptly and reclassify into a specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Number of incidents logged here pending reclassification
ITID-33435.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General BYOD Exploit
playbook.description: A bring-your-own-device is exploited in a manner not otherwise classified to gain unauthorized access to corporate data or systems.

steps.title: Identify the BYOD exploitation event and its scope
steps.desc: Review MDM/CASB/DLP alerts to confirm how the personal device was exploited and what corporate access or data was affected.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploitation method, device, and impact scope.

steps.title: Determine root cause of the exploit
steps.desc: Assess the specific gap (missing MDM control, weak policy, user behavior) that enabled the exploitation.
steps.outcome: Documented root cause.

steps.title: Revoke or selectively wipe corporate access on the device
steps.desc: Revoke the device's tokens/certificates and perform a selective corporate-data wipe via MDM.
steps.outcome: Corporate exposure via the device eliminated.

steps.title: Close the specific BYOD control gap
steps.desc: Implement the appropriate policy or technical control (MDM enrollment requirement, containerization, compliance check) to close the identified gap.
steps.outcome: Gap closed and verified.

steps.title: Restore corporate access under the corrected control
steps.desc: Confirm the user regains corporate access only under the newly-enforced control.
steps.outcome: Access restored securely.

steps.title: Review BYOD policy and MDM enrollment requirements org-wide
steps.desc: Document the incident and assess whether broader BYOD policy changes are warranted across the organization.
steps.outcome: Policy review completed.

ITID-33511.def: Unauthorized access to an authenticated web session achieved by stealing the victim's session cookie — via malware, cross-site scripting, unsecured network traffic, or exposed browser storage — and replaying it to impersonate the victim without needing their password or MFA.
ITID-33511.purpose: Provides the general/comprehensive definition of session hijacking via cookie theft, since this Tier-4 group has only one Tier-5 leaf.
scopeIncludes: Session cookie theft via infostealer malware harvesting browser storage
Cookie theft via cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities on a web application
Session cookie exfiltration via a malicious browser extension
scopeExcludes: Cookie/session capture achieved specifically through network-position man-in-the-middle interception, tracked under MITM Session Hijacking (ITID-33531)
Replaying a previously captured, unmodified session without active theft occurring in this incident (see Session Replay, ITID-33521)
ITID-33511.severity: High, since a stolen session cookie typically grants full account access, bypassing MFA entirely.
ITID-33511.priority: P1, given MFA bypass and immediate account impersonation.
ITID-33511.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately; revoke the session and force full re-authentication upon confirmation of cookie theft.
indicators: Session activity from a device/browser fingerprint inconsistent with the legitimate user's known devices
Sudden geographic/IP shift mid-session with no new authentication event
Infostealer malware detection on the victim's endpoint correlated with account activity elsewhere
vectors: Infostealer malware (e.g., RedLine, Raccoon-style) harvesting browser cookie stores
XSS vulnerabilities allowing JavaScript-based cookie exfiltration
Malicious browser extensions reading session storage
rootCauses: Session cookies not bound to device/IP or token-binding not implemented
Web application XSS vulnerabilities unpatched
No endpoint protection against infostealer malware
controls: Session token binding to device/IP characteristics
Short session lifetimes with re-authentication for sensitive actions
Endpoint protection against infostealer malware
Web application XSS remediation (CSP, input sanitization)
ITID-33511.detection: Moderate-Strong; session anomaly detection (impossible travel, device fingerprint mismatch) provides good signal where implemented.
ITID-33511.response: Revoke the stolen session token immediately, force password/MFA re-verification, and remediate the underlying theft vector (malware/XSS).
metrics: Number of cookie-theft session hijacking incidents
Mean time to detect and revoke a hijacked session
detections: Session anomaly / device fingerprint mismatch alerting
ITID-33511.notes: Sole Tier-5 child of Cookie Theft; written as the general/comprehensive definition. Scoped separately from MITM-based capture (ITID-33531) and pure replay of an already-stolen session (ITID-33521) to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cookie Theft (Session Hijacking Context)
playbook.description: An attacker steals a valid session cookie (via malware, XSS, or network capture) and reuses it to impersonate the legitimate user without needing credentials.

steps.title: Identify session-cookie reuse from an anomalous source
steps.desc: Review application/IdP logs for the same session cookie/token being used from a different IP, device fingerprint, or geolocation than the original issuance, without a corresponding new authentication event.
steps.guidance: Look for impossible-travel patterns or a sudden user-agent/device change mid-session.
steps.outcome: Confirmed cookie theft indicator, source IP, and affected account.
steps.abort: If the anomaly is explained by a legitimate VPN or shared NAT egress, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Determine how the cookie was stolen
steps.desc: Investigate whether the theft occurred via XSS, malware/infostealer on the endpoint, or network interception (e.g., missing Secure/HttpOnly flags, unencrypted transport).
steps.guidance: Check for missing Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookie attributes and recent malware alerts on the user's endpoint.
steps.outcome: Root-cause theft vector identified.

steps.title: Invalidate the stolen session and force re-authentication
steps.desc: Revoke the specific session/cookie and force the legitimate user to re-authenticate.
steps.outcome: Attacker's session access terminated.

steps.title: Block the attacker's source IP/indicators
steps.desc: Block the identified malicious source IP at the WAF/firewall.
steps.outcome: No further access from the attacker's infrastructure.

steps.title: Fix the cookie theft vector (XSS patch, cookie flags, endpoint malware removal)
steps.desc: Depending on root cause: patch the XSS vulnerability, add Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookie attributes, or remediate malware on the affected endpoint.
steps.outcome: Theft vector closed and verified.

steps.title: Verify the user's account and restore normal session behavior
steps.desc: Confirm the user can establish a normal, properly-secured session and that no residual attacker access remains.
steps.outcome: Account restored under hardened session handling.

steps.title: Enforce secure cookie attributes and session-binding checks org-wide
steps.desc: Document the incident and mandate Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies plus device/IP-binding anomaly detection across all applications.
steps.outcome: Standard updated and applied.

ITID-33521.def: Unauthorized access achieved by capturing and later resubmitting (replaying) a previously valid session token, authentication request, or transaction, without needing to actively steal a live session in the current incident — the token was already in the adversary's possession from an earlier capture.
ITID-33521.purpose: Provides the general/comprehensive definition of session replay attacks, since this Tier-4 group has only one Tier-5 leaf.
scopeIncludes: Reuse of a previously captured session token after the original theft event, in a separate access incident
Replay of a captured authentication handshake or request to re-establish access
Session tokens harvested and stored for later, delayed reuse
scopeExcludes: The initial act of stealing a live session cookie, tracked under Cookie Theft (ITID-33511)
Active network-position interception and immediate reuse, tracked under MITM Session Hijacking (ITID-33531)
ITID-33521.severity: High, since successful replay grants full session-equivalent access.
ITID-33521.priority: P1-P2 depending on how long after the original capture the replay occurs and what access it grants.
ITID-33521.escalation: Escalate to IR upon detection; revoke the replayed token and investigate the original capture event that supplied it.
indicators: A session token used successfully long after its original issuance context, from a new location/device
Application logs showing token reuse patterns inconsistent with normal session lifecycle
Replay of an authentication request lacking expected freshness/nonce validation
vectors: Storage and delayed reuse of a session token obtained from an earlier compromise
Lack of token expiration allowing indefinite replay
Replay of captured authentication requests lacking anti-replay protections (nonces, timestamps)
rootCauses: No or excessively long session token expiration
Missing anti-replay protections (nonce/timestamp validation) in authentication protocols
No device/IP binding allowing a token to be reused from a different context
controls: Short-lived, promptly expiring session tokens
Anti-replay protections (nonces, timestamps) in authentication protocols
Session binding to device/IP fingerprint
ITID-33521.detection: Moderate; requires session lifecycle and token-reuse monitoring, which many applications do not implement in depth.
ITID-33521.response: Revoke the replayed token, shorten session lifetimes where excessive, and investigate how and when the token was originally captured.
metrics: Number of session replay incidents detected
Average token age at time of replay
ITID-33521.notes: Sole Tier-5 child of Session Replay; scoped to distinguish delayed reuse of a previously captured token from the initial theft event (ITID-33511) or active MITM capture-and-reuse (ITID-33531).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Session Replay Attack
playbook.description: An attacker captures a valid authentication or session request and replays it later to gain unauthorized access without possessing the original credential.

steps.title: Identify duplicate/replayed authentication requests
steps.desc: Review logs for an identical or near-identical authentication/session-establishment request (same token, nonce, or signature) occurring more than once, which should be rejected under proper replay protection.
steps.guidance: Look for missing or reused nonce/timestamp values in the request logs.
steps.outcome: Confirmed replayed request(s), source, and affected account/session.
steps.abort: If the requests are legitimately distinct (different nonce/signature), this is not a replay — reclassify.

steps.title: Determine how the original request was captured
steps.desc: Investigate whether the request was captured via network interception, a compromised proxy, or exposed logging that recorded the sensitive request.
steps.outcome: Root cause of capture identified.

steps.title: Invalidate the replayed session/token
steps.desc: Revoke the session or token that was established via the replayed request.
steps.outcome: Attacker's access terminated.

steps.title: Block the source of the replay if identifiable
steps.desc: Block the attacking source IP/infrastructure at the firewall/WAF.
steps.outcome: No further replay attempts succeed from the source.

steps.title: Implement replay protection (nonces, timestamps, TLS)
steps.desc: Add or fix replay-protection mechanisms — unique per-request nonces, short validity windows, and encrypted transport — to the affected authentication/session flow.
steps.outcome: Fix deployed and verified to reject replayed requests.

steps.title: Restore normal session establishment and verify protection
steps.desc: Confirm legitimate users can authenticate normally and that a test replay of a captured request is now rejected.
steps.outcome: Verified replay protection in effect.

steps.title: Audit other authentication flows for replay-protection gaps
steps.desc: Document the incident and review other authentication/session flows in the application portfolio for similar missing replay protection.
steps.outcome: Audit completed and findings remediated.

ITID-33531.def: Unauthorized access to an authenticated session achieved by an adversary positioned actively between the victim and the legitimate service (e.g., via a rogue Wi-Fi access point, ARP spoofing, or a reverse-proxy phishing kit) who intercepts and captures session tokens or authentication material in real time.
ITID-33531.purpose: Provides the general/comprehensive definition of session hijacking achieved via an active adversary-in-the-middle network position, since this Tier-4 group has only one Tier-5 leaf.
scopeIncludes: Rogue/evil-twin Wi-Fi access points capturing session traffic
ARP or DNS spoofing enabling interception of session tokens on a local network
Reverse-proxy phishing kits (e.g., Evilginx-style AiTM) capturing live session tokens including post-MFA cookies
scopeExcludes: Passive theft of a cookie via malware or XSS with no active network-position interception (see Cookie Theft, ITID-33511)
Delayed reuse of a token captured in a separate, earlier incident (see Session Replay, ITID-33521)
ITID-33531.severity: Critical, since AiTM techniques can capture session tokens even after successful MFA, fully defeating that control.
ITID-33531.priority: P1, given the technique's ability to bypass MFA entirely and the typical association with targeted phishing campaigns.
ITID-33531.escalation: Escalate to IR immediately upon any confirmed AiTM/rogue-AP activity; treat as an active, MFA-bypassing compromise requiring full session and token revocation.
indicators: Login flows completing against a non-standard/proxy domain before redirecting to the legitimate service
Session tokens issued immediately reused from a second, geographically distinct IP
Endpoint/network detection of rogue access points or ARP spoofing on the local network
vectors: AiTM phishing kits (Evilginx-style) proxying the real login page while capturing session tokens
Rogue/evil-twin Wi-Fi access points at public locations
ARP spoofing/poisoning on internal or guest networks
rootCauses: Lack of phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) that AiTM cannot proxy
No token binding to device/IP to invalidate tokens replayed from a different context
Users connecting to untrusted/public Wi-Fi networks without VPN protection
controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn)
Token binding to device/IP fingerprint
Network-level protections against rogue AP/ARP spoofing (802.1X, wireless intrusion detection)
ITID-33531.detection: Moderate; requires specific AiTM/phishing-kit detection (anomalous login domains, proxy fingerprints) or network intrusion detection for rogue APs/ARP spoofing.
ITID-33531.response: Revoke all sessions/tokens issued during the suspected AiTM window, force re-authentication with phishing-resistant MFA, and hunt for the phishing infrastructure used.
metrics: Number of AiTM/MITM session hijacking incidents detected
Percentage of accounts protected by phishing-resistant MFA
detections: Rogue access point / ARP spoofing detection
ITID-33531.notes: Sole Tier-5 child of MITM Session Hijacking; written as the general/comprehensive definition, distinguished from passive cookie theft (ITID-33511) and delayed replay (ITID-33521) by the active network-position interception element.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General MITM Session Hijacking
playbook.description: An attacker positions themselves between a user and a service (e.g., via rogue Wi-Fi AP, ARP spoofing, or a malicious proxy) to intercept and hijack a live session.

steps.title: Identify the MITM indicator and hijacked session
steps.desc: Review network/endpoint logs for indicators of a man-in-the-middle position (ARP spoofing alerts, certificate warnings/mismatches, rogue access point detection) coinciding with a hijacked session.
steps.guidance: Check for TLS certificate errors reported by the user or endpoint agent around the time of the incident.
steps.outcome: Confirmed MITM technique, position, and affected session/account.

steps.title: Determine the scope of intercepted traffic and data
steps.desc: Assess what data or credentials were exposed via the intercepted session.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of exposure.

steps.title: Remove the user from the compromised network and invalidate the session
steps.desc: Disconnect the affected device from the rogue/compromised network and revoke the hijacked session/token.
steps.outcome: Attacker's man-in-the-middle position and session access terminated.

steps.title: Locate and disable the rogue AP/ARP-spoofing source if on managed infrastructure
steps.desc: If the MITM occurred on corporate-managed network infrastructure, identify and disable the rogue device/ARP-spoofing source.
steps.outcome: MITM infrastructure removed from the network.

steps.title: Enforce TLS/certificate pinning and network hardening
steps.desc: Ensure the affected application enforces strict TLS certificate validation (and pinning where applicable), and harden the network against ARP spoofing (e.g., dynamic ARP inspection) if it occurred on managed infrastructure.
steps.outcome: MITM technique no longer viable against the application/network.

steps.title: Reset affected credentials and restore secure session
steps.desc: Reset any credentials exposed via the intercepted session and confirm the user can establish a secure, verified session.
steps.outcome: Account and session restored securely.

steps.title: Educate users on rogue Wi-Fi risks and deploy VPN/TLS enforcement
steps.desc: Document the incident and reinforce user guidance on avoiding untrusted networks, plus ensure VPN or enforced TLS for all remote connectivity.
steps.outcome: Guidance and technical enforcement updated.

ITID-33611.def: Unauthorized access to network infrastructure devices (switches, routers, firewalls, wireless access points) achieved by authenticating with a factory-default administrative username and password that was never changed after deployment.
ITID-33611.purpose: Captures unauthorized access gained by using a default administrative credential still active on network infrastructure equipment such as switches, routers, and firewalls.
scopeIncludes: Login to a switch/router/firewall management interface using vendor default credentials
Exploitation of default SNMP community strings on network devices
Default credentials on wireless access points/controllers
scopeExcludes: Default admin credentials on database/application server software (see ITID-33612)
General default-credential exploitation not tied to network infrastructure device type (see ITID-33614)
ITID-33611.severity: Critical, since network infrastructure device compromise can enable traffic interception, network segmentation bypass, or full network reconfiguration.
ITID-33611.priority: P1 upon confirmation, given the potential for cascading network-wide impact.
ITID-33611.escalation: Escalate to network engineering and IR immediately; treat as a critical infrastructure compromise requiring emergency credential rotation across all similar devices.
indicators: Successful management-interface login using known default vendor credentials
Configuration changes on network devices with no corresponding change-management ticket
Vulnerability scan findings of default credentials still active on network gear
vectors: Direct login attempts using publicly documented vendor default credentials
Automated scanning tools identifying devices still using default credentials
Default SNMP community strings ('public'/'private') left unchanged
rootCauses: No hardening checklist/process requiring default credential changes at deployment
Lack of periodic vulnerability scanning for default-credential exposure
Newly deployed or replacement devices skipping the standard hardening procedure
controls: Mandatory default-credential change as part of device deployment hardening checklist
Periodic vulnerability scanning for default credentials on network infrastructure
Network device management interfaces restricted to management VLAN/jump host access
ITID-33611.detection: Strong; default-credential presence is directly and reliably detectable via vulnerability scanning and configuration audits.
ITID-33611.response: Change the credential immediately, audit configuration for unauthorized changes, and scan the broader fleet for the same exposure.
metrics: Number of network devices found with default credentials per scan cycle
Time to remediate upon discovery
ITID-33611.notes: Differentiated from ITID-33612 by device category: network infrastructure rather than server/application software.

playbook.name: Default Admin Credential on Network Infrastructure Device
playbook.description: A switch, router, or firewall is found accessible using its factory-default administrative username and password.

steps.title: Confirm the default credential is active and identify all devices affected
steps.desc: Verify the reported/discovered device is still using default admin credentials, and scan the network for other infrastructure devices with the same default credential still active.
steps.guidance: Use an authorized internal vulnerability scan or asset inventory check rather than external probing.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of all devices with active default credentials.
steps.abort: If the credential was already changed and the finding is stale, close as remediated.

steps.title: Check for evidence of unauthorized access/configuration change
steps.desc: Review device logs and configuration history for any unauthorized login or configuration changes made via the default credential.
steps.outcome: Documented whether the credential was actively exploited.

steps.title: Change the default credential on all affected devices immediately
steps.desc: Set a unique, strong administrative credential on every device found using the default.
steps.outcome: No device remains accessible via default credentials.

steps.title: Restrict management interface access to a dedicated management network
steps.desc: If not already done, restrict administrative interface access to a dedicated management VLAN/jump host, reducing exposure even if a credential issue recurs.
steps.outcome: Management interfaces no longer reachable from general network segments.

steps.title: Review any configuration changes made via the default credential and revert if unauthorized
steps.desc: If exploitation was confirmed, review the device configuration for unauthorized changes (rogue rules, backdoor accounts) and revert to a known-good configuration.
steps.outcome: Device configuration confirmed clean.

steps.title: Verify device operation and credential compliance
steps.desc: Confirm the device operates normally under the new credential and passes a compliance scan for default-credential absence.
steps.outcome: Device verified compliant.

steps.title: Implement a mandatory default-credential change step in device deployment procedure
steps.desc: Document the incident and add a mandatory, checklist-enforced default-credential change as part of the standard device deployment/provisioning procedure, with periodic scanning to catch drift.
steps.outcome: Deployment procedure updated and scanning scheduled.

ITID-33612.def: Unauthorized access to a database, application server, or middleware platform achieved by authenticating with a factory-default administrative username and password that was never changed after installation.
ITID-33612.purpose: Captures unauthorized access gained by using a default administrative credential still active on database or application server software.
scopeIncludes: Login to a database management system using default admin credentials (e.g., default 'sa', 'root', or vendor-default accounts)
Access to application server admin consoles (e.g., default management portal credentials) using unchanged defaults
Container/orchestration platform default credentials (e.g., default dashboard logins)
scopeExcludes: Default admin credentials on network infrastructure devices (see ITID-33611)
General default-credential exploitation not tied to a specific software category (see ITID-33614)
ITID-33612.severity: Critical, since database/application server compromise typically grants direct access to sensitive data or full application control.
ITID-33612.priority: P1 upon confirmation, given the direct data-access and control implications.
ITID-33612.escalation: Escalate to the application/database owner and IR immediately; treat as an active data-exposure risk requiring emergency credential rotation.
indicators: Successful login to a database/application admin console using known default credentials
Vulnerability scan or penetration test findings of default credentials on server software
Unusual administrative activity on a database/application server with no corresponding authorized change
vectors: Automated scanning tools probing for known default database/application credentials
Manual exploitation using publicly documented vendor default credentials
Newly deployed instances (cloud or on-prem) never having their default admin password changed
rootCauses: No deployment hardening checklist requiring default credential changes for databases/application servers
Lack of periodic credential/configuration auditing on server software
Rapid or ad hoc provisioning (e.g., dev/test environments) skipping standard hardening
controls: Mandatory default-credential change as part of server/database deployment hardening
Periodic vulnerability scanning for default credentials on server software
Secrets management for administrative database/application credentials
ITID-33612.detection: Strong; default-credential presence is directly detectable via vulnerability scanning and configuration audits.
ITID-33612.response: Change the credential immediately, audit for unauthorized data access or configuration changes, and scan the broader environment for the same exposure.
metrics: Number of servers/databases found with default credentials per scan cycle
Time to remediate upon discovery
ITID-33612.notes: Differentiated from ITID-33611 by device category: database/application server software rather than network infrastructure.

playbook.name: Default Admin Credential on Database/Application Server Software
playbook.description: A database or application server is found accessible using its default administrative account credentials.

steps.title: Confirm the default credential and identify all instances affected
steps.desc: Verify the affected database/application server is accessible using default credentials, and scan for other instances (dev, staging, production) with the same issue.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of all affected server instances.

steps.title: Review for unauthorized data access or modification
steps.desc: Check database/application audit logs for any unauthorized login, query, or configuration change made via the default account.
steps.outcome: Documented whether the account was exploited and what data was affected.

steps.title: Change or disable the default administrative account on all affected instances
steps.desc: Set a unique strong password (or disable the account in favor of named admin accounts) on every affected instance.
steps.outcome: No instance remains accessible via default credentials.

steps.title: Restrict network access to the database/application admin interface
steps.desc: Apply firewall/security-group rules limiting admin interface access to only authorized management hosts.
steps.outcome: Admin interface exposure reduced.

steps.title: Audit and revert any unauthorized data/configuration changes
steps.desc: If exploitation is confirmed, identify and revert any unauthorized changes made to data or configuration via the default account.
steps.outcome: System state confirmed clean.

steps.title: Verify server operation and credential compliance
steps.desc: Confirm the database/application server operates normally and passes a compliance check for default-credential absence.
steps.outcome: Server verified compliant.

steps.title: Add default-credential checks to deployment/CI pipeline
steps.desc: Document the incident and add an automated check to the deployment pipeline/CI that fails a build/deployment if default credentials remain active.
steps.outcome: Automated check implemented.

ITID-33613.def: Unauthorized access enabled because a system, device, or application's default administrative credential was never configured at all following deployment — the setup/configuration process itself was abandoned or incomplete, leaving the asset running indefinitely on factory defaults rather than a single overlooked hardening step on an otherwise-configured system.
ITID-33613.purpose: Captures the specific systemic failure of a default credential being left active because initial deployment/configuration was simply never completed, distinct from an isolated missed hardening step.
scopeIncludes: Shadow IT or forgotten systems discovered still running entirely on factory-default configuration
Proof-of-concept or trial deployments never formally decommissioned or hardened, left internet- or network-accessible
Assets missing from asset inventory entirely, found only via scanning, still on default credentials
scopeExcludes: A known, inventoried device/server that simply had its default credential change step skipped during an otherwise-completed deployment (see ITID-33611/ITID-33612 for the specific device-category cases)
ITID-33613.severity: High-Critical, since these assets are typically undiscovered and unmonitored in addition to being unauthenticated risk.
ITID-33613.priority: P1 upon discovery, given the asset is both unmanaged and exposed.
ITID-33613.escalation: Escalate to asset management/IT and security immediately; treat discovery as both a security incident and an asset-governance failure requiring root-cause review.
indicators: Discovery of an unmanaged/unknown asset during a network or attack-surface scan, still on default credentials
Shadow IT or abandoned proof-of-concept systems found accessible on the corporate network or internet
Asset inventory reconciliation revealing devices/systems with no deployment record
vectors: Attack-surface scanning tools discovering forgotten internet-facing assets with default credentials
Internal network scanning uncovering abandoned lab/POC systems
rootCauses: No formal asset lifecycle/decommissioning process for trial or proof-of-concept deployments
Incomplete IT asset inventory allowing systems to go unmanaged indefinitely
No mandatory security review gate before a new asset is connected to the network
controls: Mandatory asset inventory and lifecycle management for all deployments including POCs
Regular external and internal attack-surface scanning for default-credential and unmanaged-asset discovery
Network access control requiring security review before connection
ITID-33613.detection: Moderate; depends heavily on the maturity of attack-surface management and asset inventory scanning practices.
ITID-33613.response: Secure or decommission the asset immediately, add it to formal asset inventory if retained, and conduct a root-cause review of how it went unmanaged.
metrics: Number of never-configured/unmanaged assets discovered with default credentials
Time from discovery to remediation or decommissioning
ITID-33613.notes: Differentiated from ITID-33611/ITID-33612 by root cause: this leaf is for assets that were never brought under configuration management at all, not a single skipped step on a known, managed asset.

playbook.name: Default Admin Credential Left Active After Initial Deployment (Never Configured)
playbook.description: A system deployed into production was never configured beyond its initial setup, leaving the factory-default administrative credential active indefinitely.

steps.title: Identify the deployment gap and how long the default credential has been active
steps.desc: Confirm the system was deployed without post-installation hardening, and determine how long the default credential has been active based on deployment records/logs.
steps.guidance: Check deployment/provisioning timestamps against the current date to establish exposure duration.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exposure window and system identity.

steps.title: Review for any exploitation during the exposure window
steps.desc: Review logs (if retained for the full exposure window) for any unauthorized access via the default credential.
steps.outcome: Documented findings, noting log-retention limitations if the window exceeds retention.

steps.title: Change the default credential immediately
steps.desc: Set a unique, strong administrative credential on the system without delay.
steps.outcome: System no longer accessible via default credentials.

steps.title: Complete full post-deployment hardening
steps.desc: Complete the entire deployment hardening checklist that was originally skipped (patching, logging configuration, access restriction, etc.), not just the credential change.
steps.outcome: System fully hardened per standard baseline.

steps.title: Verify system compliance against the deployment baseline
steps.desc: Run a compliance scan to confirm the system now meets the full hardening baseline, not just credential remediation.
steps.outcome: System verified compliant.

steps.title: Implement deployment-completion verification gate
steps.desc: Document the incident and add a mandatory verification gate ensuring no system goes into production use without completed post-deployment hardening.
steps.outcome: Deployment process gate implemented.

ITID-33614.def: Unauthorized access achieved via a factory-default administrative credential, on an asset type or in circumstances not yet classified into a more specific Default Admin Credentials sibling.
ITID-33614.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for default-admin-credential exploitation cases that do not clearly fit network infrastructure, database/application server, or never-configured-asset classification.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered default-credential exploitation patterns pending triage
Cases with insufficient evidence to distinguish the specific asset category or root cause
scopeExcludes: Any case classifiable into ITID-33611, ITID-33612, or ITID-33613 once evidence is sufficient
ITID-33614.severity: Assess per incident; default High pending clarification.
ITID-33614.priority: P1-P2 pending triage; reclassify and adjust once root cause is determined.
ITID-33614.escalation: Escalate to IT/security for triage; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID once the asset category and root cause are confirmed.
indicators: Any confirmed default-credential access not yet attributable to a specific asset category
vectors: Varies — placeholder pending classification
rootCauses: Insufficient initial telemetry to determine the specific asset category/root cause
controls: Default credential vulnerability scanning
ITID-33614.detection: Varies; this bucket exists because initial detection lacks fidelity to classify further.
ITID-33614.response: Triage promptly and reclassify into a specific sibling ITID once the mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Number of incidents logged here pending reclassification
ITID-33614.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Default Admin Credential Exploitation
playbook.description: A system is accessed using its default/factory administrative credential in a manner not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the default credential exploitation and identify the system
steps.desc: Confirm the system was accessed using a default/factory credential and identify the system type and criticality.
steps.outcome: Confirmed system and exploitation details.

steps.title: Determine scope of unauthorized access/changes
steps.desc: Review logs for actions taken via the default credential.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of impact.

steps.title: Change the default credential and restrict access
steps.desc: Set a unique strong credential and restrict network access to the administrative interface.
steps.outcome: System no longer accessible via default credentials.

steps.title: Revert any unauthorized changes and complete hardening
steps.desc: Revert unauthorized configuration/data changes and complete any remaining hardening steps for the system.
steps.outcome: System confirmed clean and hardened.

steps.title: Verify system compliance and restore normal operation
steps.desc: Confirm the system passes a compliance check and operates normally.
steps.outcome: System verified compliant and operational.

steps.title: Implement fleet-wide default-credential scanning
steps.desc: Document the incident and implement periodic scanning across the fleet to catch systems with active default credentials.
steps.outcome: Scanning program implemented.

ITID-33621.def: Unauthorized access gained because a victim reused the same password across this system and an unrelated service, such that a password obtained from a breach or compromise of that other, unrelated service was sufficient to authenticate here — the device/application-side access outcome, distinct from mass automated credential-stuffing campaigns.
ITID-33621.purpose: Provides the general/comprehensive definition of unauthorized access via password reuse, since this Tier-4 group has only one Tier-5 leaf.
scopeIncludes: A single targeted login using a password known to be reused from a specific, identified other-service breach
Insider or acquaintance knowledge of a reused password leveraged for unauthorized access
Manual (non-automated, non-bulk) exploitation of a known reused password
scopeExcludes: Mass, automated testing of breached credential lists across many accounts (see Credential Stuffing, ITID-33111)
Detailed human-factor password reuse behavior analysis, tracked under the Attacks Against the Human credential domain (ITID-12210 series) — this ITID covers the resulting access event only
ITID-33621.severity: Medium-High depending on account privilege and data sensitivity.
ITID-33621.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for privileged accounts or evidence of broader data access.
ITID-33621.escalation: Escalate to SOC/IAM upon confirmation of access via a known-reused password; force reset and require unique-password guidance to the user.
indicators: Successful login using a password matching one exposed in an unrelated, known third-party breach
User confirmation that the compromised password was reused elsewhere
Login from an unfamiliar device/location shortly after an unrelated service breach affecting the same user
vectors: Targeted use of a password known from a specific other-service breach against a specific individual's account here
Acquaintance/insider exploitation of a known reused password
rootCauses: No breached-password screening at login/registration
Lack of user education on password uniqueness
Absence of MFA as a compensating control for password reuse
controls: Breached-password screening (e.g., HaveIBeenPwned API) at login/registration
MFA enforcement as a compensating control
Password manager promotion/education to reduce reuse
ITID-33621.detection: Moderate; detectable when correlated with known breach data, but harder to distinguish from a routine login without that correlation.
ITID-33621.response: Force password reset, enforce MFA if not already required, and advise the user on password hygiene.
metrics: Number of confirmed password-reuse compromise incidents
Percentage of accounts covered by breached-password screening
ITID-33621.notes: Sole Tier-5 child of Password Reuse; scoped to a single, identifiable reused-password access event, distinct from bulk automated credential stuffing (ITID-33111) and from human-factor behavioral analysis under ITID-12210 series.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Password Reuse Exploitation (Unauthorized Access Context)
playbook.description: An attacker uses a password known to be reused across multiple accounts/services to gain unauthorized access to a corporate account.

steps.title: Identify the login pattern indicating a reused/breached password
steps.desc: Review authentication logs for a successful login where the credential matches a password known from an external breach (via breach-corpus correlation) or otherwise indicates reuse from another service.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference against breach-monitoring feed alerts if available.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromised account and correlation to a reused/breached password.

steps.title: Scope post-login activity
steps.desc: Review what the attacker did after logging in with the reused password.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of impact.

steps.title: Force password reset and session revocation
steps.desc: Force a password reset and terminate all active sessions for the affected account.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Enforce MFA and breached-password screening on the account
steps.desc: Require MFA and enable breached-password screening at reset time to prevent reuse of the same or other known-breached passwords.
steps.outcome: Account protected against future reused-password logins.

steps.title: Restore access and verify controls
steps.desc: Confirm the user can log in normally under MFA and that the new password passes breach screening.
steps.outcome: Account restored under hardened controls.

steps.title: Deploy org-wide breached-password screening and MFA enforcement
steps.desc: Document the incident and implement continuous breached-password screening and MFA enforcement across the organization, not just the affected account.
steps.outcome: Org-wide control implemented.

ITID-33631.def: Unauthorized access gained by successfully guessing a commonly used, low-entropy password (e.g., 'Password123', seasonal/company-name patterns) that was not obtained from a breach list or targeted brute-force campaign, but was simply predictable enough to guess directly.
ITID-33631.purpose: Provides the general/comprehensive definition of unauthorized access via guessing of common/weak passwords, since this Tier-4 group has only one Tier-5 leaf.
scopeIncludes: Single or low-volume login attempts using well-known common password patterns
Exploitation of a weak password that meets minimum complexity policy but is still highly predictable
Manual guessing based on publicly known personal/organizational information (e.g., company name plus year)
scopeExcludes: High-volume automated password guessing against one account (see Brute Force Attacks, ITID-33121)
Use of a password known from an unrelated breach (see Password Reuse, ITID-33621)
ITID-33631.severity: Medium, escalating to High for privileged accounts.
ITID-33631.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for privileged account compromise.
ITID-33631.escalation: Escalate to SOC/IAM upon confirmation; force reset and enforce stronger complexity/entropy requirements.
indicators: Successful login using a password matching a known common-password list
Password policy audit revealing weak, easily guessed passwords in use
Low-volume, low-noise successful login with no MFA challenge triggered
vectors: Manual guessing using common password lists or organizational-knowledge-based guesses
Exploitation of weak password policies allowing low-entropy passwords to pass complexity checks
rootCauses: Weak password complexity/entropy requirements
No password strength meter or common-password blocklist at creation time
Absence of MFA as a compensating control
controls: Common-password blocklist enforced at password creation
Minimum password entropy/complexity requirements aligned to modern guidance (e.g., NIST 800-63B)
MFA enforcement as a compensating control
ITID-33631.detection: Weak-to-moderate; a single successful login using a common password often looks like normal activity unless correlated with a weak-password audit finding.
ITID-33631.response: Force password reset with common-password blocklisting enforced, and enable MFA if not already required.
metrics: Number of confirmed common-password compromise incidents
Percentage of accounts covered by common-password blocklisting
ITID-33631.notes: Sole Tier-5 child of Common Password Exploits; distinguished from Brute Force Attacks (ITID-33121) by the absence of a high-volume guessing campaign, and from Password Reuse (ITID-33621) by the password not originating from a known breach.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Common Password Exploit (Unauthorized Access Context)
playbook.description: An attacker successfully authenticates using a commonly used/easily guessable password (e.g., from a top-common-passwords list) rather than a targeted brute force.

steps.title: Confirm the common-password login and identify the account
steps.desc: Review authentication logs to confirm a successful login using a password matching a known common/weak password list, and identify the affected account.
steps.guidance: A single low-effort guess succeeding (versus a long brute-force sequence) is the key differentiator from a brute-force attack.
steps.outcome: Confirmed affected account and evidence of common-password use.

steps.title: Scope post-login activity
steps.desc: Review actions taken by the attacker after logging in.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of impact.

steps.title: Force password reset and session revocation
steps.desc: Force a compliant password reset and terminate active sessions for the account.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Enforce a strong password policy and common-password blocklist
steps.desc: Implement or verify a password policy that rejects common/weak passwords at set time and enforce MFA on the account.
steps.outcome: Account protected against future common-password logins.

steps.title: Restore access and verify controls
steps.desc: Confirm the user can authenticate normally under the new policy and MFA.
steps.outcome: Account restored under hardened controls.

steps.title: Apply common-password blocklist and MFA enforcement organization-wide
steps.desc: Document the incident and ensure the common-password blocklist and MFA enforcement apply to all accounts, not just the affected one.
steps.outcome: Org-wide policy applied.

ITID-33711.def: Unauthorized access to sensitive files achieved when a web server has directory listing enabled, allowing anyone to browse the full contents of a directory (rather than only fetching a specific known file), exposing files never intended for public discovery.
ITID-33711.purpose: Captures unauthorized access to sensitive files exposed through a web server's directory-listing feature being left enabled.
scopeIncludes: Web server auto-index/directory listing exposing backup files, configuration files, or source code
Discovery and download of sensitive files via a browsable directory index
Log or temp files inadvertently exposed via an open directory listing
scopeExcludes: Cloud storage bucket directory listing exposure (see ITID-33712)
FTP or network file share open listings (see ITID-33713)
ITID-33711.severity: Medium-High depending on the sensitivity of files exposed (source code, credentials, backups being High).
ITID-33711.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials, backups, or source code containing secrets are exposed.
ITID-33711.escalation: Escalate to the web application owner immediately for remediation; escalate to IR if evidence of active scraping/download by an external party is found.
indicators: Web server logs showing directory-index (not specific-file) requests followed by systematic file downloads
External vulnerability scan or bug-bounty finding of an open directory listing
Search engine indexing of directory listing pages exposing sensitive filenames
vectors: Manual browsing to a directory URL with no index file, revealing the listing
Automated scanners identifying and enumerating open directory listings
Search engine caching/indexing of exposed directory content
rootCauses: Web server directory listing (autoindex) not disabled by default in configuration
Sensitive files placed in web-accessible directories without access restriction
No automated configuration scanning to catch this misconfiguration pre-deployment
controls: Disable directory listing/autoindex on all web servers by default
Configuration scanning as part of deployment pipeline (infrastructure-as-code checks)
Regular external attack-surface scanning for open directory listings
ITID-33711.detection: Strong; open directory listings are readily detectable via automated external scanning and configuration audits.
ITID-33711.response: Disable the directory listing immediately, remove or relocate exposed sensitive files, and assess whether any files were downloaded by unauthorized parties.
metrics: Number of open directory listing findings per scan cycle
Time to remediate upon discovery
detections: External attack-surface scanning for open directory listings
ITID-33711.notes: Differentiated from ITID-33712/ITID-33713 by platform: traditional web server autoindex rather than cloud storage or FTP/file share.

playbook.name: Web Server Directory Listing Exposing Sensitive Files
playbook.description: A misconfigured web server exposes directory listing, allowing anyone to browse and download files not intended for public access.

steps.title: Confirm the exposed directory listing and inventory accessible files
steps.desc: Access the reported URL to confirm directory listing is enabled and catalog what files/directories are exposed and their sensitivity.
steps.guidance: Use a read-only verification request; do not download sensitive files unnecessarily during triage.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exposure and a full inventory of exposed files with sensitivity classification.
steps.abort: If directory listing is disabled upon check (already remediated), close the finding.

steps.title: Check web server access logs for evidence of prior access/download by unknown parties
steps.desc: Review web server logs for requests to the exposed directory from external/unrecognized IPs, indicating the exposure may have already been discovered and exploited.
steps.outcome: Documented history of access, including any suspicious downloads.

steps.title: Disable directory listing on the web server immediately
steps.desc: Apply the web server configuration change (e.g., disable Indexes/autoindex) to stop directory listing.
steps.outcome: Directory listing no longer accessible.

steps.title: Remove or relocate sensitive files from the publicly reachable directory
steps.desc: Move any sensitive files (backups, configs, credentials) out of the web root or restrict access to them explicitly.
steps.outcome: Sensitive files no longer reachable via the web server.

steps.title: Rotate any exposed secrets found in the accessible files
steps.desc: If configuration files, credentials, or keys were exposed, rotate them immediately.
steps.outcome: Exposed secrets invalidated.

steps.title: Verify the fix and confirm no residual exposure
steps.desc: Re-test the URL and related paths to confirm directory listing is disabled and sensitive files are inaccessible.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual exposure.

steps.title: Add directory-listing checks to the deployment security baseline
steps.desc: Document the incident and add an automated scan/check for directory listing exposure to the standard deployment and periodic external-attack-surface scanning process.
steps.outcome: Automated check implemented.

ITID-33712.def: Unauthorized access to files achieved when a cloud storage bucket (e.g., S3, Azure Blob, GCS) is configured to allow public listing of its objects, enabling enumeration and download of its full contents by anyone who discovers the bucket, rather than requiring a specific known object key.
ITID-33712.purpose: Captures unauthorized access to files exposed through a cloud storage bucket's public directory/object listing being enabled.
scopeIncludes: Public 'List' permission enabled on a cloud storage bucket, exposing its full object inventory
Automated bucket-name enumeration tools discovering and listing publicly readable buckets
Bulk download of objects following successful enumeration of a public bucket listing
scopeExcludes: Traditional web server directory listing (see ITID-33711)
A publicly writable (not just listable) bucket where the primary issue is write access rather than enumeration (see Unrestricted Access Permissions, ITID-33722)
ITID-33712.severity: High-Critical, since cloud buckets frequently contain bulk sensitive data (backups, logs, customer data).
ITID-33712.priority: P1 upon confirmation, given the scale of data typically stored in cloud buckets.
ITID-33712.escalation: Escalate to cloud infrastructure/security engineering immediately; treat as an active data-exposure incident pending scope assessment.
indicators: Cloud security posture management (CSPM) finding of a publicly listable bucket
Access logs showing high-volume anonymous/unauthenticated List and Get requests
External researcher or bug-bounty report of a publicly enumerable bucket
vectors: Automated bucket-name-guessing/enumeration tools scanning cloud provider namespaces
Misconfigured bucket policy granting public List/Read access during setup or migration
rootCauses: Cloud storage bucket policy misconfigured to allow public listing
No automated CSPM/guardrail preventing public bucket exposure
Lack of default-deny bucket policy templates in infrastructure-as-code
controls: Cloud security posture management (CSPM) with automated public-bucket detection and remediation
Default-deny bucket policies enforced via infrastructure-as-code
Block Public Access settings enabled at the account/organization level
ITID-33712.detection: Strong; CSPM tooling and cloud provider public-access flags provide direct, reliable detection.
ITID-33712.response: Restrict the bucket policy immediately, assess what data was exposed and for how long, and notify affected parties if sensitive data was accessible.
metrics: Number of publicly listable buckets identified per scan cycle
Time to remediate upon discovery
ITID-33712.notes: Differentiated from Unrestricted Access Permissions (ITID-33722) by focus on public listability/enumeration rather than write access; a bucket can appear in both if it is both listable and writable.

playbook.name: Cloud Storage Bucket Directory Listing Enabled (Public Enumeration)
playbook.description: A cloud storage bucket (S3/Azure Blob/GCS) has public listing enabled, allowing anyone to enumerate its full object inventory.

steps.title: Confirm public listing is enabled and enumerate exposed objects
steps.desc: Verify the bucket's public access/listing configuration and catalog what objects are enumerable and their sensitivity.
steps.guidance: Use the cloud provider's console/CLI to check the bucket ACL/policy rather than external tools where possible.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exposure and object inventory with sensitivity classification.

steps.title: Review access logs for evidence of prior enumeration or download
steps.desc: Check bucket access logs for list/get requests from unrecognized external sources.
steps.outcome: Documented history of external access.

steps.title: Disable public listing and set the bucket to private
steps.desc: Remove the public-read/list ACL or bucket policy statement enabling enumeration, and set the bucket to private by default.
steps.outcome: Bucket no longer publicly listable.

steps.title: Verify no other buckets in the account share the same misconfiguration
steps.desc: Scan all buckets in the account/organization for the same public-listing misconfiguration.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope limited or other affected buckets remediated.

steps.title: Rotate any exposed secrets and assess data-breach notification obligations
steps.desc: Rotate any credentials/keys exposed via the enumerable objects, and consult legal/compliance regarding notification requirements based on data sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Exposed secrets rotated; legal review documented.

steps.title: Verify bucket privacy and restore legitimate access paths
steps.desc: Confirm the bucket is private and re-establish any legitimate access via scoped, authenticated pre-signed URLs or IAM policies as needed.
steps.outcome: Bucket verified private with legitimate access restored appropriately.

steps.title: Implement organization-wide preventive guardrails against public bucket listing
steps.desc: Document the incident and deploy a cloud-provider guardrail (e.g., S3 Block Public Access at the org level) to prevent recurrence across all accounts.
steps.outcome: Guardrail policy implemented org-wide.

ITID-33713.def: Unauthorized access to files achieved when an FTP server or network file share is configured to allow anonymous or overly broad browsing/listing of its directory contents, exposing files to anyone able to connect.
ITID-33713.purpose: Captures unauthorized access to files exposed through an open FTP server or network file share directory listing.
scopeIncludes: Anonymous FTP access exposing a full directory listing of files
Network file share (SMB/NFS) with guest or unauthenticated browsing enabled
Legacy file transfer services left open to the internet with listing enabled
scopeExcludes: Web server directory listing (see ITID-33711)
Cloud storage bucket listing (see ITID-33712)
A broadly permissioned but authenticated file share, where the issue is excessive permission grants rather than anonymous listing (see Unrestricted Access Permissions, ITID-33723)
ITID-33713.severity: Medium-High depending on the sensitivity of files exposed and whether internet-facing.
ITID-33713.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the FTP/share is internet-facing and contains sensitive data.
ITID-33713.escalation: Escalate to IT infrastructure for immediate remediation; escalate to IR if evidence of external download activity is found.
indicators: External vulnerability scan finding anonymous FTP access with directory listing enabled
File share access logs showing guest/unauthenticated browsing
Discovery of the service via internet-wide scanning platforms (e.g., Shodan-style tools)
vectors: Anonymous FTP login followed by directory browsing and bulk download
Unauthenticated SMB/NFS share access from an untrusted network segment
rootCauses: Legacy FTP/file-sharing services left enabled and internet-facing
Anonymous/guest access not disabled on file shares
No periodic external attack-surface scanning covering legacy protocols
controls: Disable anonymous FTP/guest share access
Decommission legacy FTP services in favor of authenticated, encrypted transfer methods
External attack-surface scanning covering legacy file-sharing protocols
ITID-33713.detection: Strong; anonymous FTP/share access is readily detectable via external scanning and service configuration audits.
ITID-33713.response: Disable anonymous/guest access immediately, restrict or decommission the service, and assess what files were accessed.
metrics: Number of open FTP/file-share listings identified per scan cycle
Time to remediate upon discovery
detections: External attack-surface scanning for open FTP/file shares
ITID-33713.notes: Differentiated from ITID-33711/ITID-33712 by protocol/platform (FTP/network file share rather than web server or cloud storage).

playbook.name: FTP/File Share Open Directory Listing
playbook.description: An FTP server or network file share is configured to allow anonymous/unauthenticated directory listing and browsing.

steps.title: Confirm anonymous listing access and inventory exposed files
steps.desc: Verify the FTP server or file share allows anonymous/unauthenticated listing, and catalog exposed files and their sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exposure and file inventory.

steps.title: Review server logs for evidence of unauthorized access
steps.desc: Check FTP/file share access logs for connections from unrecognized sources.
steps.outcome: Documented history of unauthorized access.

steps.title: Disable anonymous access and require authentication
steps.desc: Reconfigure the FTP server/file share to require authentication for all access, disabling anonymous login.
steps.outcome: Anonymous access no longer possible.
steps.tool: FTP server config / file share ACL

steps.title: Restrict network access to the service via firewall
steps.desc: Limit the FTP/file share service to only authorized network segments.
steps.outcome: Exposure surface reduced.

steps.title: Rotate any exposed credentials/secrets found in accessible files
steps.desc: Rotate any credentials or sensitive data discovered in the exposed files.
steps.outcome: Exposed secrets invalidated.

steps.title: Verify the fix and confirm authenticated-only access
steps.desc: Re-test to confirm anonymous access is blocked and only authorized, authenticated users can access the share/server.
steps.outcome: Confirmed authenticated-only access.

steps.title: Audit all file shares/FTP servers for anonymous access
steps.desc: Document the incident and conduct an organization-wide audit of file shares and FTP services for anonymous access configuration.
steps.outcome: Audit completed and findings remediated.

ITID-33714.def: Unauthorized access to files enabled by an open directory listing, on a platform or in circumstances not yet classified into a more specific Open Directory Listings sibling.
ITID-33714.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for open-directory-listing exposure cases that do not clearly fit web server, cloud storage, or FTP/file-share classification.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered directory listing exposure patterns pending triage
Cases with insufficient evidence to distinguish the specific platform
scopeExcludes: Any case classifiable into ITID-33711, ITID-33712, or ITID-33713 once evidence is sufficient
ITID-33714.severity: Assess per incident; default Medium-High pending clarification.
ITID-33714.priority: P2 pending triage; reclassify and adjust once root cause is determined.
ITID-33714.escalation: Escalate to IT/security for triage; reclassify to a specific sibling ITID once the platform is confirmed.
indicators: Any confirmed open directory listing exposure not yet attributable to a specific platform
vectors: Varies — placeholder pending classification
rootCauses: Insufficient initial telemetry to determine the specific platform
controls: External attack-surface scanning
ITID-33714.detection: Varies; this bucket exists because initial detection lacks fidelity to classify further.
ITID-33714.response: Triage promptly and reclassify into a specific sibling ITID once the platform is confirmed.
metrics: Number of incidents logged here pending reclassification
ITID-33714.notes: Intake/catch-all leaf, not a terminal classification.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Open Directory Listing Exposure
playbook.description: A system exposes directory/file listing to unauthorized parties in a manner not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the exposure and inventory accessible content
steps.desc: Verify the reported exposure and catalog what content is accessible and its sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exposure and content inventory.

steps.title: Review logs for evidence of prior unauthorized access
steps.desc: Check relevant access logs for unauthorized access to the exposed content.
steps.outcome: Documented access history.

steps.title: Disable the listing/enumeration capability
steps.desc: Apply the appropriate configuration change to disable listing/enumeration of the affected resource.
steps.outcome: Listing no longer accessible.

steps.title: Rotate any exposed secrets and remediate root cause
steps.desc: Rotate exposed credentials/secrets and fix the underlying configuration gap that allowed the exposure.
steps.outcome: Root cause closed and secrets invalidated.

steps.title: Verify the fix and confirm no residual exposure
steps.desc: Re-test to confirm the exposure is fully remediated.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no residual exposure.

steps.title: Add exposure scanning to standard security baseline
steps.desc: Document the incident and add periodic scanning for similar exposure types to the standard security baseline.
steps.outcome: Scanning process implemented.

ITID-33721.def: Unauthorized access achieved by leveraging an overly broad cloud IAM role or policy — attached to a user, group, or service identity — that grants permissions far beyond what its function requires, allowing an adversary who compromises that identity to reach far more resources than the identity's actual job justifies.
ITID-33721.purpose: Captures unauthorized access resulting from an overly permissive cloud IAM role or policy that grants more access than intended.
scopeIncludes: Wildcard IAM policies (e.g., Action:* / Resource:*) attached to a role and subsequently abused
Cross-account IAM role trust relationships that are broader than necessary
Privilege escalation paths enabled by IAM policy misconfiguration (e.g., iam:PassRole abuse)
scopeExcludes: Publicly writable storage buckets/objects, which are a distinct manifestation of permission misconfiguration (see ITID-33722)
Overly broad on-premises file share permissions (see ITID-33723)
ITID-33721.severity: High-Critical, since IAM over-permissioning is one of the most common cloud breach amplifiers.
ITID-33721.priority: P1 upon confirmation, given the potential for the flaw to convert a minor compromise into full cloud environment takeover.
ITID-33721.escalation: Escalate to cloud security engineering and IR immediately; assess blast radius across the entire cloud account/organization.
indicators: CSPM/IAM analyzer findings of wildcard or excessively broad policies
CloudTrail/audit logs showing an identity performing actions well outside its expected function
Privilege escalation chain identified via IAM policy graph analysis
vectors: Compromise of a low-privilege credential that, due to policy misconfiguration, can escalate to admin
Exploitation of iam:PassRole or similar chaining techniques to assume broader roles
Wildcard permissions granted during rapid development with no later tightening
rootCauses: Least-privilege principle not enforced in IAM policy authoring
No automated IAM policy analysis (e.g., access analyzer) in the deployment pipeline
Broad permissions granted 'temporarily' during development and never revoked
controls: Least-privilege IAM policy design with automated policy analysis/access analyzer tooling
Periodic IAM entitlement review and right-sizing
Service control policies/guardrails preventing wildcard permission grants
ITID-33721.detection: Strong; cloud-native IAM analysis tools and CSPM provide direct visibility into over-permissioned roles.
ITID-33721.response: Tighten the IAM policy to least privilege, audit all actions performed under the identity, and review for any privilege-escalation chains exploited.
metrics: Number of over-permissioned IAM roles identified per scan cycle
Time to remediate upon discovery
ITID-33721.notes: Differentiated from ITID-33722/ITID-33723 by focus on identity/role-level permission scope rather than a specific resource's (bucket, share) permission setting.

playbook.name: Overly Permissive Cloud IAM Role/Policy Exploited
playbook.description: An IAM role or policy grants far broader permissions than needed, and an attacker (or compromised principal) uses those excess permissions to access unauthorized resources.

steps.title: Identify the overly permissive role and how it was exploited
steps.desc: Review CloudTrail/activity logs to identify the IAM role/policy involved and the specific excess-permission actions the attacker/principal performed.
steps.guidance: Use IAM Access Analyzer or equivalent to identify the exact overly-broad statement.
steps.outcome: Confirmed role, policy statement, and actions taken with the excess permission.
steps.tool: Cloud audit log (CloudTrail/Activity Log) / IAM Access Analyzer

steps.title: Determine the source of the exploitation (compromised credential vs. legitimate-but-malicious principal)
steps.desc: Establish whether the actions came from a compromised credential/instance role or a legitimate but unauthorized/malicious use.
steps.outcome: Root cause of exploitation established.

steps.title: Restrict the IAM policy to least privilege immediately
steps.desc: Apply an emergency policy update removing the excess permissions, or attach a deny policy while the role is fully re-scoped.
steps.outcome: The role can no longer perform the exploited excess actions.

steps.title: Revoke active credentials/sessions for the affected principal
steps.desc: Rotate access keys or revoke active sessions for the compromised principal (user, role, or service account).
steps.outcome: No further use of the compromised principal's credentials.

steps.title: Rebuild the IAM policy using least-privilege principles
steps.desc: Redefine the role's policy based on actual required actions (using access-history analysis) rather than restoring the original broad policy.
steps.outcome: Policy scoped to least privilege and verified functional for legitimate use cases.

steps.title: Verify legitimate workloads function under the new least-privilege policy
steps.desc: Test that legitimate applications/users relying on the role continue to function correctly under the tightened policy.
steps.outcome: Legitimate functionality confirmed intact.

steps.title: Implement continuous IAM least-privilege monitoring
steps.desc: Document the incident and deploy continuous IAM policy analysis (e.g., Access Analyzer, least-privilege recommender) to catch overly permissive roles proactively.
steps.outcome: Continuous monitoring implemented.

ITID-33722.def: Unauthorized access in which a cloud storage bucket or individual object is configured to allow public write (upload/modify/delete) access, enabling any unauthenticated party to add, alter, or remove content, in contrast to a bucket that merely permits public read/listing.
ITID-33722.purpose: Captures unauthorized write access resulting from a publicly writable cloud storage bucket or object.
scopeIncludes: Public 'Write' or 'PutObject' permission enabled on a cloud storage bucket
Object-level ACLs granting public write access on otherwise private buckets
Supply-chain-style attacks where publicly writable storage is used to plant malicious content (e.g., replacing a hosted script)
scopeExcludes: A publicly readable/listable bucket with no write access (see Open Directory Listings, ITID-33712)
Overly broad IAM role permissions not specific to bucket ACL/policy configuration (see ITID-33721)
ITID-33722.severity: Critical, since public write access enables both data destruction and malicious content injection (e.g., supply-chain compromise via a hosted asset).
ITID-33722.priority: P1 upon confirmation, given the potential for immediate, severe impact.
ITID-33722.escalation: Escalate to cloud infrastructure/security engineering and IR immediately; assess for evidence of malicious content already written to the bucket.
indicators: CSPM finding of public write/PutObject permission on a bucket or object
Unexpected new/modified objects in a bucket with no corresponding authorized change
Access logs showing anonymous PutObject/DeleteObject calls
vectors: Automated scanning tools identifying publicly writable buckets for content injection or ransom (delete-and-ransom) attacks
Supply-chain attacks replacing a publicly hosted script/asset with malicious content
rootCauses: Cloud storage bucket/object ACL or policy misconfigured to allow public write
No CSPM guardrail preventing public write exposure
Overly permissive default bucket policy templates
controls: Block Public Access settings enforced at account/organization level
CSPM with automated detection and remediation of publicly writable storage
Object versioning and integrity monitoring on publicly hosted content
ITID-33722.detection: Strong; CSPM and cloud provider public-access flags provide direct detection of writable exposure.
ITID-33722.response: Restrict the bucket/object policy immediately, audit for and remove any unauthorized/malicious content written, and assess downstream impact if the bucket serves public content (e.g., a CDN-hosted script).
metrics: Number of publicly writable buckets/objects identified per scan cycle
Time to remediate upon discovery
ITID-33722.notes: Differentiated from Open Directory Listings (ITID-33712) by the write/modify permission, not merely read/list; a resource can appear under both ITIDs if it is both listable and writable.

playbook.name: Publicly Writable Cloud Storage Bucket/Object Exploited
playbook.description: A cloud storage bucket or object is misconfigured to allow public write access, and an attacker uploads, modifies, or deletes content without authorization.

steps.title: Confirm public write access and identify unauthorized changes
steps.desc: Verify the bucket/object ACL or policy allows public write, and review object versioning/logs to identify any unauthorized uploads, modifications, or deletions.
steps.guidance: Check for unexpected new objects (e.g., malware, defacement content) or overwritten legitimate files.
steps.outcome: Confirmed misconfiguration and any unauthorized content changes.

steps.title: Determine if the bucket serves a public-facing application affected by the tampering
steps.desc: Assess whether the bucket feeds a website, CDN, or application that may now be serving attacker-modified content.
steps.outcome: Documented downstream impact.

steps.title: Remove public write access immediately
steps.desc: Update the bucket/object ACL or policy to remove public write permissions.
steps.outcome: No further unauthorized writes possible.

steps.title: Quarantine or remove attacker-uploaded content
steps.desc: Identify and remove any malicious or unauthorized objects uploaded to the bucket, and restore overwritten files from a prior version/backup.
steps.guidance: Use object versioning if enabled to restore original content.
steps.outcome: Bucket content restored to a known-good state.

steps.title: Scan restored/existing content for malware and verify integrity
steps.desc: Scan the bucket's content for malware or defacement remnants and verify overall integrity.
steps.outcome: Bucket content confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore service/website functionality and verify permissions
steps.desc: Confirm any dependent website/application functions correctly and that the bucket permissions now enforce least-privilege write access.
steps.outcome: Service restored under corrected permissions.

steps.title: Implement organization-wide guardrails against public write access
