ITID-34414.def: Data exfiltration confirmed or strongly suspected to have occurred via exploitation of a web application vulnerability, where the specific vulnerability class (SQL injection, SSRF, or IDOR) has not yet been determined at time of logging.
ITID-34414.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for web application exfiltration that cannot yet be classified into a specific vulnerability class.
scopeIncludes: Initial triage classification before the specific web application vulnerability class is confirmed
Cases with insufficient evidence to distinguish between sibling ITIDs
scopeExcludes: Any case where the specific vulnerability class has been confirmed — reclassify to ITID-34411, ITID-34412, or ITID-34413
ITID-34414.severity: Set provisionally based on suspected data volume/sensitivity; re-assess once reclassified.
ITID-34414.priority: P1 pending triage given confirmed exploitation; refine once vulnerability class is known.
ITID-34414.escalation: Escalate as for any confirmed web application exploitation; escalate priority as evidence narrows the mechanism.
indicators: WAF/application anomaly alert not yet attributed to a specific vulnerability class
vectors: Unknown at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient logging detail to fingerprint the exploited vulnerability class
controls: General WAF and application-layer monitoring
ITID-34414.detection: Variable; exists because classification is incomplete at time of intake.
ITID-34414.response: Investigate to reclassify into the correct sibling ITID as soon as possible; treat as confirmed exploitation in the interim.
metrics: Count and average time-to-reclassify of unclassified web application exfil incidents
ITID-34414.notes: Intake/overflow leaf only; every incident logged here should be actively worked toward reclassification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Web Application Exfiltration
playbook.description: For web-application-based exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly SQL injection, SSRF, or IDOR) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear.

steps.title: Characterize the exploitation technique and data accessed
steps.desc: Review WAF, application, and API gateway logs to identify the vulnerability class exploited and the scope of data accessed.
steps.outcome: Activity characterized well enough to redirect to a specific playbook or proceed here.

steps.title: Determine whether exploitation is ongoing
steps.desc: Confirm whether the source is still actively exploiting the application.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the attack is ongoing or historical.

steps.title: Block the malicious source at the WAF/gateway
steps.desc: Add a WAF rule or IP/account block to stop further exploitation immediately.
steps.outcome: Active exploitation stopped.

steps.title: Apply a virtual patch or stop-gap control
steps.desc: Deploy a targeted WAF/gateway rule to mitigate the vulnerable endpoint while the code fix is prepared.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable endpoint protected pending a permanent fix.

steps.title: Patch the underlying vulnerability
steps.desc: Work with the application team to identify and remediate the root-cause vulnerability class.
steps.outcome: Root-cause vulnerability remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the accessed data and coordinate with Legal on breach-notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Confirm remediation is complete
steps.desc: Verify the fix is deployed and the exploitation path is closed.
steps.outcome: Remediation confirmed complete.

steps.title: Document and reclassify for future reference
steps.desc: Record the case, and note the specific technique used for future classification consistency and testing scope.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34421.def: An authorized user leverages a sanctioned reporting or BI platform's native export/download functionality (CSV, PDF, or data-connector export) to pull a bulk data set out of the system for a purpose beyond their legitimate business need, using entirely legitimate tool functionality with no exploitation involved.
ITID-34421.purpose: Captures data exfiltration performed through an authorized user's use of a legitimate reporting or business intelligence tool's built-in export feature, beyond their normal business need.
scopeIncludes: Bulk export of a report or dashboard dataset via a BI tool's native 'Export to CSV/Excel' feature
Use of a BI tool's data-connector/API export feature to pull a full underlying dataset rather than the intended summarized view
scopeExcludes: Bulk export via a CRM/ERP system's own native export feature (see CRM/ERP Mass Record Export by Authorized User)
Unauthorized bulk query/export via a database administration tool rather than a reporting/BI layer (see Database Admin Tool Used for Unauthorized Bulk Query/Export)
ITID-34421.severity: Medium-High, scaling with data sensitivity and volume exported.
ITID-34421.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for large volumes of highly sensitive data or a departing employee.
ITID-34421.escalation: Escalate to Insider Threat/HR and legal in parallel with SOC/IR upon confirmation of anomalous export volume/scope.
indicators: BI tool audit log showing an export volume/frequency far exceeding the user's historical norm
Export of a full underlying dataset rather than the aggregated/summarized view the report was designed to present
Export activity immediately followed by download to an external destination (personal email, cloud storage, USB)
vectors: Employee using a legitimate 'Export' button to pull significantly more data than their role requires
Employee exploiting a data-connector feature intended for authorized integrations to bulk-export raw underlying data
rootCauses: No row-level or volume-based export limits/approval workflow in the BI/reporting platform
Lack of monitoring/alerting on BI tool export activity relative to user baseline
Overly broad data access granted at the BI layer beyond the user's actual reporting need
controls: Row-level/volume-based export limits and approval workflow in BI/reporting tools
User behavior monitoring/alerting on export volume anomalies
Least-privilege data access scoping at the BI/reporting layer
ITID-34421.detection: Good where the BI platform's native audit logging is enabled and monitored for volume anomalies; weak where export activity is not logged or reviewed.
ITID-34421.response: Preserve BI tool audit logs, identify the full scope of data exported, and determine the destination of the exported data before further action.
metrics: Count of anomalous BI/reporting tool export events detected per quarter
Volume of data exported via reporting tools per incident
ITID-34421.notes: Differentiated from sibling ITIDs by the specific tool layer (reporting/BI) as opposed to CRM/ERP systems or direct database administration tooling.

playbook.name: Response: Bulk Export via Legitimate Reporting/BI Tool Feature
playbook.description: For an insider identified as using a legitimate reporting or business-intelligence tool's export feature to extract data in bulk beyond their normal usage pattern.

steps.title: Confirm the export activity and scope of data extracted
steps.desc: Review the BI/reporting tool's audit logs to identify what reports/datasets were exported, the volume, and the destination (download, email, cloud drive).
steps.outcome: Full scope of exported data established.

steps.title: Compare against the user's normal usage baseline and role
steps.desc: Determine whether the export volume/frequency and data scope are consistent with the user's job function and historical usage.
steps.outcome: Determined whether this is anomalous relative to baseline.
steps.abort: If consistent with a documented business need, document and close as a false positive.

steps.title: Notify HR and Legal before further action
steps.desc: Loop in HR (and Legal if the data is regulated or high-sensitivity) before taking any account action that could tip off the employee.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and directing next steps.

steps.title: Restrict export/download privileges per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict the user's export capability within the BI tool, timed per HR/Legal guidance.
steps.outcome: Further bulk export prevented.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with proper chain of custody
steps.desc: Export/preserve the audit trail and any locally downloaded copies before further account action.
steps.outcome: Forensically sound evidence preserved.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal to assess business impact and appropriate response.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed with HR/Legal.

steps.title: Confirm export capability is restored appropriately once resolved
steps.desc: Once the case is resolved, confirm export privileges are set correctly for the user's ongoing role (revoked, restricted, or restored).
steps.outcome: Access state matches the resolution outcome.

steps.title: Document the case and review export monitoring/least-privilege on the BI tool
steps.desc: Record the timeline and assess whether export privileges should be more tightly scoped or alerted on for this tool.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with HR/Legal sign-off and any access-control tuning tracked.

ITID-34422.def: An authorized user leverages a CRM (e.g., Salesforce) or ERP (e.g., SAP) system's built-in mass-export or reporting-export functionality to extract a large volume of customer, sales, financial, or operational records beyond their legitimate business need, using entirely legitimate tool functionality with no exploitation involved.
ITID-34422.purpose: Captures data exfiltration performed through an authorized user's bulk record export from a CRM or ERP system's own native export functionality.
scopeIncludes: Bulk export of customer/contact records from a CRM via its native export or data-loader feature
Mass export of financial, inventory, or operational records from an ERP system's built-in reporting/export tools
scopeExcludes: Bulk export via a general-purpose reporting/BI platform rather than a CRM/ERP system directly (see Bulk Export via Legitimate Reporting/BI Tool Feature)
Unauthorized bulk query/export via a database administration tool operating below the CRM/ERP application layer (see Database Admin Tool Used for Unauthorized Bulk Query/Export)
ITID-34422.severity: Medium-High, scaling with data sensitivity (particularly customer PII) and volume exported.
ITID-34422.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for large volumes of customer/financial data or a departing employee, especially a sales role with customer-list access.
ITID-34422.escalation: Escalate to Insider Threat/HR and legal in parallel with SOC/IR upon confirmation of anomalous export volume/scope.
indicators: CRM/ERP audit log showing an export volume/frequency far exceeding the user's historical norm
Export of a full customer or record list shortly before a known resignation, particularly for sales/account-management roles
Use of a bulk data-loader or export API rather than the normal single-record view/edit workflow
vectors: Sales employee exporting the full customer/contact list before joining a competitor
Employee using a CRM/ERP bulk-export or data-loader feature to pull records well beyond their assigned territory/account scope
rootCauses: No role-based scoping limiting export access to the user's assigned accounts/territory
Lack of monitoring/alerting on CRM/ERP export activity relative to user baseline
No approval workflow required for bulk exports above a defined record-count threshold
controls: Role-based export scoping limited to assigned accounts/territory in CRM/ERP
Approval workflow for bulk exports above a defined record-count threshold
User behavior monitoring/alerting on CRM/ERP export volume anomalies
ITID-34422.detection: Good where the CRM/ERP platform's native audit logging is enabled and monitored for volume anomalies (most major platforms support this); weak where export activity is not logged or reviewed.
ITID-34422.response: Preserve CRM/ERP audit logs, identify the full scope of records exported, and determine the destination of the exported data before further action.
metrics: Count of anomalous CRM/ERP export events detected per quarter
Volume of customer/financial records exported per incident
ITID-34422.notes: Differentiated from sibling ITIDs by the specific system layer (CRM/ERP application) rather than a general BI/reporting tool or direct database administration access.

playbook.name: Response: CRM/ERP Mass Record Export by Authorized User
playbook.description: For an insider with legitimate CRM/ERP access identified as mass-exporting customer or business records beyond their normal working pattern.

steps.title: Confirm the export activity and record scope
steps.desc: Review CRM/ERP audit logs to identify the volume, record types (e.g. full customer list, pricing, contracts), and export method used.
steps.outcome: Full scope of exported records established.

steps.title: Check for correlation with resignation/role-change or competitor movement signals
steps.desc: Cross-reference the timing of the export with any resignation notice, upcoming role change, or known competitor recruitment activity.
steps.outcome: Contextual risk factors identified.

steps.title: Notify HR and Legal before further action
steps.desc: Given the customer-data and potential trade-secret implications, involve HR and Legal early.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and directing next steps.

steps.title: Restrict export privileges and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Suspend export capability and image relevant systems/devices per HR/Legal direction and timing.
steps.outcome: Further export prevented and evidence preserved.

steps.title: Assess whether exported data can be remotely revoked or tracked
steps.desc: For CRM tools with rights-managed exports (e.g. watermarked or DRM-protected files), check whether remote revocation is possible.
steps.outcome: Confirmed remediation options, if any.
steps.abort: If exported as a plain file with no DRM, remote revocation is not possible.

steps.title: Assess business/customer-notification impact with Legal
steps.desc: Determine whether customer data exposure triggers contractual or regulatory notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and notification obligations addressed.

steps.title: Determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal on appropriate disciplinary or legal response based on findings.
steps.outcome: Resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document the case and review CRM/ERP export controls
steps.desc: Record findings and assess whether export-volume alerting or role-based export limits should be tightened.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with HR/Legal sign-off.

ITID-34423.def: An authorized user with legitimate database administration access (DBA, developer, or similar privileged role) uses a database administration tool (e.g., SQL client, phpMyAdmin, a cloud database console) to run bulk SELECT/export queries against production data, extracting a volume or scope of data beyond what their role's normal duties require.
ITID-34423.purpose: Captures data exfiltration performed through an authorized user's use of a database administration tool to run unauthorized bulk queries or exports, exceeding their legitimate administrative need.
scopeIncludes: A DBA/privileged user running a full-table or full-schema bulk export/dump using their legitimate administrative credentials
Ad hoc bulk queries against sensitive tables outside the user's normal administrative task pattern
scopeExcludes: Bulk export via a CRM/ERP application's own native export feature (see CRM/ERP Mass Record Export by Authorized User)
Bulk export via a general-purpose reporting/BI platform (see Bulk Export via Legitimate Reporting/BI Tool Feature)
External exploitation of an application vulnerability to reach the database (see the Web Application Exfiltration group, e.g., SQL Injection)
ITID-34423.severity: High — direct database administrative access typically exposes the broadest and most sensitive scope of data among the insider-tool-usage siblings.
ITID-34423.priority: P1 given the scope of access involved, especially where the query pattern deviates significantly from the user's normal administrative tasks.
ITID-34423.escalation: Escalate to Insider Threat/HR and legal in parallel with SOC/IR immediately upon confirmation of anomalous bulk query/export activity.
indicators: Database audit log showing a bulk SELECT/export query against sensitive tables outside the user's normal task pattern
Query volume/row-count far exceeding what any legitimate administrative task would require
Export/dump activity occurring outside change-management windows or without an associated ticket
vectors: Privileged user running an ad hoc full-table dump using their standing database credentials
Use of a database console/client to bulk-query sensitive tables unrelated to an assigned maintenance task
rootCauses: Standing, always-on privileged database access rather than just-in-time/time-boxed access for specific tasks
No database activity monitoring (DAM) correlating queries to authorized change tickets
Lack of query-volume/row-count anomaly alerting for privileged accounts
controls: Just-in-time/time-boxed privileged database access tied to approved change tickets
Database activity monitoring (DAM) with query-volume anomaly alerting for privileged accounts
Segregation of duties between application administration and direct production data access
ITID-34423.detection: Good where DAM tooling with privileged-account baselining is deployed; weak where privileged database access is standing and unmonitored.
ITID-34423.response: Preserve database audit/DAM logs, identify the full scope of data queried/exported, and determine whether the activity ties to any legitimate authorized task.
metrics: Count of anomalous privileged database query/export events detected per quarter
Percentage of privileged database access operating under just-in-time controls
detections: Database activity monitoring (DAM) query-volume anomaly alerting
ITID-34423.notes: Differentiated from sibling ITIDs by the direct database-administration layer of access, which is broader in scope and typically requires a distinct control set (DAM, just-in-time access) from application-layer export controls.

playbook.name: Response: Database Admin Tool Used for Unauthorized Bulk Query/Export
playbook.description: For a database administrator or privileged user identified as using their admin tooling to run unauthorized bulk queries or exports outside their assigned duties.

steps.title: Confirm the query/export activity and its scope
steps.desc: Review database audit logs (query logs, admin tool session logs) to identify the queries run, tables accessed, and volume of data exported.
steps.guidance: Privileged users often have broad legitimate access, so focus on whether the specific queries/tables fall outside their assigned duties.
steps.outcome: Full scope of unauthorized activity established.
steps.tool: Database audit logs / DAM (database activity monitoring)

steps.title: Determine whether this falls within any legitimate admin task or change ticket
steps.desc: Check change-management records and manager confirmation for whether the activity ties to an approved task.
steps.outcome: Determined whether this is unauthorized or a legitimate but undocumented task.
steps.abort: If tied to an approved change with documentation gaps only, close as a process finding rather than an incident.

steps.title: Notify HR and Legal before further action
steps.desc: Given the privileged-access nature of this activity, involve HR and Legal early before restricting a privileged account.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and directing next steps.

steps.title: Restrict or step down privileged access per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Suspend or reduce the user's database privileges, timed per HR/Legal guidance, ideally without disrupting other legitimate admin duties still needed from other admins.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized access prevented.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with proper chain of custody
steps.desc: Export and preserve query logs, session recordings (if PAM session recording is in place), and any exported files.
steps.outcome: Forensically sound evidence preserved.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal to assess business impact and appropriate response.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed with HR/Legal.

steps.title: Confirm privileged access is restored appropriately once resolved
steps.desc: Once the case is resolved, confirm the user's database privileges are set correctly for their ongoing role.
steps.outcome: Access state matches the resolution outcome.

steps.title: Document the case and review privileged-access monitoring
steps.desc: Record findings and assess whether database activity monitoring/alerting on out-of-scope queries needs strengthening for privileged accounts.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with HR/Legal sign-off and any monitoring gap addressed.

ITID-34424.def: Data exfiltration confirmed or strongly suspected to have occurred through an authorized user's use of a legitimate internal tool, where the specific tool layer (reporting/BI, CRM/ERP, or database administration) has not yet been determined at time of logging.
ITID-34424.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for insider tool usage exfiltration that cannot yet be classified into a specific tool layer.
scopeIncludes: Initial triage classification before the specific insider-tool-usage pattern is confirmed
Cases with insufficient evidence to distinguish between sibling ITIDs
scopeExcludes: Any case where the specific tool layer has been confirmed — reclassify to ITID-34421, ITID-34422, or ITID-34423
ITID-34424.severity: Set provisionally based on suspected volume/sensitivity; re-assess once reclassified.
ITID-34424.priority: P2 pending triage; do not delay containment while classification is in progress.
ITID-34424.escalation: Escalate as for active exfiltration pending; escalate priority as evidence narrows the mechanism.
indicators: Generic anomalous data-access/export alert not yet attributed to a specific tool layer
vectors: Unknown at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient logging detail to fingerprint the specific tool used
controls: General insider data-access monitoring
ITID-34424.detection: Variable; exists because classification is incomplete at time of intake.
ITID-34424.response: Investigate to reclassify into the correct sibling ITID as soon as possible; treat as active exfiltration in the interim.
metrics: Count and average time-to-reclassify of unclassified insider tool usage exfil incidents
ITID-34424.notes: Intake/overflow leaf only; every incident logged here should be actively worked toward reclassification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Insider Tool Usage for Exfiltration
playbook.description: For insider-tool-usage exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly BI export, CRM/ERP export, or DB admin tool misuse) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear.

steps.title: Characterize the tool usage and scope of data extracted
steps.desc: Review the relevant application's audit logs to identify what data was accessed/exported, in what volume, and by which account.
steps.outcome: Activity characterized well enough to redirect to a specific playbook or proceed here.

steps.title: Compare against the user's role and normal usage baseline
steps.desc: Determine whether the activity is consistent with the user's job function and historical usage pattern.
steps.outcome: Determined whether this is anomalous.
steps.abort: If consistent with a documented business need, document and close as a false positive.

steps.title: Notify HR and Legal before further action
steps.desc: Loop in HR (and Legal if the data is regulated or high-sensitivity) before taking any account action.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and directing next steps.

steps.title: Restrict access per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict the user's access to the relevant tool, timed per HR/Legal guidance.
steps.outcome: Further extraction prevented.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with proper chain of custody
steps.desc: Export and preserve relevant audit logs and any locally downloaded copies.
steps.outcome: Forensically sound evidence preserved.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal to assess business impact and appropriate response.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed with HR/Legal.

steps.title: Confirm access is restored appropriately once resolved
steps.desc: Once the case is resolved, confirm the user's access to the relevant tool is set correctly for their ongoing role.
steps.outcome: Access state matches the resolution outcome.

steps.title: Document the case and reclassify for future reference
steps.desc: Record findings and note the specific tool/technique used for future classification consistency and access-control review.
steps.outcome: Finding logged with HR/Legal sign-off.

ITID-34431.def: An attacker obtains a valid API key or authentication token (via leakage in source code/config, credential theft, or reuse from another breach) and uses it to call an organization's API and extract data beyond the key's intended authorization scope, volume, or rate, exploiting the fact that the key itself is technically valid.
ITID-34431.purpose: Captures exfiltration performed via a stolen, leaked, or reused API key/token that is used to call an API beyond the scope or volume it was legitimately authorized for.
scopeIncludes: Use of an API key leaked in public source code, a config file, or a paste site to make unauthorized data-extraction calls
A legitimately-issued API key reused by an unauthorized party (e.g., a departed vendor or partner) after its intended relationship ended
scopeExcludes: High-volume automated scraping using the API's own normal authentication where the key/credential itself is not stolen/reused (see Automated Script Scraping API Endpoint at Abnormal Volume/Frequency)
Exploitation of pagination logic specifically to enumerate a full dataset (see API Pagination Abuse to Enumerate and Extract Full Dataset)
ITID-34431.severity: High, particularly where the key carries broad scope/privileges beyond what any single legitimate caller should need.
ITID-34431.priority: P1 on confirmation of unauthorized use of a valid key; revoke immediately upon detection.
ITID-34431.escalation: Escalate to SOC/IR and the API/platform owning team immediately; revoke and reissue the compromised key/token.
indicators: API access logs showing a known key used from an unexpected IP/geography inconsistent with its normal caller
API key found exposed in a public code repository, config file, or third-party breach dataset
API usage pattern/volume from a given key far exceeding its historical baseline
vectors: API key inadvertently committed to a public source code repository and later discovered and abused
Reuse of a valid but stale key from a decommissioned integration/partner relationship that was never revoked
rootCauses: No secret-scanning on source code repositories to catch leaked API keys before exposure
API keys not scoped to least-privilege or rate-limited per caller/purpose
No key rotation or deprovisioning process when a vendor/integration relationship ends
controls: Automated secret-scanning on source code repositories and CI/CD pipelines
Least-privilege scoping and rate limiting per API key
Formal key rotation/deprovisioning process tied to vendor/integration offboarding
ITID-34431.detection: Good where API gateway logging includes per-key usage baselining and geography/IP anomaly detection; weak where API keys are long-lived, broadly scoped, and unmonitored.
ITID-34431.response: Revoke the compromised key immediately, issue a replacement with least-privilege scope, and review API access logs to determine the full scope of data extracted.
metrics: Count of leaked/misused API key incidents detected per quarter
Percentage of API keys under active rotation/scoping policy
detections: API gateway per-key usage anomaly alerting
ITID-34431.notes: Differentiated from sibling ITIDs by the credential-theft/misuse element (the key itself is compromised or reused improperly) rather than sheer volume-based scraping or pagination-logic abuse using a caller's own legitimate credential.

playbook.name: Response: API Called with Stolen/Reused API Key Beyond Authorized Scope
playbook.description: For a stolen or reused API key/credential used to call an API beyond its authorized scope, resulting in unauthorized data extraction.

steps.title: Confirm the key/credential in use and scope of calls made
steps.desc: Review API gateway logs to identify the specific key used, the endpoints called, request volume, and data returned relative to the key's intended scope.
steps.outcome: Full scope of unauthorized calls established.

steps.title: Determine how the key was obtained
steps.desc: Investigate how the key was stolen or reused — leaked in a code repo, exposed in client-side code, phished, or reused from a separate breach.
steps.guidance: Check public code repositories and paste sites for leaked keys as a common source.
steps.outcome: Compromise vector identified.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised key immediately
steps.desc: Revoke/rotate the affected API key or credential to stop further unauthorized use.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized calls with this key blocked.

steps.title: Block the source IP/account associated with the abuse
steps.desc: Apply a block or rate limit at the API gateway/WAF for the source associated with the unauthorized calls.
steps.outcome: Further access from the same source blocked.

steps.title: Remediate the leak source and enforce scope restrictions
steps.desc: Remove the leaked key from its exposure point (code repo, client bundle) and tighten the key's authorized scope/permissions going forward.
steps.outcome: Leak source remediated and least-privilege scope enforced.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the data returned by the unauthorized calls and coordinate with Legal on breach-notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Issue new credentials to legitimate consumers
steps.desc: Provision a new key to the legitimate service/consumer and confirm normal operation resumes.
steps.outcome: Legitimate consumers restored to normal operation with a clean credential.

steps.title: Document the case and review key-management practices
steps.desc: Record findings and confirm secret-scanning and key-rotation practices are in place to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and process gap addressed.

ITID-34432.def: An attacker or unauthorized party writes and runs an automated script or bot that calls a legitimate, otherwise-authorized API endpoint at a volume, frequency, or sustained rate well beyond normal human or legitimate integration usage patterns, systematically scraping data over time.
ITID-34432.purpose: Captures exfiltration performed via an automated script or bot calling an API endpoint at a volume or frequency far exceeding legitimate/expected usage, using otherwise valid access.
scopeIncludes: A script making rapid, repeated calls to a public or authenticated API endpoint to harvest data at scale
Bot-driven scraping that respects individual rate limits but sustains abnormally high aggregate call volume over an extended period
scopeExcludes: Use of a stolen or improperly reused API key/credential as the enabling mechanism (see API Called with Stolen/Reused API Key Beyond Authorized Scope)
Exploitation of pagination logic specifically to enumerate and extract a complete dataset (see API Pagination Abuse to Enumerate and Extract Full Dataset)
ITID-34432.severity: Medium-High, scaling with the volume and sensitivity of data scraped over the campaign's duration.
ITID-34432.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for high-volume, sustained scraping of sensitive data categories.
ITID-34432.escalation: Escalate to SOC/IR and the API/platform owning team upon confirmation of sustained abnormal automated call volume.
indicators: API access logs showing call frequency/volume from a single caller far exceeding normal human or integration patterns
Consistent, machine-like request timing/intervals inconsistent with human interaction
Requests systematically iterating across a data range (e.g., sequential IDs, alphabetical search terms) rather than typical ad hoc usage
vectors: A scraping bot/script authenticated with a legitimate (non-stolen) account or public API key, run continuously or on a schedule to harvest data
Distributed scraping across multiple accounts/IPs to individually stay under per-account/per-IP rate limits
rootCauses: No rate limiting or aggregate volume caps on API endpoints exposing sensitive data
No behavioral/bot-detection distinguishing machine-driven request patterns from human usage
Lack of CAPTCHA or equivalent anti-automation controls on data-sensitive endpoints
controls: Rate limiting and aggregate volume caps on sensitive API endpoints
Bot-detection/behavioral analytics distinguishing automated from human request patterns
CAPTCHA or equivalent anti-automation controls on data-sensitive endpoints
ITID-34432.detection: Good where API gateway/WAF bot-detection and rate-limiting analytics are deployed; weak where endpoints have no volume-based monitoring.
ITID-34432.response: Block/rate-limit the offending source(s), review API logs to determine full scope of data scraped, and consider tightening endpoint access controls.
metrics: Count of automated scraping campaigns detected per quarter
Volume of data scraped per incident
ITID-34432.notes: Differentiated from sibling ITIDs by sustained volume/frequency abuse of an otherwise valid credential, rather than credential theft or pagination-specific logic exploitation.

playbook.name: Response: Automated Script Scraping API Endpoint at Abnormal Volume/Frequency
playbook.description: For an automated script or bot identified as scraping an API endpoint at a volume or frequency far exceeding normal usage, resulting in bulk data extraction.

steps.title: Confirm the abnormal request pattern and data scope
steps.desc: Review API gateway/rate-limiting logs to identify the source, request volume/frequency, and the data being returned relative to normal baseline usage.
steps.guidance: Look for consistent request intervals, identical user-agent strings, or absence of normal human browsing patterns.
steps.outcome: Scraping pattern confirmed and scope of data extracted established.

steps.title: Determine the source and authentication context
steps.desc: Establish whether the script is using a valid authenticated account, a stolen credential, or unauthenticated public access.
steps.outcome: Source and authentication context established.

steps.title: Rate-limit or block the offending source
steps.desc: Apply aggressive rate limiting or an outright block at the API gateway/WAF for the identified source.
steps.outcome: Further scraping stopped.

steps.title: Suspend the associated account if authenticated access was used
steps.desc: If a valid account was used, suspend it pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Account-based access to the API disabled.

steps.title: Implement or tighten anti-scraping controls
steps.desc: Deploy bot-detection, CAPTCHA, or tightened per-account rate limits on the affected endpoint.
steps.outcome: Endpoint hardened against similar future scraping.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the scraped data and coordinate with Legal on any required disclosure.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Confirm legitimate API consumers are unaffected
steps.desc: Verify the new rate limits/controls do not disrupt legitimate integrations.
steps.outcome: Legitimate usage confirmed unaffected.

steps.title: Document the case and review API abuse monitoring
steps.desc: Record findings and confirm anomaly-based alerting exists for abnormal API request volume/frequency.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and monitoring gap addressed.

ITID-34433.def: An attacker exploits an API's pagination mechanism (page tokens, offset/limit parameters, cursors) by programmatically iterating through every available page to reconstruct and extract the complete underlying dataset, exploiting the fact that pagination controls were designed for incremental browsing rather than as an access-control boundary.
ITID-34433.purpose: Captures exfiltration performed by specifically exploiting an API's pagination logic to systematically walk through and extract an entire dataset that was only ever intended to be browsed a page at a time.
scopeIncludes: Automated iteration through an API's offset/limit or cursor-based pagination to retrieve every record in a dataset
Exploitation of predictable or unbounded page-size parameters to retrieve unintended volumes of data per request
scopeExcludes: General high-volume/high-frequency scraping not specifically targeting pagination logic (see Automated Script Scraping API Endpoint at Abnormal Volume/Frequency)
Use of a stolen/reused API key as the enabling mechanism (see API Called with Stolen/Reused API Key Beyond Authorized Scope)
ITID-34433.severity: High — successful full-dataset enumeration via pagination typically results in complete rather than partial data exposure.
ITID-34433.priority: P1 on confirmation of systematic full-pagination traversal against a sensitive dataset.
ITID-34433.escalation: Escalate to SOC/IR and the API/platform owning team immediately upon confirmation.
indicators: API access logs showing sequential page/cursor traversal covering the full extent of a dataset from a single caller
Manipulation of page-size/limit parameters to values far exceeding the intended default
Total records retrieved by one caller approaching or matching the full size of the underlying dataset
vectors: Script systematically incrementing an offset or following cursor tokens until no further pages are returned
Manipulation of a page-size parameter to retrieve unusually large batches per request, accelerating full-dataset extraction
rootCauses: No aggregate limit on total records a single caller/session can retrieve via pagination over a given time window
Page-size parameter not capped or validated server-side, allowing oversized requests
No anomaly detection correlating pagination traversal patterns to full-dataset coverage
controls: Aggregate per-caller/session record-retrieval limits regardless of pagination
Server-side validation and capping of page-size parameters
Anomaly detection correlating pagination traversal patterns against full-dataset coverage
ITID-34433.detection: Moderate — requires API-layer analytics capable of tracking cumulative records retrieved per caller across many individually-legitimate-looking paginated requests.
ITID-34433.response: Cap or block the offending caller's access, review API logs to confirm the extent of dataset coverage achieved, and tighten pagination controls.
metrics: Count of pagination-abuse-based full-dataset extraction incidents per quarter
ITID-34433.notes: Differentiated from sibling ITIDs by the specific targeting of pagination mechanics as the enumeration technique, distinct from general high-frequency scraping or stolen-credential abuse.

playbook.name: Response: API Pagination Abuse to Enumerate and Extract Full Dataset
playbook.description: For an attacker or abusive user identified as systematically paging through an API's paginated results to enumerate and extract an entire dataset.

steps.title: Confirm the pagination-enumeration pattern and dataset scope
steps.desc: Review API gateway logs for sequential/exhaustive pagination requests (e.g. iterating every page/offset value) from a single source, and determine the total dataset extracted.
steps.outcome: Enumeration pattern confirmed and scope of extracted data established.

steps.title: Determine the source and authentication context
steps.desc: Establish whether the enumeration used a valid authenticated account, a stolen credential, or unauthenticated public access.
steps.outcome: Source and authentication context established.

steps.title: Block or rate-limit the offending source
steps.desc: Apply a block or aggressive rate limit at the API gateway/WAF for the identified source.
steps.outcome: Further enumeration stopped.

steps.title: Suspend the associated account if authenticated access was used
steps.desc: If a valid account was used, suspend it pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Account-based access to the API disabled.

steps.title: Implement pagination-abuse controls
steps.desc: Add per-account/per-source limits on total pages/records retrievable within a time window, and monitor for exhaustive traversal patterns.
steps.outcome: Endpoint hardened against similar future enumeration.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the enumerated dataset and coordinate with Legal on any required disclosure.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Confirm legitimate API consumers are unaffected
steps.desc: Verify the new pagination limits do not disrupt legitimate integrations relying on full-dataset retrieval.
steps.outcome: Legitimate usage confirmed unaffected.

steps.title: Document the case and review API design for enumeration resistance
steps.desc: Record findings and evaluate whether the API design should use non-sequential cursors or additional authorization checks to resist bulk enumeration.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and design gap addressed.

ITID-34434.def: Data exfiltration confirmed or strongly suspected to have occurred via unauthorized or abusive API calls, where the specific mechanism (stolen/reused key, high-volume scraping, or pagination abuse) has not yet been determined at time of logging.
ITID-34434.purpose: Catch-all intake bucket for unauthorized API call exfiltration that cannot yet be classified into a specific mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Initial triage classification before the specific API-abuse mechanism is confirmed
Cases with insufficient evidence to distinguish between sibling ITIDs
scopeExcludes: Any case where the specific mechanism has been confirmed — reclassify to ITID-34431, ITID-34432, or ITID-34433
ITID-34434.severity: Set provisionally based on suspected volume/sensitivity; re-assess once reclassified.
ITID-34434.priority: P2 pending triage; do not delay containment while classification is in progress.
ITID-34434.escalation: Escalate as for active exfiltration pending; escalate priority as evidence narrows the mechanism.
indicators: Generic API abuse/anomaly alert not yet attributed to a specific mechanism
vectors: Unknown at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient API logging detail to fingerprint the exfiltration mechanism
controls: General API gateway monitoring
ITID-34434.detection: Variable; exists because classification is incomplete at time of intake.
ITID-34434.response: Investigate to reclassify into the correct sibling ITID as soon as possible; treat as active exfiltration in the interim.
metrics: Count and average time-to-reclassify of unclassified API exfil incidents
ITID-34434.notes: Intake/overflow leaf only; every incident logged here should be actively worked toward reclassification.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Unauthorized API Call Exfiltration
playbook.description: For unauthorized-API-call exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly stolen-key misuse, scraping, or pagination abuse) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear.

steps.title: Characterize the unauthorized API activity
steps.desc: Review API gateway logs to determine the endpoint, request pattern, credential/source used, and data returned.
steps.outcome: Activity characterized well enough to redirect to a specific playbook or proceed here.

steps.title: Determine whether exploitation is ongoing
steps.desc: Confirm whether the source is still actively making unauthorized calls.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the activity is ongoing or historical.

steps.title: Block or rate-limit the offending source/credential
steps.desc: Apply a block, rate limit, or credential revocation at the API gateway to stop further unauthorized calls.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized access stopped.

steps.title: Suspend any associated account as appropriate
steps.desc: If a valid account/credential was used, suspend or rotate it pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Account-based access disabled where relevant.

steps.title: Address the underlying control gap
steps.desc: Based on the pattern observed, apply the appropriate fix — key rotation, scope restriction, rate limiting, or authorization checks.
steps.outcome: Root-cause control gap addressed.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the data accessed and coordinate with Legal on breach-notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Confirm legitimate API consumers are unaffected
steps.desc: Verify the remediation does not disrupt legitimate integrations.
steps.outcome: Legitimate usage confirmed unaffected.

steps.title: Document and reclassify for future reference
steps.desc: Record the case, and note the specific technique used for future classification consistency.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34511.def: A single identifiable event in which a user or process copies a materially large volume of files from an internal (on-prem or mapped network) file share to an external location such as removable media, a personal cloud account, or an external network path, distinguished from sibling ITIDs by its bulk-copy technical signature rather than by who performed it or why.
ITID-34511.purpose: Captures a large, discrete copy operation moving sensitive files off an internal file share to a destination outside organizational control.
scopeIncludes: Copying hundreds/thousands of files or a large byte volume from a monitored file share in a short window
Copy operations to a mounted external drive, personal cloud sync folder, or external SMB/FTP target sourced from an internal share
Automated scripts or tools used to mass-copy share contents
scopeExcludes: Generation of an external sharing link without a bulk copy (ITID-34512)
Mapping and mass-copying via a compromised/insider account as the primary vector (ITID-34513)
Insider motivation/intent analysis, covered under ITID-13111-13114
Physical removal of printed output (ITID-34633)
ITID-34511.severity: High when the share contains regulated or crown-jewel data; Medium for shares of lower sensitivity.
ITID-34511.priority: P1 if source share holds regulated/sensitive data and volume is anomalous; otherwise P2.
ITID-34511.escalation: Escalate to DLP/insider risk team and data owner immediately; involve legal/HR if the actor is an employee and volume suggests intentional exfiltration.
indicators: File-share audit logs showing a spike in read/copy events from one account/host
DLP alert on bulk file movement off a monitored share
Sudden mount of removable media or cloud-sync client immediately following mass file access
vectors: Manual drag-and-copy of an entire share to removable media
Scripted robocopy/rsync-style bulk copy job
Cloud-sync client pointed at a mapped share
rootCauses: Overly broad share permissions relative to job role
No volume-based alerting on file share access
Removable media and unmanaged cloud sync not blocked at the endpoint
mitreTechniques: T1039 Data from Network Shared Drive
controls: File share access auditing
DLP volume-based alerting on share egress
Removable media control policy
ITID-34511.detection: Strong: file-share audit logs and DLP volume thresholds give a direct technical signal for this ITID.
ITID-34511.response: Isolate the source account, preserve share audit logs, identify the destination and scope of copied data, and determine whether the copy left the organization's control.
metrics: Count of bulk-copy events per quarter
Median time-to-detection for anomalous share copy volume
ITID-34511.notes: Scoped to the bulk-copy technical mechanism only; insider motivation is tracked under ITID-13111-13114 and physical paper removal under ITID-14231-14233 to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Bulk Copy of Sensitive Files from Internal File Share to External Location
playbook.description: For confirmed data exfiltration where an account performs a bulk copy of sensitive files from an internal network file share to an external destination (cloud storage, personal email, or removable media).

steps.title: Review file-share audit logs for bulk copy/download activity
steps.desc: Review file server or NAS audit logs for the account for an unusually large number of file reads/copies in a short period, compared to the account's normal baseline usage.
steps.outcome: Confirmed bulk copy event with file list, volume, and destination identified.
steps.abort: If the volume is consistent with an approved bulk operation (e.g. scheduled migration), close as a false positive.

steps.title: Identify the destination and transfer mechanism
steps.desc: Correlate the file-share activity with endpoint and network logs to determine where the copied files went (cloud upload, email attachment, removable media).
steps.outcome: Destination and transfer mechanism identified.

steps.title: Restrict the account's access to the file share
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict the account's access to the affected file share pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Further bulk copying prevented.
steps.tool: File server access control / identity management

steps.title: Block or revoke the external destination
steps.desc: Block the destination (cloud service, external domain) at the network/CASB level or revoke any sharing link created.
steps.outcome: External destination blocked or revoked.

steps.title: Determine whether this is malware-driven or account-driven and remediate accordingly
steps.desc: Determine whether the bulk copy was performed by malware/compromised credentials or by the legitimate account holder, and remediate the host (malware removal) or engage HR/Legal (insider) accordingly.
steps.outcome: Root cause classified and appropriate remediation path initiated.

steps.title: Sweep for the same bulk-copy pattern on other file shares
steps.desc: Review other file shares accessible to the same account for similar bulk-copy activity to confirm the full scope of the exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Scope confirmed; any additional affected shares identified.

steps.title: Restore access under monitoring and review file-share permissions
steps.desc: Restore appropriate access once the investigation concludes, and review file-share permission structure to ensure least-privilege access to sensitive folders.
steps.outcome: Access restored appropriately; permission review completed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review bulk-access alerting thresholds
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether file-share monitoring needs bulk-access/anomaly alerting thresholds.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34512.def: An event in which a user generates an external (anonymous or broadly shared) link granting access to an internal file share folder or its contents, exposing sensitive data to parties outside the organization's access boundary.
ITID-34512.purpose: Captures the creation of an externally accessible sharing link on an internal file share folder as the exfiltration mechanism, independent of whether the data was actually downloaded.
scopeIncludes: Creation of an 'anyone with the link' or public share on a file share folder
Sharing link set with no expiration or overly broad permissions (edit vs. view)
Link shared to a personal or external email address
scopeExcludes: The bulk local copy of share contents (ITID-34511)
External sharing links generated on SharePoint/Google Drive documents specifically (ITID-34521, covered under Misused Collaboration Platforms)
Mass-copy via compromised/insider mapped-drive access (ITID-34513)
ITID-34512.severity: Medium-High, scaling with data sensitivity and whether the link was actually accessed externally.
ITID-34512.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if access logs confirm external retrieval of sensitive content.
ITID-34512.escalation: Escalate to data owner and security team to revoke the link and assess exposure; escalate to legal if regulated data was exposed.
indicators: File-share platform audit log showing external/anonymous link creation
Access to the link from an external or unrecognized IP
CASB alert on external sharing policy violation
vectors: Manually toggling folder sharing settings to 'external'
Misuse of a legitimate sharing feature to hand off data outside sanctioned channels
rootCauses: Default sharing settings permit external/anonymous links
Lack of CASB/DLP policy enforcement on share-link creation
Users unaware of data classification when sharing
controls: CASB policy blocking/alerting on external link creation
Default-deny external sharing configuration
ITID-34512.detection: Strong: platform sharing audit logs and CASB alerts directly capture link creation and access.
ITID-34512.response: Revoke the link, review access logs for external retrieval, and notify the data owner of exposure scope.
metrics: Count of external share links created per month
Mean time-to-revocation of flagged links
ITID-34512.notes: Scoped to internal file-share platforms; SharePoint/Google Drive document-level link sharing is tracked separately under ITID-34521 to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: External Sharing Link Generated for Internal File Share Folder
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected data exfiltration where an externally accessible sharing link is generated for an internal file share folder containing sensitive data, exposing it beyond the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the external sharing link creation and its scope
steps.desc: Review file-share/SaaS platform audit logs for the creation of an external or anonymous sharing link, and identify the folder/files it exposes and who created it.
steps.outcome: Confirmed sharing link event with exposed content and creator identified.
steps.abort: If the link was created for an approved external collaboration with appropriate sensitivity classification, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Determine whether the link was accessed externally
steps.desc: Review link access logs to determine whether and how many times the external link was accessed, and from where.
steps.outcome: Access history for the link established.

steps.title: Revoke the external sharing link immediately
steps.desc: Revoke or disable the sharing link to stop any further external access.
steps.outcome: Link revoked; no further external access possible.

steps.title: Review what was actually accessed via the link
steps.desc: Cross-reference the link's access log with the folder contents to determine precisely what sensitive data, if any, was viewed or downloaded before revocation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of data actually accessed externally.

steps.title: Correct folder sharing settings and permissions
steps.desc: Reset the folder's sharing configuration to organization-only or restricted access per data classification policy.
steps.outcome: Folder sharing settings corrected.

steps.title: Check for other externally shared links from the same source
steps.desc: Review the file share/SaaS platform for other external sharing links created by the same user or on the same folder structure that may also need revocation.
steps.outcome: All related external sharing links identified and revoked.

steps.title: Notify affected data owners and assess disclosure obligations
steps.desc: Notify the data owner and, if confirmed sensitive/regulated data was accessed externally, engage Legal/Privacy to assess breach notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Data owner notified; disclosure obligations assessed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review external sharing default settings
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether external sharing should be disabled by default or restricted for folders containing sensitive data.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34513.def: An event in which an attacker-controlled or insider-abused account maps a network file share it would not normally access at that volume, then mass-copies files, indicating the access itself (not merely the copy) is the anomaly.
ITID-34513.purpose: Captures a compromised or malicious insider account that maps an internal network share and mass-copies its contents, distinguished by the credential/access vector rather than the copy mechanics themselves.
scopeIncludes: An account mapping a share outside its normal access pattern followed by mass copy
Use of compromised credentials to reach and copy from a share the legitimate user never accesses at that volume
Lateral movement to reach a share followed by bulk copy
scopeExcludes: Bulk copy performed by an account with routine, expected access to the share (ITID-34511)
External sharing link creation without mapping/copying (ITID-34512)
ITID-34513.severity: High: combines a credential-compromise/anomalous-access signal with bulk data movement.
ITID-34513.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident response for credential compromise investigation alongside data loss assessment.
indicators: New share mount from an account/host with no prior access history to that share
Authentication anomaly (impossible travel, off-hours logon) preceding the share mapping
Mass file-read events immediately after mapping
vectors: Compromised credentials used to map and harvest a share
Insider using another user's session or unauthorized elevated access to reach a share
rootCauses: Excessive share permissions not scoped to least privilege
No anomaly detection on new share-mapping behavior
Weak credential hygiene enabling account compromise
mitreTechniques: T1039 Data from Network Shared Drive
controls: User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) on share access
Least-privilege share permissioning
ITID-34513.detection: Strong: UEBA/anomalous-access detection plus share audit logs provide a clear technical signal.
ITID-34513.response: Treat as a potential account compromise: disable/reset the account, preserve logs, and scope the data accessed.
metrics: Count of anomalous share-mapping events detected
Time-to-containment for compromised-account share access
ITID-34513.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34511 by the anomalous-access/credential dimension rather than the copy volume itself.

playbook.name: Response: Network File Share Mapped and Mass-Copied by Compromised/Insider Account
playbook.description: For confirmed data exfiltration where an account (compromised or insider) maps a network file share and performs a mass copy operation across multiple folders, often indicating reconnaissance followed by bulk collection.

steps.title: Review share-mapping and mass-access logs
steps.desc: Review file server audit logs for the account mapping the share and subsequently accessing a broad range of folders/files inconsistent with its normal scope of work.
steps.outcome: Confirmed mass-copy event with account, shares, and file scope identified.
steps.abort: If access is consistent with an approved administrative or migration task, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Determine whether the account is compromised or acting as an insider
steps.desc: Review authentication logs, EDR telemetry, and recent account activity to determine whether the account shows signs of compromise (unusual login location/time, malware) versus the legitimate user directly performing the mass copy.
steps.outcome: Root cause classified as compromised account or insider activity.

steps.title: Disable or restrict the account and disconnect the mapped share
steps.desc: Disable the account (if compromised) or restrict its access pending HR/Legal review (if insider), and forcibly disconnect the mapped network share session.
steps.outcome: Further mass copying prevented.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody if insider-related
steps.desc: If insider activity is suspected, preserve logs and evidence with documented chain of custody and engage HR/Legal before further account action.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; HR/Legal engaged if warranted.

steps.title: Reset credentials and remove any persistence if compromised
steps.desc: If the account was compromised, reset credentials, revoke active sessions/tokens, and remove any malware or persistence found on associated endpoints.
steps.outcome: Account secured; endpoint confirmed clean.

steps.title: Verify no residual mapped-share sessions remain
steps.desc: Confirm no other active sessions or scheduled tasks retain a mapped connection to the affected file share under the same or another compromised credential.
steps.outcome: No residual mapped-share access confirmed.

steps.title: Restore appropriate access and review share permission scope
steps.desc: Restore access as appropriate following remediation, and review the file share's permission structure to limit broad mapping/access to sensitive folders.
steps.outcome: Access restored appropriately; permission review completed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review anomalous access alerting
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether file-share monitoring needs improved alerting for broad, cross-folder access patterns.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34514.def: An unauthorized file share exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Unauthorized File Shares, pending further investigation.
ITID-34514.purpose: Intake bucket for unauthorized file share exfiltration activity that does not fit the bulk-copy, external-link, or compromised-access leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reported file share data loss with mechanism not yet determined
Mixed or ambiguous file share exfiltration behavior spanning multiple sub-patterns
scopeExcludes: Any event that can be classified as ITID-34511, 34512, or 34513 once investigated
ITID-34514.severity: Medium pending triage; reassess once classified.
ITID-34514.escalation: Escalate to SOC triage for reclassification into a specific sibling ITID as soon as sufficient information is available.
indicators: Generic file share DLP or audit alert lacking enough detail for specific classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient logging detail to classify the exfiltration mechanism at intake
mitreTechniques: T1039 Data from Network Shared Drive
controls: File share audit logging
DLP monitoring
ITID-34514.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34514.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Unauthorized File Shares ITID as soon as possible; do not leave incidents parked here.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34514.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Unauthorized File Share Exfiltration
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected data exfiltration via an internal file share that does not fit a more specific category (bulk copy to external location, external sharing link creation, or mass copy via mapped share).

steps.title: Confirm the file-share exfiltration activity and classify the pattern
steps.desc: Review file-share/SaaS audit logs to confirm unauthorized access or transfer and attempt to classify the specific pattern (bulk external copy, external sharing link, or mapped-share mass copy).
steps.guidance: If the pattern matches a more specific category, transition to that playbook.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exfiltration activity with account, files, and scope identified.
steps.abort: If no exfiltration is confirmed, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Estimate scope and destination of exfiltrated data
steps.desc: Review available logs to determine what data was affected and where it went.
steps.outcome: Scope and destination estimate established.

steps.title: Restrict the account's access
steps.desc: Restrict or suspend the account's access to the affected file share pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Further activity prevented.

steps.title: Revoke external access or block the destination
steps.desc: Revoke any external sharing links or block the identified external destination.
steps.outcome: External access removed.

steps.title: Remediate the underlying cause
steps.desc: Address the root cause, whether compromised credentials, malware, or insider action, coordinating with HR/Legal as needed.
steps.outcome: Root cause remediated.

steps.title: Verify no residual unauthorized access remains
steps.desc: Confirm no other accounts, sessions, or sharing configurations continue to expose the affected file share externally.
steps.outcome: No residual unauthorized access confirmed.

steps.title: Restore appropriate access and review permissions
steps.desc: Restore access as appropriate and review file-share permission structure for the affected data.
steps.outcome: Access restored appropriately; permission review completed.

steps.title: Document the incident and reclassify if a specific pattern emerges
steps.desc: Record findings and, if the technique is later identified as a specific known pattern, update the incident classification for future reference.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34521.def: An event in which a user generates an externally accessible sharing link on a document or folder within a cloud collaboration platform, exposing its contents outside the organization's managed boundary.
ITID-34521.purpose: Captures the creation of an external sharing link on a document hosted in a collaboration platform (SharePoint, Google Drive) as the exfiltration mechanism.
scopeIncludes: 'Anyone with the link' sharing enabled on a SharePoint/Google Drive document or folder
Sharing set to allow external domains beyond an approved allowlist
Link with edit permissions granted externally
scopeExcludes: External link creation on a traditional internal file share (ITID-34512)
Adding a guest/external user directly to a Teams/Slack workspace (ITID-34522)
Bulk download/sync of already-shared files (ITID-34523)
ITID-34521.severity: Medium-High, scaling with document sensitivity and whether external access occurred.
ITID-34521.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if access logs show external retrieval of regulated data.
ITID-34521.escalation: Escalate to data owner to revoke access; escalate to legal/privacy if regulated data was exposed externally.
indicators: Platform sharing audit log showing external link creation
CASB alert on external sharing policy violation
Access to the link from an unrecognized external domain/IP
vectors: Manual sharing settings misuse
Accidental oversharing of a folder containing sensitive subfolders
rootCauses: Default 'anyone with the link' sharing enabled tenant-wide
No CASB/DLP enforcement on external sharing
Lack of user training on data classification when sharing
controls: CASB external sharing policy
Tenant-level default sharing restrictions
DLP scanning of shared documents
ITID-34521.detection: Strong: SaaS platform audit logs and CASB provide direct visibility into link creation and access.
ITID-34521.response: Revoke or restrict the link, review access history, and notify the data owner of exposure scope.
metrics: Count of external sharing links created per month
Percentage remediated within SLA
ITID-34521.notes: Scoped to cloud collaboration platform document/folder sharing, distinct from ITID-34512 (traditional file share links).

playbook.name: Response: External Sharing Link Created on SharePoint/Google Drive Document
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected data exfiltration where an externally accessible sharing link is created on a SharePoint or Google Drive document containing sensitive data.

steps.title: Confirm the external sharing link creation event
steps.desc: Review SharePoint/Google Drive admin audit logs for the creation of an 'anyone with the link' or external-domain sharing link on a sensitive document, and identify the creator and document.
steps.outcome: Confirmed sharing link event with document and creator identified.
steps.abort: If the link was created for approved external collaboration with appropriate classification, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Determine link access history
steps.desc: Review the platform's link access logs to determine whether and how the external link was accessed.
steps.outcome: Access history established.

steps.title: Revoke the external sharing link immediately
steps.desc: Revoke or disable the sharing link to stop further external access.
steps.outcome: Link revoked.

steps.title: Review what was actually accessed via the link
steps.desc: Cross-reference access logs with document contents to determine what sensitive data was viewed or downloaded before revocation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of data accessed externally.

steps.title: Correct document/site sharing settings
steps.desc: Reset the document or site's sharing configuration to organization-only per data classification policy.
steps.outcome: Sharing settings corrected.

steps.title: Check for other externally shared links from the same source
steps.desc: Review the platform for other external sharing links created by the same user or on the same document library that may also need revocation.
steps.outcome: All related external sharing links identified and revoked.

steps.title: Notify data owners and assess disclosure obligations
steps.desc: Notify the data owner and, if confirmed sensitive/regulated data was exposed externally, engage Legal/Privacy to assess breach notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Data owner notified; disclosure obligations assessed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review external sharing default policy
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether external sharing should be restricted by default at the tenant/site level for sensitive content.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34522.def: An event in which a guest or external identity is invited into or added to an internal collaboration workspace, granting standing access to channels, files, and conversations beyond the organization's boundary.
ITID-34522.purpose: Captures the addition of a guest or external user account to an internal Teams/Slack workspace as the mechanism enabling ongoing data access by an outsider.
scopeIncludes: Guest account invited to a workspace/channel containing sensitive content
External domain added to workspace-wide allowlist without business justification
Guest access granted with broader permissions than required
scopeExcludes: A one-time external sharing link on a single document (ITID-34521)
Bulk download/sync activity by an already-present external user (ITID-34523)
ITID-34522.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the workspace contains regulated or highly sensitive content.
ITID-34522.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if guest access to sensitive channels is confirmed unauthorized.
ITID-34522.escalation: Escalate to workspace/data owner to review and revoke unjustified guest access; escalate to security if the guest addition was not authorized by a known business process.
indicators: Workspace admin log showing guest invite with no matching approval record
Guest account accessing channels/files inconsistent with stated business purpose
Unusual volume of guest logins or file views
vectors: Legitimate collaboration invite feature misused to add an external party for data access
Compromised admin account used to add a guest
rootCauses: No approval workflow required for guest invitations
Guest access not time-bound or periodically reviewed
Overly permissive default guest role
controls: Guest access approval workflow
Periodic guest account access review
Time-bound guest expiration policy
ITID-34522.detection: Moderate-Strong: workspace admin logs capture guest additions, but business-justification anomalies require manual/UEBA review.
ITID-34522.response: Review the guest's access scope and activity history; revoke if unjustified and assess what data was exposed during the access window.
metrics: Count of guest accounts added per month
Percentage of guest accounts with expiration set
ITID-34522.notes: Distinguished from ITID-34521 by granting standing workspace membership rather than a single document link.

playbook.name: Response: Guest/External User Added to Internal Teams/Slack Workspace for Data Access
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected data exfiltration where an external guest account is added to an internal Teams or Slack workspace/channel, granting ongoing access to sensitive conversations and files.

steps.title: Confirm the guest account addition and identify who added it
steps.desc: Review the collaboration platform's admin audit logs to confirm the addition of an external guest account, identify who added it, and identify which channels/files the guest can access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed guest addition event with adder, guest identity, and access scope identified.
steps.abort: If the guest was added through an approved external-collaboration process, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Review what the guest account accessed
steps.desc: Review the guest account's activity logs to determine what messages, files, or channels it accessed since being added.
steps.outcome: Scope of guest access activity established.

steps.title: Remove the guest account from the workspace/channels
steps.desc: Remove the external guest account's access to the workspace and any sensitive channels immediately.
steps.outcome: Guest access revoked.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and engage HR/Legal if added by an insider deliberately
steps.desc: If the guest was added deliberately by an employee to facilitate data access rather than in error, preserve evidence with chain of custody and engage HR/Legal.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; HR/Legal engaged if warranted.

steps.title: Review and tighten guest-invitation permissions
steps.desc: Review who has permission to add external guests to the workspace and restrict this capability per policy.
steps.outcome: Guest-invitation permissions tightened.

steps.title: Audit for other guest accounts added by the same individual
steps.desc: Review the platform's audit logs for other guest accounts added by the same employee to determine whether this is an isolated event or a broader pattern.
steps.outcome: Full scope of guest additions by the individual established.

steps.title: Notify affected channel owners and assess disclosure obligations
steps.desc: Notify owners of affected channels and, if sensitive/regulated data was exposed, engage Legal/Privacy to assess disclosure obligations.
steps.outcome: Channel owners notified; disclosure obligations assessed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review guest-access governance
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether guest-access approval workflows and periodic guest-access reviews need strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34523.def: An event in which a user (internal or guest) bulk-downloads or syncs a large volume of files from a collaboration platform, moving data from the managed cloud environment to an unmanaged local endpoint or external storage.
ITID-34523.purpose: Captures bulk download or desktop-sync activity pulling large volumes of shared collaboration-platform files to a local or external destination.
scopeIncludes: Bulk 'download all' actions on a SharePoint/Google Drive/Teams library
Desktop sync client pulling large volumes of shared files to an unmanaged device
Third-party sync tool connected via OAuth to mass-download files
scopeExcludes: Creation of the sharing link/guest access itself without a bulk download (ITID-34521, 34522)
Bulk copy from a traditional network file share (ITID-34511)
ITID-34523.severity: High when the destination device is unmanaged or the volume is a large fraction of the library.
ITID-34523.priority: P1 if download is to an unmanaged/external device with sensitive content; otherwise P2.
ITID-34523.escalation: Escalate to DLP/CASB team to confirm destination and device management status; involve insider risk if the actor is a departing employee.
indicators: CASB alert on abnormal download volume from a SaaS platform
Sync client registered from an unmanaged/unrecognized device
OAuth app with broad file-read scope authorized shortly before mass download
vectors: Native platform bulk-download feature
Unsanctioned OAuth-connected sync/backup app
Personal device sync client added to a work account
rootCauses: No CASB download-volume policy enforcement
Device trust/management not required for sync access
Overly permissive OAuth app consent policy
controls: CASB download volume alerting
Managed-device-only sync policy
OAuth app allowlisting
ITID-34523.detection: Strong: CASB provides volume- and device-aware detection for this pattern.
ITID-34523.response: Identify destination device/account, block further sync, and assess scope of data downloaded.
metrics: Count of bulk-download alerts per month
Percentage from unmanaged devices
ITID-34523.notes: Focused on the download/sync volume mechanism, complementing rather than duplicating the access-grant leaves ITID-34521/34522.

playbook.name: Response: Collaboration Platform Bulk Download/Sync of Shared Files
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected data exfiltration where an account performs a bulk download or sync of files shared via a collaboration platform (Teams, Slack, SharePoint), often just before departure or as part of an insider scheme.

steps.title: Review collaboration platform audit logs for bulk download/sync events
steps.desc: Review the platform's audit logs for the account for an unusually large number of file downloads or a full sync of shared folders in a short period, compared to the account's normal baseline.
steps.outcome: Confirmed bulk download/sync event with account, files, and volume identified.
steps.abort: If consistent with an approved bulk migration or backup task, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Determine the destination of the downloaded/synced data
steps.desc: Correlate with endpoint and DLP logs to determine where the downloaded/synced files were subsequently stored or transferred.
steps.outcome: Destination of the data identified.

steps.title: Restrict the account's download/sync capability
steps.desc: Restrict or suspend the account's ability to download or sync files pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Further bulk download/sync prevented.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and engage HR/Legal given likely insider involvement
