steps.desc: Preserve logs and evidence with documented chain of custody and engage HR/Legal, since this pattern often indicates insider activity ahead of departure.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; HR/Legal engaged.

steps.title: Remove local copies where technically possible
steps.desc: Where the downloaded files reside on a managed endpoint, remove or quarantine local copies per HR/Legal direction.
steps.outcome: Local copies remediated where possible.

steps.title: Verify no residual sync/cache copies remain on the endpoint
steps.desc: Check the endpoint for locally cached or synced copies of the downloaded files that may persist after platform-level restriction.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed free of residual copies, or copies identified and removed.

steps.title: Apply HR/Legal-directed personnel action and restore appropriate access
steps.desc: Implement the personnel action determined by HR/Legal and restore access appropriately once the investigation concludes.
steps.outcome: Personnel action applied; access restored appropriately.

steps.title: Document the case and review bulk download/sync alerting
steps.desc: Record the incident with HR/Legal and evaluate whether the platform needs bulk-download/sync anomaly alerting, particularly tied to resignation/termination workflows.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendations tracked.

ITID-34524.def: A misused collaboration platform exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID, pending further investigation.
ITID-34524.purpose: Intake bucket for misused collaboration platform exfiltration activity that does not fit the external-link, guest-access, or bulk-download leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reported collaboration platform data loss with mechanism not yet determined
Mixed or ambiguous collaboration platform misuse spanning multiple sub-patterns
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34521, 34522, or 34523 once investigated
ITID-34524.severity: Medium pending triage; reassess once classified.
ITID-34524.escalation: Escalate to SOC triage for reclassification into a specific sibling ITID.
indicators: Generic CASB/DLP alert on a collaboration platform lacking enough detail for specific classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient logging detail to classify the exfiltration mechanism at intake
mitreTechniques: T1213.002 Data from Information Repositories: Sharepoint
T1567.002 Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
controls: CASB monitoring
Collaboration platform audit logging
ITID-34524.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34524.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Misused Collaboration Platforms ITID as soon as possible.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34524.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Misused Collaboration Platform Exfiltration
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected data exfiltration via a collaboration platform that does not fit a more specific category (external sharing link on a document, guest account addition, or bulk download/sync).

steps.title: Confirm the collaboration platform misuse and classify the pattern
steps.desc: Review collaboration platform audit logs to confirm unauthorized data exposure or transfer and attempt to classify the specific pattern (sharing link, guest access, or bulk download/sync).
steps.guidance: If the pattern matches a more specific category, transition to that playbook.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exfiltration activity with account, content, and scope identified.
steps.abort: If no exfiltration is confirmed, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Estimate scope and destination of exposed/transferred data
steps.desc: Review available logs to determine what data was affected and where it went or who accessed it.
steps.outcome: Scope and destination estimate established.

steps.title: Revoke the identified access path
steps.desc: Revoke the sharing link, guest access, or download/sync capability identified as the exfiltration path.
steps.outcome: Access path revoked.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and engage HR/Legal as warranted
steps.desc: Preserve logs and evidence with documented chain of custody; engage HR/Legal if insider involvement is suspected.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; HR/Legal engaged if warranted.

steps.title: Correct the underlying sharing/permission configuration
steps.desc: Reset sharing, permission, or guest-access settings to comply with data classification policy.
steps.outcome: Configuration corrected.

steps.title: Verify no residual access or copies remain
steps.desc: Confirm no other sharing links, guest accounts, or local copies remain that would allow the same exposure to persist.
steps.outcome: Residual exposure confirmed closed.

steps.title: Notify data owners and restore appropriate access
steps.desc: Notify affected data owners and restore access appropriately once the investigation concludes.
steps.outcome: Data owners notified; access restored appropriately.

steps.title: Document the incident and reclassify if a specific pattern emerges
steps.desc: Record findings and, if the technique is later identified as a specific known pattern, update the incident classification for future reference.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34531.def: An event in which a user installs and uses a BitTorrent or similar P2P client to upload/seed sensitive organizational data, distributing it to external peers outside any single controllable destination.
ITID-34531.purpose: Captures use of a BitTorrent or other peer-to-peer file-sharing client to move sensitive data out to a distributed swarm of external peers.
scopeIncludes: Installation and use of a torrent client on a managed endpoint
Creation of a torrent/magnet link for a file containing sensitive data
Seeding of organizational data to external peers
scopeExcludes: Direct device-to-device transfer via AirDrop/Nearby Share (ITID-34532)
File sharing via sanctioned collaboration platforms (Misused Collaboration Platforms group)
ITID-34531.severity: High: P2P distribution is effectively uncontained once seeded.
ITID-34531.escalation: Escalate immediately; treat as an active, likely unrecoverable data loss event once seeding is confirmed.
indicators: Endpoint process execution of known torrent client binaries
Network traffic on BitTorrent protocol ports/patterns from a managed endpoint
EDR alert on unauthorized P2P application installation
vectors: Manual installation of a torrent client to distribute data
Use of a portable/USB-run torrent client to bypass application allowlisting
rootCauses: Application allowlisting not enforced on endpoints
No network-layer blocking of P2P protocol traffic
Lack of monitoring for unauthorized software installation
controls: Application allowlisting
Network-layer P2P protocol blocking
EDR unauthorized software alerting
ITID-34531.detection: Strong: network protocol signatures and EDR process monitoring reliably detect P2P client use.
ITID-34531.response: Immediately isolate the endpoint, kill the client process, and treat any seeded data as compromised/publicly exposed.
metrics: Count of P2P client detections per quarter
Time-to-isolation once detected
ITID-34531.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34532 by the swarm/distributed-peer nature of BitTorrent versus direct device-to-device transfer.

playbook.name: Response: BitTorrent/P2P File-Sharing Client Used to Exfiltrate Data
playbook.description: For confirmed data exfiltration where a BitTorrent or similar peer-to-peer file-sharing client is installed and used to upload sensitive organizational data to a distributed swarm, making the data publicly and widely retrievable.

steps.title: Confirm the P2P client installation and upload activity
steps.desc: Review endpoint software inventory and network/firewall logs for the presence of a P2P client and associated outbound traffic on typical torrent ports/protocols, and identify what files were added to the client's shared/seed folder.
steps.outcome: Confirmed P2P exfiltration event with client, host, and shared files identified.
steps.abort: If the client and files relate to an approved business use case, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Assess public exposure of the shared data
steps.desc: Determine how long the files were seeding and, where possible, estimate how widely the data may have propagated across the swarm given P2P's distributed, largely irreversible exposure.
steps.outcome: Exposure window and propagation risk assessed.

steps.title: Isolate the host and terminate the P2P client
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host and terminate the P2P client process to stop further seeding immediately.
steps.outcome: Seeding stopped; host isolated.

steps.title: Block P2P protocols/ports at the network perimeter
steps.desc: Block common P2P/torrent ports and protocol signatures at the firewall organization-wide.
steps.outcome: P2P traffic blocked organization-wide.

steps.title: Uninstall the P2P client and remove shared files
steps.desc: Remove the P2P client and any local copies of the shared files, and check endpoint policy for how the unauthorized software was installed.
steps.outcome: Host confirmed clean of the P2P client and shared data.

steps.title: Sweep for the same P2P client on other endpoints
steps.desc: Check endpoint software inventory fleet-wide for the same P2P client installed on other hosts.
steps.outcome: Scope confirmed; any additional affected endpoints remediated.

steps.title: Notify data owners and assess disclosure obligations given likely public exposure
steps.desc: Notify the data owner and engage Legal/Privacy to assess breach notification obligations, given that data seeded via P2P should be treated as effectively public and largely unrecoverable.
steps.outcome: Data owner notified; disclosure obligations assessed.

steps.title: Document the incident and review application allowlisting policy
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether endpoint application allowlisting should block P2P client installation by default.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34532.def: An event in which a user transfers sensitive files directly to another device using a proximity-based P2P protocol (AirDrop, Nearby Share, or similar), bypassing network-layer monitoring entirely since the transfer never traverses the corporate network.
ITID-34532.purpose: Captures use of a direct, network-monitoring-evading peer-to-peer transfer mechanism such as AirDrop or Nearby Share to move data device-to-device.
scopeIncludes: AirDrop transfer of sensitive files from a managed device to an unmanaged/personal device
Android Nearby Share or similar Wi-Fi Direct/Bluetooth-based transfer of sensitive files
Transfer to a device not enrolled in MDM
scopeExcludes: Distributed swarm-based P2P transfer such as BitTorrent (ITID-34531)
Data moved via removable USB media (covered elsewhere under physical exfiltration ITIDs)
ITID-34532.severity: Medium-High, depending on data sensitivity and whether the receiving device is unmanaged.
ITID-34532.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the receiving device is confirmed external/personal and data is regulated.
ITID-34532.escalation: Escalate to endpoint security if AirDrop/Nearby Share is not centrally disabled and sensitive data transfer is confirmed.
indicators: MDM/EDR log showing AirDrop or Nearby Share feature invocation with file transfer
Endpoint configuration showing AirDrop set to 'Everyone' rather than restricted
Sensitive file access immediately followed by a proximity-transfer event
vectors: AirDrop set to allow transfers to/from any nearby device
Nearby Share used to bypass DLP that only monitors network egress
rootCauses: Proximity-sharing features not restricted via MDM policy
DLP/network monitoring blind to on-device peer transfer features
Lack of awareness that these features bypass network controls
controls: MDM policy restricting AirDrop/Nearby Share to managed devices only
Endpoint DLP with local peripheral/feature awareness
ITID-34532.detection: Weak-Moderate: these transfers occur off-network, so detection depends heavily on endpoint/MDM telemetry rather than network monitoring.
ITID-34532.response: Confirm via endpoint logs what was transferred and to what device; restrict the feature going forward if not already MDM-managed.
metrics: Count of proximity-transfer policy violations detected
Percentage of managed devices with AirDrop/Nearby Share restricted
ITID-34532.notes: Distinguished from ITID-34531 as a direct device-to-device, network-invisible transfer rather than a distributed swarm upload.

playbook.name: Response: Direct P2P File Transfer App (AirDrop/Nearby Share) Used to Bypass Network Monitoring
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected data exfiltration where an employee uses a direct device-to-device transfer feature (AirDrop, Nearby Share, or similar) to move sensitive files to a personal or unmanaged device, bypassing network-based monitoring entirely.

steps.title: Confirm the direct transfer event via endpoint logs
steps.desc: Review endpoint OS-level logs (e.g. AirDrop transfer logs, Nearby Share activity) and DLP endpoint agent logs for evidence of a direct device-to-device transfer of sensitive files.
steps.guidance: Since this bypasses network monitoring, endpoint-level (OS and DLP agent) logs are the primary evidence source.
steps.outcome: Confirmed direct transfer event with files and receiving device identified if possible.
steps.abort: If the transfer was to another company-managed device for an approved purpose, close as a false positive.
steps.tool: Endpoint OS logs / DLP endpoint agent

steps.title: Determine identity of the receiving device where possible
steps.desc: Review device name/identifier captured in the transfer log to determine whether the receiving device is a managed corporate asset or unmanaged/personal device.
steps.outcome: Receiving device classified as managed or unmanaged.

steps.title: Disable direct transfer features via endpoint policy
steps.desc: Apply or enforce endpoint management policy to disable AirDrop/Nearby Share or restrict it to organization-managed devices only.
steps.outcome: Direct transfer capability disabled or restricted.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and engage HR/Legal if deliberate insider action is suspected
steps.desc: Preserve logs with documented chain of custody and engage HR/Legal if the transfer appears to be a deliberate attempt to bypass monitoring.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; HR/Legal engaged if warranted.

steps.title: Confirm policy applied fleet-wide
steps.desc: Confirm the direct-transfer restriction policy is applied consistently across the managed device fleet, not just the affected device.
steps.outcome: Policy confirmed applied fleet-wide.

steps.title: Verify the direct-transfer restriction closes the specific bypass observed
steps.desc: Test that the applied endpoint policy actually blocks the specific direct-transfer feature/protocol observed in this incident.
steps.outcome: Policy confirmed effective against the observed bypass.

steps.title: Apply appropriate personnel action and monitor
steps.desc: Apply personnel action per HR/Legal direction if applicable, and monitor for recurrence via available endpoint telemetry.
steps.outcome: No recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the case and review endpoint DLP coverage for local transfer methods
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate whether DLP/endpoint policy coverage adequately addresses local, network-independent transfer methods.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendations tracked.

ITID-34533.def: A P2P transfer exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Peer-to-Peer Transfers, pending further investigation.
ITID-34533.purpose: Intake bucket for peer-to-peer transfer exfiltration activity that does not fit the BitTorrent or direct-device-transfer leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reported P2P-related data loss with mechanism not yet determined
Use of a P2P protocol not covered by the named sibling leaves
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34531 or 34532 once investigated
ITID-34533.severity: Medium pending triage; reassess once classified.
ITID-34533.escalation: Escalate to SOC triage for reclassification.
indicators: Generic P2P protocol detection lacking enough detail for specific classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient logging detail to classify the P2P mechanism at intake
controls: Network protocol monitoring
Endpoint application monitoring
ITID-34533.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34533.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Peer-to-Peer Transfers ITID as soon as possible.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34533.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Peer-to-Peer Transfer Exfiltration
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected data exfiltration via a peer-to-peer transfer method that does not fit a more specific category (BitTorrent/P2P swarm sharing or direct device-to-device transfer apps).

steps.title: Confirm the P2P transfer activity and classify the method
steps.desc: Review available endpoint and network logs to confirm unauthorized P2P transfer activity and attempt to classify the specific method (swarm-based sharing vs. direct device-to-device transfer).
steps.guidance: If the method matches a more specific category, transition to that playbook.
steps.outcome: Confirmed transfer activity with method and scope identified as far as possible.
steps.abort: If no exfiltration is confirmed, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Estimate scope of data affected
steps.desc: Review available logs to estimate what data was transferred and to whom or where.
steps.outcome: Best-available scope estimate established.

steps.title: Isolate the host or restrict the transfer capability
steps.desc: Network-isolate the host or disable the relevant transfer feature/application.
steps.outcome: Further transfer prevented.

steps.title: Preserve evidence and engage HR/Legal as warranted
steps.desc: Preserve available logs and evidence with a documented chain of custody; engage HR/Legal if insider involvement is suspected.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved; HR/Legal engaged if warranted.

steps.title: Remove the transfer mechanism and remediate policy gaps
steps.desc: Remove the P2P application or feature enabling the transfer and close any policy gap that allowed it.
steps.outcome: Mechanism removed; gap remediated.

steps.title: Verify no residual exposure remains
steps.desc: Confirm no residual technical or policy gap remains that would allow the same peer-to-peer transfer method to recur.
steps.outcome: Residual exposure confirmed closed.

steps.title: Apply appropriate action and monitor for recurrence
steps.desc: Apply personnel action per HR/Legal direction if applicable, and monitor for recurrence.
steps.outcome: No recurrence observed.

steps.title: Document the case and reclassify if a specific pattern emerges
steps.desc: Record findings and, if the technique is later identified as a specific known pattern, update the incident classification for future reference.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34611.def: A pattern of an employee or contractor accessing and/or locally storing a broad set of files spanning topics, departments, or systems unrelated to their current job function, without an accompanying exfiltration event yet observed.
ITID-34611.purpose: Captures the behavioral pattern of an insider accumulating files unrelated to their current role, as an early-stage precursor signal to later exfiltration.
scopeIncludes: Access to file repositories/systems outside the user's department or project scope with no legitimate business reason on record
Local accumulation of downloaded files spanning unrelated topics over a sustained period
Requests for access grants beyond role requirements that are then used to browse broadly
scopeExcludes: Repeated, targeted access to a specific sensitive record set over time (ITID-34612)
Hoarding detected specifically in the pre-resignation window (ITID-34613)
Any confirmed external transfer of the hoarded data (tracked under the specific exfiltration-channel ITID used)
ITID-34611.severity: Low-Medium as a standalone behavioral signal; increases when correlated with other insider risk indicators.
ITID-34611.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if correlated with other insider risk indicators (role change, HR case, access anomalies).
ITID-34611.escalation: Escalate to insider risk program for correlation with HR/behavioral indicators; do not treat in isolation as conclusive of intent.
indicators: UEBA baseline deviation showing access to files/systems outside normal role pattern
Local endpoint storage growth in file categories unrelated to job function
Access request patterns inconsistent with stated business need
vectors: Legitimate access rights used to browse and accumulate unrelated data over time
rootCauses: Overly broad standing access not scoped to least privilege
No periodic access review/recertification
Lack of UEBA baselining for role-appropriate access
controls: Least-privilege access review
UEBA baselining and anomaly alerting
ITID-34611.detection: Moderate: UEBA can flag the access-pattern deviation, but this is a behavioral precursor without a hard exfiltration signal.
ITID-34611.response: Correlate with insider risk program data; do not escalate to HR/legal action on this signal alone without corroboration.
metrics: Count of UEBA role-deviation alerts per quarter
Percentage correlated with subsequent insider risk cases
ITID-34611.notes: Scoped strictly to the technical exfiltration/access-hoarding method and its detection surface; motivational/behavioral case management is owned by the Insider Risk program, and specific theft-content leaves (ITID-13111-13114) and physical document theft (ITID-14230-series) are cross-referenced rather than duplicated here.

playbook.name: Response: Bulk Accumulation of Files Unrelated to Current Job Function
playbook.description: For suspected insider data hoarding where an employee accumulates a large volume of sensitive files unrelated to their current job function, typically identified as a behavioral pattern over an extended review window rather than a single event. Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling.

steps.title: Review access and file-copy history over an extended window
steps.desc: Review the employee's file access, download, and local copy history over an extended window (e.g. weeks to months, not a single session) to establish whether accumulation of files unrelated to their role forms a genuine pattern rather than an isolated event.
steps.guidance: Data hoarding is defined by a sustained pattern; a single access event is not sufficient to substantiate this classification.
steps.outcome: Behavioral pattern confirmed and documented with a timeline of accumulation.
steps.abort: If the accumulated files are relevant to a documented project or role change, close as a false positive.
steps.tool: File server / DLP / SIEM long-window audit logs

steps.title: Correlate accumulation with role, project, or employment context
steps.desc: Review the employee's job function, recent role changes, and any known employment context (e.g. performance issues, upcoming reorganization) that might explain or heighten concern about the pattern.
steps.outcome: Context established to support risk assessment.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before any account action
steps.desc: Preserve the access history, file lists, and timeline with a documented chain of custody before taking any account or personnel action, given potential disciplinary or legal use.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal before further investigative or account action
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal of the suspected pattern and obtain guidance on further monitoring, evidence handling, and any account restriction before proceeding.
steps.guidance: Do not confront the employee or take unilateral account action until HR/Legal have weighed in.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged with an agreed investigative plan.

steps.title: Restrict access to unrelated sensitive data per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Once authorized, restrict the employee's access to systems/data unrelated to their current job function.
steps.outcome: Access restricted appropriately.

steps.title: Determine the destination of the accumulated data
steps.desc: Determine where the accumulated files were ultimately stored or transferred (local device, removable media, personal cloud) to scope full exposure.
steps.outcome: Destination(s) of accumulated data identified.

steps.title: Apply HR/Legal-directed personnel action
steps.desc: Implement the personnel action determined by HR/Legal based on investigation findings.
steps.outcome: Personnel action applied per HR/Legal direction.

steps.title: Document the case and review long-window access anomaly monitoring
steps.desc: Record the incident with HR/Legal and evaluate whether insider-risk monitoring adequately detects slow accumulation patterns over extended windows, not just single-session anomalies.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendations tracked.

ITID-34612.def: A pattern in which a user repeatedly accesses and locally copies a specific sensitive dataset (e.g., a customer list, source code repository, or financial record set) over an extended period, indicating deliberate, targeted staging rather than incidental browsing.
ITID-34612.purpose: Captures a sustained pattern of repeated, targeted access and local copying of a specific sensitive record set over time, distinguishing focused hoarding from broad unrelated-file accumulation.
scopeIncludes: Recurring access-and-copy of the same sensitive record set across multiple sessions/days
Local caching of query results or exports from a sensitive repository on a recurring basis
Access frequency to a specific dataset significantly exceeding the user's peer group over time
scopeExcludes: Broad, unrelated-file accumulation without a focused target (ITID-34611)
Hoarding specifically concentrated in the pre-resignation window (ITID-34613)
ITID-34612.severity: Medium-High, scaling with the sensitivity of the targeted record set and access frequency.
ITID-34612.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if correlated with departure signals or external transfer indicators.
ITID-34612.escalation: Escalate to insider risk program for a formal review once repeated targeted access is confirmed against peer baselines.
indicators: UEBA alert on repeated access to a specific sensitive dataset above peer baseline
Recurring export/download events from the same repository over weeks/months
Local file system artifacts showing repeated retention of the same dataset
vectors: Legitimate query/export access used repeatedly to build a local copy of a sensitive dataset over time
rootCauses: No alerting on cumulative access frequency to a single sensitive dataset
Export/download activity not rate-limited or reviewed
Local retention of exported sensitive data not restricted by DLP
controls: Cumulative access-frequency alerting per dataset
DLP restriction on local retention of exported sensitive data
ITID-34612.detection: Moderate-Strong: repository access logs and UEBA provide a clear cumulative-pattern signal over time.
ITID-34612.response: Review the full access history against the user's role, and correlate with other insider risk indicators before escalation.
metrics: Count of repeated-targeted-access alerts per quarter
Average access frequency multiplier over peer baseline at time of alert
ITID-34612.notes: Scoped to the technical access/copy pattern; cross-references ITID-13111-13114 for theft-content classification once an actual exfiltration event is confirmed.

playbook.name: Response: Repeated Access and Local Copying of Sensitive Records Over Time
playbook.description: For suspected insider data hoarding where an employee repeatedly accesses and locally copies sensitive records over an extended period, indicating a sustained collection pattern rather than a single incident. Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling.

steps.title: Review repeated access and copy history over an extended window
steps.desc: Review the employee's access and local copy history over an extended window to establish the frequency, consistency, and growth of the pattern, distinguishing sustained hoarding from occasional legitimate reference use.
steps.guidance: Look for repeated access to the same or similar record sets on a recurring cadence over weeks or months.
steps.outcome: Sustained pattern confirmed and documented with frequency and volume over time.
steps.abort: If access frequency is consistent with the employee's documented job duties, close as a false positive.
steps.tool: File server / DLP / SIEM long-window audit logs

steps.title: Identify where locally copied data resides
steps.desc: Determine where the copied records were stored locally (workstation, removable media, personal cloud) to scope potential further exposure.
steps.outcome: Storage locations of copied data identified.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before any account action
steps.desc: Preserve the access history, copy logs, and timeline with a documented chain of custody before taking any account or personnel action.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal before further investigative or account action
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal of the sustained pattern and obtain guidance on evidence handling and any account restriction before proceeding.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged with an agreed investigative plan.

steps.title: Remove or secure locally hoarded copies per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Once authorized, secure or remove locally stored copies of the hoarded records from the employee's devices.
steps.outcome: Locally hoarded data secured or removed.

steps.title: Check for other repeated-access patterns by the same individual
steps.desc: Review other systems and record sets the individual has access to for similar repeated-access patterns, to establish the full scope of the behavior.
steps.outcome: Full scope of repeated-access behavior established.

steps.title: Apply HR/Legal-directed personnel action
steps.desc: Implement the personnel action determined by HR/Legal based on investigation findings.
steps.outcome: Personnel action applied per HR/Legal direction.

steps.title: Document the case and review repeated-access alerting thresholds
steps.desc: Record the incident with HR/Legal and evaluate whether monitoring should alert on repeated access/copy patterns to the same sensitive record sets over time.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendations tracked.

ITID-34613.def: A pattern of file accumulation, local copying, or access-volume increase by a user in the window immediately preceding or following their resignation notice or termination, where the timing itself is the primary risk-elevating signal.
ITID-34613.purpose: Captures data hoarding activity whose defining differentiator is timing: detected in close proximity to an employee's resignation or termination, sharply raising exfiltration risk.
scopeIncludes: Elevated data access/copy activity in the days-to-weeks before a resignation date on record
Access-volume spike immediately following notice of termination but before offboarding completes
Hoarding activity correlated with an HR-flagged departure case
scopeExcludes: Hoarding behavior with no correlated departure event (ITID-34611, 34612)
Confirmed bulk email exfiltration tied to departure, tracked separately under ITID-34213
ITID-34613.severity: High: departure timing is a strong aggravating factor for insider exfiltration risk.
ITID-34613.escalation: Escalate immediately to insider risk program and HR; consider expedited access revocation/offboarding controls.
indicators: Access/copy volume spike within the standard pre-resignation lookback window
HR departure-case flag correlated with a UEBA anomaly alert
Access to systems outside normal duties immediately after notice is given
vectors: Legitimate residual access retained through the notice period used to accumulate data before departure
rootCauses: Standing access not reduced immediately upon resignation notice
No automated departure-triggered UEBA sensitivity increase
Offboarding process not synchronized with HR notice date
controls: Departure-triggered access reduction
HR-to-security departure notification integration
Elevated UEBA sensitivity during notice period
ITID-34613.detection: Strong when HR departure data is integrated with UEBA; weak if that integration is absent.
ITID-34613.response: Immediately review access scope, consider access reduction/monitoring increase, and preserve logs for potential investigation.
metrics: Count of departure-window hoarding alerts per quarter
Median time from resignation notice to access reduction
ITID-34613.notes: The differentiating axis versus ITID-34611/34612 is timing relative to departure, not the access mechanism itself.

playbook.name: Response: Data Hoarding Detected Shortly Before Resignation/Termination
playbook.description: For suspected insider data hoarding identified in connection with an employee's resignation or upcoming termination, where accumulation of sensitive files over time coincides with departure. Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling given heightened likelihood of intended use elsewhere.

steps.title: Review access history over an extended window leading up to departure
steps.desc: Review the employee's file access and copy history over an extended window (not just the days immediately before departure) to establish whether accumulation began earlier and accelerated near the resignation/termination date.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR to obtain the resignation/termination date and reason as context.
steps.outcome: Pattern confirmed with timeline relative to the departure date documented.
steps.abort: If accumulation is consistent with a documented handover or transition task, close as a false positive.
steps.tool: File server / DLP / SIEM long-window audit logs; HR coordination

steps.title: Assess destination and potential use of hoarded data
steps.desc: Determine where the hoarded data was moved (personal email, cloud storage, removable media) to assess likely intended use with a new employer or competitor.
steps.outcome: Destination and risk of external use assessed.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before any account action
steps.desc: Preserve the access history, copy logs, and destination evidence with a documented chain of custody before taking any account or personnel action, given the strong likelihood of legal proceedings.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal to coordinate timing of account restriction with the departure process
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR and Legal on the timing and manner of any account restriction so it aligns with the formal offboarding process and does not compromise the evidence or legal position.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged with an agreed timeline for account action.

steps.title: Disable access and revoke devices/accounts per the offboarding process
steps.desc: Disable the employee's access and recover company devices per standard offboarding procedure, timed per HR/Legal direction.
steps.outcome: Access disabled; devices recovered.

steps.title: Verify no residual copies remain accessible after departure
steps.desc: Confirm no residual local copies, cloud copies, or shared links related to the hoarded data remain accessible following the employee's departure.
steps.outcome: No residual accessible copies confirmed.

steps.title: Pursue recovery of exfiltrated data and applicable legal remedies
steps.desc: Support Legal in pursuing recovery of the hoarded data (e.g. cease-and-desist, litigation hold, coordination with the new employer) as directed.
steps.outcome: Legal remedies pursued per Legal's direction.

steps.title: Document the case and review pre-departure monitoring procedures
steps.desc: Record the incident with HR/Legal and evaluate whether standard offboarding procedures should include a pre-departure access/download review for at-risk roles.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendations tracked.

ITID-34614.def: A data hoarding event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Data Hoarding, pending further investigation.
ITID-34614.purpose: Intake bucket for data hoarding activity that does not fit the broad-accumulation, targeted-access, or departure-timing leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reported hoarding behavior with pattern/timing not yet determined
Mixed hoarding behavior spanning multiple sub-patterns
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34611, 34612, or 34613 once investigated
ITID-34614.severity: Low-Medium pending triage; reassess once classified.
ITID-34614.escalation: Escalate to insider risk program for reclassification.
indicators: Generic UEBA behavioral alert lacking enough detail for specific classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient context available to classify the hoarding pattern at intake
controls: UEBA behavioral monitoring
ITID-34614.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34614.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Data Hoarding ITID as soon as possible.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34614.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Data Hoarding
playbook.description: For suspected insider data hoarding that does not fit a more specific category (unrelated-to-role accumulation, repeated copying over time, or pre-departure hoarding). Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling and identification based on a sustained pattern over an extended window rather than a single event.

steps.title: Review access history over an extended window to establish a pattern
steps.desc: Review the employee's access, download, and copy history over an extended review window to establish whether a genuine hoarding pattern exists and attempt to classify it against more specific categories.
steps.guidance: If the pattern matches a more specific category, transition to that playbook. Data hoarding requires a sustained pattern, not a single event.
steps.outcome: Pattern confirmed or ruled out, with timeline documented.
steps.abort: If no sustained pattern is found, close as a false positive.
steps.tool: File server / DLP / SIEM long-window audit logs

steps.title: Assess scope and destination of hoarded data
steps.desc: Determine what data was accumulated and where it currently resides or was moved to.
steps.outcome: Scope and destination established.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before any account action
steps.desc: Preserve the access history and evidence with a documented chain of custody before any account or personnel action.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal before further investigative or account action
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal and obtain guidance before taking further action.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged with an agreed investigative plan.

steps.title: Restrict or remove hoarded access/data per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Restrict the employee's access to the relevant data or remove locally hoarded copies once authorized.
steps.outcome: Access restricted or data removed appropriately.

steps.title: Determine the destination of the accumulated data
steps.desc: Determine where the hoarded data was ultimately stored or transferred to scope full exposure.
steps.outcome: Destination(s) of hoarded data identified.

steps.title: Apply HR/Legal-directed personnel action
steps.desc: Implement the personnel action determined by HR/Legal based on investigation findings.
steps.outcome: Personnel action applied per HR/Legal direction.

steps.title: Document the case and reclassify if a specific pattern emerges
steps.desc: Record findings with HR/Legal and, if the pattern is later identified as a specific known category, update the incident classification for future reference.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34621.def: An event in which a user creates a mail-flow rule on their own mailbox that automatically forwards messages (all mail or a filtered subset) to a personal email address, establishing a standing, low-visibility exfiltration channel.
ITID-34621.purpose: Captures an insider configuring a mailbox auto-forward rule that silently routes incoming/sent mail to their own personal email address for ongoing exfiltration.
scopeIncludes: Inbox rule forwarding all mail or a keyword-filtered subset to a personal (e.g., Gmail, Outlook.com) address
Forwarding rule with no corresponding business justification on file
Rule configured to forward silently without leaving a visible copy in Sent Items
scopeExcludes: Forwarding rule targeting an external competitor/new employer domain, tracked separately for its higher-severity destination signal (ITID-34622)
A one-time manual self-forward of a specific email (ITID-34211, Internal Email Account Exfiltration)
Rules configured with delayed activation timed to a resignation (ITID-34623)
ITID-34621.severity: Medium-High, scaling with mailbox sensitivity and forwarding rule scope (all mail vs. filtered).
ITID-34621.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for executive/high-sensitivity mailboxes or all-mail forwarding rules.
ITID-34621.escalation: Escalate to security operations to disable the rule immediately and assess how much mail was exfiltrated during its active window.
indicators: Mail platform audit log showing a new forwarding rule creation to an external personal domain
Automated alert on forwarding rule targeting a consumer webmail domain
Rule configured to hide/delete the forwarded copy
vectors: Native mailbox rule feature misused for standing self-exfiltration
Rule created via mail client rules wizard or via API/PowerShell
rootCauses: No policy blocking or alerting on auto-forward rules to external domains
Mail platform default allows user-created external forwarding rules
Lack of periodic audit of active forwarding rules
controls: Mail platform policy blocking external auto-forwarding
Automated alerting on new forwarding rule creation
Periodic audit of active mailbox rules
ITID-34621.detection: Strong: mail platform audit logs directly capture forwarding rule creation and target address.
ITID-34621.response: Disable the rule immediately, review the forwarding window for exposed content, and interview the user per insider risk process.
metrics: Count of external forwarding rules created per month
Mean time-to-disable once detected
detections: Mail platform external auto-forward rule alert
ITID-34621.notes: Scoped to the standing-rule mechanism specifically to a personal address; a competitor/new-employer destination is tracked as the higher-severity ITID-34622 to keep the severity axis clean.

playbook.name: Response: Insider-Configured Auto-Forward Rule to Personal Email Address
playbook.description: For confirmed insider data exfiltration where an employee configures a mailbox auto-forwarding rule to send incoming or sent email to their personal email address. Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling given potential disciplinary or legal use.

steps.title: Confirm the forwarding rule and its scope
steps.desc: Review mailbox configuration/audit logs to confirm the auto-forwarding rule, its creation date, the personal destination address, and the scope of mail it forwards (all mail vs. specific senders/keywords).
steps.outcome: Confirmed forwarding rule with destination, scope, and creation date documented.
steps.abort: If the forwarding rule was approved through a documented exception process, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Determine how much mail has already been forwarded
steps.desc: Review mail flow logs to estimate the volume and sensitivity of email already forwarded since the rule was created.
steps.outcome: Volume and sensitivity of forwarded mail estimated.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before any account action
steps.desc: Preserve the rule configuration, mail flow logs, and forwarded content list with a documented chain of custody before disabling the rule or taking account action, given potential disciplinary or legal use.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal, then disable the forwarding rule
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal, and once evidence is preserved and direction obtained, disable the forwarding rule to stop further mail leaving the organization.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged; forwarding rule disabled.
steps.tool: HR case management / email admin console

steps.title: Audit the mailbox for other exfiltration mechanisms
steps.desc: Check the mailbox for other forwarding rules, delegate access grants, or connected apps that could provide alternative exfiltration paths.
steps.outcome: Mailbox confirmed clean of other exfiltration mechanisms.

steps.title: Verify the personal destination address received no further mail after rule removal
steps.desc: Confirm through mail flow logs that no further messages were forwarded to the personal address after the rule was disabled.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further forwarding occurred after remediation.

steps.title: Apply HR/Legal-directed personnel action
steps.desc: Implement the personnel action determined by HR/Legal based on investigation findings.
steps.outcome: Personnel action applied per HR/Legal direction.

steps.title: Document the case and review auto-forward rule monitoring
steps.desc: Record the incident with HR/Legal and evaluate whether the organization should alert on or block auto-forwarding rules to external/personal domains by default.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendations tracked.

ITID-34622.def: An event in which a user creates a mailbox forwarding rule that routes mail to an email address on a domain identified as a competitor or the user's confirmed new employer, indicating likely intentional competitive data transfer.
ITID-34622.purpose: Captures an insider configuring a mailbox auto-forward rule to a known competitor or new-employer domain, the highest-severity destination variant of insider email forwarding.
scopeIncludes: Forwarding rule targeting a domain matching a known competitor or a new employer identified via HR/exit interview
Forwarding rule to an address later confirmed to belong to a competing organization
scopeExcludes: Forwarding to a personal/generic webmail address with no known competitor affiliation (ITID-34621)
Delayed-activation rules set up pre-resignation regardless of destination domain (ITID-34623)
ITID-34622.severity: High-Critical: competitor destination strongly indicates intentional trade-secret or competitive data transfer.
ITID-34622.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal, HR, and insider risk leadership; consider legal hold and potential trade-secret litigation posture.
indicators: Forwarding rule target domain matching a maintained competitor watchlist
HR confirmation of employee's new employer matching the forwarding domain
Rule created shortly before or after resignation notice
vectors: Native mailbox rule feature misused to route ongoing correspondence to a competitor domain
rootCauses: No competitor-domain watchlist integrated into forwarding rule alerting
Lack of coordination between HR exit data and security monitoring
controls: Competitor-domain watchlist alerting on forwarding rules
Legal hold trigger integration with insider risk program
ITID-34622.detection: Strong: mail platform audit logs plus a maintained competitor-domain watchlist give high-confidence detection.
ITID-34622.response: Disable the rule immediately, preserve full forensic record for potential legal action, and coordinate response with legal/HR.
metrics: Count of competitor-domain forwarding rules detected per year
Time-to-legal-notification once confirmed
ITID-34622.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34621 solely by destination-domain risk classification (competitor/new employer vs. generic personal).

playbook.name: Response: Insider-Configured Auto-Forward Rule to External Competitor/New Employer Domain
playbook.description: For confirmed insider data exfiltration where an employee configures a mailbox auto-forwarding rule targeting a known competitor or new employer's email domain, indicating likely intent to benefit a future or competing employer. Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling.

steps.title: Confirm the forwarding rule and identify the destination organization
steps.desc: Review mailbox configuration/audit logs to confirm the auto-forwarding rule and identify the destination domain, researching whether it belongs to a known competitor or a company the employee may be joining.
steps.outcome: Confirmed forwarding rule with destination domain and organizational affiliation identified.

steps.title: Determine volume and sensitivity of forwarded mail
steps.desc: Review mail flow logs to estimate the volume and sensitivity (e.g. client lists, pricing, trade secrets) of email already forwarded to the competitor/new employer domain.
steps.outcome: Volume and sensitivity of forwarded mail estimated.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before any account action
steps.desc: Preserve the rule configuration, mail flow logs, and forwarded content list with a documented chain of custody, given the strong likelihood of legal proceedings involving a competitor.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal immediately, then disable the forwarding rule
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal immediately given the competitive/trade-secret implications, and once direction is obtained, disable the forwarding rule.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged; forwarding rule disabled.
steps.tool: HR case management / Legal / email admin console

steps.title: Audit the mailbox for other exfiltration mechanisms
steps.desc: Check the mailbox for other forwarding rules, delegate access, or connected apps that could provide alternative exfiltration paths to the same or other external destinations.
steps.outcome: Mailbox confirmed clean of other exfiltration mechanisms.

steps.title: Verify the competitor/new employer domain received no further mail after rule removal
steps.desc: Confirm through mail flow logs that no further messages were forwarded to the competitor/new employer domain after the rule was disabled.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further forwarding occurred after remediation.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedies and apply HR-directed personnel action
steps.desc: Support Legal in pursuing appropriate remedies (e.g. cease-and-desist to the competitor, litigation hold) and implement the personnel action determined by HR/Legal.
steps.outcome: Legal remedies pursued; personnel action applied.

steps.title: Document the case and review auto-forward monitoring for known competitor domains
steps.desc: Record the incident with HR/Legal and evaluate whether email security policy should specifically flag forwarding rules to known competitor domains.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendations tracked.

ITID-34623.def: An event in which a user creates a mailbox forwarding rule configured to activate at a future date, after a triggering condition, or well before their resignation notice is given, so that the exfiltration channel is already established before heightened departure-window scrutiny begins.
ITID-34623.purpose: Captures a forwarding rule deliberately configured with delayed or conditional activation ahead of a planned resignation, indicating premeditated evasion of pre-departure monitoring.
scopeIncludes: Forwarding rule with a future-dated or conditional activation set weeks/months before resignation notice
Rule created significantly earlier than the standard pre-resignation lookback window used for departure monitoring, indicating deliberate evasion
Rule discovered retroactively during offboarding review that predates the notice date
scopeExcludes: Forwarding rule created during or immediately around the resignation notice window (ITID-34621, 34622)
Non-forwarding hoarding behavior timed to departure (ITID-34613)
ITID-34623.severity: High: premeditated timing indicates deliberate evasion of standard departure monitoring.
ITID-34623.escalation: Escalate to insider risk leadership and legal; the premeditation signal warrants treating this as intentional rather than opportunistic.
indicators: Forwarding rule creation timestamp significantly predating the resignation notice date
Rule with a scheduled or conditional trigger rather than immediate activation
Rule discovered only during retroactive offboarding audit, not real-time alerting
vectors: Mail platform rule feature misused with delayed/conditional logic to evade real-time departure monitoring
rootCauses: Departure-window monitoring only looks back a fixed short period, missing rules created earlier
No periodic full-tenant audit of standing forwarding rules independent of departure events
controls: Periodic full-tenant forwarding rule audit independent of departure triggers
Extended retroactive lookback during offboarding review
ITID-34623.detection: Weak-Moderate: standard departure-window monitoring can miss these; requires periodic full-population rule audits to close the gap.
ITID-34623.response: Treat as premeditated; disable the rule, preserve the full history, and involve legal given the evasion pattern.
metrics: Count of pre-dated forwarding rules discovered per offboarding audit cycle
Average lead time between rule creation and resignation notice
ITID-34623.notes: Differentiating axis is premeditation/timing relative to standard monitoring windows, not the destination address (which may overlap with ITID-34621/34622).

playbook.name: Response: Delayed-Activation Forwarding Rule Set Up Before Resignation
playbook.description: For confirmed insider data exfiltration where an employee sets up a mailbox auto-forwarding rule configured to activate after a delay or on a future date, timed to continue exfiltrating mail after their resignation or departure. Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling.

steps.title: Confirm the delayed/future-dated forwarding rule and its activation logic
steps.desc: Review mailbox configuration/audit logs to confirm the forwarding rule, its creation date, its activation condition (delay, scheduled date, or trigger tied to account status change), and the destination address.
steps.guidance: Pay particular attention to rules created shortly before a resignation date but configured to activate later, since these are designed to survive normal offboarding review.
steps.outcome: Confirmed delayed-activation rule with destination, activation logic, and creation date documented.
steps.abort: If the rule was approved through a documented exception process, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Cross-reference with HR departure records and check for other pending mechanisms
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR to confirm the resignation/departure date and timeline, and search the mailbox and account for other delayed or conditional exfiltration mechanisms (e.g. additional rules, scheduled tasks, delegate grants).
steps.outcome: Departure timeline confirmed; other pending mechanisms identified or ruled out.
steps.tool: HR coordination / email platform admin console

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before disabling the rule
steps.desc: Preserve the rule configuration and activation logic with a documented chain of custody before disabling it, given the clear indication of premeditated intent and potential legal use.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal, then disable the rule before it activates
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal immediately given the premeditated nature of the delayed rule, and disable it before its activation condition is met.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged; rule disabled before activation.
steps.tool: HR case management / Legal / email admin console

steps.title: Audit the account for all conditional or scheduled exfiltration mechanisms
steps.desc: Thoroughly audit the account for any other conditional, scheduled, or delayed mechanisms that could exfiltrate data after departure.
steps.outcome: Account confirmed clean of pending exfiltration mechanisms.
steps.tool: Email platform admin console / identity management

steps.title: Confirm the rule never activated and no mail was forwarded
steps.desc: Confirm through mail flow logs that the delayed/conditional rule was disabled before its activation condition was met and that no mail was ever forwarded under it.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the rule never activated.
steps.abort: If the rule had already activated before disabling, quantify the mail forwarded during the active window.

steps.title: Complete offboarding with heightened review and apply HR/Legal-directed action
steps.desc: Complete the employee's offboarding with a heightened access-termination review, and implement the personnel/legal action determined by HR/Legal.
steps.outcome: Offboarding completed; personnel action applied.

steps.title: Document the case and add delayed-rule detection to offboarding procedure
steps.desc: Record the incident with HR/Legal and recommend that standard offboarding procedures include a review for delayed/conditional mailbox rules created in the weeks before departure.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; offboarding procedure enhancement tracked.

ITID-34624.def: An insider email forwarding rule exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Email Forwarding Rules, pending further investigation.
ITID-34624.purpose: Intake bucket for insider email forwarding rule exfiltration activity that does not fit the personal-address, competitor-destination, or delayed-activation leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reported forwarding rule with destination/timing not yet determined
Ambiguous forwarding rule behavior spanning multiple sub-patterns
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34621, 34622, or 34623 once investigated
ITID-34624.severity: Medium pending triage; reassess once classified.
ITID-34624.escalation: Escalate to SOC triage for reclassification.
indicators: Generic forwarding rule alert lacking enough detail for specific classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient context available to classify the rule's destination/timing at intake
controls: Mail platform forwarding rule monitoring
ITID-34624.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34624.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Email Forwarding Rules ITID as soon as possible.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34624.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Insider Email Forwarding Rule Exfiltration
playbook.description: For confirmed insider data exfiltration via a mailbox auto-forwarding rule that does not fit a more specific category (personal address, competitor/new employer domain, or delayed-activation rule). Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling.

steps.title: Confirm the forwarding rule and classify its type
steps.desc: Review mailbox configuration/audit logs to confirm the auto-forwarding rule and attempt to classify it against more specific categories (personal address, competitor domain, or delayed activation).
steps.guidance: If the rule matches a more specific category, transition to that playbook.
steps.outcome: Confirmed forwarding rule with destination and scope documented.
steps.abort: If the rule was approved through a documented exception process, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Determine volume and sensitivity of forwarded mail
steps.desc: Review mail flow logs to estimate the volume and sensitivity of email forwarded since the rule was created.
steps.outcome: Volume and sensitivity estimated.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before any account action
steps.desc: Preserve the rule configuration and mail flow logs with a documented chain of custody before disabling the rule or taking account action.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal, then disable the forwarding rule
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal, and once direction is obtained, disable the forwarding rule.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged; forwarding rule disabled.
steps.tool: HR case management / email admin console

steps.title: Audit the mailbox for other exfiltration mechanisms
steps.desc: Check the mailbox for other forwarding rules, delegate access, or connected apps that could provide alternative exfiltration paths.
steps.outcome: Mailbox confirmed clean of other exfiltration mechanisms.

steps.title: Verify the destination address received no further mail after rule removal
steps.desc: Confirm through mail flow logs that no further messages were forwarded to the destination address after the rule was disabled.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no further forwarding occurred after remediation.

steps.title: Apply HR/Legal-directed personnel action
steps.desc: Implement the personnel action determined by HR/Legal based on investigation findings.
steps.outcome: Personnel action applied per HR/Legal direction.

steps.title: Document the case and reclassify if a specific pattern emerges
steps.desc: Record findings with HR/Legal and, if the pattern is later identified as a specific known category, update the incident classification for future reference.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34631.def: An event in which a user's print activity, measured by page/document count of sensitive material, significantly exceeds what their role would normally require, independent of when the printing occurred.
ITID-34631.purpose: Captures an insider printing a large volume of sensitive documents disproportionate to their normal job function, as the volume-based signal for print-channel exfiltration.
scopeIncludes: Print job volume for a sensitive document class significantly above the user's historical baseline or peer group
Bulk printing of an entire sensitive repository or record set in a single session
scopeExcludes: Printing during unusual hours regardless of volume (ITID-34632)
Confirmed physical removal of the printed material from the facility (ITID-34633)
ITID-34631.severity: Medium-High, scaling with document sensitivity and volume.
ITID-34631.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if correlated with other insider risk indicators.
ITID-34631.escalation: Escalate to insider risk program for review; correlate with badge/facility data if physical removal is suspected.
indicators: Print server/MFP audit log showing volume spike for sensitive document types
Print job count for one user significantly exceeding peer baseline
Printing of a full export/report not matching normal task patterns
vectors: Legitimate print access used to output large volumes of sensitive material for physical removal
rootCauses: No volume-based alerting on print jobs for sensitive document classifications
Print auditing not enabled/retained on MFPs
Sensitive documents not classification-tagged for print monitoring
controls: Print auditing/logging on MFPs
Volume-based print alerting for classified content
Watermarking of sensitive print output
ITID-34631.detection: Moderate: dependent on print auditing being enabled and document classification tagging being in place.
ITID-34631.response: Correlate with the user's role and other insider indicators; interview if volume is unexplained by legitimate business need.
metrics: Count of print-volume anomaly alerts per quarter
Percentage of MFPs with audit logging enabled
ITID-34631.notes: Cross-references ITID-14231-14233 for the physical-document-theft ITIDs; this leaf covers the print-volume signal itself, not the physical removal, which is ITID-34633 within this same group.

playbook.name: Response: Bulk Printing of Sensitive Documents Outside Normal Job Function
playbook.description: For suspected insider data exfiltration where an employee bulk-prints sensitive documents unrelated to their normal job function, indicating potential intent to remove data physically. Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling.

steps.title: Review print logs for volume and content unrelated to job function
steps.desc: Review print server/managed print service audit logs for the employee's account for an unusually high volume of print jobs and document titles/content inconsistent with their job function.
steps.outcome: Confirmed bulk printing event with volume and document types identified.
steps.abort: If the printing is consistent with a documented project or role, close as a false positive.
steps.tool: Print server / managed print service audit logs

steps.title: Identify the specific documents printed and their sensitivity
steps.desc: Cross-reference print job metadata with document management/file server records to identify exactly which sensitive documents were printed.
steps.outcome: Specific documents and sensitivity classification identified.
steps.tool: Document management system / file server logs

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before any account action
steps.desc: Preserve print logs and document identification with a documented chain of custody before taking any account or personnel action.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal before further investigative action
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal of the suspected activity and obtain guidance on further monitoring and any access restriction before proceeding.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged with an agreed investigative plan.

steps.title: Restrict print access to sensitive document repositories per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Once authorized, restrict the employee's print permissions or access to the relevant sensitive document repositories.
steps.outcome: Print/access restricted appropriately.

steps.title: Check for prior bulk printing sessions by the same individual
steps.desc: Review print logs over an extended window for prior instances of similar bulk printing by the same individual to establish whether this is a pattern.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the individual's printing pattern established.

steps.title: Apply HR/Legal-directed personnel action
steps.desc: Implement the personnel action determined by HR/Legal based on investigation findings.
steps.outcome: Personnel action applied per HR/Legal direction.

steps.title: Document the case and review print activity monitoring
steps.desc: Record the incident with HR/Legal and evaluate whether print monitoring needs volume/content anomaly alerting for sensitive document repositories.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendations tracked.

ITID-34632.def: An event in which a user prints sensitive documents outside their normal working hours or established printing pattern, where the timing anomaly itself is the primary indicator, regardless of print volume.
ITID-34632.purpose: Captures print activity of sensitive records occurring at unusual times, using timing rather than volume as the differentiating risk signal.
scopeIncludes: Print jobs for sensitive content occurring late at night, on weekends, or during a scheduled leave/holiday
Printing from an unusual location/device outside the user's normal pattern combined with off-hours timing
scopeExcludes: High-volume printing during normal working hours (ITID-34631)
Physical removal of previously printed material (ITID-34633)
ITID-34632.severity: Medium-High: off-hours timing is a strong behavioral anomaly signal even at modest volume.
ITID-34632.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if combined with facility access anomalies.
ITID-34632.escalation: Escalate to insider risk program and correlate with badge access logs to confirm physical presence at time of printing.
indicators: Print server timestamp outside the user's established working-hours baseline
Print job correlated with off-hours badge access to the printer's facility
Printing pattern inconsistent with the user's typical schedule
vectors: Legitimate print access exercised deliberately outside normal hours to reduce observation risk
rootCauses: No time-of-day anomaly alerting on print activity
Facility access not correlated with print server logs
Off-hours facility access not restricted for roles with no legitimate need
controls: Time-of-day print anomaly alerting
Badge-to-print-log correlation
ITID-34632.detection: Moderate: depends on print logging and badge correlation being available and integrated.
ITID-34632.response: Correlate print timing with badge/facility access; investigate if no legitimate business reason for off-hours presence is found.
metrics: Count of off-hours print anomaly alerts per quarter
Percentage correlated with badge access anomalies
ITID-34632.notes: Differentiating axis versus ITID-34631 is timing, not volume; the two signals commonly co-occur but are tracked separately to keep each axis clean.

playbook.name: Response: After-Hours/Unusual-Time Printing of Sensitive Records
playbook.description: For suspected insider data exfiltration where an employee prints sensitive records at unusual times (e.g. late at night, weekends, or immediately before scheduled leave), suggesting an attempt to avoid observation. Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling.

steps.title: Review print logs for after-hours/unusual-time activity
steps.desc: Review print server audit logs for the employee's account for print jobs occurring well outside their normal working hours or established schedule, and identify the documents printed.
steps.guidance: Compare against the employee's typical badge-in/badge-out and system-login patterns to confirm the timing is genuinely anomalous.
steps.outcome: Confirmed after-hours/unusual-time printing event with documents and timing documented.
steps.abort: If the timing is consistent with an approved flexible or shift schedule, close as a false positive.
steps.tool: Print server audit logs / badge access records

steps.title: Correlate with facility access to confirm physical presence
steps.desc: Coordinate with physical security to confirm the employee's badge access to the facility/printer location at the time of printing.
steps.outcome: Physical presence at the time of printing confirmed.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before any account action
steps.desc: Preserve print logs, badge records, and document identification with a documented chain of custody before taking any account or personnel action.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal before further investigative action
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal of the suspected activity and obtain guidance before proceeding further.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged with an agreed investigative plan.

steps.title: Restrict after-hours access or print permissions per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Once authorized, restrict the employee's after-hours facility access or print permissions as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Access restricted appropriately.

steps.title: Check for prior after-hours printing sessions by the same individual
steps.desc: Review print and badge access logs over an extended window for prior instances of similar after-hours printing to establish whether this is a pattern.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the individual's after-hours printing pattern established.
steps.tool: Print server audit logs / badge access records

steps.title: Apply HR/Legal-directed personnel action
steps.desc: Implement the personnel action determined by HR/Legal based on investigation findings.
steps.outcome: Personnel action applied per HR/Legal direction.

steps.title: Document the case and review after-hours facility/print monitoring
steps.desc: Record the incident with HR/Legal and evaluate whether after-hours facility access and print activity need correlated anomaly alerting.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendations tracked.

ITID-34633.def: An event in which printed sensitive documents are confirmed to have left the facility with an employee or contractor, whether observed directly, inferred from badge-out correlation, or discovered after the fact.
ITID-34633.purpose: Captures the confirmed physical removal of printed sensitive material from the facility, the terminal/confirmed-loss stage of the print-channel exfiltration sequence.
scopeIncludes: Physical security or witness observation of printed material being carried out of the facility
Badge-out event correlated with a recent print job for sensitive material and no legitimate business reason to remove it
Printed material discovered missing from a controlled print/output tray
scopeExcludes: Print volume or timing anomalies without confirmed physical removal (ITID-34631, 34632)
Theft of already-filed paper records not tied to a recent print event (ITID-14231-14233, Physical Theft of Confidential Paper Files)
ITID-34633.severity: High-Critical: confirmed physical removal represents realized, not merely suspected, data loss.
ITID-34633.escalation: Escalate immediately to physical security, insider risk leadership, HR, and legal.
indicators: Physical security observation/CCTV of printed material being removed
Badge-out timestamp shortly after a large or sensitive print job with no return of the material
Missing output reported at a controlled/secured printer
vectors: Direct physical carrying of printed output past facility controls with no inspection
rootCauses: No exit inspection/control for printed material at high-security facilities
Print jobs for highly sensitive content not restricted to secure/attended printers
Lack of correlation between print logs and physical exit events
controls: Secure/attended printing for highly sensitive content
Exit inspection controls at high-security facilities
Print-to-badge-exit correlation alerting
ITID-34633.detection: Weak-Moderate: physical removal is inherently hard to detect in real time without dedicated exit controls or CCTV/badge correlation.
ITID-34633.response: Treat as confirmed data loss; initiate investigation, determine document scope, and involve legal/HR/law enforcement as appropriate.
metrics: Count of confirmed physical print-removal incidents per year
Percentage of secure printers with exit control coverage
ITID-34633.notes: This leaf, not ITID-14231-14233, owns the case where removal is directly tied to a recent print event; theft of pre-existing filed paper records without a triggering print event stays under ITID-14231-14233 to avoid duplication.

playbook.name: Response: Printed Documents Removed from Facility (Physical Exfiltration)
playbook.description: For suspected or confirmed insider data exfiltration where printed sensitive documents are physically removed from the facility, confirmed or suspected via security camera observation, exit screening, or witness report. Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling and physical security/facility coordination.

steps.title: Correlate print logs with physical removal evidence
steps.desc: Review print logs to identify what was printed, then coordinate with physical security to review camera footage at exits, security checkpoint records, or witness reports corroborating physical removal of printed material.
steps.outcome: Confirmed or strongly corroborated physical removal event with documents and timing identified.
steps.abort: If no corroborating evidence of removal can be obtained, document as an unconfirmed report based on print activity alone.
steps.tool: Print server logs / facility security camera system / exit checkpoint records

steps.title: Identify the specific documents and their sensitivity
steps.desc: Cross-reference print job metadata with document management records to identify exactly which documents were printed and removed.
steps.outcome: Specific documents and sensitivity classification identified.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before any personnel action
steps.desc: Preserve print logs, camera footage, and any witness statements with a documented chain of custody before taking any personnel action, given potential disciplinary or legal use.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR, Legal, and physical security before further action
steps.desc: Notify HR, Legal, and physical security of the suspected physical removal and coordinate a joint response plan, including whether facility access should be restricted.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal/physical security engaged with an agreed plan.

steps.title: Attempt recovery of the physical documents where authorized
steps.desc: If authorized by HR/Legal, coordinate an attempt to recover the physical documents from the employee.
steps.outcome: Documents recovered where possible.
steps.abort: If recovery is not possible or not authorized, document the attempt and proceed with available evidence.

steps.title: Assess whether secure print release could have prevented removal
steps.desc: Evaluate whether a secure print-release (pull printing) control would have prevented or delayed the physical removal, informing the physical control recommendation.
steps.outcome: Assessment completed and documented for the lessons-learned recommendation.

steps.title: Apply HR/Legal-directed personnel action and tighten physical print/exit controls
steps.desc: Implement the personnel action determined by HR/Legal, and coordinate with physical security on whether print-release controls or exit screening need strengthening.
steps.outcome: Personnel action applied; physical control gap addressed.

steps.title: Document the case and review physical document security controls
steps.desc: Record the incident with HR/Legal and physical security, and evaluate controls such as secure print release, watermarking, or exit screening for sensitive document removal.
steps.outcome: Finding logged; recommendations tracked.

ITID-34634.def: A printout exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Printouts, pending further investigation.
ITID-34634.purpose: Intake bucket for printout exfiltration activity that does not fit the volume, timing, or confirmed-removal leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reported print-related data loss with pattern not yet determined
Ambiguous print activity spanning multiple sub-patterns
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34631, 34632, or 34633 once investigated
ITID-34634.severity: Medium pending triage; reassess once classified.
ITID-34634.escalation: Escalate to insider risk program for reclassification.
indicators: Generic print audit alert lacking enough detail for specific classification
