vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient print logging detail to classify the pattern at intake
controls: Print auditing/logging
ITID-34634.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34634.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Printouts ITID as soon as possible.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34634.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Printout Exfiltration
playbook.description: For suspected or confirmed insider data exfiltration via printed documents that does not fit a more specific category (bulk printing outside job function, after-hours/unusual-time printing, or confirmed physical removal from the facility). Requires HR/Legal-coordinated handling.

steps.title: Review print activity and classify the pattern
steps.desc: Review print server audit logs for the employee's account to confirm the suspicious printing activity and attempt to classify it against more specific categories (bulk/unrelated printing, unusual timing, or confirmed physical removal).
steps.guidance: If the pattern matches a more specific category, transition to that playbook.
steps.outcome: Confirmed printing activity with documents and pattern identified as far as possible.
steps.abort: If the activity is consistent with the employee's job function, close as a false positive.

steps.title: Identify the specific documents and their sensitivity
steps.desc: Cross-reference print job metadata with document management records to identify the documents printed and their sensitivity classification.
steps.outcome: Documents and sensitivity identified.

steps.title: Preserve evidence with documented chain of custody before any account action
steps.desc: Preserve print logs and document identification with a documented chain of custody before taking any account or personnel action.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and chain of custody documented.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal before further investigative action
steps.desc: Notify HR and Legal of the suspected activity and obtain guidance before proceeding.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged with an agreed investigative plan.

steps.title: Restrict print/document access per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Once authorized, restrict the employee's print permissions or access to the relevant sensitive document repositories.
steps.outcome: Access restricted appropriately.

steps.title: Check for prior printing activity by the same individual
steps.desc: Review print logs over an extended window for prior instances of similar suspicious printing by the same individual to establish whether this is a pattern.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the individual's printing pattern established.

steps.title: Apply HR/Legal-directed personnel action
steps.desc: Implement the personnel action determined by HR/Legal based on investigation findings.
steps.outcome: Personnel action applied per HR/Legal direction.

steps.title: Document the case and reclassify if a specific pattern emerges
steps.desc: Record findings with HR/Legal and, if the pattern is later identified as a specific known category, update the incident classification for future reference.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34711.def: An event in which sensitive data is encoded into an image file using least-significant-bit (LSB) or similar pixel-level steganographic techniques, then moved out through a channel where the modified image appears visually and structurally unremarkable.
ITID-34711.purpose: Captures data exfiltrated by hiding it within the least-significant bits of an image file, evading content-inspection tools that only scan for plaintext or known file signatures.
scopeIncludes: Use of a known steganography tool to embed data payloads into image files (PNG, BMP, JPEG)
Detection of LSB-pattern anomalies in outbound image files via specialized tooling
Image files with statistically anomalous pixel-level entropy sent through email/web/upload channels
scopeExcludes: Steganographic hiding in audio/video containers (ITID-34712)
Data hidden in document metadata/whitespace rather than pixel data (ITID-34713)
ITID-34711.severity: High: use of steganography indicates deliberate evasion of content-inspection controls.
ITID-34711.priority: P1 once confirmed; P2 during investigation of a suspected case.
ITID-34711.escalation: Escalate to forensics for payload extraction and to insider risk/threat intel to assess sophistication and likely actor.
indicators: Statistical steganalysis tooling flagging anomalous entropy/LSB patterns in image files
Known steganography tool execution detected on an endpoint (EDR)
Unusually large image files for their visual content relative to expected compression ratios
vectors: LSB embedding tools used to hide payloads in images before upload/email
Custom scripts embedding data in image pixel data
rootCauses: Content-inspection/DLP tools scan for text patterns only, not image steganalysis
No endpoint alerting on known steganography tool binaries
controls: Steganalysis-capable DLP/content inspection
EDR alerting on known steganography tool execution
ITID-34711.detection: Weak: standard DLP lacks steganalysis capability; detection requires specialized tooling and is inherently low-coverage.
ITID-34711.response: Forensically extract and analyze the suspected payload; treat confirmed cases as sophisticated, deliberate exfiltration.
metrics: Count of confirmed steganographic exfiltration cases per year
Steganalysis tool coverage percentage of outbound image traffic
ITID-34711.notes: Scoped to image-carrier steganography specifically; audio/video and metadata/whitespace carriers are tracked as sibling leaves to keep the carrier-type axis clean.

playbook.name: Response: Data Hidden in Image File (LSB Steganography)
playbook.description: For data suspected or confirmed to have been exfiltrated by hiding it within an image file using least-significant-bit or similar steganographic encoding.

steps.title: Be aware detection here is typically retrospective
steps.desc: Recognize that steganographic exfiltration is rarely caught proactively — it is usually found during a broader forensic investigation (e.g. after a related incident led to reviewing this user's/host's outbound files), not by routine monitoring.
steps.guidance: Set expectations with stakeholders accordingly: absence of an active alert does not mean this technique isn't in use elsewhere.
steps.outcome: Investigation scoped appropriately around a forensic/retrospective posture.

steps.title: Forensically analyze the suspect image(s) for hidden payloads
steps.desc: Run steganalysis tooling against the identified image file(s) to confirm the presence of an embedded payload and, where possible, extract and identify its contents.
steps.guidance: Compare file size/statistical properties against a known-clean baseline image where available.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence and content of the hidden payload, or ruled out as a false positive.
steps.abort: If steganalysis is inconclusive, treat the file as suspect pending deeper forensic lab analysis.
steps.tool: Steganalysis tooling (e.g. StegExpose, forensic imaging suite)

steps.title: Identify the exfiltration vector used to move the image out
steps.desc: Determine how the image left the environment — email attachment, cloud upload, social media post, USB transfer — using DLP/proxy/mail logs.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration vector and destination identified.

steps.title: Block the identified exfiltration vector/destination
steps.desc: Block the destination (site, account, address) used to move the image, and suspend the associated user/device account pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Further transfer via this vector prevented.

steps.title: Preserve the device and account for forensic review
steps.desc: Image the source device/account to identify the tool used to create the steganographic payload and any other affected files.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for full scope determination.

steps.title: Remove the steganography tool and review the device for other hidden payloads
steps.desc: Identify and remove any steganography tooling found on the device, and scan other outbound image files for similar hidden content.
steps.outcome: Tool removed and no other hidden payloads remain undetected.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal (if insider-driven) or standard IR escalation (if external) to assess impact and next steps.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document the case and review DLP/forensic coverage for steganography
steps.desc: Record findings and evaluate whether periodic proactive steganalysis sampling of outbound images is warranted, acknowledging full prevention is impractical.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and monitoring posture reviewed.

ITID-34712.def: An event in which sensitive data is encoded into an audio or video file's data stream using steganographic techniques, then exfiltrated through a channel where the modified media file appears to play/render normally.
ITID-34712.purpose: Captures data exfiltrated by hiding it within audio or video file streams, a carrier type offering higher payload capacity than images and different detection challenges.
scopeIncludes: Data embedded in audio waveform data (echo hiding, spread spectrum, LSB audio encoding)
Data embedded in video frame data or container metadata streams
Detection of anomalous audio/video file size or encoding artifacts inconsistent with normal compression
scopeExcludes: Image-carrier steganography (ITID-34711)
Document metadata/whitespace hiding (ITID-34713)
ITID-34712.severity: High: audio/video carriers can hold substantially larger payloads than images, raising potential data loss volume.
ITID-34712.priority: P1 once confirmed; P2 during investigation of a suspected case.
ITID-34712.escalation: Escalate to forensics for payload extraction; assess data volume given the higher carrier capacity of media files.
indicators: Steganalysis tooling flagging anomalous audio/video encoding artifacts
Media files with file size inconsistent with their runtime/quality
Known audio/video steganography tool execution detected via EDR
vectors: Audio steganography tools embedding payloads in waveform data before upload
Video container manipulation to embed data in unused stream channels
rootCauses: DLP/content inspection has no media steganalysis capability
No endpoint alerting on known media steganography tool binaries
Large media file uploads not scrutinized due to expected legitimate use
controls: Media steganalysis-capable content inspection
EDR alerting on known media steganography tools
ITID-34712.detection: Weak: media steganalysis is specialized and rarely deployed at scale; this remains a significant blind spot.
ITID-34712.response: Forensically extract and analyze the suspected payload; assess volume given the higher capacity of media carriers.
metrics: Count of confirmed audio/video steganographic exfiltration cases per year
ITID-34712.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34711 by carrier medium (audio/video vs. static image), which affects both payload capacity and detection tooling requirements.

playbook.name: Response: Data Hidden in Audio/Video File
playbook.description: For data suspected or confirmed to have been exfiltrated by embedding it within an audio or video file's data stream.

steps.title: Be aware detection here is typically retrospective
steps.desc: Recognize this technique is usually found during a broader forensic investigation rather than proactive monitoring, given the difficulty of detecting embedded payloads in media files at scale.
steps.outcome: Investigation scoped appropriately around a forensic/retrospective posture.

steps.title: Forensically analyze the suspect media file(s) for hidden payloads
steps.desc: Run audio/video steganalysis tooling against the identified file(s), checking for anomalous file size, unusual codec artifacts, or embedded data streams.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence and content of the hidden payload, or ruled out as a false positive.
steps.abort: If inconclusive, treat as suspect pending deeper forensic lab analysis.

steps.title: Identify the exfiltration vector used to move the file out
steps.desc: Determine how the media file left the environment using DLP/proxy/mail/cloud logs.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration vector and destination identified.

steps.title: Block the identified exfiltration vector/destination
steps.desc: Block the destination used to move the file, and suspend the associated user/device account pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Further transfer via this vector prevented.

steps.title: Preserve the device and account for forensic review
steps.desc: Image the source device/account to identify the tool used and any other affected files.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for full scope determination.

steps.title: Remove the steganography/encoding tool and review for other hidden payloads
steps.desc: Identify and remove any tooling found on the device, and scan other outbound media files for similar hidden content.
steps.outcome: Tool removed and no other hidden payloads remain undetected.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal (if insider-driven) or standard IR escalation (if external) to assess impact and next steps.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document the case and review detection posture for media-based covert channels
steps.desc: Record findings and evaluate whether periodic sampling of outbound media files is warranted, acknowledging full prevention is impractical.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and monitoring posture reviewed.

ITID-34713.def: An event in which sensitive data is encoded into a document's metadata fields (author, comments, custom properties) or hidden via whitespace/formatting-based encoding (e.g., trailing spaces, font-color-matched text), then exfiltrated as an apparently normal business document.
ITID-34713.purpose: Captures data exfiltrated by embedding it in document metadata fields or invisible whitespace patterns, a carrier type that moves easily through routine business document exchange.
scopeIncludes: Data encoded in Office/PDF document custom metadata properties or comment fields
Whitespace-pattern or invisible-text (white-on-white) encoding within a document body
Documents with metadata field content inconsistent with the document's stated authorship/purpose
scopeExcludes: Image-carrier steganography (ITID-34711)
Audio/video-carrier steganography (ITID-34712)
ITID-34713.severity: Medium-High: lower payload capacity than media carriers but very high plausibility as routine business traffic.
ITID-34713.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if confirmed as a deliberate, repeated channel.
ITID-34713.escalation: Escalate to forensics for metadata/whitespace extraction and analysis once flagged.
indicators: Document metadata scanning revealing anomalous or oversized custom property fields
Whitespace/formatting anomaly detection flagging unusual character density
Documents sent externally with metadata inconsistent with normal authoring patterns
vectors: Manual or scripted embedding of data into document metadata fields before sending externally
Whitespace encoding tools used to hide text within a document body
rootCauses: DLP/content inspection does not scan document metadata fields
No document sanitization applied before external send removing metadata/hidden content
Lack of awareness that metadata fields can carry arbitrary data
controls: Document metadata scanning/sanitization on external send
DLP inspection extended to metadata fields
ITID-34713.detection: Moderate: metadata scanning is more tractable than pixel/waveform steganalysis but still rarely deployed comprehensively.
ITID-34713.response: Extract and analyze metadata/hidden content once flagged; sanitize outbound document metadata as a standing control.
metrics: Count of confirmed metadata/whitespace exfiltration cases per year
Percentage of outbound documents passing through metadata sanitization
ITID-34713.notes: Differentiated from the image and audio/video leaves by carrier type (document metadata/whitespace) and by its higher plausibility as routine business correspondence.

playbook.name: Response: Data Hidden in Document Metadata/Whitespace
playbook.description: For data suspected or confirmed to have been exfiltrated by hiding it within a document's metadata fields, hidden text, or whitespace patterns.

steps.title: Be aware detection here is typically retrospective
steps.desc: Recognize this technique is usually found during a broader forensic investigation rather than proactive monitoring, as metadata/whitespace encoding is not typically inspected by standard DLP content scanning.
steps.outcome: Investigation scoped appropriately around a forensic/retrospective posture.

steps.title: Forensically inspect the suspect document(s) for hidden content
steps.desc: Examine document metadata fields (custom properties, revision history, comments), hidden text/white-on-white formatting, and whitespace/character-spacing patterns for encoded data.
steps.guidance: Compare against a known-clean template of the same document type where available.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence and content of the hidden data, or ruled out as a false positive.
steps.abort: If inconclusive, treat as suspect pending deeper forensic lab analysis.

steps.title: Identify the exfiltration vector used to move the document out
steps.desc: Determine how the document left the environment using DLP/proxy/mail/cloud logs.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration vector and destination identified.

steps.title: Block the identified exfiltration vector/destination
steps.desc: Block the destination used to move the document, and suspend the associated user/device account pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Further transfer via this vector prevented.

steps.title: Preserve the device and account for forensic review
steps.desc: Image the source device/account to identify how the document was created and any other affected files.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for full scope determination.

steps.title: Review for other documents using the same hiding technique
steps.desc: Scan other outbound documents from the same source for similar metadata/whitespace encoding patterns.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no other hidden payloads remain undetected.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal (if insider-driven) or standard IR escalation (if external) to assess impact and next steps.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document the case and review DLP content-inspection depth
steps.desc: Record findings and evaluate whether DLP tooling should be extended to inspect document metadata/hidden-text fields, acknowledging full prevention is impractical.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and monitoring posture reviewed.

ITID-34714.def: A steganographic exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Steganography, pending further investigation or carrier identification.
ITID-34714.purpose: Intake bucket for steganographic exfiltration activity that does not fit the image, audio/video, or document-metadata carrier leaves.
scopeIncludes: Suspected steganographic exfiltration with carrier type not yet identified
Novel or unusual carrier formats not covered by the named sibling leaves
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34711, 34712, or 34713 once investigated
ITID-34714.severity: Medium-High pending triage; reassess once carrier and payload are identified.
ITID-34714.escalation: Escalate to forensics for carrier identification and reclassification.
indicators: Generic steganalysis alert lacking enough detail to identify carrier type
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient forensic detail to classify the carrier/technique at intake
controls: General steganalysis monitoring
ITID-34714.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34714.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Steganography ITID as soon as the carrier is identified.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34714.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Steganographic Exfiltration
playbook.description: For steganography-based exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly image, audio/video, or document-metadata based) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear.

steps.title: Be aware detection here is typically retrospective
steps.desc: Recognize steganographic exfiltration is rarely caught proactively and is usually found during a broader forensic investigation.
steps.outcome: Investigation scoped appropriately around a forensic/retrospective posture.

steps.title: Forensically analyze the suspect file(s) and identify the carrier medium
steps.desc: Determine the carrier file type (image, audio/video, document) and run the appropriate steganalysis technique to confirm and extract the hidden payload.
steps.outcome: Carrier type identified and payload confirmed or ruled out.
steps.abort: If confirmed as a specific carrier type, redirect to the corresponding specific playbook for subsequent steps.

steps.title: Identify the exfiltration vector used to move the file out
steps.desc: Determine how the file left the environment using DLP/proxy/mail/cloud logs.
steps.outcome: Exfiltration vector and destination identified.

steps.title: Block the identified exfiltration vector/destination
steps.desc: Block the destination used to move the file, and suspend the associated user/device account pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Further transfer via this vector prevented.

steps.title: Preserve the device and account for forensic review
steps.desc: Image the source device/account to identify the tool used and any other affected files.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved for full scope determination.

steps.title: Remove the tooling and review for other hidden payloads
steps.desc: Identify and remove any steganography tooling found on the device, and scan other outbound files for similar hidden content.
steps.outcome: Tool removed and no other hidden payloads remain undetected.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal (if insider-driven) or standard IR escalation (if external) to assess impact and next steps.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document and reclassify for future reference
steps.desc: Record the case, and note the specific carrier/technique used for future classification consistency.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34721.def: An event in which sensitive data is encoded (via text pattern, hashtag sequence, or embedded image steganography) into a publicly posted social media post or caption, allowing an external party to retrieve it without any direct connection to the victim organization's network.
ITID-34721.purpose: Captures data encoded into a public-facing social media post or image caption, using the platform's public content as a covert, asynchronous exfiltration channel.
scopeIncludes: Text or hashtag-pattern encoding of data within a public post/caption
Steganographically embedded data within an image attached to a public post
Sequential/coded public posts designed to be reassembled by a receiving party
scopeExcludes: Data sent via a private direct message to an attacker-controlled account (ITID-34722)
Data staged in a draft/scheduled post that is never published (ITID-34723)
ITID-34721.severity: High: public posting is effectively an uncontained, permanent disclosure once published.
ITID-34721.escalation: Escalate immediately for takedown coordination with the platform and legal/comms review of public exposure.
indicators: Social media monitoring flagging posts from a corporate-associated account with anomalous encoded-looking content
Employee account posting content inconsistent with their normal social media behavior
Image posts with steganalysis-flagged embedded data
vectors: Legitimate personal or corporate social media account used to publish covertly encoded data
Public posting used specifically because it requires no direct network connection to the victim organization
rootCauses: No monitoring of employee/corporate social media accounts for anomalous posting behavior
DLP has no visibility into social media platform content
controls: Social media monitoring for corporate-associated accounts
Platform takedown coordination process
ITID-34721.detection: Weak: public social media content is largely outside standard DLP/network monitoring visibility.
ITID-34721.response: Coordinate immediate takedown with the platform, assess what was disclosed, and treat as public data exposure.
metrics: Count of confirmed social media covert-channel posts per year
Mean time-to-takedown once identified
ITID-34721.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34722/34723 by the public, permanently-disclosed nature of the channel versus private messaging or an unpublished draft.

playbook.name: Response: Data Encoded in Social Media Post/Image Caption
playbook.description: For data suspected or confirmed to have been exfiltrated by encoding it within a public or semi-public social media post or image caption.

steps.title: Be aware detection here is typically retrospective
steps.desc: Recognize this technique is usually found during a broader investigation (e.g. an insider or account-monitoring case) rather than proactive social-media DLP scanning, since encoded content in a public post rarely triggers automated alerting.
steps.outcome: Investigation scoped appropriately around a forensic/retrospective posture.

steps.title: Identify and decode the suspect post(s)
steps.desc: Review the identified social media account's posting history for encoded content (e.g. unusual character patterns, encoded text disguised as a caption, or base64-like strings) and attempt to decode.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence and content of the encoded data, or ruled out as a false positive.
steps.abort: If inconclusive, preserve the post for deeper analysis before concluding.

steps.title: Identify the account owner and device used to post
steps.desc: Determine whether this was posted from a corporate device/network or a personal device, and identify the individual involved.
steps.outcome: Source device and individual identified.

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal and preserve the post as evidence
steps.desc: Given the personnel implications, loop in HR/Legal before further action, and preserve (screenshot/archive) the post before it can be deleted.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and HR/Legal directing next steps.

steps.title: Restrict device/network access as directed
steps.desc: Restrict the individual's access to corporate systems/network per HR/Legal direction.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration via this channel prevented.

steps.title: Assess feasibility of post takedown
steps.desc: Determine whether the post can be removed via the platform's reporting/legal-takedown process.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether takedown is possible.
steps.abort: If the platform is uncooperative or the post has already spread, note in the impact assessment and proceed to Legal for further options.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal to assess impact and appropriate response.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document the case and review social-media monitoring posture
steps.desc: Record findings and evaluate whether OSINT/brand-monitoring coverage should be extended, acknowledging full prevention is impractical.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and monitoring posture reviewed.

ITID-34722.def: An event in which a user sends sensitive data through a social media platform's direct/private messaging feature to an account outside the organization, using the platform's messaging infrastructure rather than public posting or email/IM.
ITID-34722.purpose: Captures data sent via a private direct message on a social media platform to an attacker-controlled or unauthorized external account.
scopeIncludes: Direct message containing sensitive data/attachments sent to an external or unrecognized social media account
Sustained private-message exchange transferring data incrementally over time
scopeExcludes: Public post/caption-based encoding (ITID-34721)
Data staged in an unpublished draft/scheduled post (ITID-34723)
Messaging via a dedicated instant messaging app such as WhatsApp/Signal/Telegram (ITID-34731, Instant Messaging Apps)
ITID-34722.severity: High: private messaging is a direct, targeted transfer to a specific external party.
ITID-34722.escalation: Escalate immediately; identify the receiving account and attempt platform cooperation for content preservation/takedown.
indicators: Endpoint/browser activity showing large attachments sent via a social media platform's messaging feature
CASB/network alert on social media platform data transfer
Employee account messaging an external/unrecognized contact with sensitive file attachments
vectors: Native platform direct-messaging feature used to send files/data directly to an external account
rootCauses: DLP has no content inspection coverage for social media messaging traffic
Social media platforms not blocked/restricted on managed endpoints where not business-required
controls: CASB/DLP coverage extended to social media messaging
Social media platform access restriction policy for non-business roles
ITID-34722.detection: Weak-Moderate: depends on whether CASB/network DLP has visibility into the specific platform's messaging traffic.
ITID-34722.response: Identify the receiving account, preserve evidence, and pursue platform cooperation for takedown/content recovery.
metrics: Count of confirmed social media DM exfiltration cases per year
ITID-34722.notes: Distinguished from ITID-34731 (Instant Messaging Apps) by platform category: this leaf is scoped to social media platforms' native messaging feature specifically.

playbook.name: Response: Data Exfiltrated via Direct Message to Attacker-Controlled Account
playbook.description: For data suspected or confirmed to have been exfiltrated by sending it via direct/private message on a social media platform to an attacker-controlled or unauthorized account.

steps.title: Be aware detection here is typically retrospective
steps.desc: Recognize that private direct-message content is generally not visible to corporate monitoring tools, so this is usually discovered during a broader investigation (device forensics, insider tip, or platform cooperation) rather than proactive DLP alerting.
steps.outcome: Investigation scoped appropriately around a forensic/retrospective posture.

steps.title: Establish evidence of the DM exchange and its content
steps.desc: Where possible, obtain evidence of the DM exchange via device forensics (app cache/local storage), the sender's own account history, or a legal request to the platform.
steps.outcome: Confirmed content and scope of data sent via DM.
steps.abort: If the platform does not cooperate and no local evidence exists, document the limitation and proceed on a worst-case assumption with Legal.

steps.title: Identify the recipient account and any known affiliation
steps.desc: Investigate the recipient account for ties to a known threat actor, competitor, or other adversarial affiliation.
steps.outcome: Recipient context established to inform severity and response.

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal and restrict device/network access as directed
steps.desc: Loop in HR/Legal given the personnel and platform-legal implications, and restrict the individual's access per their direction.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and access restricted appropriately.

steps.title: Preserve the device for forensic imaging
steps.desc: Image the device used to send the DM before any account action that could result in evidence loss.
steps.outcome: Forensically sound evidence preserved.

steps.title: Assess feasibility of platform-level takedown or account reporting
steps.desc: Determine whether the recipient account can be reported/actioned via the platform's abuse process or a legal request.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether takedown/reporting is possible.
steps.abort: If the platform is uncooperative, note in the impact assessment and proceed to Legal for further options.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal to assess impact and appropriate response.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document the case and review social-media/messaging monitoring posture
steps.desc: Record findings and evaluate whether acceptable-use policy or device management controls should be tightened, acknowledging full prevention of private DM content is impractical.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and policy reviewed.

ITID-34723.def: An event in which a user encodes sensitive data into a social media draft or scheduled post and leaves it unpublished, using the platform account itself as a shared storage location (dead drop) accessible to a colluding party with access to the same account credentials.
ITID-34723.purpose: Captures data staged in a social media draft or scheduled post that is deliberately never published, using the platform's storage rather than its broadcast function as a covert dead-drop.
scopeIncludes: Data encoded into an unpublished draft post accessible to anyone with the account credentials
Scheduled post created and then cancelled/left pending, used as a retrievable storage location
Shared/compromised account credentials used by a second party to retrieve draft content
scopeExcludes: Data published in a live public post (ITID-34721)
Data sent via direct message (ITID-34722)
ITID-34723.severity: High: this is a deliberate dead-drop technique indicating premeditated, collusive exfiltration.
ITID-34723.escalation: Escalate immediately to insider risk and legal given the premeditated, likely collusive nature of this technique.
indicators: Draft/scheduled post content discovered during account forensic review containing encoded data
Shared account credential use pattern (multiple disparate access locations/devices)
Account activity showing draft creation with no corresponding publish event
vectors: Native draft/scheduling feature used as a covert shared storage location between colluding parties
rootCauses: No monitoring/forensic review of draft or scheduled content on corporate-associated social accounts
Shared account credential practices not restricted or monitored
controls: Forensic review of draft/scheduled content on corporate-associated accounts
Shared credential monitoring
ITID-34723.detection: Weak: draft content is generally invisible to standard monitoring and only found via targeted forensic review.
ITID-34723.response: Preserve draft content forensically, identify all parties with access to the account, and treat as likely collusive exfiltration.
metrics: Count of confirmed dead-drop draft exfiltration cases per year
ITID-34723.notes: This is the dead-drop/storage-based variant of social media covert channel use, distinct from the broadcast (ITID-34721) and direct-transfer (ITID-34722) variants.

playbook.name: Response: Data Exfiltrated via Social Media Draft/Scheduled Post Never Published
playbook.description: For data suspected or confirmed to have been staged for exfiltration in a social media draft or scheduled post that was never actually published, evading normal social-media monitoring.

steps.title: Check drafts and scheduled-post queues specifically
steps.desc: Since the content was never published, standard social-media monitoring/OSINT tools will not see it — specifically inspect the account's drafts and scheduled-post queue (via the platform's own interface, an authorized business tool, or device forensics) for staged content.
steps.guidance: This is the key identification step for this technique, analogous to checking a mailbox's Drafts folder in email-based exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence/absence of staged draft or scheduled content and what data it contains.

steps.title: Determine who has access to create/view the draft
steps.desc: Identify who authored the draft and whether a second party (e.g. a linked account or shared social media management tool) can view drafts without the content ever being published.
steps.outcome: Access pattern and likely second-party access point identified.
steps.tool: Social media management platform audit logs

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal and restrict account access as directed
steps.desc: Loop in HR/Legal given the personnel implications, and restrict the individual's access per their direction.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and access restricted appropriately.

steps.title: Preserve and remove the draft content
steps.desc: Export/screenshot the draft for evidence before removing it, and audit for shared access that enabled the second party to view it.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and exfiltration channel closed.

steps.title: Review and restrict shared social media account/tool access
steps.desc: Audit and tighten permissions on any shared social media management tool or account to prevent unauthorized draft visibility.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized access paths closed.

steps.title: Scope data exposure from staged draft content
steps.desc: Assess what sensitive data was staged to determine breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Impact scoped.

steps.title: Determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal on appropriate disciplinary or legal response based on findings.
steps.outcome: Resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document the case and add draft/scheduled-post checks to monitoring scope
steps.desc: Record the incident and evaluate adding periodic draft/scheduled-content review to social-media monitoring, since this vector is otherwise invisible to standard controls.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and monitoring gap addressed.

ITID-34724.def: A social media covert channel exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Social Media Channels, pending further investigation.
ITID-34724.purpose: Intake bucket for social media covert channel exfiltration activity that does not fit the public-post, direct-message, or draft/dead-drop leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reported social media-related data loss with mechanism not yet determined
Ambiguous social media platform misuse spanning multiple sub-patterns
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34721, 34722, or 34723 once investigated
ITID-34724.severity: Medium-High pending triage; reassess once classified.
ITID-34724.escalation: Escalate to social media/insider risk triage for reclassification.
indicators: Generic social media monitoring alert lacking enough detail for specific classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient context available to classify the social media exfiltration mechanism at intake
controls: Social media monitoring
ITID-34724.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34724.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Social Media Channels ITID as soon as possible.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34724.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Social Media Covert Channel Exfiltration
playbook.description: For social-media-based covert-channel exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly encoded posts, DM exfiltration, or draft/scheduled-post staging) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear.

steps.title: Be aware detection here is typically retrospective
steps.desc: Recognize that social media covert-channel exfiltration is usually found during a broader investigation rather than proactive monitoring.
steps.outcome: Investigation scoped appropriately around a forensic/retrospective posture.

steps.title: Characterize the specific technique and data involved
steps.desc: Determine whether the activity matches encoded public posts, direct messages, or draft/scheduled posts, and establish the scope of data involved.
steps.outcome: Activity characterized well enough to redirect to a specific playbook or proceed here.

steps.title: Identify the account owner and device used
steps.desc: Determine whether this involved a corporate device/network or a personal device, and identify the individual involved.
steps.outcome: Source device and individual identified.

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal and preserve evidence
steps.desc: Loop in HR/Legal given the personnel implications, and preserve relevant evidence before it can be deleted.
steps.outcome: Evidence preserved and HR/Legal directing next steps.

steps.title: Restrict access as directed
steps.desc: Restrict the individual's access to corporate systems/network per HR/Legal direction.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration via this channel prevented.

steps.title: Address the specific vector identified
steps.desc: Apply the appropriate remediation once the specific technique is confirmed (takedown request, access revocation, tool removal).
steps.outcome: Exfiltration channel closed.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal to assess impact and appropriate response.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document and reclassify for future reference
steps.desc: Record the case, and note the specific technique used for future classification consistency.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34731.def: An event in which a user sends sensitive organizational data through a third-party instant messaging application (WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram, or similar) installed on a corporate or BYOD device, where end-to-end encryption prevents network-layer content inspection.
ITID-34731.purpose: Captures data sent via a personal, often end-to-end-encrypted messaging app such as WhatsApp, Signal, or Telegram to an external contact, using an app-based channel that evades standard network content inspection.
scopeIncludes: Sensitive file/text sent via WhatsApp/Signal/Telegram to a personal or external contact
Installation and use of an unsanctioned messaging app on a managed device for business data transfer
Encrypted messaging app traffic to a known external number/contact
scopeExcludes: Native platform iMessage/RCS transfer to a personal device (ITID-34732)
Use of the app's ephemeral/disappearing-message feature specifically to evade retention (ITID-34733)
ITID-34731.severity: High: end-to-end encryption means content is typically unrecoverable once sent.
ITID-34731.priority: P1 once confirmed; P2 during investigation of suspected use.
ITID-34731.escalation: Escalate immediately; because content is encrypted in transit, response focuses on endpoint/device forensics rather than network interception.
indicators: EDR/MDM detection of app installation and large attachment send events
Network metadata showing volume/timing of encrypted messaging traffic to an external endpoint, without content visibility
Endpoint file-access-then-share correlation with the messaging app
vectors: Personal messaging app installed on a managed or BYOD device used to transfer sensitive files
Screenshots or photos of sensitive on-screen data sent via the app
rootCauses: Unsanctioned messaging apps not restricted via MDM/application allowlisting
No DLP visibility into encrypted app-layer traffic
BYOD policy permits unmanaged personal app installation with corporate data access
controls: MDM application allowlisting restricting unsanctioned messaging apps
Endpoint DLP with file-access-to-share correlation
ITID-34731.detection: Weak: end-to-end encryption blinds network content inspection; detection relies on endpoint telemetry and metadata patterns only.
ITID-34731.response: Focus forensics on the endpoint (file access logs, share events) since network content is unrecoverable; interview the user and assess scope from endpoint evidence.
metrics: Count of confirmed messaging-app exfiltration cases per year
Percentage of managed devices with app allowlisting enforced
ITID-34731.notes: Scoped to third-party cross-platform messaging apps; native OS messaging (iMessage/RCS) is tracked separately under ITID-34732 due to differing platform telemetry and control options.

playbook.name: Response: Data Sent via Personal WhatsApp/Signal/Telegram Message
playbook.description: For data suspected or confirmed to have been exfiltrated by sending it via a personal instant messaging app (WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram) to an outside recipient.

steps.title: Be aware detection here is typically retrospective
steps.desc: Recognize that end-to-end encrypted messaging content is generally invisible to network-level monitoring, so this is usually discovered via device forensics, an insider tip, or a related investigation rather than proactive DLP alerting.
steps.outcome: Investigation scoped appropriately around a forensic/retrospective posture.

steps.title: Establish evidence of the message exchange via device forensics
steps.desc: Image the device (if corporate-owned or subject to a lawful/consented review) to recover local app data/cache showing the message content, attachments sent, and recipient.
steps.guidance: For personal devices, coordinate with HR/Legal on what access/consent is required before forensic review.
steps.outcome: Confirmed content and scope of data sent via the app, or confirmed access is not legally available.
steps.abort: If forensic access to the device is not legally available, document the limitation and proceed on available circumstantial evidence with Legal.

steps.title: Identify the recipient and any known affiliation
steps.desc: Investigate the recipient (phone number/account) for ties to a competitor, known threat actor, or other adversarial affiliation.
steps.outcome: Recipient context established to inform severity and response.

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal before further action
steps.desc: Loop in HR/Legal given the personnel and device-access implications.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and directing next steps.

steps.title: Restrict access per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Restrict the individual's access to corporate systems/network per HR/Legal direction.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration via this channel prevented.

steps.title: Review mobile device management policy for messaging app controls
steps.desc: Assess whether MDM/MAM policy should restrict installation or corporate-data sharing with personal messaging apps on managed devices.
steps.outcome: Policy gap identified and remediation tracked.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal to assess impact and appropriate response.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document the case and review acceptable-use/MDM policy
steps.desc: Record findings and evaluate whether policy or technical controls on personal messaging apps should be tightened, acknowledging encrypted content is largely unmonitorable.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and policy reviewed.

ITID-34732.def: An event in which a user transfers sensitive data using the device's native messaging protocol (Apple iMessage or Android RCS) to a personal device, relying on OS-level messaging infrastructure that is typically outside the visibility of enterprise mobile DLP tools.
ITID-34732.purpose: Captures data sent via native platform messaging (iMessage/RCS) from a managed device to a personal device, exploiting built-in OS messaging that often bypasses third-party DLP entirely.
scopeIncludes: iMessage/RCS text or attachment containing sensitive data sent to a personal number/device
Native messaging used specifically because it is pre-installed and not subject to app-allowlisting controls
scopeExcludes: Third-party app messaging such as WhatsApp/Signal/Telegram (ITID-34731)
Ephemeral/disappearing-message feature use for retention evasion (ITID-34733)
ITID-34732.severity: High: native messaging is typically the least-monitored channel on managed mobile devices.
ITID-34732.priority: P1 once confirmed; P2 during investigation of suspected use.
ITID-34732.escalation: Escalate immediately; involve mobile device management team since native messaging often falls outside standard MDM content controls.
indicators: MDM message-count/attachment-size metadata anomaly (where available)
Endpoint file-access event immediately followed by native messaging app foreground activity
Device backup/forensic extraction revealing sensitive content in message history
vectors: Native OS messaging used to send screenshots or files of sensitive data to a personal device, since it cannot be blocked without disabling core device functionality
rootCauses: Native messaging cannot typically be disabled without breaking core device functionality, leaving it as a persistent blind spot
No mobile DLP solution with native-messaging-aware monitoring deployed
controls: Mobile DLP with native messaging awareness (where technically feasible)
Corporate data containerization (MAM) limiting native app access to managed content
ITID-34732.detection: Weak: native messaging is one of the least-visible corporate mobile channels; detection largely depends on device forensic extraction after the fact.
ITID-34732.response: Pursue device forensic extraction/backup review where legally permitted; treat this as a known, hard-to-monitor gap requiring compensating controls (containerization).
metrics: Count of confirmed native-messaging exfiltration cases per year
Percentage of mobile fleet under MAM containerization
ITID-34732.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34731 by using built-in OS messaging rather than an installable third-party app, which changes both the control surface (MAM/containerization vs. allowlisting) and detection approach.

playbook.name: Response: Data Sent via iMessage/RCS to Personal Device
playbook.description: For data suspected or confirmed to have been exfiltrated by sending it via iMessage or RCS from a corporate device to a personal device.

steps.title: Be aware detection here is typically retrospective
steps.desc: Recognize that iMessage/RCS content is generally invisible to network-level monitoring, so this is usually discovered via device forensics, MDM message-backup review, or a related investigation.
steps.outcome: Investigation scoped appropriately around a forensic/retrospective posture.

steps.title: Establish evidence via device/MDM backup review
steps.desc: Where the device is corporate-managed, review MDM-enforced backups or perform device forensics to recover the message content, attachments, and recipient.
steps.outcome: Confirmed content and scope of data sent, or confirmed access is not available.
steps.abort: If the device is personal (BYOD) and not subject to review, document the limitation and proceed on available circumstantial evidence with Legal.

steps.title: Identify the recipient device/number and its owner
steps.desc: Determine who owns the recipient device/number and their relationship to the sender.
steps.outcome: Recipient context established.

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal before further action
steps.desc: Loop in HR/Legal given the personnel and device-access implications.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and directing next steps.

steps.title: Restrict access per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Restrict the individual's access to corporate systems/network per HR/Legal direction.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration via this channel prevented.

steps.title: Review MDM policy for messaging and data-sharing restrictions
steps.desc: Assess whether MDM policy should restrict cross-device messaging of corporate data (e.g. via containerization/MAM controls).
steps.outcome: Policy gap identified and remediation tracked.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal to assess impact and appropriate response.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document the case and review device-management policy
steps.desc: Record findings and evaluate whether MDM/MAM containerization should be extended, acknowledging native messaging content is largely unmonitorable.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and policy reviewed.

ITID-34733.def: An event in which a user configures or uses a messaging app's disappearing/self-destructing message feature when transferring sensitive data, indicating deliberate intent to prevent later forensic recovery or retention-policy capture, regardless of the specific platform.
ITID-34733.purpose: Captures deliberate use of an ephemeral/disappearing-message feature specifically to defeat retention and DLP review, independent of which underlying app is used.
scopeIncludes: Enabling disappearing/timed-deletion message settings before sending sensitive content
Use of screenshot-blocking or view-once media features alongside sensitive data transfer
Pattern of a user consistently using ephemeral mode only for specific, sensitive conversations
scopeExcludes: Standard (non-ephemeral) use of WhatsApp/Signal/Telegram (ITID-34731)
Standard (non-ephemeral) use of iMessage/RCS (ITID-34732)
ITID-34733.severity: High-Critical: deliberate anti-forensic configuration is a strong indicator of premeditated, knowing exfiltration.
ITID-34733.escalation: Escalate immediately to insider risk and legal; the anti-forensic intent itself elevates this beyond standard messaging-app exfiltration.
indicators: MDM/app configuration data showing disappearing-message mode enabled
User behavior pattern showing selective use of ephemeral mode correlated with access to sensitive data
Witness or corroborating evidence of ephemeral-mode conversations involving sensitive topics
vectors: Deliberate activation of an app's ephemeral messaging feature specifically to avoid leaving a retrievable record
rootCauses: No policy/technical control preventing ephemeral messaging mode on devices with access to sensitive data
Retention/DLP policies assume standard message persistence and do not account for ephemeral features
controls: MDM policy restricting or flagging ephemeral messaging mode on managed devices
Insider risk behavioral monitoring for anti-forensic feature use
ITID-34733.detection: Weak: by design, ephemeral messaging defeats standard retrospective forensic recovery; detection depends on real-time metadata/configuration monitoring.
ITID-34733.response: Treat as premeditated; pursue any available real-time metadata, device configuration evidence, and witness corroboration since message content itself is unrecoverable.
metrics: Count of confirmed ephemeral-mode exfiltration cases per year
ITID-34733.notes: Differentiating axis versus ITID-34731/34732 is the deliberate anti-forensic evasion strategy (ephemeral mode), independent of which underlying app or platform is used.

playbook.name: Response: Ephemeral/Disappearing Message App Used to Evade Retention/DLP
playbook.description: For data suspected or confirmed to have been exfiltrated using an ephemeral/disappearing-message feature specifically to evade retention policy and DLP review.

steps.title: Be aware detection here is typically retrospective and evidence-limited
steps.desc: Recognize that the disappearing-message feature is deliberately chosen to defeat later review — content may be unrecoverable once the retention window expires, so this is usually identified from surrounding circumstantial evidence (app installation, screenshots by a third party, contextual behavior) rather than the message content itself.
steps.outcome: Investigation scoped realistically around likely evidence limitations.

steps.title: Attempt recovery through any available forensic artifact
steps.desc: Check for notification previews, third-party screenshots, cloud backup snapshots taken before expiry, or app metadata (installation, message counts) that may survive even if message bodies do not.
steps.guidance: Act quickly — evidence may expire on its own timeline regardless of investigation pace.
steps.outcome: Any recoverable evidence captured before further loss.
steps.abort: If no evidence is recoverable, document the limitation and proceed on available circumstantial evidence with Legal.

steps.title: Identify the recipient and app used
steps.desc: Determine which ephemeral messaging app was used and, where possible, the recipient's identity or affiliation.
steps.outcome: App and recipient context established where available.

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal before further action
steps.desc: Loop in HR/Legal immediately given the deliberate evidence-evasion nature of this technique.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and directing next steps.

steps.title: Restrict access per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Restrict the individual's access to corporate systems/network per HR/Legal direction.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration via this channel prevented.

steps.title: Review policy on ephemeral messaging apps on managed devices
steps.desc: Assess whether corporate policy should prohibit or block installation of disappearing-message apps on managed devices, given their specific evasion purpose.
steps.outcome: Policy gap identified and remediation tracked.

steps.title: Assess data exposure on a worst-case basis and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Given likely evidence limitations, work with HR/Legal to assess impact conservatively and determine appropriate response.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed despite evidentiary gaps.

steps.title: Document the case and review acceptable-use/app-blocking policy
steps.desc: Record findings and evaluate whether ephemeral-messaging apps should be blocked outright on managed devices given the inherent evidentiary blind spot.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and policy reviewed.

ITID-34734.def: An instant messaging app exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Instant Messaging Apps, pending further investigation.
ITID-34734.purpose: Intake bucket for instant messaging app exfiltration activity that does not fit the third-party app, native messaging, or ephemeral-mode leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reported messaging-app-related data loss with platform/mechanism not yet determined
Ambiguous messaging app misuse spanning multiple sub-patterns
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34731, 34732, or 34733 once investigated
ITID-34734.severity: Medium-High pending triage; reassess once classified.
ITID-34734.escalation: Escalate to SOC/insider risk triage for reclassification.
indicators: Generic MDM/endpoint alert on messaging app activity lacking enough detail for specific classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient context available to classify the messaging channel at intake
controls: MDM/mobile monitoring
ITID-34734.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34734.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Instant Messaging Apps ITID as soon as possible.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34734.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Instant Messaging App Exfiltration
playbook.description: For instant-messaging-app-based exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly WhatsApp/Signal/Telegram, iMessage/RCS, or ephemeral-app based) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear.

steps.title: Be aware detection here is typically retrospective
steps.desc: Recognize that instant-messaging content is generally invisible to network-level monitoring, so this is usually discovered via device forensics or a related investigation.
steps.outcome: Investigation scoped appropriately around a forensic/retrospective posture.

steps.title: Characterize the specific app and data involved
steps.desc: Determine which messaging app was used and establish, where possible, the scope of data sent.
steps.outcome: Activity characterized well enough to redirect to a specific playbook or proceed here.

steps.title: Identify the recipient and device used
steps.desc: Determine whether a corporate or personal device was used, and identify the recipient where possible.
steps.outcome: Source device and recipient context established.

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal before further action
steps.desc: Loop in HR/Legal given the personnel and device-access implications.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal aware and directing next steps.

steps.title: Restrict access per HR/Legal direction
steps.desc: Restrict the individual's access to corporate systems/network per HR/Legal direction.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration via this channel prevented.

steps.title: Review MDM/acceptable-use policy relevant to the app identified
steps.desc: Assess whether policy or technical controls should be tightened for the specific app/technique observed.
steps.outcome: Policy gap identified and remediation tracked.

steps.title: Assess data exposure and determine disciplinary/legal action
steps.desc: Work with HR/Legal to assess impact and appropriate response.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and resolution path agreed.

steps.title: Document and reclassify for future reference
steps.desc: Record the case, and note the specific app/technique used for future classification consistency.
steps.outcome: Finding logged.

ITID-34811.def: An event in which an advanced persistent threat actor exfiltrates data to a server or infrastructure element it owns and operates as a dedicated staging point, distinguished by attribution to attacker-controlled (not third-party or compromised) infrastructure.
ITID-34811.purpose: Captures exfiltration routed through infrastructure that the intruding advanced threat actor operates and controls specifically for staging stolen data before final retrieval.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration to an IP/domain attributed via threat intelligence to a known or suspected APT actor's infrastructure
Custom exfiltration tooling communicating with attacker-registered domains/servers
Staging server used exclusively for this campaign, identified via infrastructure pivoting
scopeExcludes: Use of compromised third-party infrastructure to mask origin (ITID-34813)
Exfiltration timing strategy independent of infrastructure ownership (ITID-34812)
ITID-34811.severity: Critical: APT-attributed infrastructure indicates a sophisticated, targeted, well-resourced adversary.
ITID-34811.escalation: Escalate immediately to threat intelligence and executive leadership; treat as a targeted APT campaign requiring full incident response activation.
indicators: Network traffic to an IP/domain matching known APT infrastructure in threat intelligence feeds
Custom malware/tooling with known APT-associated signatures communicating outbound
DNS requests to infrastructure with registration/hosting patterns consistent with APT tradecraft
vectors: Custom exfiltration tooling built specifically for the campaign, communicating with dedicated attacker infrastructure
rootCauses: Threat intelligence feeds not integrated into network egress monitoring
Lack of network traffic analysis capable of identifying novel/unattributed C2 infrastructure
mitreTechniques: T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
controls: Threat intelligence-integrated network egress monitoring
Network traffic analysis / anomalous destination detection
ITID-34811.detection: Moderate: strong when threat intelligence attribution exists, weak for previously unseen APT infrastructure.
ITID-34811.response: Full incident response activation: containment, threat intel sharing, forensic scoping of all systems touched by the campaign.
metrics: Count of confirmed APT-attributed exfiltration events per year
Dwell time from initial compromise to exfiltration detection
ITID-34811.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34813 by infrastructure ownership: this leaf is attacker-operated staging infrastructure, not a compromised legitimate third party used for cover.

playbook.name: Response: Exfiltration via APT-Operated Dedicated Staging Server
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exfiltration to a dedicated staging server operated by an advanced persistent threat actor, indicating a sophisticated, likely ongoing compromise rather than an isolated exfiltration event.

steps.title: Detect via baseline/anomaly-based analysis, not signatures
steps.desc: Identify the staging server communication through behavioral/anomaly detection (unusual destination, timing, volume, or protocol use) rather than signature-based tools, since APT infrastructure is typically not on commodity threat-intelligence blocklists.
steps.guidance: Review netflow/DNS/proxy logs for long-lived, low-volume, or unusually-timed connections to external infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Suspicious staging server communication identified and characterized.
steps.tool: NDR / netflow analysis / threat hunting platform

steps.title: Establish full scope across hosts and channels
steps.desc: Determine which hosts are communicating with the staging server, over what time period, and whether multiple channels or protocols are in use, treating this as a full compromise investigation rather than a single-host exfiltration event.
steps.guidance: Assume the visible staging activity is only part of a larger operation until proven otherwise.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected hosts and channels established.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Given the APT indicators, formally escalate this from a single exfiltration event to a full incident-response engagement covering initial access, persistence, lateral movement, and command-and-control, not just the exfiltration channel.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Contain affected hosts without tipping off the actor prematurely
steps.desc: Isolate confirmed-affected hosts using methods that avoid alerting a sophisticated actor to the response (e.g. network-layer isolation rather than obvious endpoint actions), per IR lead direction.
steps.guidance: Premature, visible containment actions can cause an APT actor to accelerate destructive action or go further underground.
steps.outcome: Affected hosts contained with minimal signal to the actor.

steps.title: Block the staging server and related infrastructure
steps.desc: Block identified staging server IPs/domains and any associated infrastructure at the network perimeter, informed by threat intelligence on related infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Known exfiltration channel blocked.
steps.tool: Firewall / DNS sinkhole / threat intelligence platform

steps.title: Eradicate persistence mechanisms across the full scope
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors, scheduled tasks, and other persistence mechanisms across every affected host identified in the full investigation, not just the staging endpoint.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms removed across the full scope.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Given the likely scale, coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the full scope of data accessed.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review with threat-intelligence follow-up
steps.desc: Document the full incident timeline, indicators of compromise, and lessons learned, and share IOCs with threat-intelligence sharing partners as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced and IOCs shared.

ITID-34812.def: An event in which an advanced threat actor times data exfiltration activity to coincide with periods of reduced security monitoring coverage — nights, weekends, or holidays specific to the victim organization's time zone — as a deliberate detection-evasion strategy.
ITID-34812.purpose: Captures exfiltration deliberately scheduled around the target security team's working hours and time zone to reduce the likelihood of real-time detection and response.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration activity timestamps clustering around the victim's off-hours/weekend/holiday periods with no operational reason
Exfiltration timing that shifts to match a target's regional time zone across a multi-region campaign
Correlation of exfiltration timing with known SOC staffing/coverage gaps
scopeExcludes: Infrastructure attribution/staging point selection (ITID-34811)
Use of compromised third-party infrastructure for origin masking (ITID-34813)
ITID-34812.severity: Critical: deliberate SOC-coverage-aware timing indicates sophisticated adversary reconnaissance of the target's operations.
ITID-34812.escalation: Escalate immediately; treat as evidence the actor has performed reconnaissance on the SOC's operational tempo, warranting a broader compromise assessment.
indicators: Exfiltration event timestamps statistically clustered in the victim's off-hours/weekend windows
Absence of exfiltration activity during known full-staffing SOC hours despite otherwise continuous access
Exfiltration timing shift following a change in the organization's SOC operating hours
vectors: Scheduled/automated exfiltration jobs configured to run only during known low-coverage windows
rootCauses: SOC coverage gaps (nights/weekends) not backed by equivalent automated detection/alerting capability
No 24/7 alerting parity between staffed and unstaffed hours
controls: 24/7 automated alerting parity independent of staffed hours
Follow-the-sun or MDR coverage for off-hours monitoring
ITID-34812.detection: Moderate: automated detection can close this gap even without human coverage, but requires deliberate off-hours alerting design.
ITID-34812.response: Treat off-hours timing itself as a high-confidence indicator warranting immediate full investigation regardless of alert severity scoring.
metrics: Percentage of confirmed exfiltration events occurring in off-hours windows
Mean time-to-detection comparison between staffed and unstaffed hours
ITID-34812.notes: Differentiating axis is timing strategy specifically; may co-occur with ITID-34811/34813 but is tracked separately to isolate the SOC-coverage-evasion signal.

playbook.name: Response: Exfiltration Timed to Avoid Security Team Working Hours (Time-Zone-Aware)
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exfiltration deliberately timed to occur outside the security team's working hours or during shift-change windows, indicating a sophisticated actor aware of the target's operational tempo.

steps.title: Detect via baseline/anomaly-based analysis across time-of-day patterns
steps.desc: Analyze activity logs specifically for a pattern of anomalous access clustering outside normal business hours or security team coverage windows, which signature-based tools will not flag on their own.
steps.guidance: Correlate against known SOC shift schedules/holidays to confirm the timing is not coincidental.
steps.outcome: Time-of-day exfiltration pattern confirmed.
steps.tool: SIEM time-series analysis / threat hunting platform

steps.title: Establish full scope across hosts and channels
steps.desc: Determine the full extent of activity during these off-hours windows across all potentially affected hosts and channels, treating this as a broader compromise investigation.
steps.guidance: Assume the timing sophistication indicates a capable actor likely to have additional footholds.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected hosts and channels established.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Formally escalate to a full IR engagement given the operational sophistication indicated by time-zone-aware timing.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Adjust monitoring coverage before further containment action
steps.desc: Ensure continuous (follow-the-sun or on-call) monitoring coverage is in place before taking containment actions, so the actor cannot exploit a coverage gap during the response itself.
steps.outcome: Monitoring gap closed for the duration of the response.

steps.title: Contain affected hosts and block identified exfiltration channels
steps.desc: Isolate confirmed-affected hosts and block identified destination infrastructure at the network perimeter.
steps.outcome: Known exfiltration channels blocked and hosts contained.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence mechanisms across the full scope
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors and persistence mechanisms across every affected host.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms removed across the full scope.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the full scope of data accessed.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Review SOC coverage model and conduct full post-incident review
steps.desc: Document the full incident and specifically assess whether SOC shift coverage or after-hours alerting needs strengthening to close the exploited timing gap.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced and coverage gap addressed.

ITID-34813.def: An event in which an advanced threat actor exfiltrates data via infrastructure it does not own but has compromised (a legitimate third-party server, cloud tenant, or trusted vendor system), using that legitimacy to evade destination-based network defenses.
ITID-34813.purpose: Captures exfiltration routed through compromised legitimate third-party infrastructure specifically to mask the true origin/destination and blend in with expected traffic.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration routed through a compromised legitimate vendor/partner system as a relay
Use of a compromised cloud tenant belonging to an unrelated organization as an exfiltration relay
Traffic destined for infrastructure with a legitimate reputation/history, later confirmed compromised
scopeExcludes: Exfiltration to attacker-owned/operated dedicated infrastructure (ITID-34811)
Timing-based evasion strategy independent of infrastructure choice (ITID-34812)
ITID-34813.severity: Critical: use of compromised trusted infrastructure indicates high sophistication and defeats reputation-based network controls.
ITID-34813.escalation: Escalate immediately; coordinate with the compromised third party and threat intelligence, since this also represents a supply-chain/trusted-relationship compromise.
indicators: Exfiltration destination later confirmed by threat intelligence to be a compromised legitimate system, not attacker-owned
Traffic to a previously trusted/allowlisted destination showing anomalous volume or data patterns
Third-party notification of compromise on infrastructure that also received data from this organization
vectors: Compromise of a trusted vendor/partner system, then routing stolen data through it to evade destination-reputation filtering
rootCauses: Network egress filtering relies heavily on destination reputation without content/behavior analysis
No supply-chain compromise notification integration with egress monitoring
controls: Behavior-based (not reputation-only) egress monitoring
Third-party/vendor compromise notification integration
ITID-34813.detection: Weak-Moderate: reputation-based controls are specifically defeated by this technique; behavioral/volume analysis is required to catch it.
ITID-34813.response: Full incident response including coordination with the compromised third party; reassess all trust relationships with reputationally-allowlisted destinations.
metrics: Count of confirmed compromised-third-party-relay exfiltration events per year
detections: Behavioral egress anomaly detection on trusted destinations
ITID-34813.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34811 by infrastructure ownership: compromised legitimate third party versus attacker-operated dedicated infrastructure.

playbook.name: Response: Exfiltration Using Compromised Third-Party Infrastructure to Mask Origin
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exfiltration routed through compromised third-party infrastructure (a legitimate but hijacked external server/service) to mask the true destination and evade reputation-based blocking.

steps.title: Detect via baseline/anomaly-based analysis, not reputation lists
steps.desc: Identify the exfiltration channel through behavioral anomalies (unusual destination for this environment, unexpected protocol/volume to an otherwise-legitimate service) since the third-party infrastructure will likely have a clean reputation and evade signature/blocklist-based tools.
steps.outcome: Suspicious use of legitimate-appearing third-party infrastructure identified.
steps.tool: NDR / netflow analysis / threat hunting platform

steps.title: Confirm the third party is genuinely compromised, not complicit or coincidental
steps.desc: Investigate whether the third-party service is a hijacked victim itself (worth notifying) or a knowing party, using available threat intelligence and, where appropriate, direct coordination.
steps.outcome: Nature of third-party involvement clarified.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Formally escalate to a full IR engagement given the infrastructure sophistication indicated by third-party masking.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Contain affected hosts and block the masked channel
steps.desc: Isolate confirmed-affected hosts and block the identified third-party endpoint at the network perimeter, understanding this may also affect legitimate traffic to that service.
steps.outcome: Known exfiltration channel blocked with awareness of collateral impact.

steps.title: Notify the compromised third party where appropriate
steps.desc: Where the third-party infrastructure is a victim, notify them (via Legal/vendor-management channels) so they can remediate on their side.
steps.outcome: Third party informed and coordinating remediation where appropriate.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence mechanisms across the full scope
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors and persistence mechanisms across every affected host.
