steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms removed across the full scope.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the full scope of data accessed.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review with threat-intelligence follow-up
steps.desc: Document the full incident timeline, indicators of compromise, and lessons learned, and share IOCs with threat-intelligence sharing partners as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced and IOCs shared.

ITID-34814.def: An APT-driven exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under APT-Driven Exfiltration, pending further threat intelligence attribution.
ITID-34814.purpose: Intake bucket for APT-driven exfiltration activity that does not fit the dedicated-infrastructure, timing-evasion, or compromised-third-party leaves.
scopeIncludes: Suspected APT exfiltration with infrastructure/timing pattern not yet determined
Confirmed sophisticated exfiltration pending full threat intelligence attribution
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34811, 34812, or 34813 once investigated
ITID-34814.severity: Critical pending triage; treat as high-severity by default given the APT context.
ITID-34814.escalation: Escalate immediately to threat intelligence for attribution and reclassification.
indicators: Generic advanced-threat exfiltration indicator lacking enough detail for specific sub-classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient threat intelligence attribution available at intake
controls: Threat intelligence monitoring
ITID-34814.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34814.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific APT-Driven Exfiltration ITID as soon as attribution allows.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34814.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General APT-Driven Exfiltration
playbook.description: For APT-driven exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly dedicated staging server, time-zone-aware timing, or third-party infrastructure masking) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear. Always treat as part of a broader compromise, not an isolated exfiltration event.

steps.title: Detect via baseline/anomaly-based analysis, not signatures
steps.desc: Identify the suspected APT activity through behavioral/anomaly detection rather than signature-based tools, since sophisticated actors typically evade commodity detection.
steps.outcome: Suspicious activity characterized well enough to redirect to a specific playbook or proceed here.
steps.tool: NDR / netflow analysis / threat hunting platform

steps.title: Establish full scope across hosts and channels
steps.desc: Determine which hosts and channels are involved, treating this as a full compromise investigation rather than a single-host exfiltration event.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected hosts and channels established.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Formally escalate this to a full IR engagement covering initial access, persistence, lateral movement, and command-and-control, not just the exfiltration channel.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Contain affected hosts without tipping off the actor prematurely
steps.desc: Isolate confirmed-affected hosts using methods that minimize signal to a sophisticated actor, per IR lead direction.
steps.outcome: Affected hosts contained with minimal signal to the actor.

steps.title: Block identified exfiltration infrastructure
steps.desc: Block identified destination IPs/domains and related infrastructure at the network perimeter.
steps.outcome: Known exfiltration channels blocked.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence mechanisms across the full scope
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors and persistence mechanisms across every affected host.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms removed across the full scope.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the full scope of data accessed.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review and reclassify for future reference
steps.desc: Document the full incident and note the specific APT technique observed for future classification consistency and IOC sharing.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced.

ITID-34821.def: An event in which an advanced threat actor collects and consolidates data onto one or more internal staging hosts in preparation for bulk transfer, distinguished as the pre-exfiltration internal-collection stage rather than the outbound transfer itself.
ITID-34821.purpose: Captures the internal staging stage of a multi-stage exfiltration campaign, where data is consolidated on an internal host before the actual transfer out of the network.
scopeIncludes: Data from multiple sources copied/aggregated onto a single internal host or share prior to transfer
Compression/archiving of collected data on an internal staging system observed prior to any outbound transfer
Internal host showing abnormal storage growth consistent with data staging
scopeExcludes: Splitting exfiltration across multiple compromised hosts specifically to avoid volume detection (ITID-34822)
Sequential handoff between multiple C2 channels during transfer (ITID-34823)
ITID-34821.severity: High: internal staging indicates an active campaign approaching the exfiltration phase, an opportunity for pre-loss interdiction.
ITID-34821.escalation: Escalate immediately; this is a critical interdiction window before data actually leaves the network.
indicators: Sudden storage/file-count growth on an internal host with no corresponding legitimate business process
Archive/compression tool execution on a host not normally used for that purpose
Data from multiple distinct sensitive repositories converging on a single internal host
vectors: Internal staging host used to aggregate and compress data collected from multiple compromised systems before a single bulk transfer
rootCauses: No monitoring for abnormal internal data aggregation/storage growth patterns
Lack of alerting on archive/compression tool use on atypical hosts
controls: Internal storage growth anomaly monitoring
Alerting on unexpected archive/compression tool execution
ITID-34821.detection: Moderate: staging behavior leaves detectable internal artifacts and represents a key opportunity to interdict before actual data loss.
ITID-34821.response: Treat as a pre-loss interdiction opportunity: isolate the staging host immediately and prevent any outbound transfer before it occurs.
metrics: Count of staging events interdicted before outbound transfer
Mean time from staging detection to host isolation
ITID-34821.notes: This leaf owns the internal, pre-transfer staging stage specifically; the outbound multi-host split (ITID-34822) and multi-channel handoff (ITID-34823) cover distinct later stages of a multi-stage campaign.

playbook.name: Response: Data Staged Internally Before Bulk Transfer Out
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exfiltration where data was first aggregated/staged on an internal host before a subsequent bulk transfer out, a multi-stage technique indicating a sophisticated actor.

steps.title: Detect the staging host via baseline/anomaly-based analysis
steps.desc: Identify the internal host used for staging through anomalous internal data-aggregation activity (unusual inbound file volume/variety from many sources onto one host) rather than signature-based tools.
steps.guidance: Staging hosts often show disk-usage spikes or unusual archive-creation activity shortly before the outbound transfer.
steps.outcome: Staging host and aggregated dataset identified.
steps.tool: EDR / file integrity monitoring / SIEM correlation

steps.title: Trace the full scope: source hosts feeding the stage and the outbound destination
steps.desc: Identify every source host that fed data into the staging host, and the destination(s) the bulk transfer went to, treating this as a full compromise investigation.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected hosts and the exfiltration destination established.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Formally escalate this to a full IR engagement given the multi-stage sophistication indicated.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Contain the staging host and source hosts without tipping off the actor
steps.desc: Isolate the staging host and identified source hosts using methods that minimize signal to a sophisticated actor, per IR lead direction.
steps.outcome: Affected hosts contained with minimal signal to the actor.

steps.title: Block the outbound destination
steps.desc: Block the identified destination IP/domain at the network perimeter to stop any further bulk transfer.
steps.outcome: Known exfiltration channel blocked.

steps.title: Remove staged data and eradicate persistence across the full scope
steps.desc: Securely remove the staged aggregate dataset from the staging host and eliminate all identified persistence mechanisms across every affected host.
steps.outcome: Staged data removed and persistence eliminated.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the full scope of the staged dataset.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review and review internal data-aggregation monitoring
steps.desc: Document the full incident and assess whether monitoring for anomalous internal data aggregation (a leading indicator of staged exfiltration) should be strengthened.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced and monitoring gap addressed.

ITID-34822.def: An event in which an advanced threat actor exfiltrates data by dividing the transfer across several compromised hosts, each sending a sub-threshold volume, so that per-host monitoring fails to flag any individual host as anomalous while aggregate loss is substantial.
ITID-34822.purpose: Captures exfiltration deliberately split across multiple compromised hosts so that no single host's outbound volume crosses a DLP or network monitoring threshold.
scopeIncludes: Multiple compromised hosts each transferring a modest volume to the same or related destinations within a similar timeframe
Data set fragments reassembled at the destination from parts sent by different internal hosts
Per-host transfer volumes consistently just below known DLP/monitoring alert thresholds
scopeExcludes: Internal staging/consolidation prior to transfer (ITID-34821)
Sequential C2 channel handoff during a single host's transfer (ITID-34823)
ITID-34822.severity: Critical: this technique is specifically engineered to defeat per-host volume-based detection.
ITID-34822.escalation: Escalate immediately upon pattern recognition; requires cross-host correlation to even identify the full scope.
indicators: Multiple hosts showing sub-threshold outbound transfers to the same or related external destinations within a short window
Aggregate cross-host transfer volume to a single destination significantly exceeding any individual host's volume
Correlated timing of multiple hosts' outbound activity
vectors: Coordinated malware/tooling on multiple compromised hosts each exfiltrating a sub-threshold portion of the target data set
rootCauses: DLP/network monitoring alerts on a per-host basis without cross-host aggregate correlation
No enterprise-wide destination-aggregation analytics
controls: Cross-host aggregate destination correlation analytics
SIEM/SOAR correlation rules spanning multiple hosts to the same destination
ITID-34822.detection: Weak: requires purpose-built cross-host correlation analytics; standard per-host DLP thresholds miss this by design.
ITID-34822.response: Once identified, correlate across the full host population to scope every participating system before containment.
metrics: Count of confirmed multi-host split-exfiltration campaigns per year
Average number of hosts involved per confirmed campaign
ITID-34822.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34821 by being the outbound-split stage rather than internal staging, and from ITID-34823 by splitting across hosts rather than across sequential channels from one host.

playbook.name: Response: Exfiltration Split Across Multiple Compromised Hosts to Avoid Volume Detection
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exfiltration where the actor split transfer volume across multiple compromised hosts specifically to stay under per-host volume-detection thresholds.

steps.title: Detect via cross-host baseline/anomaly correlation, not per-host thresholds
steps.desc: Since no single host's volume triggers alerting, correlate outbound activity across hosts sharing indicators (timing, destination, protocol) to reveal the aggregate exfiltration pattern.
steps.guidance: Per-host volume-based DLP/NDR alerting will not catch this by design — cross-host correlation is essential.
steps.outcome: Aggregate exfiltration pattern and full set of participating hosts identified.

steps.title: Establish full scope and total aggregate volume
steps.desc: Determine every host involved and reconstruct the total data volume/content exfiltrated in aggregate, treating this as a full compromise investigation.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected hosts and total exfiltrated volume established.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Formally escalate this to a full IR engagement given the multi-host coordination sophistication indicated.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Contain all identified hosts simultaneously
steps.desc: Isolate all identified compromised hosts at the same time where possible, to prevent the actor from shifting volume to remaining hosts once one is contained.
steps.outcome: All known participating hosts contained.

steps.title: Block the common exfiltration destination(s)
steps.desc: Block the identified destination IP(s)/domain(s) at the network perimeter to stop any further split transfers.
steps.outcome: Known exfiltration channel(s) blocked.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence mechanisms across the full scope
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors and persistence mechanisms across every affected host.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms removed across the full scope.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the aggregate scope of data accessed.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review and implement cross-host correlation detection
steps.desc: Document the full incident and confirm cross-host correlation rules are in place to catch aggregate volume patterns that per-host thresholds miss.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced and detection gap addressed.

ITID-34823.def: An event in which an advanced threat actor exfiltrates data using a sequence of different C2 channels or protocols in succession (e.g., DNS tunneling, then HTTPS, then a cloud storage API), rather than a single consistent channel, to avoid building a detectable single-protocol pattern.
ITID-34823.purpose: Captures exfiltration that hands off between multiple distinct command-and-control channels during a single campaign, complicating detection and attribution by fragmenting the traffic pattern.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration activity attributed to the same campaign/actor observed shifting protocol or destination channel over the course of the operation
Use of a channel-switching or protocol-fallback capability built into observed malware/tooling
Correlated indicators tying together distinct-looking traffic across different protocols to a single campaign
scopeExcludes: Splitting the same channel's traffic across multiple hosts (ITID-34822)
Internal staging prior to any outbound transfer (ITID-34821)
ITID-34823.severity: Critical: multi-channel handoff indicates significant operational sophistication and complicates full-scope attribution.
ITID-34823.escalation: Escalate immediately; requires cross-protocol threat hunting to establish full campaign scope.
indicators: Distinct-protocol traffic patterns later correlated via shared indicators (file hashes, timing, destination infrastructure) to one campaign
Malware/tooling observed with multi-protocol C2 fallback capability
Sequential detection of different protocol anomalies from the same host over a short timeframe
vectors: Malware built with multiple C2/exfiltration protocol modules, switching channels to evade single-protocol detection or in response to blocking
rootCauses: Detection tooling siloed by protocol without cross-protocol campaign correlation
No threat hunting capability to link disparate protocol anomalies to a single actor/campaign
mitreTechniques: T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
controls: Cross-protocol threat hunting and campaign correlation
Full-packet/metadata retention enabling retrospective multi-protocol analysis
ITID-34823.detection: Weak: requires dedicated threat hunting and retrospective correlation; automated single-protocol tooling will not connect the stages.
ITID-34823.response: Conduct cross-protocol threat hunting to establish full campaign timeline and scope before containment/eradication.
metrics: Count of confirmed multi-channel-handoff campaigns per year
detections: Cross-protocol campaign correlation via threat hunting
ITID-34823.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34822 by fragmenting across sequential C2 channels/protocols rather than across parallel hosts on one channel.

playbook.name: Response: Exfiltration via Sequential Handoff Between Multiple C2 Channels
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exfiltration where the actor moved data through a sequential handoff between multiple command-and-control channels, evading detection tied to any single channel.

steps.title: Detect via correlation across channel transitions, not single-channel signatures
steps.desc: Identify the sequential handoff pattern by correlating activity across different C2 channels/protocols used by the same host or actor over time, since each individual channel may appear benign or low-volume in isolation.
steps.outcome: Full C2 channel chain and handoff pattern identified.
steps.tool: NDR / threat hunting platform / SIEM correlation

steps.title: Establish full scope across all channels and hosts involved
steps.desc: Determine every channel and host used across the handoff sequence, treating this as a full compromise investigation.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected hosts and channels established.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Formally escalate this to a full IR engagement given the multi-channel sophistication indicated.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Block all identified channels simultaneously
steps.desc: Block every identified C2 channel/destination at the network perimeter at the same time, to prevent the actor from simply continuing on a channel not yet blocked.
steps.outcome: All known C2 channels blocked simultaneously.

steps.title: Contain affected hosts without tipping off the actor prematurely
steps.desc: Isolate confirmed-affected hosts using methods that minimize signal to a sophisticated actor, per IR lead direction.
steps.outcome: Affected hosts contained with minimal signal to the actor.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence mechanisms across the full scope
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors and persistence mechanisms across every affected host.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms removed across the full scope.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the full scope of data accessed.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review with threat-intelligence follow-up
steps.desc: Document the full incident timeline, indicators of compromise across all channels, and lessons learned, and share IOCs with threat-intelligence sharing partners.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced and IOCs shared.

ITID-34824.def: A multi-stage exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Multi-Stage Exfiltration, pending further investigation.
ITID-34824.purpose: Intake bucket for multi-stage exfiltration activity that does not fit the internal-staging, host-splitting, or channel-handoff leaves.
scopeIncludes: Suspected multi-stage exfiltration with the specific stage/pattern not yet determined
Complex campaigns combining elements of multiple sibling leaves pending full scoping
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34821, 34822, or 34823 once investigated
ITID-34824.severity: High pending triage; treat as high-severity by default given the multi-stage/advanced-threat context.
ITID-34824.escalation: Escalate immediately to threat hunting/incident response for scoping and reclassification.
indicators: Generic advanced/multi-stage exfiltration indicator lacking enough detail for specific sub-classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient scoping available to classify the specific multi-stage pattern at intake
controls: Threat hunting and campaign correlation
ITID-34824.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34824.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Multi-Stage Exfiltration ITID as soon as scoping allows.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34824.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Multi-Stage Exfiltration
playbook.description: For multi-stage exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly internal staging, split-host transfer, or sequential C2 handoff) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear. Always treat as part of a broader compromise, not an isolated exfiltration event.

steps.title: Detect via baseline/anomaly-based correlation, not single-point signatures
steps.desc: Identify the multi-stage pattern through cross-host/cross-channel correlation rather than any single signature, since the technique is specifically designed to avoid single-point detection.
steps.outcome: Multi-stage pattern characterized well enough to redirect to a specific playbook or proceed here.
steps.tool: SIEM correlation / NDR / threat hunting platform

steps.title: Establish full scope across all hosts and stages involved
steps.desc: Determine every host and stage involved in the multi-stage chain, treating this as a full compromise investigation.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected hosts and stages established.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Formally escalate this to a full IR engagement given the multi-stage sophistication indicated.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Contain all identified hosts and channels simultaneously
steps.desc: Isolate all identified hosts and block all identified channels at the same time, per IR lead direction, to prevent the actor from shifting to an uncontained stage.
steps.outcome: All known hosts and channels contained simultaneously.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence mechanisms across the full scope
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors and persistence mechanisms across every affected host.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms removed across the full scope.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the full scope of data accessed.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review and reclassify for future reference
steps.desc: Document the full incident and note the specific multi-stage technique observed for future classification consistency and IOC sharing.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced.

ITID-34831.def: An event in which an advanced threat actor exfiltrates data in small increments deliberately calibrated to remain under configured DLP or network monitoring volume thresholds, prioritizing threshold evasion as the primary technique over duration or scheduling.
ITID-34831.purpose: Captures exfiltration deliberately throttled to stay below DLP volume alert thresholds, the core 'low-and-slow' technique defining this Tier-4 group.
scopeIncludes: Per-transfer volume consistently just under a known/configured DLP alert threshold
Manual or automated throttling of transfer rate/size to avoid triggering volume-based alerts
Transfer volume pattern showing evidence of threshold-awareness (e.g., consistently 5-10% below the known limit)
scopeExcludes: Exfiltration spread over an extended dwell time to avoid baseline-deviation detection specifically (ITID-34832)
Fully scheduled/automated periodic small-batch transfers (ITID-34833)
ITID-34831.severity: Critical: threshold-aware throttling indicates the actor has knowledge of the specific defensive configuration.
ITID-34831.escalation: Escalate immediately; threshold-awareness may indicate reconnaissance of internal DLP configuration, warranting a broader compromise assessment.
indicators: Statistical analysis showing per-transfer volumes clustering just below a known DLP threshold
Aggregate cumulative volume to one destination significantly exceeding any single alerted transfer
Transfer sizes that shift downward following a DLP threshold configuration change
vectors: Malware/tooling configured with a maximum per-transfer size calibrated to known or inferred DLP thresholds
rootCauses: DLP volume thresholds configured statically without cumulative/aggregate destination tracking
DLP configuration details exposed or inferable by an attacker with internal reconnaissance access
controls: Cumulative/aggregate destination volume tracking independent of per-transfer thresholds
DLP threshold configuration kept confidential and periodically randomized/reviewed
ITID-34831.detection: Weak: this technique is specifically designed to defeat threshold-based DLP; aggregate/cumulative analytics are required to detect it.
ITID-34831.response: Investigate for evidence of DLP configuration reconnaissance; implement cumulative destination-volume analytics going forward.
metrics: Count of confirmed threshold-evasion exfiltration cases per year
Aggregate volume detected via cumulative analytics vs. per-transfer alerting
ITID-34831.notes: Core differentiator versus siblings is threshold-awareness (volume-per-transfer) rather than duration (ITID-34832) or scheduling automation (ITID-34833), though these often co-occur in practice.

playbook.name: Response: Low-and-Slow Exfiltration Below DLP Volume Thresholds
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exfiltration deliberately conducted at a slow, low-volume rate specifically calibrated to stay below DLP volume-based detection thresholds.

steps.title: Detect via long-window baseline/anomaly analysis, not real-time volume thresholds
steps.desc: Since per-event volume stays below alerting thresholds by design, analyze cumulative outbound activity over extended time windows (weeks/months) for a persistent low-rate trickle to an unusual destination.
steps.guidance: Standard real-time DLP thresholds will not catch this — the detection has to look at trend/aggregate volume over a long baseline window.
steps.outcome: Low-and-slow exfiltration pattern and cumulative volume identified.

steps.title: Establish full scope across hosts, timeframe, and total cumulative data
steps.desc: Determine the full duration of the activity, all hosts/accounts involved, and reconstruct the total cumulative volume/content exfiltrated, treating this as a full compromise investigation given the sophistication implied.
steps.outcome: Full scope and total cumulative exfiltrated volume established.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Formally escalate this to a full IR engagement given the deliberate low-and-slow sophistication indicated.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Contain affected hosts without tipping off the actor prematurely
steps.desc: Isolate confirmed-affected hosts using methods that minimize signal to a sophisticated, patient actor, per IR lead direction.
steps.outcome: Affected hosts contained with minimal signal to the actor.

steps.title: Block the identified low-rate exfiltration destination
steps.desc: Block the identified destination IP/domain at the network perimeter to stop the ongoing trickle.
steps.outcome: Known exfiltration channel blocked.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence mechanisms across the full scope
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors and persistence mechanisms across every affected host.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms removed across the full scope.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the full cumulative scope of data accessed.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review and implement long-window trend detection
steps.desc: Document the full incident and confirm long-window trend/aggregate-volume detection is in place to catch low-and-slow patterns that real-time thresholds miss.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced and detection gap addressed.

ITID-34832.def: An event in which an advanced threat actor spreads data exfiltration across a long time horizon (weeks to months), calibrating the pace so that behavioral baselining tools never observe a statistically significant deviation from normal activity.
ITID-34832.purpose: Captures exfiltration deliberately spread across an extended dwell time so that the resulting activity never deviates enough from the account/host's established baseline to trigger UEBA-style anomaly detection.
scopeIncludes: Exfiltration activity that blends into an account/host's normal historical access pattern when viewed at a short time window
Data loss only apparent when analyzed over a long retrospective window (months) rather than in real time
Actor observed intentionally pacing activity to stay within the account's established behavioral baseline
scopeExcludes: Per-transfer volume throttling to beat a static DLP threshold (ITID-34831)
Fully scheduled/automated periodic transfers as the defining mechanism (ITID-34833)
ITID-34832.severity: Critical: baseline-evasion timing indicates a highly sophisticated, patient adversary.
ITID-34832.escalation: Escalate immediately once identified via retrospective analysis; requires an extended forensic timeline review to scope full data loss.
indicators: Retrospective long-window analysis revealing a slow cumulative increase in access/transfer activity invisible to short-window baselining
UEBA baseline itself showing gradual, actor-manipulated drift rather than a sharp anomaly
Total data volume moved over the extended period being disproportionate to any single detected event
vectors: Deliberately paced exfiltration timed to avoid triggering baseline-deviation alerts, sometimes gradually shifting the baseline itself over time
rootCauses: UEBA/behavioral baselining tuned only to short-window anomalies without long-term trend analysis
No periodic long-window retrospective review of cumulative account/host activity
controls: Long-window retrospective UEBA trend analysis
Periodic extended-timeline forensic review for high-value accounts/hosts
ITID-34832.detection: Weak: standard short-window UEBA misses this by design; only long-window retrospective analysis surfaces the pattern.
ITID-34832.response: Conduct an extended forensic timeline review once suspected, to scope the full duration and volume of the slow-drift exfiltration.
metrics: Count of confirmed baseline-drift exfiltration cases per year
Average detected campaign duration (dwell time) for this pattern
ITID-34832.notes: Differentiator versus ITID-34831 is the dwell-time/baseline-drift dimension rather than per-transfer threshold evasion; the two techniques often co-occur but are tracked on separate axes.

playbook.name: Response: Exfiltration Spread Across Extended Dwell Time to Avoid Baseline Deviation Detection
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exfiltration spread across an extended dwell time specifically to keep activity within the normal statistical baseline and avoid deviation-based anomaly detection.

steps.title: Detect via slow-drift baseline analysis, not point-in-time deviation alerts
steps.desc: Since the actor deliberately stayed within normal baseline variance at any single point, look for a slow drift in the baseline itself over an extended period, or corroborating indicators (unusual access patterns, unexplained persistence) alongside the traffic.
steps.guidance: This may require re-baselining analysis over a longer historical window than standard UEBA tools default to.
steps.outcome: Slow-drift exfiltration pattern identified despite staying within normal short-term variance.

steps.title: Establish full scope across the extended dwell period
steps.desc: Determine the full duration of dwell time, all hosts/accounts involved, and reconstruct the total data exfiltrated over the period, treating this as a full compromise investigation.
steps.outcome: Full scope and total exfiltrated volume over the dwell period established.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Formally escalate this to a full IR engagement given the extended dwell-time sophistication indicated.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Contain affected hosts without tipping off the actor prematurely
steps.desc: Isolate confirmed-affected hosts using methods that minimize signal to a sophisticated, patient actor, per IR lead direction.
steps.outcome: Affected hosts contained with minimal signal to the actor.

steps.title: Block the identified exfiltration destination
steps.desc: Block the identified destination IP/domain at the network perimeter to stop the ongoing exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Known exfiltration channel blocked.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence mechanisms across the full scope
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors and persistence mechanisms across every affected host that has allowed the actor to remain resident this long.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms removed across the full scope.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the extended compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the full scope of data accessed over the dwell period.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review and re-baseline detection thresholds
steps.desc: Document the full incident and confirm anomaly-detection baselines are periodically re-validated against longer historical windows to catch slow-drift compromise.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced and detection gap addressed.

ITID-34833.def: An event in which data exfiltration is carried out through a scheduled task, cron job, or automated script that periodically transfers small batches of data at consistent, predictable intervals, distinguishing this leaf by its automated-scheduling mechanism rather than volume-threshold or dwell-time evasion strategy.
ITID-34833.purpose: Captures exfiltration executed via a fully scheduled or automated mechanism performing periodic small-batch transfers, where automation/scheduling itself is the defining technique.
scopeIncludes: A scheduled task/cron job/automated script identified as performing periodic outbound data transfers
Consistent, regular-interval transfer timing (e.g., every N hours) detected in network or host logs
Malware with a built-in scheduling/beacon-interval capability used for periodic exfiltration
scopeExcludes: Manual/ad hoc throttling of transfer volume without a fixed automated schedule (ITID-34831)
Extended dwell-time pacing without a fixed periodic schedule (ITID-34832)
ITID-34833.severity: High-Critical, scaling with data sensitivity and total cumulative volume moved by the automated schedule.
ITID-34833.escalation: Escalate immediately upon identifying the scheduling mechanism; prioritize locating and disabling the scheduled task/job across the environment.
indicators: Scheduled task or cron job creation event with no legitimate business owner/purpose
Network traffic showing highly regular, fixed-interval timing to an external destination
Host forensic artifact showing an automated script configured for periodic execution
vectors: Malicious scheduled task, cron job, or beaconing malware configured for periodic small-batch outbound transfer
rootCauses: No monitoring/alerting on new scheduled task or cron job creation
Lack of network beacon-interval detection capability
controls: Scheduled task/cron job creation monitoring and alerting
Network beacon-interval detection analytics
ITID-34833.detection: Moderate: regular-interval traffic patterns are a well-established detection signature when beacon analytics are deployed.
ITID-34833.response: Locate and disable the scheduling mechanism across all affected hosts, and determine total cumulative volume exfiltrated over its active lifetime.
metrics: Count of confirmed scheduled/automated exfiltration mechanisms found per year
Average lifetime (days active) before detection
ITID-34833.notes: Differentiator versus ITID-34831/34832 is the automated, fixed-interval scheduling mechanism as the defining technical signature, which produces a distinct beacon-interval detection opportunity the other two lack.

playbook.name: Response: Scheduled/Automated Periodic Small-Batch Exfiltration
playbook.description: For confirmed or suspected exfiltration conducted via a scheduled/automated mechanism sending small batches of data out at regular intervals over time.

steps.title: Detect via recurring-pattern analysis across a long window, not single-event alerting
steps.desc: Identify the scheduled/automated pattern by correlating recurring, similarly-sized outbound transfers at regular intervals over an extended period, since any single batch is small enough to appear benign.
steps.guidance: Look for suspiciously consistent timing (e.g. exactly every 24 hours) which is characteristic of an automated/scripted mechanism rather than human behavior.
steps.outcome: Recurring exfiltration pattern and underlying automation mechanism identified.

steps.title: Locate and analyze the automation mechanism itself
steps.desc: Identify the scheduled task, cron job, script, or malware component responsible for the periodic transfers, and determine its full configuration and scope.
steps.outcome: Automation mechanism identified and its full scope of affected hosts established.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Formally escalate this to a full IR engagement given the automation/persistence sophistication indicated.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Disable the automation mechanism and contain affected hosts
steps.desc: Disable the identified scheduled task/script/malware and isolate affected hosts, per IR lead direction.
steps.outcome: Ongoing periodic exfiltration stopped.

steps.title: Block the identified periodic exfiltration destination
steps.desc: Block the identified destination IP/domain at the network perimeter as a defense-in-depth measure.
steps.outcome: Known exfiltration channel blocked.

steps.title: Remove the automation mechanism and eradicate persistence across the full scope
steps.desc: Fully remove the scheduled task/script/malware and any other persistence mechanisms across every affected host.
steps.outcome: Automation mechanism and all known persistence removed.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the full cumulative scope of data accessed.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review and implement recurring-pattern detection
steps.desc: Document the full incident and confirm detection rules exist for recurring low-volume transfer patterns over extended windows.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced and detection gap addressed.

ITID-34834.def: An exfiltration-over-time event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Exfiltration Over Time, pending further investigation.
ITID-34834.purpose: Intake bucket for exfiltration-over-time activity that does not fit the threshold-evasion, baseline-drift, or scheduled-automation leaves.
scopeIncludes: Suspected low-and-slow exfiltration with the specific evasion technique not yet determined
Long-duration data loss patterns pending full technical characterization
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34831, 34832, or 34833 once investigated
ITID-34834.severity: High pending triage; treat as high-severity by default given the advanced-threat context.
ITID-34834.escalation: Escalate immediately to threat hunting for scoping and reclassification.
indicators: Generic low-and-slow exfiltration indicator lacking enough detail for specific sub-classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient scoping available to classify the specific low-and-slow technique at intake
controls: Threat hunting and long-window behavioral analytics
ITID-34834.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34834.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Exfiltration Over Time ITID as soon as scoping allows.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34834.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Exfiltration Over Time
playbook.description: For time-spread exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly low-and-slow, extended-dwell, or scheduled-batch) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear. Always treat as part of a broader compromise, not an isolated exfiltration event.

steps.title: Detect via long-window baseline/anomaly analysis, not real-time thresholds
steps.desc: Identify the time-spread exfiltration pattern through extended-window trend/correlation analysis, since the technique is specifically designed to evade point-in-time detection.
steps.outcome: Pattern characterized well enough to redirect to a specific playbook or proceed here.

steps.title: Establish full scope across the time period and hosts involved
steps.desc: Determine the full duration, all hosts/accounts involved, and reconstruct the total data exfiltrated, treating this as a full compromise investigation.
steps.outcome: Full scope and total exfiltrated volume established.

steps.title: Pivot into a full incident investigation
steps.desc: Formally escalate this to a full IR engagement given the sophistication indicated by the time-spread technique.
steps.outcome: Broader IR engagement formally opened with appropriate resourcing.

steps.title: Contain affected hosts without tipping off the actor prematurely
steps.desc: Isolate confirmed-affected hosts using methods that minimize signal to a sophisticated, patient actor, per IR lead direction.
steps.outcome: Affected hosts contained with minimal signal to the actor.

steps.title: Block the identified exfiltration destination
steps.desc: Block the identified destination IP/domain at the network perimeter.
steps.outcome: Known exfiltration channel blocked.

steps.title: Eradicate persistence mechanisms across the full scope
steps.desc: Remove all identified backdoors and persistence mechanisms across every affected host.
steps.outcome: All known persistence mechanisms removed across the full scope.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials potentially exposed during the compromise
steps.desc: Rotate credentials for all accounts/systems that may have been accessed during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with executive leadership, Legal, and regulators as required based on the full scope of data accessed.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review and reclassify for future reference
steps.desc: Document the full incident and note the specific time-spread technique observed for future classification consistency.
steps.outcome: Comprehensive post-incident report produced.

ITID-34911.def: An event in which sensitive data is downloaded in bulk by a party who located a cloud storage bucket (e.g., S3, Azure Blob, GCS) left publicly accessible due to misconfiguration, distinguished from automated scanning campaigns by its single-target, manually-driven nature.
ITID-34911.purpose: Captures a single actor manually discovering and bulk-downloading data from a publicly accessible, misconfigured cloud storage bucket.
scopeIncludes: Bulk download activity from a bucket confirmed to have public/anonymous read access enabled
Discovery of a misconfigured bucket via manual reconnaissance, a bucket-name guess, or a leaked reference
Single-session bulk retrieval of bucket contents by one identifiable external party
scopeExcludes: Automated, at-scale scanning-and-harvesting campaigns hitting many organizations' buckets (ITID-34912)
Exfiltration via a misconfigured database snapshot/backup export specifically (ITID-34913)
ITID-34911.severity: Critical: public exposure combined with confirmed bulk download represents realized, often unrecoverable data loss.
ITID-34911.escalation: Escalate immediately to cloud security, legal, and privacy; initiate breach notification assessment given confirmed external access.
indicators: Cloud provider access logs showing anonymous/public reads from an unrecognized external IP
Bucket policy audit revealing public read access with no business justification
Third-party/researcher disclosure of the exposed bucket
vectors: Bucket left with public-read ACL/policy due to misconfiguration, discovered via manual search or bucket-name enumeration
rootCauses: No automated cloud security posture management (CSPM) scanning for public bucket exposure
Bucket policy misconfigured during setup with no periodic review
Default-deny public access not enforced at the account/organization level
controls: CSPM continuous public-exposure scanning
Account/organization-level block-public-access enforcement
ITID-34911.detection: Strong: cloud provider access logs and CSPM tooling give a direct, reliable signal once configured.
ITID-34911.response: Immediately restrict bucket access, review full access logs for the exposure window, and assess breach notification obligations.
metrics: Count of confirmed public bucket exposure incidents per year
Mean time-to-remediation from CSPM alert to access restriction
ITID-34911.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34912 by scale/actor: a single manual discovery-and-download event rather than an automated scanning campaign hitting many targets.

playbook.name: Response: Bulk Download from Publicly Accessible Misconfigured Cloud Bucket
playbook.description: For data confirmed or suspected to have been bulk-downloaded from a cloud storage bucket left publicly accessible due to misconfiguration.

steps.title: Confirm the misconfiguration and review cloud audit logs for access
steps.desc: Review the bucket's access policy to confirm public accessibility, and review cloud audit/access logs (e.g. CloudTrail-equivalent) for all read/download requests from external sources.
steps.outcome: Misconfiguration confirmed and full list of accessing parties/timestamps established.
steps.tool: Cloud audit logs (CloudTrail-equivalent) / bucket access logs

steps.title: Determine what data was exposed and for how long
steps.desc: Inventory the bucket's contents and establish how long the misconfiguration had been in place, to bound the exposure window.
steps.outcome: Data inventory and exposure window established.
steps.tool: Cloud storage console / data classification tooling

steps.title: Immediately close the misconfiguration
steps.desc: Correct the bucket's access policy to remove public access, restoring least-privilege access controls.
steps.guidance: This is the highest-priority containment action — every minute the bucket remains public is further exposure.
steps.outcome: Public access removed immediately.

steps.title: Revoke or rotate any credentials that may have facilitated the misconfiguration
steps.desc: If the misconfiguration was introduced via a compromised credential or pipeline, rotate the relevant credentials.
steps.outcome: Any credential-based contributing factor addressed.

steps.title: Audit for similar misconfigurations across the cloud estate
steps.desc: Scan all other buckets/storage resources in the environment for similar public-access misconfigurations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no other instances of the same misconfiguration exist.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the exposed data and coordinate with Legal on breach-notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Confirm remediation is complete
steps.desc: Verify the bucket policy is correctly restricted and no residual public access paths remain (e.g. via a misconfigured ACL alongside the bucket policy).
steps.outcome: Remediation confirmed complete.

steps.title: Document the case and implement preventive guardrails
steps.desc: Record findings and implement/strengthen automated guardrails (e.g. block-public-access settings, CSPM alerting) to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and preventive controls strengthened.

ITID-34912.def: An event in which sensitive data is accessed or downloaded from a misconfigured cloud storage resource by an automated scanning/harvesting tool operating at internet scale, indicated by scanning patterns, generic tooling signatures, or correlation with mass-scanning campaigns rather than targeted reconnaissance of this organization specifically.
ITID-34912.purpose: Captures automated, internet-scale scanning tools that systematically discover and harvest data from misconfigured cloud storage across many organizations, of which this org is one target.
scopeIncludes: Access patterns matching known mass cloud-bucket-scanning tool signatures (e.g., systematic bucket-name permutation)
Access originating from infrastructure associated with known internet-wide scanning services/researchers/threat actors
Rapid, broad enumeration access pattern preceding the actual data download
scopeExcludes: Single manually-targeted bucket discovery and download (ITID-34911)
Misconfigured database snapshot/backup export exfiltration (ITID-34913)
ITID-34912.severity: Critical: automated harvesting tools frequently exfiltrate data within minutes of exposure, and the actor may be unknown/unattributable.
ITID-34912.escalation: Escalate immediately; treat as opportunistic mass exploitation with a high likelihood of the data already being resold/republished.
indicators: Access log pattern showing systematic enumeration (bucket-name permutation) prior to download
Source IP/ASN associated with known mass-scanning infrastructure or research/threat-actor scanning services
Extremely rapid time-to-access following initial public exposure (often under an hour)
vectors: Internet-wide automated scanners that continuously enumerate cloud provider namespaces for misconfigured public resources
rootCauses: No CSPM continuous scanning to catch exposure before automated internet scanners do
Misconfiguration window (time between exposure and remediation) long enough for automated discovery
controls: CSPM continuous scanning to minimize exposure window
Real-time public-exposure alerting with automated remediation
ITID-34912.detection: Strong: automated scanner traffic patterns are well-documented and detectable via access log analysis.
ITID-34912.response: Assume worst-case (data already harvested and potentially redistributed) given automated tooling speed; prioritize breach notification assessment.
metrics: Mean time from public exposure to first detected automated scan access
Count of confirmed automated-harvesting incidents per year
ITID-34912.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34911 by the automated, at-scale, likely-unattributed nature of the access versus a single targeted actor.

playbook.name: Response: Automated Scanning-and-Harvesting of Misconfigured Cloud Storage at Scale
playbook.description: For data confirmed or suspected to have been harvested by an automated scanner systematically discovering and downloading from misconfigured cloud storage resources at scale (not a single targeted download).

steps.title: Confirm the automated scanning pattern via cloud audit log review
steps.desc: Review cloud audit/access logs for a high-volume, systematic access pattern (e.g. many sequential bucket-name guesses, consistent tooling signatures) rather than a single manual download.
steps.guidance: Automated scanners often probe many bucket names in rapid succession before finding an accessible one.
steps.outcome: Automated scanning pattern confirmed and source(s) identified where possible.

steps.title: Determine the full scope of data exposed and downloaded
steps.desc: Inventory the affected resource's contents and confirm what was actually downloaded versus merely enumerated/probed.
steps.outcome: Data inventory and confirmed-downloaded scope established.
steps.tool: Cloud storage console / data classification tooling

steps.title: Immediately close the misconfiguration
steps.desc: Correct the resource's access policy to remove public/overly-broad access.
steps.outcome: Public access removed immediately.

steps.title: Block the scanning source where identifiable
steps.desc: Where the scanning source IP/range is identifiable and not a legitimate scanner (e.g. a security researcher), apply a block at the cloud network/WAF layer.
steps.outcome: Further scanning from the identified source blocked where feasible.
steps.abort: Public cloud scanning often originates from constantly-rotating infrastructure — blocking may have limited effect; prioritize closing the misconfiguration instead.

steps.title: Audit for similar misconfigurations across the entire cloud estate at scale
steps.desc: Given the scanner's scale-oriented approach, run a comprehensive scan across all storage resources in the environment (and any linked accounts/subscriptions) for similar misconfigurations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no other instances of the same misconfiguration exist anywhere in the estate.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the exposed/downloaded data and coordinate with Legal on breach-notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Confirm remediation is complete across the estate
steps.desc: Verify all identified resources are correctly restricted and no residual public access paths remain.
steps.outcome: Remediation confirmed complete across the full scope.

steps.title: Document the case and implement account-wide preventive guardrails
steps.desc: Record findings and implement organization-wide guardrails (block-public-access defaults, continuous CSPM monitoring) given the scale at which this class of scanner operates.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and preventive controls strengthened organization-wide.

ITID-34913.def: An event in which sensitive data is exposed and exfiltrated via a cloud-hosted database snapshot, automated backup, or export file left with overly permissive access, exposing structured records (databases) rather than arbitrary file objects.
ITID-34913.purpose: Captures exfiltration occurring through a misconfigured cloud database snapshot or backup export left accessible, a structured-data variant distinct from generic object storage exposure.
scopeIncludes: Database snapshot/backup file (RDS snapshot, database export) left publicly or overly broadly accessible
Automated backup job writing to a location with misconfigured access permissions
Bulk download/query of an exposed managed database instance due to a network/access-control misconfiguration
scopeExcludes: Generic object storage bucket exposure without a database/backup-specific artifact (ITID-34911, 34912)
ITID-34913.severity: Critical: database snapshots/exports typically contain complete, highly structured, and often more sensitive record sets than arbitrary file storage.
ITID-34913.escalation: Escalate immediately to cloud security, legal, and privacy; database exports often contain full customer/financial record sets warranting expedited breach assessment.
indicators: Cloud provider audit log showing a database snapshot marked public/shared broadly
External access to a managed database endpoint from an unrecognized network
Automated backup job configuration audit revealing an overly permissive destination
vectors: Database snapshot shared publicly or with an overly broad account list during a backup/migration/testing process
Managed database instance left accessible from the public internet with weak/default credentials
rootCauses: No CSPM coverage specifically for database snapshot/backup sharing settings
Backup/export processes not subject to the same access-control review as primary production data stores
Database instances provisioned with public network access enabled by default
controls: CSPM coverage of database snapshot/backup sharing configuration
Network access restriction (no public endpoint) for managed database instances
ITID-34913.detection: Moderate-Strong: cloud provider audit logs capture snapshot sharing changes when CSPM/logging is properly scoped to include backup/snapshot resources specifically.
ITID-34913.response: Immediately revoke snapshot/backup sharing, audit access logs, and assess the full scope of the exposed record set given the structured nature of database exports.
metrics: Count of confirmed database snapshot/backup exposure incidents per year
Percentage of database resources covered by CSPM snapshot-sharing monitoring
ITID-34913.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34911/34912 by the structured-database-artifact nature of the exposure (snapshot/backup/export) rather than generic file-object storage.

playbook.name: Response: Exfiltration via Misconfigured Cloud Database Snapshot/Backup Export
playbook.description: For data confirmed or suspected to have been exfiltrated via a cloud database snapshot or backup that was misconfigured to be publicly accessible or exportable.

steps.title: Confirm the misconfiguration and review cloud audit logs for access
steps.desc: Review the snapshot/backup's access policy and cloud audit logs (CloudTrail-equivalent) to confirm public/overly-broad accessibility and identify all access/export/download events.
steps.outcome: Misconfiguration confirmed and full list of accessing parties/timestamps established.

steps.title: Determine what data the snapshot/backup contains and the exposure window
steps.desc: Identify the database(s) the snapshot/backup represents, the data classification, and how long the misconfiguration had been in place.
steps.outcome: Data inventory and exposure window established.
steps.tool: Cloud database console / data classification tooling

steps.title: Immediately close the misconfiguration
steps.desc: Correct the snapshot/backup's access policy to remove public/overly-broad access.
steps.guidance: This is the highest-priority containment action.
steps.outcome: Public access removed immediately.

steps.title: Revoke or rotate any credentials that may have facilitated the misconfiguration
steps.desc: If the misconfiguration was introduced via a compromised credential or automated pipeline, rotate the relevant credentials.
steps.outcome: Any credential-based contributing factor addressed.

steps.title: Audit for similar misconfigurations across all snapshots/backups in the estate
steps.desc: Scan all other database snapshots and backups in the environment for similar public-access or overly-broad-sharing misconfigurations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no other instances of the same misconfiguration exist.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the exposed data and coordinate with Legal on breach-notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Confirm remediation is complete
steps.desc: Verify the snapshot/backup policy is correctly restricted and no residual public access paths remain.
steps.outcome: Remediation confirmed complete.

steps.title: Document the case and implement preventive guardrails for snapshots/backups
steps.desc: Record findings and implement/strengthen automated guardrails (default-private snapshots, CSPM alerting on backup sharing changes) to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and preventive controls strengthened.

ITID-34914.def: A public cloud misconfiguration exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Public Cloud Misconfiguration, pending further investigation.
ITID-34914.purpose: Intake bucket for public cloud misconfiguration exfiltration activity that does not fit the manual bucket, automated scanning, or database snapshot leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reported cloud exposure with resource type/actor not yet determined
Ambiguous cloud misconfiguration exposure spanning multiple sub-patterns
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34911, 34912, or 34913 once investigated
ITID-34914.severity: High pending triage; treat as high-severity by default given the public-exposure context.
ITID-34914.escalation: Escalate immediately to cloud security triage for reclassification.
indicators: Generic CSPM public-exposure alert lacking enough detail for specific classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient detail available to classify the specific cloud misconfiguration pattern at intake
controls: CSPM monitoring
ITID-34914.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34914.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Public Cloud Misconfiguration ITID as soon as possible.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34914.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Public Cloud Misconfiguration Exfiltration
playbook.description: For public-cloud-misconfiguration exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly a public bucket, automated scanner harvesting, or snapshot/backup export) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear.

steps.title: Confirm the misconfiguration and review cloud audit logs for access
steps.desc: Review the resource's access policy and cloud audit logs to confirm the misconfiguration and identify all access/download events.
steps.outcome: Misconfiguration confirmed and access activity established.

steps.title: Determine what data was exposed and the exposure window
steps.desc: Inventory the resource's contents and establish how long the misconfiguration had been in place.
steps.outcome: Data inventory and exposure window established.

steps.title: Immediately close the misconfiguration
steps.desc: Correct the resource's access policy to remove public/overly-broad access.
steps.outcome: Public access removed immediately.

steps.title: Revoke or rotate any credentials that may have contributed
steps.desc: If a compromised credential or pipeline introduced the misconfiguration, rotate the relevant credentials.
steps.outcome: Any credential-based contributing factor addressed.

steps.title: Audit for similar misconfigurations across the cloud estate
steps.desc: Scan all other resources of the same type in the environment for similar misconfigurations.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no other instances of the same misconfiguration exist.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the exposed data and coordinate with Legal on breach-notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Confirm remediation is complete
steps.desc: Verify the resource policy is correctly restricted and no residual public access paths remain.
steps.outcome: Remediation confirmed complete.

steps.title: Document and reclassify for future reference
steps.desc: Record the case, note the specific resource type/technique for future classification consistency, and strengthen relevant preventive guardrails.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and preventive controls strengthened.

ITID-34921.def: An event in which an actor authenticates to a cloud provider's management console using compromised or stolen valid credentials and directly downloads storage objects, distinguished from Public Cloud Misconfiguration leaves by requiring valid authentication rather than exploiting a public-exposure gap.
ITID-34921.purpose: Captures an actor using compromised valid credentials to log into the cloud provider console and directly download storage objects, a credential-driven (not misconfiguration-driven) exfiltration path.
scopeIncludes: Console login with compromised credentials followed by bulk object download from storage
Use of stolen API keys/access keys to download objects via console or CLI
Download activity from an account authenticated via credentials known to be phished/leaked
scopeExcludes: Download from a publicly/anonymously accessible resource requiring no valid credentials (Public Cloud Misconfiguration group, ITID-34911-34914)
Bulk database export/dump specifically (ITID-34922)
VM disk snapshot export (ITID-34923)
ITID-34921.severity: Critical: valid-credential access combined with bulk download indicates a confirmed account compromise with realized data loss.
ITID-34921.escalation: Escalate immediately to incident response for credential compromise investigation alongside data loss assessment.
indicators: Console/API login from an anomalous location/device for the credential owner
Access key usage pattern inconsistent with the key's normal/expected automation source
Bulk object download immediately following an authentication anomaly
vectors: Phished or leaked console credentials/access keys used to authenticate and bulk-download storage objects
rootCauses: No MFA enforced on cloud console access
Long-lived static access keys not rotated or scoped to least privilege
No anomaly detection on cloud console/API authentication patterns
controls: MFA enforcement on cloud console access
Access key rotation and least-privilege scoping
Cloud authentication anomaly detection
ITID-34921.detection: Strong: cloud provider audit/CloudTrail-equivalent logs give direct visibility into authentication and download events.
ITID-34921.response: Treat as a confirmed account compromise: revoke/rotate the compromised credential, preserve logs, and scope exactly what was downloaded.
metrics: Count of confirmed compromised-credential cloud download incidents per year
Percentage of cloud accounts with MFA enforced
ITID-34921.notes: Differentiated from the Public Cloud Misconfiguration group by requiring valid (albeit compromised) credentials rather than exploiting a public-exposure gap.

playbook.name: Response: Direct Console Download of Cloud Storage Objects Using Compromised Credentials
playbook.description: For data confirmed or suspected to have been exfiltrated via direct download of cloud storage objects through the management console, using compromised legitimate credentials.

steps.title: Confirm the console download activity and scope via cloud audit logs
steps.desc: Review cloud audit logs (CloudTrail-equivalent) for console-based GetObject/download events under the compromised identity, identifying the objects, volume, and timing.
steps.guidance: Console-based downloads may not always be logged at the same granularity as API calls — check console session logs specifically.
steps.outcome: Full scope of downloaded objects established.
steps.tool: Cloud audit logs (CloudTrail-equivalent) / console session logs

steps.title: Determine the credential compromise vector
steps.desc: Review sign-in logs to establish how the credentials were compromised (phishing, credential stuffing, leaked key) and the access timeline.
steps.outcome: Compromise vector and timeline established.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised credentials and active sessions immediately
steps.desc: Disable/rotate the compromised credentials and terminate any active console sessions.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Review and remove any additional access the attacker may have granted themselves
steps.desc: Check for new IAM users, roles, or access keys created during the compromise window, and remove any unauthorized additions.
steps.outcome: Confirmed no additional persistence mechanisms remain.

steps.title: Enforce MFA and conditional access on the affected identity
steps.desc: Ensure MFA is enrolled and enforced, and apply conditional access/least-privilege policies to prevent re-compromise.
steps.outcome: Identity hardened against repeat compromise.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the downloaded data and coordinate with Legal on breach-notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Issue new credentials to the legitimate user
steps.desc: Provision new credentials to the legitimate user/service and confirm normal operation resumes.
steps.outcome: Legitimate access restored with a clean credential.

steps.title: Document the case and review credential-security practices
steps.desc: Record findings and confirm MFA enforcement and credential-hygiene practices are consistently applied across the cloud estate.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and process gap addressed.

ITID-34922.def: An event in which an actor with cloud database administrative console access performs a full or large-scale export/dump of a managed database instance, using legitimate admin functionality rather than object storage download or snapshot mechanisms.
ITID-34922.purpose: Captures a bulk database export or dump performed through legitimate admin console access, distinguished from generic object downloads by its structured-database, admin-privilege-driven nature.
scopeIncludes: Full or near-full database export/dump initiated via the cloud provider's admin console or CLI
Export volume significantly exceeding the admin user's normal operational pattern
Export destination pointing outside the organization's managed environment
scopeExcludes: Direct storage object download using compromised credentials (ITID-34921)
VM disk snapshot export (ITID-34923)
Exfiltration via a misconfigured/publicly exposed snapshot (ITID-34913)
ITID-34922.severity: Critical: full database exports typically contain complete, highly sensitive structured record sets.
ITID-34922.escalation: Escalate immediately; a full database export by an admin account warrants both compromise investigation and insider risk review.
indicators: Database admin console log showing a full/large export operation initiated outside normal maintenance windows
Export destination outside the organization's approved network/account boundary
Export volume significantly above the admin's historical baseline
vectors: Legitimate database admin export/dump functionality used to exfiltrate a complete data set, whether by a compromised admin account or a malicious insider with admin rights
rootCauses: No alerting on large database export operations
Database admin privileges not scoped/reviewed to least privilege
Export destination not restricted to approved internal locations
controls: Alerting on large-scale database export/dump operations
Least-privilege database admin access review
Export destination allowlisting
ITID-34922.detection: Strong: cloud database admin console logs directly capture export operations and their scope.
ITID-34922.response: Determine whether the admin account is compromised or the actor is an authorized insider; scope the exported data and destination immediately.
metrics: Count of confirmed large-scale database export incidents per year
Percentage of database admin accounts under export-volume alerting
detections: Database admin console export volume alert
ITID-34922.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34921 by the admin-console database-export mechanism (structured, privileged) versus general object storage download, and from ITID-34923 by targeting database export rather than VM disk snapshots.

playbook.name: Response: Bulk Cloud Database Export/Dump via Admin Console Access
playbook.description: For data confirmed or suspected to have been exfiltrated via a bulk database export/dump performed through cloud database admin console access, using either compromised or misused legitimate credentials.

steps.title: Confirm the export/dump activity and scope via cloud/database audit logs
steps.desc: Review cloud audit logs and database engine logs for export/snapshot-creation/dump events, identifying the tables/databases, volume, and destination of the export.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the export activity established.
steps.tool: Cloud audit logs / database engine logs

steps.title: Determine whether this is a compromised credential or an insider misuse of legitimate access
steps.desc: Review sign-in logs and the account's normal duties to establish root cause.
steps.guidance: If insider-driven, escalate to HR/Legal per insider-data-handling policy.
steps.outcome: Root cause established.

steps.title: Revoke compromised credentials or restrict insider access as appropriate
steps.desc: If compromised, disable/rotate credentials and terminate sessions; if insider-driven, notify HR/Legal before restricting access.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized export activity prevented.

steps.title: Determine whether the exported dump/snapshot is still accessible and secure it
steps.desc: Locate where the export was stored (a storage bucket, downloaded locally, etc.) and secure or delete it if not needed for evidence.
steps.outcome: Exported data secured or removed from further exposure.

steps.title: Review and tighten export permissions on the database
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege restrictions on who can perform bulk export/snapshot operations on the affected database going forward.
steps.outcome: Export capability appropriately restricted.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the exported data and coordinate with Legal on breach-notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Confirm remediation is complete
steps.desc: Verify credentials are rotated/access restricted appropriately and the exported data is secured or removed.
steps.outcome: Remediation confirmed complete.

steps.title: Document the case and review database export monitoring/least-privilege
steps.desc: Record findings and assess whether export-operation alerting or role-based restrictions need strengthening.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and monitoring gap addressed.
