ITID-34923.def: An event in which an actor creates a snapshot of a cloud virtual machine's disk volume, exports it, and downloads it outside the organization's cloud environment, exposing the complete file system and any data at rest on that VM.
ITID-34923.purpose: Captures a cloud VM disk snapshot that is exported and downloaded externally, exposing the entire contents of a virtual machine's disk rather than a specific database or object set.
scopeIncludes: VM disk snapshot created and exported to an external account/location
Snapshot download activity via console or CLI from an account without a documented business need
Snapshot sharing setting changed to allow an external account, followed by access from that account
scopeExcludes: Database-specific export/dump via admin console (ITID-34922)
Direct object storage download using compromised credentials (ITID-34921)
Publicly exposed snapshot discovered via misconfiguration scanning (ITID-34913)
ITID-34923.severity: Critical: a full VM disk snapshot exposes the entire file system, potentially including credentials, application data, and configuration secrets.
ITID-34923.escalation: Escalate immediately; treat as a full-system compromise given the breadth of data exposed in a complete disk image.
indicators: Cloud provider audit log showing snapshot creation followed by an export/share-to-external-account action
Snapshot access from an account or network outside the organization's boundary
Snapshot export volume/timing inconsistent with routine backup/DR processes
vectors: Legitimate snapshot creation/export functionality used to exfiltrate an entire VM's disk contents to an attacker-controlled or personal cloud account
rootCauses: No alerting on snapshot sharing changes or exports to external accounts
Snapshot creation/export permissions not scoped to least privilege
Routine backup snapshots not distinguished from ad hoc exports in monitoring
mitreTechniques: T1578.002 Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Create Cloud Instance
controls: Alerting on VM snapshot sharing/export to external accounts
Least-privilege snapshot permission scoping
ITID-34923.detection: Strong: cloud provider audit logs directly capture snapshot creation, sharing, and export actions.
ITID-34923.response: Immediately revoke external snapshot access/sharing, identify the destination account, and treat the source VM's entire contents as potentially exposed.
metrics: Count of confirmed external snapshot export incidents per year
Mean time-to-revocation once detected
ITID-34923.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34922 by targeting a full VM disk snapshot (entire file system) rather than a structured database export, and from ITID-34913 by requiring valid access to trigger export rather than being discovered via public misconfiguration.

playbook.name: Response: Cloud VM Disk Snapshot Exported and Downloaded Externally
playbook.description: For data confirmed or suspected to have been exfiltrated by creating a disk snapshot of a cloud VM and exporting/downloading it externally, exposing the entire disk contents.

steps.title: Confirm the snapshot creation and export activity via cloud audit logs
steps.desc: Review cloud audit logs for snapshot-creation, sharing, and export/download events, identifying the source VM, snapshot destination, and who performed the actions.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the snapshot export activity established.

steps.title: Determine whether this is a compromised credential or an insider misuse of legitimate access
steps.desc: Review sign-in logs and the account's normal duties to establish root cause.
steps.guidance: If insider-driven, escalate to HR/Legal per insider-data-handling policy.
steps.outcome: Root cause established.

steps.title: Revoke compromised credentials or restrict insider access as appropriate
steps.desc: If compromised, disable/rotate credentials and terminate sessions; if insider-driven, notify HR/Legal before restricting access.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized snapshot activity prevented.

steps.title: Revoke sharing on the exported snapshot and delete unneeded copies
steps.desc: Revoke any cross-account sharing on the snapshot and delete copies not needed for evidence preservation.
steps.outcome: Further access to the exported snapshot prevented.

steps.title: Review and tighten snapshot-sharing/export permissions
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege restrictions and, where available, organization policies preventing external sharing of disk snapshots.
steps.outcome: Snapshot export/sharing capability appropriately restricted.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the disk contents (which may include far more than the attacker's original target, given a full-disk snapshot) and coordinate with Legal on breach-notification requirements.
steps.guidance: A full VM disk snapshot often exposes secrets, cached credentials, and data well beyond what the attacker specifically sought — scope broadly.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed comprehensively and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Rotate any secrets/credentials found on the affected VM's disk
steps.desc: Given the full-disk exposure, rotate any secrets, keys, or credentials that were stored on the source VM.
steps.outcome: Secondary credential exposure remediated.

steps.title: Document the case and review snapshot-export organization policy
steps.desc: Record findings and implement/strengthen organization-wide policy restricting external snapshot sharing.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and preventive controls strengthened.

ITID-34924.def: A direct cloud download exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Direct Downloads, pending further investigation.
ITID-34924.purpose: Intake bucket for direct cloud download exfiltration activity that does not fit the compromised-credential object download, database export, or VM snapshot leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reported direct cloud download data loss with resource type/actor not yet determined
Ambiguous direct cloud download activity spanning multiple sub-patterns
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34921, 34922, or 34923 once investigated
ITID-34924.severity: High pending triage; treat as high-severity by default given the confirmed-access context.
ITID-34924.escalation: Escalate immediately to cloud security triage for reclassification.
indicators: Generic cloud console/API download alert lacking enough detail for specific classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient detail available to classify the specific direct-download pattern at intake
controls: Cloud audit log monitoring
ITID-34924.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34924.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Direct Downloads ITID as soon as possible.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34924.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Direct Cloud Download Exfiltration
playbook.description: For direct-cloud-download exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly console object download, database dump, or VM snapshot export) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear.

steps.title: Confirm the download/export activity and scope via cloud audit logs
steps.desc: Review cloud audit logs to identify what was downloaded/exported, by whom, and the volume/sensitivity involved.
steps.outcome: Activity characterized well enough to redirect to a specific playbook or proceed here.

steps.title: Determine whether this is a compromised credential or an insider misuse of legitimate access
steps.desc: Review sign-in logs and the account's normal duties to establish root cause.
steps.guidance: If insider-driven, escalate to HR/Legal per insider-data-handling policy.
steps.outcome: Root cause established.

steps.title: Revoke compromised credentials or restrict insider access as appropriate
steps.desc: If compromised, disable/rotate credentials and terminate sessions; if insider-driven, notify HR/Legal before restricting access.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized activity prevented.

steps.title: Secure or remove any remaining copies of the exfiltrated data
steps.desc: Locate and secure or remove any accessible copies of the downloaded/exported data that are not needed for evidence.
steps.outcome: Further exposure of the exfiltrated copies prevented.

steps.title: Review and tighten the relevant access/export permissions
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege restrictions appropriate to the specific resource type and access path identified.
steps.outcome: Access/export capability appropriately restricted.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess the sensitivity of the accessed data and coordinate with Legal on breach-notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and obligations addressed.

steps.title: Confirm remediation is complete
steps.desc: Verify credentials are rotated/access restricted appropriately and copies are secured.
steps.outcome: Remediation confirmed complete.

steps.title: Document and reclassify for future reference
steps.desc: Record the case, note the specific access path/technique for future classification consistency, and strengthen relevant monitoring.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and monitoring gap addressed.

ITID-34931.def: An event in which an actor provisions a temporary, short-lived cloud VM instance and uses it as a staging point or relay for data exfiltration, taking advantage of the VM's ephemeral lifecycle to minimize the window available for forensic analysis.
ITID-34931.purpose: Captures an actor spinning up a short-lived cloud virtual machine specifically to serve as an exfiltration staging or relay point before it is torn down.
scopeIncludes: Cloud VM instance created, used briefly for data transfer/staging, and terminated within a short window (hours to a few days)
VM instance created using compromised credentials or an unauthorized account within the organization's cloud environment
VM instance created in an unusual region/account specifically to receive staged data
scopeExcludes: Serverless function abuse for exfiltration specifically (ITID-34932)
Temporary storage bucket creation/deletion (ITID-34933)
ITID-34931.severity: High-Critical: the short lifecycle is a deliberate anti-forensic choice indicating premeditation.
ITID-34931.escalation: Escalate immediately upon detection; the ephemeral nature means evidence degrades quickly, so preserve logs/snapshots before termination if possible.
indicators: Cloud provider audit log showing VM instance creation and termination within an unusually short window
VM instance created by an account/role with no legitimate compute-provisioning need
Network traffic from the temporary instance matching known exfiltration patterns before termination
vectors: Compromised cloud account used to spin up a short-lived VM as a relay/staging point for stolen data before the instance is deleted to remove forensic evidence
rootCauses: No alerting on anomalous VM provisioning by accounts/roles without a compute-provisioning business need
Cloud audit log retention insufficient to capture short-lived instance activity after termination
mitreTechniques: T1578.002 Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Create Cloud Instance
controls: Anomalous VM provisioning alerting
Extended cloud audit log retention independent of resource lifecycle
ITID-34931.detection: Moderate: detection depends on real-time provisioning alerts, since the resource itself disappears quickly and post-hoc forensics is limited.
ITID-34931.response: Capture and preserve all available logs/network telemetry immediately upon detection, before the instance's data or logs age out.
metrics: Count of confirmed ephemeral-VM staging incidents per year
Mean time from VM creation to detection
ITID-34931.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34932 by using a full VM instance rather than a serverless function, and from ITID-34933 by the compute-instance (not storage-bucket) resource type.

playbook.name: Response: Ephemeral Cloud VM Spun Up as Exfiltration Staging Point
playbook.description: For an ephemeral cloud VM confirmed or suspected to have been spun up by an attacker as a temporary staging point for exfiltration, then torn down — an anti-forensic pattern requiring a hunt for other similar ephemeral resources.

steps.title: Confirm the ephemeral VM's creation, activity, and teardown via cloud audit logs
steps.desc: Review cloud audit logs (which persist even after the resource itself is deleted) for the VM's creation, network activity, and termination events, since the resource itself will typically be gone by the time this is investigated.
steps.outcome: Ephemeral VM's full lifecycle and activity reconstructed from logs.

steps.title: Hunt for other ephemeral resources the same actor may have spun up and already torn down
steps.desc: Given the anti-forensic pattern, proactively search cloud audit logs for other short-lived resource creation/deletion events from the same account/credential/timeframe, since the actor likely used more than one such resource.
steps.guidance: This hunting step is critical — the actor's use-and-discard pattern means a single identified instance is likely not the whole picture.
steps.outcome: Full inventory of ephemeral resources created and torn down by the actor established.
steps.tool: Cloud audit logs / CSPM historical analysis

steps.title: Determine the compromised credential/account used to spin up the resources
steps.desc: Identify the account/credential responsible and how it was obtained.
steps.outcome: Compromise vector established.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised credentials immediately
steps.desc: Disable/rotate the compromised credentials and terminate any active sessions.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Terminate and preserve evidence from any remaining active ephemeral resources
steps.desc: For any ephemeral resources identified as still running, preserve forensic evidence (memory/disk snapshot) before termination.
steps.outcome: Any still-active resources contained with evidence preserved.

steps.title: Apply guardrails to detect and constrain future ephemeral-resource abuse
steps.desc: Implement alerting on rapid resource creation-and-deletion patterns and apply organization policies restricting who can create compute resources.
steps.outcome: Detection and preventive guardrails strengthened against this anti-forensic pattern.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal and executive leadership on the full scope of data staged/exfiltrated across all identified ephemeral resources.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Document the case and review log-retention sufficiency for ephemeral resources
steps.desc: Record findings and confirm cloud audit-log retention is sufficient to reconstruct short-lived resource activity, since this is the only evidence source once resources are torn down.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and log-retention gap addressed if found.

ITID-34932.def: An event in which an actor deploys or modifies a serverless function within the organization's cloud environment to automate the collection and transfer of sensitive data, exploiting serverless compute's typically lighter logging/monitoring footprint compared to traditional VMs.
ITID-34932.purpose: Captures a serverless function (e.g., Lambda, Cloud Function) abused to automate data exfiltration, exploiting the low-visibility, event-driven, no-persistent-infrastructure nature of serverless compute.
scopeIncludes: Serverless function created/modified to read from a data store and transfer contents to an external endpoint
Function triggered on a schedule or event to perform repeated automated exfiltration
Function deployed by an account/role with no legitimate serverless development responsibility
scopeExcludes: Full VM instance used as a staging point (ITID-34931)
Temporary storage bucket creation/deletion (ITID-34933)
ITID-34932.severity: High-Critical: serverless functions often have broad IAM permissions and minimal default logging, making this a stealthy, high-impact technique.
ITID-34932.escalation: Escalate immediately; review the function's IAM role permissions to scope exactly what data stores it could access.
indicators: Serverless function deployment/modification by an account without a legitimate development role
Function IAM role with broad read access to sensitive data stores disproportionate to its stated purpose
Function invocation logs showing outbound network calls to an external/unrecognized endpoint
vectors: Compromised cloud credentials used to deploy or modify a serverless function that reads sensitive data and transfers it externally on a trigger or schedule
rootCauses: Serverless function deployment not subject to the same change-review process as traditional infrastructure
Overly broad IAM roles assigned to serverless functions by default
Serverless function invocation/network logging not enabled or centrally aggregated
controls: Serverless function deployment change-review process
Least-privilege IAM role scoping for serverless functions
Serverless function invocation/network logging
ITID-34932.detection: Weak-Moderate: depends heavily on whether serverless-specific logging and IAM review are in place, an often-overlooked area.
ITID-34932.response: Disable/quarantine the function immediately, review its full IAM permission scope, and audit invocation history for the actual data accessed.
metrics: Count of confirmed serverless-function exfiltration incidents per year
Percentage of serverless functions with least-privilege IAM roles
ITID-34932.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34931 by using serverless (function-as-a-service) compute rather than a persistent VM instance, exploiting a distinct and often less-monitored control surface.

playbook.name: Response: Serverless Function Abused for Automated Data Exfiltration
playbook.description: For a serverless function (e.g. cloud function/lambda) confirmed or suspected to have been abused by an attacker to automate data exfiltration, an ephemeral-compute pattern that is easy to deploy and hard to spot amid legitimate function activity.

steps.title: Confirm the malicious function's deployment and activity via cloud audit logs
steps.desc: Review cloud audit logs and function-execution logs to identify the malicious function, its trigger mechanism, execution history, and outbound network activity.
steps.guidance: Malicious functions are often deployed with innocuous names to blend in with legitimate serverless workloads.
steps.outcome: Malicious function's full activity reconstructed.
steps.tool: Cloud audit logs / function execution logs

steps.title: Hunt for other similar abused functions or resources from the same actor
steps.desc: Given the ease of deploying additional serverless resources, search for other functions/triggers created by the same account/credential/timeframe.
steps.outcome: Full inventory of abused serverless resources established.
steps.tool: Cloud audit logs / CSPM historical analysis

steps.title: Determine the compromised credential/account used to deploy the function
steps.desc: Identify the account/credential responsible and how it was obtained.
steps.outcome: Compromise vector established.

steps.title: Disable/delete the malicious function and revoke the compromised credentials
steps.desc: Immediately disable or delete the malicious function and revoke/rotate the compromised credentials.
steps.outcome: Ongoing automated exfiltration stopped and attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Review and remove the function's associated triggers, roles, and permissions
steps.desc: Remove any event triggers, IAM roles, or resource permissions the attacker configured to support the function.
steps.outcome: All supporting configuration removed.

steps.title: Apply guardrails on serverless function deployment and outbound access
steps.desc: Implement organization policies restricting who can deploy functions and what outbound network access functions are permitted by default.
steps.outcome: Preventive guardrails strengthened against serverless abuse.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal and executive leadership on the full scope of data exfiltrated via the function(s).
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Document the case and review serverless-workload monitoring
steps.desc: Record findings and confirm monitoring/alerting exists for anomalous function deployment and outbound data-transfer patterns.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and monitoring gap addressed.

ITID-34933.def: An event in which an actor creates a cloud storage bucket, uses it briefly to stage or relay exfiltrated data, and deletes the bucket shortly afterward, using the create-use-delete lifecycle itself as a deliberate anti-forensic technique.
ITID-34933.purpose: Captures a temporary cloud storage bucket created specifically to receive staged exfiltration data and then deleted afterward as an anti-forensic step.
scopeIncludes: Storage bucket created and deleted within an unusually short window (hours to days) with data transfer activity in between
Bucket created by an account/role without a legitimate storage-provisioning business need
Bucket deletion event closely following a period of unusual object write/read activity
scopeExcludes: Ephemeral VM instance used as a staging point (ITID-34931)
Serverless function abuse for exfiltration (ITID-34932)
Publicly exposed, long-standing bucket discovered via misconfiguration scanning (ITID-34911-34913)
ITID-34933.severity: High-Critical: the deliberate create-delete lifecycle indicates premeditated anti-forensic intent.
ITID-34933.escalation: Escalate immediately upon detection; attempt to preserve any available logs/versioning data before they age out or are permanently lost.
indicators: Cloud provider audit log showing bucket creation and deletion within a short window
Object write activity to the bucket immediately preceding its deletion
Bucket created by an account/role inconsistent with normal storage-provisioning patterns
vectors: Compromised cloud account used to create a short-lived storage bucket as a relay/dead-drop for exfiltrated data, deleted immediately after to remove evidence
rootCauses: No alerting on anomalous bucket creation-then-deletion patterns
Cloud audit log retention insufficient to capture short-lived resource activity after deletion
No object versioning/retention lock on storage resources to preserve evidence of deleted content
controls: Anomalous bucket create-then-delete pattern alerting
Extended audit log retention independent of resource lifecycle
Object versioning/retention lock on sensitive storage resources
ITID-34933.detection: Weak-Moderate: detection depends on real-time provisioning/deletion alerting since the resource and its contents disappear quickly.
ITID-34933.response: Capture and preserve all available logs immediately upon detection; treat any recoverable log/versioning data as critical forensic evidence.
metrics: Count of confirmed temporary-bucket anti-forensic incidents per year
Mean time from bucket creation to detection
ITID-34933.notes: Differentiated from ITID-34931/34932 by the storage-bucket (not compute-instance or serverless-function) resource type used in the ephemeral staging-and-teardown pattern.

playbook.name: Response: Temporary Storage Bucket Created and Deleted After Exfiltration (Anti-Forensic)
playbook.description: For a temporary cloud storage bucket confirmed or suspected to have been created by an attacker as a collection point, then deleted after exfiltration to remove evidence — an anti-forensic pattern requiring a hunt for other similar temporary resources.

steps.title: Confirm the temporary bucket's creation, activity, and deletion via cloud audit logs
steps.desc: Review cloud audit logs (which persist even after the bucket itself is deleted) for the bucket's creation, object uploads/downloads, and deletion events.
steps.outcome: Temporary bucket's full lifecycle and activity reconstructed from logs.

steps.title: Hunt for other temporary buckets/resources the same actor may have already created and deleted
steps.desc: Given the anti-forensic use-and-discard pattern, proactively search cloud audit logs for other short-lived bucket creation/deletion events from the same account/credential/timeframe.
steps.guidance: This hunting step is critical — assume the identified bucket is not the only one used.
steps.outcome: Full inventory of temporary buckets created and deleted by the actor established.
steps.tool: Cloud audit logs / CSPM historical analysis

steps.title: Determine the compromised credential/account used to create the bucket
steps.desc: Identify the account/credential responsible and how it was obtained.
steps.outcome: Compromise vector established.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised credentials immediately
steps.desc: Disable/rotate the compromised credentials and terminate any active sessions.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Check for and secure any still-existing copies of the collected data
steps.desc: Since the collection bucket itself is deleted, check whether the objects were also copied elsewhere before deletion, and secure any remaining copies.
steps.outcome: Any remaining copies of exfiltrated data secured or confirmed absent.
steps.abort: If the bucket and all copies are confirmed gone, note in the impact assessment that direct data recovery is not possible.

steps.title: Apply guardrails to detect and constrain future temporary-bucket abuse
steps.desc: Implement alerting on rapid bucket creation-and-deletion patterns and apply organization policies restricting who can create storage resources.
steps.outcome: Detection and preventive guardrails strengthened against this anti-forensic pattern.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal and executive leadership on the full scope of data collected/exfiltrated across all identified temporary buckets.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Document the case and review log-retention sufficiency for deleted resources
steps.desc: Record findings and confirm cloud audit-log retention is sufficient to reconstruct deleted-resource activity, since this is the only evidence source once resources are torn down.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and log-retention gap addressed if found.

ITID-34934.def: A temporary cloud instance exfiltration event that cannot yet be classified into a more specific sibling ITID under Temporary Instances, pending further investigation.
ITID-34934.purpose: Intake bucket for temporary cloud instance exfiltration activity that does not fit the ephemeral VM, serverless function, or temporary bucket leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reported temporary-resource-based cloud data loss with resource type not yet determined
Ambiguous ephemeral cloud resource activity spanning multiple sub-patterns
scopeExcludes: Any event classifiable as ITID-34931, 34932, or 34933 once investigated
ITID-34934.severity: High pending triage; treat as high-severity by default given the anti-forensic/ephemeral-resource context.
ITID-34934.escalation: Escalate immediately to cloud security triage for reclassification.
indicators: Generic ephemeral cloud resource creation/deletion alert lacking enough detail for specific classification
vectors: Not yet determined at time of intake
rootCauses: Insufficient detail available to classify the specific ephemeral resource type at intake
controls: Cloud audit log monitoring for ephemeral resource lifecycle
ITID-34934.detection: Variable; depends on the underlying alert source that triggered intake.
ITID-34934.response: Triage and reclassify to a specific Temporary Instances ITID as soon as possible.
metrics: Count and aging of incidents left in this unclassified bucket
ITID-34934.notes: Catch-all leaf; used only when a specific sibling ITID cannot yet be determined.

playbook.name: Response: Unclassified / General Temporary Instance Exfiltration
playbook.description: For ephemeral/temporary-cloud-resource exfiltration activity that does not fit a more specific sub-category (not clearly a staging VM, abused serverless function, or temporary storage bucket) — use as a general starting checklist and escalate to a specific playbook once the pattern is clear. Always hunt for other ephemeral resources given the anti-forensic pattern.

steps.title: Confirm the temporary resource's creation, activity, and teardown via cloud audit logs
steps.desc: Review cloud audit logs (which persist even after the resource itself is deleted) for the resource's creation, activity, and deletion events.
steps.outcome: Resource's full lifecycle and activity reconstructed from logs.

steps.title: Hunt for other ephemeral resources the same actor may have already created and torn down
steps.desc: Given the anti-forensic use-and-discard pattern common to this leaf category, proactively search cloud audit logs for other short-lived resource creation/deletion events from the same account/credential/timeframe.
steps.guidance: Assume the identified resource is not the only one used.
steps.outcome: Full inventory of ephemeral resources created and torn down by the actor established.
steps.tool: Cloud audit logs / CSPM historical analysis

steps.title: Determine the compromised credential/account used
steps.desc: Identify the account/credential responsible and how it was obtained.
steps.outcome: Compromise vector established.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised credentials immediately
steps.desc: Disable/rotate the compromised credentials and terminate any active sessions.
steps.outcome: Attacker access terminated.

steps.title: Terminate and secure any remaining active ephemeral resources
steps.desc: For any resources identified as still running, preserve forensic evidence before termination and secure any remaining copies of exfiltrated data.
steps.outcome: Any still-active resources contained with evidence preserved.

steps.title: Apply guardrails to detect and constrain future ephemeral-resource abuse
steps.desc: Implement alerting on rapid resource creation-and-deletion patterns and apply organization policies restricting who can create resources.
steps.outcome: Detection and preventive guardrails strengthened against this anti-forensic pattern.

steps.title: Scope data exposure and coordinate executive/legal/regulatory response
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal and executive leadership on the full scope of data staged/exfiltrated across all identified ephemeral resources.
steps.outcome: Full-scale impact assessed and appropriate stakeholders engaged.

steps.title: Document the case and review log-retention sufficiency for deleted resources
steps.desc: Record findings and confirm cloud audit-log retention is sufficient to reconstruct short-lived resource activity, and note the specific resource type for future classification consistency.
steps.outcome: Finding logged and log-retention gap addressed if found.
